Getting this wrong would move every information criterion.  @param structure An mclust model code. @param n_profiles How many profiles. @param n_continuous How many continuous indicators. @return A single integer. @noRd

.multilpa_structure_variances.name: .multilpa_structure_variances
.multilpa_structure_variances.documentation: Maximize the diagonal covariances under a constrained structure  @param diagonals One row per profile and column per indicator of the   posterior-weighted squared deviations the M-step accumulates. @param weights The effective membership of each profile. @param structure An axis-parallel mclust model code. @param min_variance The variance lower bound. @param max_iter Iterations allowed for the one structure that needs them. @param tol Relative convergence tolerance for that iteration. @return A matrix of variances, one row per profile and column per indicator. @noRd

.multilpa_evi_variances.name: .multilpa_evi_variances
.multilpa_evi_variances.documentation: Equal volume, varying shape: a closed form  Sigma_k = lambda * A_k with |A_k| = 1, so A_k is the profile's own scatter rescaled to determinant one and lambda is the average of the determinants those rescalings divided out. Celeux and Govaert (1995), model `[lambda B_k]`.  @param diagonals One row of scatter diagonals per profile. @param n The total effective membership. @param min_variance The variance lower bound, which also keeps the geometric   mean away from zero. @return A matrix of variances. @noRd

.multilpa_vei_variances.name: .multilpa_vei_variances
.multilpa_vei_variances.documentation: Varying volume, equal shape: a bounded fixed point  Sigma_k = lambda_k * A with |A| = 1. Each half has a closed form given the other and neither has one alone, so the two are alternated. Celeux and Govaert (1995), model `[lambda_k B]`.  @param diagonals One row of scatter diagonals per profile. @param weights The effective membership of each profile. @param min_variance The variance lower bound. @param max_iter The iteration cap. @param tol Relative convergence tolerance on the shape. @return A matrix of variances. @noRd

.multilpa_scatter_diagonals.name: .multilpa_scatter_diagonals
.multilpa_scatter_diagonals.documentation: The scatter diagonals of a list of per-profile scatter matrices  The observed-data M-step accumulates full matrices even for a diagonal model, because a missing pair contributes an off-diagonal adjustment. Only the diagonal identifies an axis-parallel structure.  @param scatter A list of per-profile scatter matrices. @return One row per profile and column per indicator. @noRd

.multilpa_check_structure_inference.name: .multilpa_check_structure_inference
.multilpa_check_structure_inference.documentation: Refuse a standard error the coordinates cannot express  Every structure this package fits has a chart, so this refuses only a fit recording a structure code it does not know, such as one made by a newer version.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @return `NULL`, invisibly, when the structure is one that is covered. @noRd

.multilpa_project_start.name: .multilpa_project_start
.multilpa_project_start.documentation: Put starting variances inside the family they will be maximized in  EM only promises a likelihood that does not decrease *within* the family it is maximizing over. A start taken from a wider structure -- a free diagonal handed to an equal-volume model, which is what `start =` does when the two fits differ -- sits outside it, and the first M-step projects onto the family, which can lower the likelihood and trip the monotonicity guard. Projecting the start first means every iteration, including the first, is a step inside the family.  @param parameters A starting parameter list. @param structure An mclust model code, or `NULL` to leave it alone. @param n_observations How many observations the weights should sum to. @param min_variance The variance lower bound. @return The parameter list, with `variances` inside the structure. @noRd

.multilpa_scaled_determinant.name: .multilpa_scaled_determinant
.multilpa_scaled_determinant.documentation: The determinant of a scatter matrix, raised to the power 1/d  Computed in logs: a determinant of a d-by-d scatter underflows long before any of its entries does.  @param scatter A symmetric matrix. @param d Its dimension. @return A positive scalar. @noRd

.multilpa_structure_covariances.name: .multilpa_structure_covariances
.multilpa_structure_covariances.documentation: Maximize the full covariances under a constrained ellipsoidal structure  @param scatter A list of per-profile scatter matrices, posterior weighted. @param weights The effective membership of each profile. @param structure An mclust model code. @param min_variance The eigenvalue lower bound. @param max_iter Iterations allowed for the structures that need them. @param tol Relative convergence tolerance for those. @param inner_steps `NULL` to solve EVE and VVE's orientation to `tol`, or a   number of minorize-maximize steps to take from the warm start. The EM   loop passes a small number: a generalized EM step that improves the   M-step objective without solving it, which keeps every EM iteration   monotone and makes the EM map a fixed function of its input. @return A `d` by `d` by `k` array of covariances. @noRd

.multilpa_eev_covariances.name: .multilpa_eev_covariances
.multilpa_eev_covariances.documentation: Equal volume and shape, varying orientation  Each profile keeps its own eigenvectors; the shared shape is the normalized sum of the eigenvalues and the volume is what that normalization divided out. Celeux and Govaert (1995), model `[lambda D_k A D_k']`.  @param scatter Symmetrized per-profile scatter matrices. @param n The total effective membership. @param d The dimension. @return A list of covariance matrices. @noRd

.multilpa_vev_covariances.name: .multilpa_vev_covariances
.multilpa_vev_covariances.documentation: Varying volume, equal shape, varying orientation  The orientations are each profile's own, so only the volume and the shared shape alternate --- the same fixed point as the diagonal equal-shape model, one dimension up. Celeux and Govaert (1995), model `[lambda_k D_k A D_k']`.  @param scatter Symmetrized per-profile scatter matrices. @param weights The effective membership of each profile. @param d The dimension. @param max_iter The iteration cap. @param tol Relative convergence tolerance on the shape. @return A list of covariance matrices. @noRd

.multilpa_evv_covariances.name: .multilpa_evv_covariances
.multilpa_evv_covariances.documentation: Equal volume, varying shape and orientation  Each profile keeps its whole scatter, rescaled to determinant one; the shared volume averages what those rescalings divided out. No eigenvectors are needed. Celeux and Govaert (1995), model `[lambda D_k A_k D_k']`.  @param scatter Symmetrized per-profile scatter matrices. @param n The total effective membership. @param d The dimension. @return A list of covariance matrices. @noRd

.multilpa_vee_covariances.name: .multilpa_vee_covariances
.multilpa_vee_covariances.documentation: Varying volume, equal shape and orientation  `Sigma_k = lambda_k * C` with `|C| = 1`. The shared matrix and the volumes alternate, exactly as the diagonal equal-shape model does, except that `C` is a full matrix and needs no orthogonal optimization. Celeux and Govaert (1995), model `[lambda_k C]`.  @param scatter Symmetrized per-profile scatter matrices. @param weights The effective membership of each profile. @param d The dimension. @param max_iter The iteration cap. @param tol Relative convergence tolerance on the shared matrix. @return A list of covariance matrices. @noRd

.multilpa_eve_covariances.name: .multilpa_eve_covariances
.multilpa_eve_covariances.documentation: Common orientation with varying shape, at equal or varying volume  `Sigma_k = lambda_k * D * A_k * D'` with one orthogonal `D` shared by every profile. Unlike every other model here, `D` has no closed form: it minimizes `sum_k tr(D A_k^-1 D' W_k) / lambda_k` over the orthogonal matrices. The minorize-maximize step of Browne and McNicholas (2014) is used, which majorizes each term by a linear one and solves the resulting orthogonal Procrustes problem with a singular value decomposition.  @param scatter Symmetrized per-profile scatter matrices. @param weights The effective membership of each profile. @param d The dimension. @param max_iter The iteration cap. @param tol Relative convergence tolerance on the orientation. @param equal_volume `TRUE` for EVE, `FALSE` for VVE. @return A list of covariance matrices. @noRd

.multilpa_reset_structure_log.name: .multilpa_reset_structure_log
.multilpa_reset_structure_log.documentation: Start counting M-steps that stopped at their cap  Called once per fit, so a count never carries from one fit into the next.  @return `NULL`, invisibly. @noRd

.multilpa_warn_structure.name: .multilpa_warn_structure
.multilpa_warn_structure.documentation: Record that a structure's iteration stopped at its cap @param structure The model code. @param max_iter The cap it reached. @return `NULL`, invisibly. @noRd

.multilpa_report_structure_log.name: .multilpa_report_structure_log
.multilpa_report_structure_log.documentation: Report the M-steps that stopped at their cap, once  The expectation-maximization loop keeps going after a partial M-step, and usually converges anyway, so this qualifies the fit rather than rejecting it. The count is the part worth reading: one M-step in three hundred is a different thing from all of them.  @return `NULL`, invisibly. @noRd

.multilpa_structure_arguments.name: .multilpa_structure_arguments
.multilpa_structure_arguments.documentation: The `multilpa()` arguments that ask for a named structure  `enumerate_classes()` grids over model codes, and `multilpa()` takes the three pieces a code is made of. This turns one into the other, so the grid and the fitter cannot disagree about what a code means.  @param structure An mclust model code, or `NA_character_` to leave the   caller's own arguments alone. @return A named list of arguments, empty when nothing was asked for. @noRd

.multilpa_seed_block.name: .multilpa_seed_block
.multilpa_seed_block.documentation: One covariance slice of a previous iteration, as a seed  The structures that iterate share one matrix across profiles, so any slice of the previous answer carries it. `NULL` when there is nothing to start from, which is the first iteration.  @param start A `d` by `d` by `k` array, or `NULL`. @param d The dimension. @return A `d` by `d` matrix, or `NULL`. @noRd

.multilpa_orientation_steps.name: .multilpa_orientation_steps
.multilpa_orientation_steps.documentation: Orientation steps per EM iteration for EVE and VVE  Their shared orientation has no closed form. Solving it to convergence in every M-step spent a median of 220 minorize-maximize steps per EM iteration on work the next iteration discards; a few warm-started steps per iteration reach the same maximum (a generalized EM step). Over 18 fits (three datasets, EVE and VVE, three seeds), 3, 5 and 10 steps landed within 1e-5 to 3e-3 of the full solve's likelihood whenever they reached the same maximum, and took 3.5 to 8 times less time; which maximum a fit reached varied without pattern across settings, the full solve included.  @return A single positive integer. @noRd

.multilpa_eigenvalue_design.name: .multilpa_eigenvalue_design
.multilpa_eigenvalue_design.documentation: Log-eigenvalue design for volume and shape constraints @param k,d Numbers of profiles and dimensions. @param structure Covariance structure code. @return A design whose rows are profile-major log eigenvalues. @noRd

.multilpa_bounded_variances.name: .multilpa_bounded_variances
.multilpa_bounded_variances.documentation: Optimize floored variances inside a volume/shape family  The Gaussian M-step objective is convex in log eigenvalues. The volume and determinant-one shape coordinates make its equality constraints linear; the eigenvalue floor is a linear inequality in those same coordinates. Thus a bound never changes the requested family, unlike clipping individual eigenvalues after an unrestricted update. @param scatter Posterior-weighted scatter diagonals, profiles by dimensions. @param weights Effective membership per profile. @param structure Axis-parallel structure code. @param min_variance Eigenvalue floor. @return Feasible profile-by-dimension variances. @noRd

.multilpa_bounded_orientation.name: .multilpa_bounded_orientation
.multilpa_bounded_orientation.documentation: Rotate a common orientation while retaining its eigenvalues @param orientation Shared orthogonal eigenvectors. @param scatter Posterior-weighted scatter matrices. @param variances Profile-by-dimension eigenvalues. @return Orientation after one exact sweep of pairwise rotations. @noRd

.multilpa_bounded_covariances.name: .multilpa_bounded_covariances
.multilpa_bounded_covariances.documentation: Covariance M-step with eigenvalue floors inside the ellipsoidal family @param scatter,weights Posterior-weighted scatter and membership. @param structure Covariance structure code. @param min_variance Eigenvalue floor. @param start Previous covariance array, or NULL for initial projection. @param max_iter,tol Orientation iteration controls. @return A dimension-by-dimension-by-profile covariance array. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_encode.name: .multilpa_cov_encode
.multilpa_cov_encode.documentation: Pack a covariate fit's free parameters into one vector  Variances are carried on the log scale so the optimizer and the numerical Hessian both work on an unbounded space; the delta method returns them.  @param object A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @return A numeric vector: means, log variances, categorical response logits,   profile logits, group logits. A block is empty when the fit has no   indicator of that kind. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_is_full.name: .multilpa_cov_is_full
.multilpa_cov_is_full.documentation: Does this covariate fit carry unrestricted residual covariances? @param object A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @return A single logical. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_spread_rows.name: .multilpa_cov_spread_rows
.multilpa_cov_spread_rows.documentation: Which rows of the spread block are estimated separately @param object A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @return Integer profile indices, or `1L` when the spread is shared. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_cholesky_coordinates.name: .multilpa_cov_cholesky_coordinates
.multilpa_cov_cholesky_coordinates.documentation: Residual covariances as log-Cholesky coordinates  The same parameterization the covariate-free model uses: the lower triangle of the Cholesky factor, with its diagonal logged so the parameter is unconstrained and the covariance it implies is positive definite by construction.  @param object A fitted full-covariance `multilpa_covariates` model. @return A numeric vector, one block per estimated profile. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_cholesky_decode.name: .multilpa_cov_cholesky_decode
.multilpa_cov_cholesky_decode.documentation: Rebuild a covariance array from log-Cholesky coordinates @param values Numeric vector of coordinates, one block per estimated profile. @param dimension Number of continuous indicators. @param n_profiles Number of profiles the array must carry. @param shared Whether one block is shared across profiles. @return An indicators-by-indicators-by-profiles array. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_decode.name: .multilpa_cov_decode
.multilpa_cov_decode.documentation: Unpack a parameter vector for a covariate fit @param theta Numeric vector as built by `.multilpa_cov_encode()`. @param object The fit supplying the shapes. @return A list with `parameters` (means, variances), `beta` and `gamma`. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_group_scores.name: .multilpa_cov_group_scores
.multilpa_cov_group_scores.documentation: Per-group score contributions for a covariate fit  The observed-data score equals the expected complete-data score at the maximum, so each block is a posterior-weighted residual: observed responsibility minus model-implied probability for the two multinomial logits, and the usual Gaussian residuals for the measurement model. Rows are summed within group because groups are the independent units.  @param theta Parameter vector. @param x Centred continuous indicator matrix, possibly with no columns. @param object The fit, supplying designs and shapes. @param codes Integer code matrix of the categorical indicators, or `NULL`. @return A matrix with one row per group and one column per parameter. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_full_scores.name: .multilpa_cov_full_scores
.multilpa_cov_full_scores.documentation: Per-group measurement scores in log-Cholesky coordinates  The same quantities the covariate-free model forms, but kept one row per group rather than summed, because groups are the independent units the sandwich resamples over. By the Fisher identity the observed-data score is the complete-data score's conditional expectation, so a missing value enters through its conditional mean given the row's observed values, and the scatter gains that conditional covariance. With complete data the moments are the data and the corrections vanish.  @param x Centred continuous indicator matrix, `NA` where unobserved. @param parameters Decoded means and covariances. @param posteriors Observation-by-profile responsibilities. @param object The fit, supplying the group index and shapes. @param moments The E-step's conditional moments, one element per profile,   from `.multilpa_gaussian_moments()`. @return A list with `means` and `covariances`, each a groups-by-parameters   matrix in encode order. @noRd

parameter_inference.multilpa_covariates.name: parameter_inference.multilpa_covariates
parameter_inference.multilpa_covariates.documentation: Tidy inference for a covariate fit  For a `multilpa(profile_covariates = )` fit, returns standard errors, tests and intervals for every free parameter at all three levels: the measurement model, the profile logits and the group-class logits.  @param x A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @param data Optional data frame the model was fitted to. When omitted it is   rebuilt from the indicators, group index and designs the fit stores. @param level Confidence level for the intervals, between 0 and 1. @param step Finite-difference step for the observed information. @param vcov_type `"observed"` uses the observed information; `"robust"`   uses the group-clustered sandwich (with the CR1 factor `G / (G - 1)` for   `G` groups), appropriate when the measurement model may be misspecified;   `"opg"` inverts the outer product of the group scores, as `glca` does. @param adjust Multiplicity correction applied to `p_value` to give   `p_adjusted`; default `"none"`. See [parameter_inference()]. @return For a covariate fit, a base `data.frame` with one row per free   parameter and the same columns as for every other class: `level`   (`"measurement"`, `"profile"` or `"group"`), `outcome` (the profile or   group class the coefficient predicts, or the profile a measurement   parameter belongs to), `term`, `parameter` (`"mean"`, `"variance"`,   `"covariance"`, `"response"` or `"coefficient"`), `estimate`,   `standard_error`, `statistic`, `p_value`, `p_adjusted`, `conf_low` and   `conf_high`. Variances and covariances are in their natural units, with   standard errors obtained by the delta method from the log and   log-Cholesky coordinates on which they are estimated. Each categorical   indicator contributes one `"response"` row per profile, indicator and   category, named `indicator:category`: the category probability, with its   standard error from the multinomial logits and no Wald test. @details Class-membership coefficients of a covariate fit are on the   multinomial logit scale, with the final profile and the final group class   as references, so each coefficient is a log odds against that reference.   The tests are Wald tests, which are invalid for a coefficient driven to   the boundary by separation or an empty class. A fit with a membership   logit above 20 in coordinates independent of the covariates' units and   origin (roughly, a slope per standard deviation of its covariate and an   intercept at the covariates' means) raises `latents_boundary_fit`; the   fit itself warns with `latents_extreme_coefficients`. Only   `method = "wald"` is implemented for a covariate fit; `"bootstrap"`   raises `latents_unsupported_inference`. @examples # Two separated profiles, membership driven by `x` and by the group's class. set.seed(5) school <- rep(seq_len(16), each = 8) high_class <- rep(rep(c(FALSE, TRUE), length.out = 16), each = 8) x <- rnorm(128) profile <- ifelse(   runif(128) < plogis(-1 + 2 * high_class + 0.8 * x), 2L, 1L ) example_data <- data.frame(   school = school, x = x,   y1 = rnorm(128, ifelse(profile == 2L, 2, -2), 0.7),   y2 = rnorm(128, ifelse(profile == 2L, 1.5, -1.5), 0.7) ) fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("y1", "y2"), "school", n_profiles = 2,                 n_group_classes = 2, profile_covariates = "x",                 n_starts = 2, seed = 1) parameter_inference(fit, example_data) @rdname parameter_inference @export

.multilpa_cov_covariance.name: .multilpa_cov_covariance
.multilpa_cov_covariance.documentation: Covariance of a covariate fit's free parameters @param object A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @param data Optional. The data frame the model was fitted to; when omitted   it is rebuilt from the indicators, group index and designs the fit stores.   Supplying it is the stronger check that the caller still holds that frame. @param step Finite-difference step for the observed information. @param vcov_type `"observed"`, `"robust"` or `"opg"`. @param boundary `"error"` or `"fix"`, as for [parameter_inference()]. @return A square matrix, ordered as `.multilpa_cov_encode()`. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_parameter_names.name: .multilpa_cov_parameter_names
.multilpa_cov_parameter_names.documentation: Names for the free parameters of a covariate fit @param object A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @return A character vector, ordered as `.multilpa_cov_encode()`. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_estimation_labels.name: .multilpa_cov_estimation_labels
.multilpa_cov_estimation_labels.documentation: Tidy labels of a covariate fit on the scale it is estimated on  The same rows as `.multilpa_cov_labels()`, with the spread block renamed to the coordinate it really is: a log variance, or a Cholesky entry whose diagonal is logged. This is the vocabulary [coef.multilpa()] already uses for the covariate-free model, so both classes spell an estimation-scale coordinate the same way.  @param object A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @return A data frame with `level`, `outcome`, `term` and `parameter`. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_inference_frame.name: .multilpa_cov_inference_frame
.multilpa_cov_inference_frame.documentation: Assemble the tidy inference table @param object The fit; `theta` the estimates; `covariance` their covariance. @param level Confidence level. `vcov_type` is recorded as an attribute. @return One row per free parameter, at every level. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_front_estimate.name: .multilpa_cov_front_estimate
.multilpa_cov_front_estimate.documentation: Natural-unit estimates of a covariate fit's free parameters  Means come back to input units, variances out of logs and covariances out of log-Cholesky coordinates; the membership coefficients are already the logits they are reported as.  @param object A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @param theta The estimation-scale parameter vector. @param labels The tidy labels of `theta`, in the same order. @return A numeric vector the same length as `theta`. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_front_jacobian.name: .multilpa_cov_front_jacobian
.multilpa_cov_front_jacobian.documentation: Delta-method Jacobian from estimation to natural coordinates  A mean is a location shift and a membership coefficient is reported as estimated, so both differentiate to one. A variance is `exp()` of its coordinate. A covariance block needs a whole matrix rather than a scalar derivative, because every entry depends on several log-Cholesky coordinates.  @param object A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @param theta The estimation-scale parameter vector. @param labels The tidy labels of `theta`, in the same order. @return A square matrix, rows natural coordinates and columns estimation   coordinates, in the order `.multilpa_cov_encode()` packs them. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_blocks.name: .multilpa_cov_blocks
.multilpa_cov_blocks.documentation: Where the categorical response block sits in the parameter vector  The encoding packs means, spread, response logits, profile logits and group logits, so the response block is located by counting back from the end.  @param object A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @param n_theta Length of the estimation-scale parameter vector. @return A list of integer positions: `front` (means and spread), `response`   (the free logits) and `back` (the membership logits). @noRd

.multilpa_cov_natural_estimate.name: .multilpa_cov_natural_estimate
.multilpa_cov_natural_estimate.documentation: Natural-unit estimates of a covariate fit's parameters  Means come back to input units, variances out of logs and covariances out of log-Cholesky coordinates, and each categorical response logit block becomes the probabilities of every category; the membership coefficients are already the logits they are reported as.  @param object A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @param theta The estimation-scale parameter vector. @param labels The natural labels, one row per natural parameter. @return A numeric vector with one entry per row of `labels`. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_natural_jacobian.name: .multilpa_cov_natural_jacobian
.multilpa_cov_natural_jacobian.documentation: Delta-method Jacobian from estimation to natural coordinates  Block diagonal. The measurement block is square and handled by `.multilpa_cov_front_jacobian()`; each profile-by-indicator response row is a simplex of `K` probabilities driven by `K - 1` logits, with derivative `p_c * (1{c = j} - p_j)`; the membership logits map to themselves.  @param object A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @param theta The estimation-scale parameter vector. @param labels The natural labels, one row per natural parameter. @return A matrix with one row per natural parameter and one column per   estimated coordinate. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_cholesky_natural.name: .multilpa_cov_cholesky_natural
.multilpa_cov_cholesky_natural.documentation: The covariance a log-Cholesky block implies, in vech order @param values Log-Cholesky coordinates for one profile. @param dimension Number of continuous indicators. @return The lower triangle of the implied covariance matrix. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_cholesky_jacobian.name: .multilpa_cov_cholesky_jacobian
.multilpa_cov_cholesky_jacobian.documentation: Jacobian of the log-Cholesky to covariance map  Computed by central differences on an explicit, cheap and smooth map, rather than derived by hand: the derivative of a matrix product through a logged diagonal is easy to get subtly wrong, and the map costs one small multiplication to evaluate.  @param values Log-Cholesky coordinates for one profile. @param dimension Number of continuous indicators. @return A square matrix of derivatives of the covariance entries with   respect to the coordinates, both in vech order. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_labels.name: .multilpa_cov_labels
.multilpa_cov_labels.documentation: Level, outcome, term and kind for every parameter  Categorical response probabilities are the one block whose natural and estimation coordinates differ in number: every category has a probability, but only all but the last carry a free logit. `response = "natural"` labels every category, as [parameter_inference()] reports them; `"free"` labels the logits in the order `.multilpa_cov_encode()` packs them.  @param object A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @param response `"natural"` or `"free"`. @return A data frame with `level`, `outcome`, `term` and `parameter`. @noRd

.multilpa_softmax.name: .multilpa_softmax
.multilpa_softmax.documentation: Baseline-category multinomial probabilities @param design Numeric design matrix. @param coefficients Coefficients for all except the final category. @return Row probabilities. @noRd

.multilpa_log_softmax.name: .multilpa_log_softmax
.multilpa_log_softmax.documentation: Log multinomial probabilities without losing finite rare-class logits @param design Numeric design matrix. @param coefficients Coefficients for all except the final category. @return Matrix of log probabilities, one row per design row. @noRd

.multilpa_weighted_logits.name: .multilpa_weighted_logits
.multilpa_weighted_logits.documentation: Fit weighted multinomial logits  Newton-Raphson with the exact Hessian and step halving: the weighted multinomial log likelihood is concave, so each accepted step cannot lower it and the score falls quadratically to the tolerance. (BFGS, used before, stalled above the tolerance on about half of the steps of an ordinary fit, at small coefficients and differently on each platform.) The search runs on unit-free coordinates, not on the covariates as supplied: a covariate held in units a few orders of magnitude away from the rest would otherwise make the Hessian badly scaled, and so would one held far from zero relative to its spread, which is nearly collinear with the intercept. Because the logit is the same model under any invertible linear map of the design, the entire search is moved onto the orthonormal columns `Q` of `design = Q R` (see `.multilpa_design_basis()`; columns divided by their root-mean-square, `.multilpa_design_scale()`, when the design is rank deficient) and the coefficients are mapped back afterwards, so the caller receives estimates in the units the covariates arrived in and the search itself depends neither on those units nor on the covariates' origin. Convergence is then judged by the score in those unit-free coordinates rather than by the optimizer's own return code.  @param design Design matrix. @param counts Expected category counts in each row. @param initial Initial coefficient matrix, in the units of `design`. @param score_tol Relative tolerance for the unit-free score: the step counts   as solved when the largest absolute scaled score is at most   `score_tol * (1 + sum(counts))`, which is the total weight the score is   accumulated over. The default is tight enough that the inner solve is not   what stops the outer EM iteration; a step that cannot reach it is one whose   coefficient is drifting towards infinity, and that is reported rather than   passed off as a maximum. @param max_newton Most Newton steps before the step is declared unconverged. @return A list with `coefficients` (in the units of `design`), `converged`,   and `scaled_score`, the largest absolute unit-free score at the solution. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_expectation.name: .multilpa_cov_expectation
.multilpa_cov_expectation.documentation: Covariate-dependent nested expectation @param x Centred continuous indicator matrix, `NA` where unobserved. @param group_index Group indices. @param parameters Measurement parameters. @param profile_design List of profile design matrices, one per group class. @param group_design Group-level design matrix. @param beta Profile logit coefficients. @param gamma Group logit coefficients. @return Log likelihood and posterior responsibilities. @noRd

.multilpa_fit_covariates.name: .multilpa_fit_covariates
.multilpa_fit_covariates.documentation: Fit multilevel LPA with class-membership covariates  The estimator behind `multilpa(profile_covariates =, group_covariates =)`. Numeric covariates predict individual-profile and group-class membership via multinomial logits, using the final class as reference. Individual-profile slopes are shared across group classes; profile intercepts differ by group class. The measurement model is the one [multilpa()] fits and stays invariant across group classes. This is one-step maximum likelihood, not regression on assigned classes. Covariates are used in their supplied units. Under `missing = "fiml"` missing indicators are integrated out of the measurement density, exactly as in the covariate-free model; covariates must still be complete.  @param data,vars,id,n_profiles,n_group_classes As in [multilpa()]. @param profile_covariates,group_covariates Names of numeric predictors of   profile membership, and of group-class membership. @param variance_model,n_starts,max_iter,tol,min_variance As in [multilpa()]. @param seed,time,covariance_model,categorical,min_probability As in   [multilpa()]. @param call The user-facing call to record on the result, so the object   reports the `multilpa()` the caller wrote rather than this delegation. @return An object of class `multilpa_covariates`. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_stored_data.name: .multilpa_cov_stored_data
.multilpa_cov_stored_data.documentation: Rebuild the fitting data a covariate fit was estimated from  A covariate fit stores its centred indicator matrix, both membership design matrices and the group index, which between them carry every column the likelihood reads. This reassembles that data frame so the inference verbs need not demand data the object already owns. It is exact, not approximate: the indicators come back as stored, and the covariates are read off the designs they were built into.  @param object A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @return A `data.frame` carrying the indicators, the group identifier and   every profile and group covariate, in fitting row order. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_check_covariates.name: .multilpa_cov_check_covariates
.multilpa_cov_check_covariates.documentation: Validate covariate columns  Covariates enter the membership regressions directly, so a non-finite or non-numeric column would propagate silently into the logits.  @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises on the first broken contract. @noRd

.multilpa_design_basis.name: .multilpa_design_basis
.multilpa_design_basis.documentation: Coordinates in which a design matrix is orthonormal  The upper-triangular `R` of `design = Q R`, divided by the square root of the number of rows and signed so that its diagonal is positive. In the coordinates `R %*% coefficients` the design is `Q`, whose columns are orthogonal with root-mean-square one: an intercept stays an intercept, measured at the covariates' means, and a slope is measured per standard deviation of what its covariate adds to the columns before it. Those coordinates do not move when a covariate is shifted or rescaled, which dividing each column by its root-mean-square alone does not achieve: a covariate held far from zero relative to its spread then carries a huge root-mean-square and leaves the intercept a huge value, both looking like separation.  @param design A numeric design matrix. @return The scaled `R` factor, or `NULL` when the design is rank deficient   (or needed pivoting), in which case callers fall back to the per-column   root-mean-square scale. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_extreme.name: .multilpa_cov_extreme
.multilpa_cov_extreme.documentation: Whether a covariate fit's membership logits are near separation  Each coefficient is measured in the coordinates in which its design is orthonormal (see `.multilpa_design_basis()`): an intercept at the covariates' means and a slope per standard deviation of its covariate, so the verdict depends neither on the units a covariate arrived in nor on where its zero lies. A logit that moves by more than `limit` over one such unit (an odds ratio above `exp(20)`) is drifting to the boundary of the parameter space: the class is separated by the covariate, or empty. The fit warns with `latents_extreme_coefficients`, and Wald inference is refused, because a standard error at a coefficient heading to infinity is meaningless (Hauck and Donner, 1977). A rank-deficient design falls back to the per-column root-mean-square scale (`.multilpa_design_scale()`).  @param profile_coefficients Profile logit coefficients, one row per column   of the stacked profile design. @param group_coefficients Group-class logit coefficients, one row per   column of `group_design`. @param profile_design List of profile design matrices. @param group_design Group-level design matrix. @param limit Largest unit-free coefficient treated as finite. @return `TRUE` or `FALSE`. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_designs.name: .multilpa_cov_designs
.multilpa_cov_designs.documentation: Build the centered indicator matrix and both membership designs  The profile design repeats one group-class indicator block per group class, so that stacking it gives the weighted multinomial regression its rows. The group design takes one row per group, at its first occurrence.  With `profile_slopes = "shared"` the covariates follow the indicators once, so every group class uses the same slopes. With `"group_class"` they follow once per group class, and group class `h`'s design carries them only in its own block: the slopes are then the covariates' interactions with the group classes. Either way the first block after the indicators holds the covariates themselves in group class 1's design.  @param row_weights Optional sampling weights in observation order, used   only to omit excluded rows from the internal Gaussian origin. @return A list with `x`, `center`, `w`, `profile_design` and `stacked_design`. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_start.name: .multilpa_cov_start
.multilpa_cov_start.documentation: Run one covariate EM start to convergence  The first start resumes from the covariate-free base fit; later starts use a fresh random initialization. Membership coefficients begin at the implied logits with zero slopes, so the first iteration reproduces the base model.  @return A list with the fitted parameters, expectation, both coefficient   matrices, and the convergence diagnostics for this start. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_initial.name: .multilpa_cov_initial
.multilpa_cov_initial.documentation: The initial state of one covariate EM start  @param kind The kind of start, as for `.multilpa_initialize()`; start 1   always resumes from the base fit. @return A list of `parameters`, `beta` and `gamma`. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_run.name: .multilpa_cov_run
.multilpa_cov_run.documentation: Run covariate EM from an initial state  @param state A list of `parameters`, `beta` and `gamma`. @param pause,resume As for `.latents_em()`. @return As `.multilpa_cov_start()`; with `pause` or `resume`, also the   `checkpoint`. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_assemble.name: .multilpa_cov_assemble
.multilpa_cov_assemble.documentation: Assemble the covariate fit result @return An `multilpa_covariates` object. @noRd

.cross_level_arguments.name: .cross_level_arguments
.cross_level_arguments.documentation: Arguments `multilpa()` accepts for a cross-level family @noRd

.cross_level_group_density.name: .cross_level_group_density
.cross_level_group_density.documentation: Class-conditional log densities of the group means, groups x classes @noRd

.cross_level_between_update.name: .cross_level_between_update
.cross_level_between_update.documentation: Means and variances of the group means given class weights (M-step) @noRd

.cross_level_initialize.name: .cross_level_initialize
.cross_level_initialize.documentation: Starting values for the full cross-level model from one partition of the groups (by their means), so both parts share the group-class labels @param sampling_weights Optional normalized weights in group order. Excluded   groups do not contribute to either level's initialization geometry. @noRd

.cross_level_em.name: .cross_level_em
.cross_level_em.documentation: EM for the full cross-level model from one start  `pause` and `resume` are as for `.latents_em()`. @noRd

.cross_level_count.name: .cross_level_count
.cross_level_count.documentation: Free parameters of a cross-level model @noRd

.cross_level_fit.name: .cross_level_fit
.cross_level_fit.documentation: Fit a cross-level family  Called by `multilpa(family = "restricted_cross_level" | "full_cross_level")`. @return An object of class `multilpa_cross_level`. @noRd

.cross_level_select.name: .cross_level_select
.cross_level_select.documentation: Keep the best start of the full cross-level EM, with every start's record  Failed starts are kept in the record and announced with a `latents_failed_starts` warning, as in every other family. @noRd

.cross_level_restricted.name: .cross_level_restricted
.cross_level_restricted.documentation: The restricted cross-level model through its factorization  With profile prevalences equal across group classes the likelihood is the product of a profile model of every rating and a profile model of the group means, so each is fitted on its own by the package's single-level EM. @noRd

.cross_level_table.documentation: Build one table of a cross-level fit @noRd

descriptives.name: descriptives
descriptives.documentation: Descriptive statistics and intraclass correlations of model variables  Returns a table with one row per variable giving the number of observed and missing values, the mean, standard deviation, minimum, maximum and number of distinct values, and, when groups are known, the number of groups and the intraclass correlation (ICC): the share of the variable's variance that lies between groups.  An ICC near zero indicates little between-group variation in that variable's mean. It does not rule out group classes that differ in other variables, in profile prevalence, or in other features of the distributions.  @param x A data frame, or a fitted model of this package, whose own `vars`   and `id` are then used. A single-level fit has no groups, so its table   has no `n_groups` or `icc`. @param vars Character vector of column names to describe; repeated names   are described once. Columns must be vectors: matrix-valued columns raise   `latents_bad_data`. For a data frame, defaults to every numeric column   other than `id` and `by`. @param id Optional. The column identifying the groups the rows are nested   in. Supplying it adds `n_groups` and `icc`. @param by Optional. On a fitted model, `"profile"` or `"group_class"`; on a   data frame, a column name. Each variable is then described once per level   of it. Rows whose stratifier is `NA` form their own stratum, labelled `NA`   and reported last, so every input row is counted in exactly one stratum. @param ... Not used. For a data frame, any further argument raises a   `latents_unused_argument` warning; for a fit, it raises   `latents_bad_argument`. @return A base `data.frame`, one row per variable (or per variable and `by`   level), with the columns   \describe{     \item{`variable`}{character: the column described.}     \item{`n`}{integer: observations with a value.}     \item{`n_missing`}{integer: observations without one.}     \item{`mean`,`sd`,`min`,`max`}{numeric; `NA_real_` for a variable       that is not numeric.}     \item{`n_distinct`}{integer: distinct observed values.}     \item{`n_groups`,`icc`}{present only when `id` is known. `icc` is the       one-way random-effects estimate; it can be slightly negative when the       between-group mean square is below the within-group one, which       indicates no group structure. Rows with a missing group ID do not       contribute to either statistic.}   }   With `by`, a first column named after the stratifier holds each stratum's   value (`NA` for the stratum of missing values). For every variable,   `n + n_missing` summed over the strata equals the number of input rows.   When describing a fit by `"profile"` or `"group_class"`, the model's   assignment is used as the stratifier without replacing an indicator of   the same name. A `by` named like one of the summary's own columns raises   `latents_bad_data`. Describing no variables raises   `latents_nothing_to_describe`. @references Bliese, P. D. (2000). Within-group agreement, non-independence,   and reliability. In K. J. Klein & S. W. J. Kozlowski (Eds.), *Multilevel   theory, research, and methods in organizations*. @seealso [multilpa()] to fit, [diagnostics()] for the after-the-fit   counterpart. @examples descriptives(   course_engagement,   vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),   id = "student" )  # A missing stratifier is a stratum of its own, not a silent loss and not # missingness invented in a variable that has none. descriptives(data.frame(cohort = c("A", "A", "B", NA), score = 1:4),              vars = "score", by = "cohort")  fit <- multilpa(   course_engagement,   vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),   id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,   seed = 1 ) descriptives(fit) descriptives(fit, by = "profile") @export

.multilpa_assignment_values.name: .multilpa_assignment_values
.multilpa_assignment_values.documentation: The class a fit assigned to each of its observations  Read from the fit rather than written into the frame it describes, so that the assignment can never displace a column of the caller's own.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @param by `"profile"` or `"group_class"`. @return A vector with one element per observation of the fit. @noRd

.multilpa_describe_by.name: .multilpa_describe_by
.multilpa_describe_by.documentation: Describe each variable once per stratum  The stratifier arrives as a vector beside the frame, not as a column of it, so describing by a class the model assigned cannot overwrite an indicator of the same name.  Rows are keyed to their stratum with `match()`, which returns `NA` for a missing stratifier. Selecting with `which()` on that key therefore drops the missing rows from every observed stratum instead of turning each selector into a vector of `NA`s, which is what `x[[by]] == level` did: `NA` selectors fabricate rows that are missing on every variable and lose the observed values of the rows that carry them.  @param data A data frame. @param vars Column names to describe. @param id Optional grouping column name. @param by_values One stratifier value per row of `data`. @param by_label The name the stratum column takes in the result. @return A base `data.frame`, one row per stratum and variable, the stratum of   rows with a missing stratifier last. @noRd

.multilpa_describe.name: .multilpa_describe
.multilpa_describe.documentation: Describe each variable of one frame @param data A data frame. @param vars Column names to describe. @param id Optional grouping column name. @return A base `data.frame`, one row per variable. @noRd

.multilpa_check_descriptive_columns.name: .multilpa_check_descriptive_columns
.multilpa_check_descriptive_columns.documentation: Require one descriptive value per data-frame row @param data A data frame. @param columns The variables, identifier and stratifier to be used. @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises `latents_bad_data` for matrix/array columns. @noRd

.multilpa_icc.name: .multilpa_icc
.multilpa_icc.documentation: One-way random-effects intraclass correlation  The share of variance lying between groups, from the one-way ANOVA mean squares. `n0` is the size-corrected average group size, which equals the common size when the groups are balanced and is smaller when they are not, so a few large groups cannot inflate the estimate.  The estimate is returned as computed. It can fall slightly below zero when the between-group mean square is smaller than the within-group one, which is the estimator saying there is no group structure; truncating it at zero would hide that rather than report it.  @param values Numeric observations, already complete. @param groups The group each observation belongs to. @return A single number, or `NA_real_` where the design cannot support one. @noRd

.multilpa_entropy_sum.name: .multilpa_entropy_sum
.multilpa_entropy_sum.documentation: Classification entropy sum @param probabilities Posterior probability matrix, rows summing to one. @return Sum of `-p log p` over every cell, the classification entropy. @noRd

.multilpa_relative_entropy.name: .multilpa_relative_entropy
.multilpa_relative_entropy.documentation: Relative classification entropy @param probabilities Posterior probability matrix, rows summing to one. @return Entropy on the zero-to-one scale, or `NA_real_` for a single class. @noRd

.multilpa_criterion_definitions.name: .multilpa_criterion_definitions
.multilpa_criterion_definitions.documentation: The formula behind each criterion, keyed by its name @param criterion Character vector of criterion names. @return Character vector of formulas, the same length as `criterion`. @noRd

.multilpa_information_criteria.name: .multilpa_information_criteria
.multilpa_information_criteria.documentation: Every likelihood-penalty criterion a fit supports  The formulas, the two sample-size conventions, the entropy each criterion penalizes and the references are documented on `?get_results`, which is where a caller reaches this table from.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @param definitions `TRUE` adds the formula and the reference per criterion,   which only the long form has a row for. @param format `"wide"` for the one-row reporting shape, `"long"` for one row   per criterion and sample-size convention. @return A base `data.frame`, one row in the wide form and one row per   criterion and convention in the long form. @noRd

.multilpa_criteria_wide.name: .multilpa_criteria_wide
.multilpa_criteria_wide.documentation: One criterion per column, the shape a model-comparison table is reported in  The same pivot the enumeration grid uses, so a single fit and a row of `as.data.frame(enumerate_classes(...))` cannot name the same quantity differently. `.multilpa_enumeration_criteria()` owns the column order.  @param indices The long table, one row per criterion and convention. @param fit The model the indices came from, for the likelihood and count. @return A one-row base `data.frame`. @noRd

.multilpa_criterion_labels.name: .multilpa_criterion_labels
.multilpa_criterion_labels.documentation: The wide column name each long row maps to  A criterion that uses no sample size carries `NA` as its convention and keeps its bare name; the rest take a `_groups` or `_individual` suffix.  @param indices The long table. @return A character vector, one label per row of `indices`. @noRd

.multilpa_posterior_levels.name: .multilpa_posterior_levels
.multilpa_posterior_levels.documentation: The posterior matrices of the levels a diagnostic was asked for @param object A fitted model of this package. @param level One of `"individuals"`, `"groups"` or `"both"`. @return A named list of posterior matrices, in reporting order. @noRd

.multilpa_classification_levels.name: .multilpa_classification_levels
.multilpa_classification_levels.documentation: Which levels a request for one, the other or both resolves to  `"both"` on a model with no discrete group classes is the individual level rather than a refusal: the caller asked for every level the fit has, and it has one. Naming `"groups"` explicitly is a different request and refuses.  @param object A fitted model of this package. @param level `"individuals"`, `"groups"` or `"both"`. @return A character vector of level names, in reporting order. @noRd

.multilpa_classification_table.name: .multilpa_classification_table
.multilpa_classification_table.documentation: Per-class classification quality at one or both levels  The columns, the odds-of-correct-classification formula and the reference are documented on `?get_results`, which is where a caller reaches this table from.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @param level `"individuals"`, `"groups"` or `"both"`. @return A base `data.frame`, one row per level and class. @noRd

.multilpa_level_weights.name: .multilpa_level_weights
.multilpa_level_weights.documentation: The sampling weight of every row of one level's posterior matrix  Weights belong to the independent units: the groups' own posterior rows carry them directly, and an individual row carries its unit's weight.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @param level `"individuals"` or `"groups"`. @param n_rows Rows of that level's posterior matrix. @return `NULL` for an unweighted fit, otherwise one weight per row. @noRd

.multilpa_average_posteriors.name: .multilpa_average_posteriors
.multilpa_average_posteriors.documentation: Mean posterior of every class within each modal assignment  Documented on `?get_results`, which is where a caller reaches this table from.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @param level `"individuals"`, `"groups"` or `"both"`. @return A base `data.frame`, one row per level and ordered pair of classes. @noRd

.multilpa_average_posterior_matrix.name: .multilpa_average_posterior_matrix
.multilpa_average_posterior_matrix.documentation: Mean posterior of every class within each modal assignment group @param probabilities Posterior probability matrix. @return A square matrix, rows indexed by assigned class, columns by class. @noRd

.multilpa_classification_summary.name: .multilpa_classification_summary
.multilpa_classification_summary.documentation: One row per class of classification diagnostics for one level  Modal counts and average posteriors describe the rows supplied; the estimated class sizes and shares (and so the odds of correct classification) are the model's, which under sampling weights are the weighted posterior totals.  @param probabilities Posterior probability matrix. @param level Label recorded in the `level` column. @param weights `NULL`, or one sampling weight per row. @return A tidy `data.frame`, one row per class. @noRd

.multilpa_average_posterior_rows.name: .multilpa_average_posterior_rows
.multilpa_average_posterior_rows.documentation: One row per assigned class and class of average posteriors for one level @param probabilities Posterior probability matrix. @param level Label recorded in the `level` column. @return A tidy `data.frame`, one row per assigned class and class. @noRd

.multilpa_class_labels.name: .multilpa_class_labels
.multilpa_class_labels.documentation: The class numbers a posterior matrix reports  Its columns in order, except that a final `noise` column --- a fit's noise component --- is class 0, the number mclust gives it.  @param probabilities Posterior probability matrix. @return An integer vector, one label per column. @noRd

.multilpa_odds_correct.name: .multilpa_odds_correct
.multilpa_odds_correct.documentation: Odds of correct classification @param average Average posterior probability in the assigned class. @param proportion Model-estimated class proportion. @return Odds ratio; `Inf` for a class whose average posterior is one to   within rounding (perfect classification), and `NA_real_` where the ratio   is undefined (no modal members, or a class proportion of zero or one). @noRd

.multilpa_entropy_table.name: .multilpa_entropy_table
.multilpa_entropy_table.documentation: Classification entropy at each level a fit has  Documented on `?get_results`, which is where a caller reaches this table from.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @return A base `data.frame`, one row per level, with `level`, `n_classes`,   `n_units`, `entropy_sum` and `relative_entropy`. @noRd

.latents_parse_direct_effects.name: .latents_parse_direct_effects
.latents_parse_direct_effects.documentation: Parse direct-effect specifications  @param direct_effects A character vector of `"indicator ~ covariate"`   terms; several covariates are joined with `+`. @return A data frame with `indicator` and `covariate`, one row per effect,   in the order given. @noRd

.latents_check_direct_conflicts.name: .latents_check_direct_conflicts
.latents_check_direct_conflicts.documentation: Refuse the settings direct effects are not fitted with @param conflicts A named logical vector, `TRUE` where a setting is in use. @return `NULL`, invisibly. @noRd

.latents_add_direct.name: .latents_add_direct
.latents_add_direct.documentation: Put prepared direct effects into the extra carrier @param extra The carrier of the ordinal and count indicators, or `NULL`. @param direct From `.latents_prepare_direct()`. @return The carrier with `direct`; a carrier without ordinal or count   indicators when there were none. @noRd

.latents_center_direct.name: .latents_center_direct
.latents_center_direct.documentation: Centre the covariates of direct effects for fitting  The model y = m + B z is the same model as y = (m + B c) + B (z - c), so EM can run on centred covariates, where the intercepts and the effects are nearly uncorrelated, and `.latents_uncenter_direct()` moves the means back.  @param extra The extra carrier, or `NULL`. @param x Continuous indicators, used to select the observations of each   effect's target; `NULL` uses every row. @param row_weights Optional sampling weights in observation order. @return The carrier with one centred internal covariate column per effect,   its target-specific `centers` and `scales`. The original carrier is kept   on the reported fit, retaining the caller's covariate names and columns. @noRd

.latents_uncenter_direct.name: .latents_uncenter_direct
.latents_uncenter_direct.documentation: Express means fitted on centred covariates at a covariate value of zero @param parameters The fitted parameters, means at the covariates' centres. @param extra The carrier the fit was made with, from `.latents_center_direct()`. @return `parameters` with `means` at zero covariate values. @noRd

.latents_direct_key.name: .latents_direct_key
.latents_direct_key.documentation: A fit's direct effects as a set, for comparing two fits @param fit A fitted model. @return The sorted `"indicator:covariate"` names; empty without effects. @noRd

.latents_direct_terms.name: .latents_direct_terms
.latents_direct_terms.documentation: The `direct_effects` terms that give a table of effects back @param effects From `.latents_parse_direct_effects()`. @return One `"indicator ~ covariate + ..."` term per indicator. @noRd

.latents_prepare_direct.name: .latents_prepare_direct
.latents_prepare_direct.documentation: Validate direct effects against the data and prepare the covariates  @param data The fitting data. @param effects From `.latents_parse_direct_effects()`. @param vars,continuous The fit's indicators and its continuous ones, in   the order of the continuous matrix. @return A list with `covariates` (rows by covariates, numeric) and   `effects`, which adds `column` (the indicator's column of the continuous   matrix) and `covariate_column`. @noRd

.latents_direct_covariates.name: .latents_direct_covariates
.latents_direct_covariates.documentation: The covariate columns of a direct effect, checked @param data A data frame holding the covariates. @param covariates Their names. @return A rows-by-covariates numeric matrix. @noRd

.latents_direct_matrix.name: .latents_direct_matrix
.latents_direct_matrix.documentation: The direct effects as an indicators-by-covariates coefficient matrix @param direct The `direct` entry of the extra carrier. @param values The effects, one per row of `direct$effects`. @param n_indicators Columns of the continuous matrix. @return An `n_indicators` by covariates matrix, zero where no effect is fitted. @noRd

.latents_direct_shift.name: .latents_direct_shift
.latents_direct_shift.documentation: Remove the direct effects from the continuous indicators  @param x The continuous matrix, `NA` where unobserved. @param extra The extra carrier, or `NULL`. @param parameters A parameter list, possibly with `direct_effects`. @return `x - Z B'`; `x` itself when there are no effects. @noRd

.latents_direct_maximize.name: .latents_direct_maximize
.latents_direct_maximize.documentation: Update the direct effects given the class means and variances  With the means and the diagonal variances held, the expected complete-data log likelihood of indicator j is a weighted least squares in its effects: sum_i sum_k r_ik (x_ij - mu_kj - b_j' z_i)^2 / s2_kj, whose minimum solves (sum_i w_ij z_i z_i') b_j = sum_i z_i sum_k r_ik (x_ij - mu_kj) / s2_kj with w_ij = sum_k r_ik / s2_kj. Rows where the indicator is unobserved carry no information about it under a diagonal covariance.  @param x The continuous matrix, unshifted. @param extra The extra carrier. @param posteriors Rows by profiles. @param means,variances Profiles by indicators. @return The effects, one per row of `extra$direct$effects`. @noRd

.latents_direct_scores.name: .latents_direct_scores
.latents_direct_scores.documentation: Scores of the direct effects  The score of b_jc is sum_i z_ic sum_k r_ik (x~_ij - mu_kj) / s2_kj, where x~ is the indicator with the effects removed: the mean score of indicator j weighted by the covariate.  @param x The continuous matrix, unshifted. @param extra The extra carrier. @param posteriors Rows by profiles (weighted, under sampling weights). @param parameters The point, with `means`, `variances` and `direct_effects`. @param group_index Group of each row, or `NULL` for the total. @return Groups (or one row) by effects. @noRd

.latents_direct_like.name: .latents_direct_like
.latents_direct_like.documentation: Rebuild a fit's direct-effect covariates from a data frame @param direct The fit's `direct` entry. @param data A data frame with the covariate columns. @return The `direct` entry with the covariates read from `data`. @noRd

.latents_direct_frame.name: .latents_direct_frame
.latents_direct_frame.documentation: The direct effects of a fit, with their standard errors  @param x A fit with direct effects. @param data The fitting data, or `NULL` for the columns the fit carries. @return One row per effect: `indicator`, `covariate`, `estimate`,   `standard_error`, `statistic`, `p_value`, `conf_low` and `conf_high`. @noRd

.latents_check_enumeration_type.name: .latents_check_enumeration_type
.latents_check_enumeration_type.documentation: Validate an explicit enumeration type and its routing arguments @param type NULL or a single model type. @param time Occasion column, or NULL. @param family Enumeration family. @return NULL or the matched model type. @noRd

.latents_enumeration_measurement_type.name: .latents_enumeration_measurement_type
.latents_enumeration_measurement_type.documentation: Infer a profile grid's measurement label without changing its arguments @param vars Indicator names. @param extra Candidate arguments. @return lca, lpa or mixed. @noRd

.latents_enumeration_type_label.name: .latents_enumeration_type_label
.latents_enumeration_type_label.documentation: Show the resolved model type in an enumeration header @param x An enumeration, including objects saved before type was recorded. @return A header suffix, or an empty string for older objects. @noRd

enumerate_classes.name: enumerate_classes
enumerate_classes.documentation: Enumerate numbers of individual profiles and group classes  Fits every requested combination of profile count, group-class count and covariance structure and returns the candidates with their information criteria and classification diagnostics. Errors and warnings of each candidate are kept in the table alongside the successful fits. Information criteria are descriptive: neither the smallest BIC nor high entropy guarantees the correct number of classes. Unconverged, boundary and unreplicated fits are reported, not silently selected. @param data Data frame. @param vars Indicator column names. @param id The column identifying the groups the observations are nested in   (students in schools, reports in students). Required; `NULL` enumerates   single-level models, with a message. [enumerate_lpa()] and   [enumerate_lca()] fit single-level models directly. @param n_profiles Positive integer profile counts to try. Default `1:4`. @param n_group_classes Positive integer group-class counts to try. Default   `1:3`. With `id = NULL` it is 1 and may be left out. @param model The covariance structures to cross with the class counts.   `"basic"` (the default) fits four structures: `"EEI"` (equal variances,   no covariances), `"VVI"` (varying variances, no covariances), `"EEE"`   (one covariance matrix shared by all profiles) and `"VVV"` (a covariance   matrix for each profile). Omitting covariances between correlated   indicators tends to favour additional profiles. `"all"` fits all 14   structures of Celeux and Govaert (1995). Otherwise, name structures by   their three-letter codes, as [multilpa()]'s `model` takes them: the   letters give the volume, shape and orientation of each profile's   covariance matrix, each equal (`E`) or varying (`V`) across profiles,   with `I` for no covariances. `NULL` crosses no structures. With one   continuous indicator, codes that coincide (equal or varying variance)   are fitted once; with only categorical indicators no structure is   crossed. A structure set through `variance_model`, `covariance_model`,   `volume`, `shape` or `orientation` in `...` replaces the default. @param seed Optional seed for each fit: a whole number `set.seed()`   accepts. Anything else raises `latents_bad_argument` before any candidate   is fitted. @param family `"profiles"` (the default) enumerates the profile model over   `n_profiles`, `n_group_classes` and `model`. One or more of the   group-class families `"additive"`, `"dispersion"` and   `"additive_dispersion"` enumerates those instead, over `family`,   `n_group_classes` and `between_variance`; these need `id`, `n_profiles`   and `model` are then refused, and the result is a   `latents_family_enumeration`, read with [get_results()] and   [get_candidate()]. @param between_variance For group-class families: the between-variance   restrictions to cross, `"varying"`, `"equal"` or both (the default). The   dispersion family is always fitted with `"equal"`. Refused for the   profile family. @param time The occasion column. Enumerates latent transition models   ([lta()]) over `n_profiles` (default `2:4`) and `n_group_classes`   (default `1`), with every other `lta()` argument given in `...` held   fixed. `model`, when given, crosses those covariance structures. Only   the profile family is available. The result is a   `latents_transition_enumeration`, read with [get_results()] and   [get_candidate()]. @param cores Number of processor cores to fit the candidates on (default   1). Each candidate sets and restores its own random seed, so with `seed`   given the result is identical to `cores = 1`. Candidates are fitted by   forked processes on macOS and Linux, and by a socket cluster on Windows   and on macOS when R uses Apple's Accelerate BLAS (socket workers load the   installed package). Warnings and messages from the workers are passed on   in grid order once all have finished. Without `seed`, the random starts   differ between runs on any number of cores. Lost worker results are retried   once with half as many workers (rounded up). One `latents_worker_lost`   warning reports how many tasks were lost and recovered, and suggests fewer   cores. A task still lost becomes a failed start (for flat start grids) or   a failed candidate; the other results are retained. On sockets, bounded   chunks preserve earlier results when a connection breaks; completed tasks   within the failed chunk may also be retried. Each core holds its own copy   of the fits it computes; `parallel::detectCores()` gives the number   available.   Transition grids (`time`) and profile grids (including categorical-only   latent class models) distribute individual starts across one pool,   longest estimated first, with at most `cores` workers and no nested   workers. Both emEM screening and finalist runs use the pool; `search`   keeps the same defaults as [multilpa()]. Setup, ordered starting values,   start selection and finalisation stay in the current process. Profile   models with membership covariates or joined categorical `local_dependence`   pairs instead occupy one worker per candidate in the same pool, with   serial starts. Group-class families also keep candidate-level parallelism. @param verbose Whether to report progress: one message each when the   candidates are prepared, when their starts are fitted, and when the grid   is done, with the elapsed time. The default reports when `cores > 1`,   where a grid is usually long. Group-class families (`family`) are not   reported. @param type Optional model type: `"lca"`, `"lpa"` or `"lta"`. `NULL`   (the default) keeps the existing routing and measurement settings.   `"lca"` treats every indicator as categorical, as [multilca()] does:   indicators named in `ordinal` or `count` keep those distributions, and   `categorical` adds to the set rather than replacing it. Numeric response   codes are categorical with `type = "lca"`. `"lpa"` requires continuous   indicators and refuses non-empty `categorical`, `ordinal` or `count`.   Both require `time = NULL`. `"lta"` requires `time` and takes its   measurement settings from `categorical`, as [lta()] does; it does not   make numeric indicators categorical. An explicit type requires   `family = "profiles"`; leave `type = NULL` for group-class families. @param ... Further arguments to [multilpa()] (or to [lta()] with `time`),   applied to every candidate, such as `n_starts` (random starts per   candidate), `max_iter`, `missing`, `categorical`, `centering`, `scaling`,   `drop_empty` and `boundary` (`"exclude"` sets aside starts with a   variance at `min_variance`, degenerate solutions that become more likely   as `n_starts` grows). For example, `enumerate_classes(data, vars, id,   n_profiles = 2:6, n_starts = 20, seed = 1)`. Group-class families take   only `n_starts`, `max_iter`, `tol` and `min_variance`. @return An object of class `multilpa_enumeration` (or the transition or   family enumeration described above). Its `type` records the resolved   model: `"lca"`, `"lpa"` or `"lta"`, or `"mixed"`/`"family"` for   those grids under `type = NULL`. The print header shows this type; table   columns are unchanged. [as.data.frame()] gives   one row per candidate, starting with its name (`"profiles3_groups2"`),   with every criterion and diagnostic (including both entropies and, at   each level, the smallest, largest and mean average posterior probability   and the number of classes below a cutoff) and the candidate's warnings   and error. `get_results(x, "best")` names the candidate at each   criterion's minimum; `get_results(x, "classification")` gives every   class's average posterior probability and relative entropy for every   candidate; `get_results(x, "deltas")` and `"knees"` give model-selection   evidence. [summary()] prints each criterion's minimum and every table,   [plot()] draws the information criteria (and, with `what`,   classification quality and model-selection views), [get_candidate()]   returns the fitted model of one candidate, and [compare_models()] puts   candidates side by side; these verbs take candidates by name. @seealso [get_candidate()] to take one fitted model out of the grid,   `summary()` for the criterion-by-criterion comparison. @section Conditions:   `latents_bad_argument` when `model` names an unknown structure, when it is   given together with another way of setting the structure, or when it is   given although no indicator is continuous; when `seed` is not a seed   `set.seed()` accepts; when `...` contains an argument [multilpa()] does   not take; when `n_group_classes` other than 1 is given with `id = NULL`;   when `id` is missing; when `between_variance` is given for the profile   family; when `n_profiles` or `model` is given for a group-class family,   or `id` is `NULL`; when `time` is combined with a group-class family or   with `between_variance`; and when `cores` is not a whole number of at   least 1; and when `type` is invalid or conflicts with `time`, `family`   or the requested measurement distributions. @references Celeux, G., & Govaert, G. (1995). Gaussian parsimonious clustering models. *Pattern Recognition*, 28(5), 781--793. @examples set.seed(1) d <- data.frame(g = rep(1:10, each = 10), y = rnorm(100)) candidates <- enumerate_classes(d, "y", "g", n_profiles = 1:2,                               n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1) as.data.frame(candidates) summary(candidates)  # Numeric response codes, explicitly categorical: codes <- data.frame(g = rep(seq_len(10), each = 10), item = rep(0:1, 50)) classes <- enumerate_classes(codes, "item", "g", type = "lca",                              n_profiles = 1, n_group_classes = 1,                              n_starts = 1, seed = 1)  # Single level, crossing class counts with two named structures: single <- enumerate_lpa(iris, c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width",                                 "Petal.Length", "Petal.Width"),                         n_profiles = 1:3, model = c("VVV", "EEE"),                         n_starts = 2, seed = 1) summary(single) @export

.latents_candidate_call.name: .latents_candidate_call
.latents_candidate_call.documentation: A candidate's call as the caller would have written it  A fit made through `do.call(multilpa, arguments)` records the function's whole body and every argument's value, the data frame included, as its `call`, so a grid held one copy of the data in every candidate. A fit's call is only displayed, never evaluated; this one names the verb and the caller's expression for the data, with the other arguments written out.  @param verb The fitting function's name. @param data_expression The caller's expression for `data`. @param arguments The other arguments the candidate was fitted with. @return A call. @noRd

.multilpa_enumeration_models.name: .multilpa_enumeration_models
.multilpa_enumeration_models.documentation: The covariance structures an enumeration crosses  Expands the named sets and drops the structures the data cannot tell apart: with one continuous indicator there are no covariances and no orientation, so only the volume (equal or varying variance) distinguishes two codes, and with none there is no covariance structure at all.  @param model `enumerate_classes()`'s `model`. @param model_given Whether the caller passed `model` rather than taking the   default. @param vars The indicator names. @param extra The further arguments for `multilpa()`, as `list(...)`. @return A character vector of structure codes, or `NA_character_` when no   structure is to be crossed. @noRd

get_candidate.name: get_candidate
get_candidate.documentation: Take one fitted model out of an enumeration grid or a comparison  Returns one fitted model from an enumeration, selected by its name or by its number of profiles and group classes (and its covariance structure when the grid has several), or one model from a comparison, selected by its row label.  A candidate is selected by its name, as the grid's `candidate` column shows it (`get_candidate(grid, "profiles3_groups4")`; `classes` instead of `profiles` when every indicator is categorical); by its class counts, `get_candidate(grid, 3, 4)` or `get_candidate(grid, c(3, 4))`; or, on a grid that crosses covariance structures, by its counts and `model`. From a comparison, give the row label: `get_candidate(comparison, "profiles3_groups4")`.  @param x An enumeration grid from [enumerate_classes()] (a profile, latent   class, transition or group-class family grid), or a comparison from   [compare_models()]. On a family grid, give the name, or `n_group_classes`   with `model`. @param n_profiles Number of individual profiles of the candidate, the   candidate's name (`"profiles3_groups4"`), or its two class counts   (`c(3, 4)`). For a comparison, the row label, as its `model` column shows   it. @param n_group_classes Number of group classes of the candidate. Default 1. @param model The covariance structure of the candidate, needed when   [enumerate_classes()] crossed several structures and the class counts   match several candidates; on a group-class family grid, the family model   as the grid's `model` column shows it. @return The fitted model of that candidate, the same kind of object its   fitting function returns (for a profile grid, class `multilpa`), so the   verbs for a fitted model apply to it. @section Conditions:   `latents_unknown_candidate` for a name or class counts not in the grid,   for counts that match several candidates (the message lists their   names), and for a label that is not a row of a comparison;   `latents_failed_candidate` when the candidate's fit raised an error, so   there is no model to return; `latents_bad_argument` for a name or pair of   counts given together with `n_group_classes` or `model`, for a value that   names no candidate, and for a comparison given no label;   `latents_incomplete_fit` for a comparison that no longer carries its   models. Counts that are not single positive whole numbers fail the   argument checks. @examples set.seed(1) d <- data.frame(g = rep(1:10, each = 10), y = rnorm(100)) candidates <- enumerate_classes(d, "y", "g", n_profiles = 1:2,                               n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1) get_candidate(candidates, n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 1, model = "VVI") # This grid crosses two structures, so the names carry them: candidates get_candidate(candidates, "profiles2_groups1_VVI") compared <- compare_models(candidates, "profiles1_groups1_VVI",                            "profiles2_groups1_VVI") get_candidate(compared, "profiles2_groups1_VVI") @export

.latents_check_candidate_counts.name: .latents_check_candidate_counts
.latents_check_candidate_counts.documentation: Check the class counts that name a candidate @param n_profiles,n_group_classes The counts [get_candidate()] received. @return `NULL`, invisibly; an argument error for anything but a single   positive whole number each. @noRd

candidate_fit.name: candidate_fit
candidate_fit.documentation: @rdname get_candidate @details `candidate_fit()` is the former name of `get_candidate()`, kept   for compatibility. It takes the same arguments, forwards to   `get_candidate()` and gives no warning. @export

.multilpa_enumeration_minima.name: .multilpa_enumeration_minima
.multilpa_enumeration_minima.documentation: Which candidate minimises each information criterion @param grid The enumeration table. @return One row per criterion carried by the grid. @noRd

.multilpa_enumeration_grid.name: .multilpa_enumeration_grid
.multilpa_enumeration_grid.documentation: The candidates table of an enumeration, with its AvePP columns  The average posterior probability (AvePP) summaries at each level are computed here from the stored fits, each time the table is read, rather than when the grid is fitted. Grids fitted before these columns existed carry the same fits, so they report the same numbers without refitting. The columns sit after `group_entropy`, beside the entropies they are read with.  @param x A `multilpa_enumeration` result. @param cutoff The AvePP below which a class is counted in `*_avepp_below`. @return `x$table` with `avepp_min`, `_max`, `_mean`, `_below` and   the same four for `group_`; `NA` for a candidate whose fit failed. @noRd

.multilpa_avepp_summary.name: .multilpa_avepp_summary
.multilpa_avepp_summary.documentation: Smallest, largest and mean AvePP at one level, and the classes below a cutoff  AvePP is the diagonal of the average posterior matrix: for the units modally assigned to a class, their mean posterior of belonging to it (Nagin, 2005). A class with no assigned unit has no AvePP; the smallest, largest and mean are taken over the classes that have one, and such a class is counted as below the cutoff, since nothing is classified into it. A level with no posteriors or a single class classifies nothing and gives `NA`s, the same rule as relative entropy.  @param probabilities Posterior probability matrix, or `NULL`. @param cutoff The AvePP below which a class is counted. @return A numeric vector: `min`, `max`, `mean`, `below`. @noRd

.multilpa_informative_classification.name: .multilpa_informative_classification
