.multilpa_informative_classification.documentation: One fit's classification table with its relative entropy, one-class levels left out  @param fit A fitted model of this package. @return The fit's `"classification"` rows at every level with two or more   classes, with that level's `relative_entropy`. @noRd

.multilpa_enumeration_classification.name: .multilpa_enumeration_classification
.multilpa_enumeration_classification.documentation: Per-class classification quality of every candidate in a grid  The `"classification"` table of each fitted candidate, keyed by the candidate's class counts and model and carrying that level's relative entropy, so AvePP and entropy are compared across the grid in one table. Candidates whose fit failed have no posteriors and contribute no rows, and neither does a level with a single class.  @param x A `multilpa_enumeration` result. @return A base `data.frame`, one row per candidate, level and class. @noRd

.multilpa_compact_candidates.name: .multilpa_compact_candidates
.multilpa_compact_candidates.documentation: The columns of an enumeration grid worth printing  The grid carries every criterion at both levels, which wraps a printed table across several screens. The print keeps the columns a reader compares candidates on, drops identifiers that do not vary, and shows a criterion once where its group-level and individual-level versions are the same numbers, as they are in a single-level grid. The full table is unchanged.  @param grid The enumeration table. @return A data frame with fewer columns. @noRd

.multilpa_enumeration_patterned.name: .multilpa_enumeration_patterned
.multilpa_enumeration_patterned.documentation: Does an enumeration fit covariances for chosen continuous pairs? @param vars The indicators. @param extra The other arguments of the enumeration. @return A single logical. @noRd

.multilpa_enumeration_arguments.name: .multilpa_enumeration_arguments
.multilpa_enumeration_arguments.documentation: The `multilpa()` arguments of one enumerated structure @param code A structure code, or `NA`. @param vars,extra As for `.multilpa_enumeration_patterned()`. @return A named list. @noRd

.multilpa_simulate.name: .multilpa_simulate
.multilpa_simulate.documentation: Generate observations from a fitted discrete multilevel model @param object Fitted model. @return Simulated data frame with the original group layout. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_simulate.name: .multilpa_cov_simulate
.multilpa_cov_simulate.documentation: Generate observations from a fitted covariate model, holding the covariates  The model conditions on its covariates, so the simulation does too: every group keeps its observed group covariates and every row its profile covariates. The group class is drawn from the group logits, the profile from the row's profile logits in that class, and the indicators from the profile.  @param object A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @param frame The fitting data; its indicator columns are replaced, and every   other column (identifier and covariates) is kept as observed. @return `frame` with simulated indicators. @noRd

.multilpa_carry_missingness.name: .multilpa_carry_missingness
.multilpa_carry_missingness.documentation: Give simulated data the observed data's missing values  A bootstrap of a `missing = "fiml"` fit must refit replicates that lose the same information the observed data lost, or the reference distribution is that of a complete-data statistic. The observed pattern is carried over cell for cell, which treats it as fixed: independent of the profiles and of the values that went missing (missing completely at random given the pattern).  @param simulated The simulated data frame. @param observed The fitting data, in the same row order. @param vars The indicator columns. @return `simulated` with `NA` wherever `observed` has one among `vars`. @noRd

.multilpa_draw_indicators.name: .multilpa_draw_indicators
.multilpa_draw_indicators.documentation: Draw indicators for given profiles from a fitted measurement model @param object A fitted model carrying the measurement blocks. @param profile Integer profile per observation. @return A data frame with one column per indicator, in `object$vars` order. @noRd

.multilpa_bootstrap_constraint.name: .multilpa_bootstrap_constraint
.multilpa_bootstrap_constraint.documentation: The measurement constraint both bootstrap refits must carry  A fit made with `fixed` treats its measurement blocks as known, so its likelihood is conditional on those values and its free parameters are only the ones the constraint left. A bootstrap that refits the replicates without the constraint compares unrestricted models, while the observed statistic compares constrained ones, and the resulting p-value answers a question nobody asked. This decides, once, what every refit must be given, and refuses the pairs whose constrained nesting cannot be established.  Nesting holds when both models hold the same blocks at the same values and differ only in the number of group classes: the extra class is a mixing parameter, and the null is the alternative with that class emptied. It does not hold when the models differ in the number of profiles, because the held measurement then has a different shape in each model and the smaller one is not a restriction of the larger one.  @param null_model The smaller fitted `multilpa` model. @param alternative_model The larger fitted `multilpa` model. @return A list with `start`, the `multilpa_start` carrying the held   measurement values (`NULL` when nothing is held), and `fixed`, the   character vector of held block names (`character(0)` when nothing is   held). Raises `latents_bad_nesting` when the two constrained models are   not nested. @noRd

.multilpa_check_covariate_nesting.name: .multilpa_check_covariate_nesting
.multilpa_check_covariate_nesting.documentation: Are two covariate models nested for a bootstrap comparison  The alternative must be the null with one more profile or group class and the same membership regressions. A null with one group class cannot carry group covariates or slopes by group class (both need a second class), and it is still the alternative with one class emptied, so there the alternative may add them.  @param null_model,alternative_model Fitted `multilpa_covariates` models. @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises `latents_bad_nesting`. @noRd

.multilpa_cov_check_likelihood.name: .multilpa_cov_check_likelihood
.multilpa_cov_check_likelihood.documentation: Check that data reproduce a covariate fit's likelihood @param model A fitted `multilpa_covariates` model. @param data The fitting data. @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises `latents_bad_inference_data`. @noRd

bootstrap_lrt.name: bootstrap_lrt
bootstrap_lrt.documentation: Parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio test of two nested models  Tests a model against one with one more individual profile or one more group class. Indicators are simulated from the null model with the observed group sizes, both models are refitted to every simulated dataset, and the observed likelihood-ratio statistic is compared with the simulated ones. The p-value is `(1 + b) / (iter + 1)`, where `b` counts simulated statistics at least as large as the observed one; no chi-square reference distribution is used. This is a native parametric bootstrap, not an implementation of Mplus TECH14.  The two models must differ by exactly one individual profile or one group class, with the observations, group layout, covariance structure, centering and scaling, missing-data handling and `drop_empty` the same. Grand-mean centering is repeated in every simulated refit. Person-centred or person-scaled fits are refused, because the model specifies no distribution for the group baselines that transformation removes. If any replicate fails validation (fails, does not converge, or has a reversed likelihood), the p-value is `NA`; no replicate is dropped.  Fits made with `missing = "fiml"` are supported when both models were: every replicate is given the observed data's missing cells before it is refitted. Calibration requires missingness independent of the indicators and latent classes, conditional on any fixed covariates. A fixed mask does not reproduce a MAR mechanism that depends on observed indicators, or an MNAR mechanism, and FIML estimation under MAR does not by itself validate this bootstrap under MAR; the size study covers MCAR only.  Membership-covariate fits (`multilpa(profile_covariates = , group_covariates = )`) are supported: the covariates are held at their observed values, group classes are drawn from the fitted group logits and profiles from each row's profile logits. Both models must use the same profile covariates, group covariates and slope specification, except that a one-group-class null, which cannot carry group covariates or slopes by group class, may be compared with an alternative that adds them. When `data` is omitted it is rebuilt from the alternative, whose columns include the null's. A covariate replicate counts as valid when its likelihood has converged even if a membership logit is still changing, as happens for an empty or separated class in an over-fitted alternative, because the statistic uses only the maximised likelihood. The replicate table's `logits_settled` column records whether both refits' logits had also converged. The original models must be fully converged.  Models fitted with `fixed`, including those from [fit_staged()], are supported: every replicate is refitted with the same blocks held at the same values. The p-value is then conditional on that measurement solution, whose own uncertainty is not propagated. A constrained pair whose nesting cannot be established is refused.  Two transition fits ([lta()]) or two group-class family fits are also accepted; each is handled by its own family's bootstrap. @section Conditions:   `latents_bad_nesting` when the models do not differ by exactly one class   at one level; when only one of them holds measurement blocks fixed, when   they hold different blocks or the same blocks at different values, or   when they hold a measurement fixed while differing in the number of   profiles; when the alternative does not estimate more free parameters   than the null; and when two covariate models use different covariates or   slope specifications (other than a one-group-class null).   `latents_incomparable_models` when the models differ in their   observations, grouping, covariance structure, centering, scaling,   missing-data handling or `drop_empty`.   `latents_unsupported_bootstrap` for person-centred or person-scaled fits.   `latents_unsupported_prior` for fits estimated with a prior, whose   likelihoods are evaluated at posterior modes rather than ML estimates.   `latents_unsupported_weights` for fits with sampling weights;   `latents_unsupported_noise` for fits with a noise component.   `latents_bad_data` when the data have missing indicators and the models   were not fitted with `missing = "fiml"`; `latents_bad_inference_data`   when `data` does not reproduce a fitted likelihood or the original   observations and their order.   `latents_no_converge` when either original model has not converged or   has an active variance bound; `latents_reversed_likelihood` when the   alternative's log likelihood is below the null's by more than `tol` can   explain; `latents_bad_argument` for an invalid `seed`, or for a   transition fit paired with a fit of another family.   `latents_failed_replicates` is a warning, given when some replicate   fails validation; the p-value is then `NA`. @param null_model The smaller model: a converged [multilpa()] fit, with or   without membership covariates. @param alternative_model The larger model, fitted to the same data. @param data Optional. The data both models were fitted to, used to verify   both fitted likelihoods. When omitted it is rebuilt from what the null   model stores (from the alternative for covariate fits). @param iter Number of simulated datasets, at least 2. Default 199; use many   for inference. @param n_starts Number of starts for each simulated fit. `NULL` (the   default) refits each model with the starts it was fitted with, by the same   `search`; a number applies to both models. @param max_iter Maximum EM iterations for each simulated fit; `NULL` (the   default) takes each model's own. @param tol Relative likelihood convergence tolerance; `NULL` (the default)   takes each model's own. @param seed Optional seed: a whole number `set.seed()` accepts. The   caller's random-number state is restored on exit. @return An object of class `multilpa_bootstrap_lrt`, holding the observed   statistic, the p-value, its Monte Carlo standard error, the measurement   blocks held fixed in every fit, and one record per replicate.   [as.data.frame()] gives the single-row test result,   `get_results(what = "replicates")` one row per simulated replicate,   [summary()] the test beside the replicate diagnostics, and [plot()] the   simulated null distribution with the observed statistic marked. Failed   starts, boundary flags and likelihood replication should be inspected   before the result is interpreted. @examples set.seed(1) example_data <- data.frame(   school = rep(seq_len(10), each = 10),   score = rnorm(100, rep(c(-2, 2), each = 50)) ) smaller <- multilpa(example_data, "score", "school", n_profiles = 1,                     n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1) larger <- multilpa(example_data, "score", "school", n_profiles = 2,                    n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1) # `iter` is small so the example runs quickly; use many more for inference. comparison <- bootstrap_lrt(smaller, larger, iter = 9, n_starts = 1,                             max_iter = 2000, tol = 1e-6, seed = 1) comparison @export

.multilpa_bootstrap_test_frame.name: .multilpa_bootstrap_test_frame
.multilpa_bootstrap_test_frame.documentation: The bootstrap test as a single tidy row @param x An `multilpa_bootstrap_lrt` result. @return A one-row `data.frame` describing the comparison. @noRd

.multilpa_enumeration_indices.name: .multilpa_enumeration_indices
.multilpa_enumeration_indices.documentation: Spread the information criteria of one candidate into a single row @param fit A fitted `multilpa` model, or `NULL` for a failed candidate. @return A one-row `data.frame` of criteria, all `NA_real_` when `fit` is `NULL`. @noRd

.multilpa_enumeration_criteria.name: .multilpa_enumeration_criteria
.multilpa_enumeration_criteria.documentation: The information criteria an enumeration grid carries  Named once so that the failed-candidate row and the fitted row cannot drift apart, and so that a renamed criterion is caught rather than silently turned into a missing column.  @return A character vector of grid column names, in grid order. @noRd

.latents_prepare_extra.name: .latents_prepare_extra
.latents_prepare_extra.documentation: Prepare ordinal and count indicators  @param data The data frame of the fit. @param ordinal,count Names of the ordinal and count indicators. @param missing `"error"` or `"fiml"`. @return `NULL` when neither is given; otherwise a list with `ordinal` (an   integer code matrix, codes 1..K), `ordinal_levels` (the category labels   per indicator), `ordinal_categories` (K per indicator) and `count` (a   numeric matrix of non-negative integers). @noRd

.latents_extra_names.name: .latents_extra_names
.latents_extra_names.documentation: The names of a fit's ordinal and count indicators @noRd

.latents_ordinal_log_probabilities.name: .latents_ordinal_log_probabilities
.latents_ordinal_log_probabilities.documentation: Log category probabilities of one ordinal indicator, profiles x categories  @param intercepts The K - 1 intercepts a_2..a_K (a_1 = 0). @param locations The C profile locations (the last is 0). @return A C x K matrix of log probabilities. @noRd

.latents_extra_log_density.name: .latents_extra_log_density
.latents_extra_log_density.documentation: Row-by-profile log densities of the ordinal and count indicators  @param extra Result of `.latents_prepare_extra()`, or `NULL`. @param parameters A parameter list carrying `ordinal_intercepts` (a list of   intercept vectors), `ordinal_locations` (C x J matrix), `count_means`   (C x J matrix) and, for negative-binomial counts, `count_dispersion`   (C x J matrix). @param n_rows,n_profiles Dimensions of the result. @return An n x C matrix; zero when there is nothing to add. @noRd

.latents_ordinal_counts.name: .latents_ordinal_counts
.latents_ordinal_counts.documentation: Posterior-weighted category counts of one ordinal indicator, C x K @noRd

.latents_ordinal_maximize.name: .latents_ordinal_maximize
.latents_ordinal_maximize.documentation: Maximize one ordinal indicator's expected log likelihood  The objective `sum_ck N_ck log P(k | c)` is concave in the intercepts and locations (a multinomial logit), so Newton-Raphson with the exact Hessian and step halving climbs it monotonically. The free coordinates are the K - 1 intercepts then the first C - 1 locations.  @param counts C x K posterior-weighted category counts. @param intercepts,locations The current point. @param max_newton Most Newton steps. @return A list with `intercepts` and `locations`. @noRd

.latents_extra_maximize.name: .latents_extra_maximize
.latents_extra_maximize.documentation: M-step of the ordinal and count indicators  @param extra Prepared indicators. @param posteriors n x C posterior weights (weighted, under sampling weights). @param previous The current parameters, the Newton start for ordinal ones. @return A list with `ordinal_intercepts`, `ordinal_locations`,   `count_means` and `count_dispersion` (negative-binomial counts only), each   `NULL` when absent. @noRd

.latents_extra_initialize.name: .latents_extra_initialize
.latents_extra_initialize.documentation: Starting values from a hard assignment of the rows @param extra Prepared indicators. @param assignments Profile of each row. @param n_profiles Number of profiles. @return The parameter blocks, as `.latents_extra_maximize()` returns them. @noRd

.latents_extra_clustering.name: .latents_extra_clustering
.latents_extra_clustering.documentation: Standardized columns for the initial clustering @return An n x J matrix (ordinal codes and log counts, mean-imputed and   standardized), or `NULL`. @noRd

.latents_extra_n_parameters.name: .latents_extra_n_parameters
.latents_extra_n_parameters.documentation: Free parameters of the ordinal and count indicators @noRd

.latents_extra_matrix.name: .latents_extra_matrix
.latents_extra_matrix.documentation: Distinct observed rows of the ordinal and count indicators, for the identification check @noRd

.latents_check_extra_arguments.name: .latents_check_extra_arguments
.latents_check_extra_arguments.documentation: Validate the ordinal and count indicator names and their pairings  @param vars,categorical,ordinal,count The indicator arguments of the fit. @param unsupported Named logicals: options the new indicators do not take   yet; a `TRUE` one is refused. @return `NULL`, invisibly. @noRd

.latents_label_extra.name: .latents_label_extra
.latents_label_extra.documentation: Name the ordinal and count parameter blocks of a fit @noRd

.latents_measurement_model.name: .latents_measurement_model
.latents_measurement_model.documentation: The measurement model a fit's indicator types make up @noRd

.latents_extra_coordinates.name: .latents_extra_coordinates
.latents_extra_coordinates.documentation: Inference coordinates of the ordinal and count indicators  Per ordinal indicator: its K - 1 intercepts (shared by every profile), then the first C - 1 profile locations (the last is the reference, zero); then per count indicator its C means, then (negative binomial) its dispersions, one shared or one per profile. Ordinal coordinates are already on the logit scale, so the natural and unconstrained values coincide; count means and dispersions are estimated on the log scale.  @param parameters A parameter list or fit carrying the blocks. @param extra Prepared indicators (for names and levels). @param n_profiles Number of profiles. @param scale `"natural"` or `"unconstrained"`. @return A named numeric vector in the package's `kind[...]` label grammar. @noRd

.latents_extra_width.name: .latents_extra_width
.latents_extra_width.documentation: Number of ordinal and count coordinates (the same on both scales) @noRd

.latents_extra_decode.name: .latents_extra_decode
.latents_extra_decode.documentation: Rebuild the ordinal and count blocks from unconstrained coordinates @return A list with `ordinal_intercepts`, `ordinal_locations`,   `count_means` and `count_dispersion` (`NULL` for Poisson counts). @noRd

.latents_extra_scores.name: .latents_extra_scores
.latents_extra_scores.documentation: Scores of the ordinal and count coordinates  By Fisher's identity each row's score is its posterior-weighted complete-data score: for an ordinal indicator the observed feature minus its expectation in each profile, for a Poisson count `y - lambda` on the log mean; negative-binomial counts use `.latents_negative_binomial_scores()` on the log mean and log dispersion. Missing values contribute nothing.  @param extra Prepared indicators. @param posteriors n x C posteriors (weighted, under sampling weights). @param parameters The blocks at which to evaluate. @param group_index Group of each row, or `NULL` for the total. @param x The continuous matrix, unshifted; needed for direct effects, whose   scores are `.latents_direct_scores()`. @return Groups (or one row) by `.latents_extra_width()` columns. @noRd

.latents_extra_jacobian.name: .latents_extra_jacobian
.latents_extra_jacobian.documentation: Natural-by-unconstrained Jacobian of the ordinal and count block @return A square diagonal matrix: one for ordinal coordinates, the value   itself for count means and dispersions (estimated on the log scale). @noRd

.latents_ordinal_frame.name: .latents_ordinal_frame
.latents_ordinal_frame.documentation: The ordinal indicators as a tidy table  @param x A fit carrying ordinal indicators. @param data Optional fitting data, as for the other measurement tables. @return One row per profile, ordinal indicator and category: `profile`,   `indicator`, `category`, `probability`, the profile's `location` on that   indicator (zero for the last, reference profile) and   `location_standard_error`. @noRd

.latents_count_frame.name: .latents_count_frame
.latents_count_frame.documentation: The count indicators as a tidy table @param x A fit carrying count indicators. @param data Optional fitting data. @return One row per profile and count indicator: `profile`, `indicator`,   `mean` and, for negative-binomial counts, `dispersion`; with   `standard_errors`, also `standard_error` and (negative binomial)   `dispersion_standard_error`. @noRd

.latents_extra_catalogue.name: .latents_extra_catalogue
.latents_extra_catalogue.documentation: The `get_results()` tables a fit with ordinal or count indicators adds @noRd

.latents_draw_extra.name: .latents_draw_extra
.latents_draw_extra.documentation: Draw ordinal and count indicators from a fit, given each row's profile  Ordinal indicators come back as ordered factors with the fit's levels, so a refit re-encodes the same categories even when one is not drawn.  @param object A fit carrying the blocks and `extra_data`. @param profile Profile of each row. @return A named list of columns, empty when the fit has none. @noRd

.latents_prepare_extra_like.name: .latents_prepare_extra_like
.latents_prepare_extra_like.documentation: Encode new rows' ordinal and count indicators as a fit encoded its own  @param object A fit carrying `extra_data`. @param newdata A data frame with the fit's indicator columns. @return Prepared indicators on the fit's categories, or `NULL`. A category   the fit never saw, or an invalid count, raises `latents_bad_data`. @noRd

.latents_print_extra.name: .latents_print_extra
.latents_print_extra.documentation: Print the ordinal and count indicators of a fit @return `NULL`, invisibly; one line naming them and their tables. @noRd

.latents_draw_extra_columns.name: .latents_draw_extra_columns
.latents_draw_extra_columns.documentation: The stored ordinal and count indicators as data columns @param extra Prepared indicators, or `NULL`. @return A named list of columns: ordered factors with the fit's levels for   ordinal indicators, numbers for counts. @noRd

.latents_extra_labels.name: .latents_extra_labels
.latents_extra_labels.documentation: Tidy labels of the ordinal and count coordinates  One row per coordinate, in `.latents_extra_coordinates()` order, with the level, outcome, term and parameter columns every inference table uses.  @param object A fit carrying `extra_data`. @param profiles Profile labels. @param free `TRUE` names count means on the log scale they are estimated on. @return A data frame, with no rows when the fit has neither type. @noRd

.latents_extra_rows.name: .latents_extra_rows
.latents_extra_rows.documentation: The rows of prepared ordinal and count indicators @param extra Prepared indicators, or `NULL`. @param rows Row indices to keep. @return The same structure on those rows only. @noRd

.lta_extra_table.name: .lta_extra_table
.lta_extra_table.documentation: Ordinal or count table of a transition fit, one block per measurement  As the transition `profiles` table: estimates by profile, with an `occasion` column that is `NA` when measurement is invariant.  @param fit A `multilpa_lta` fit. @param what `"ordinal"` or `"count_means"`. @return A data frame. @noRd

.latents_as_column_type.name: .latents_as_column_type
.latents_as_column_type.documentation: Put drawn values into the type of the column they replace  An ordinal draw is an ordered factor on the fit's levels; a column held as numbers gets the numbers back, a factor column the labels.  @param drawn Drawn values. @param column The original column. @return `drawn` in `column`'s type. @noRd

.latents_negative_binomial.name: .latents_negative_binomial
.latents_negative_binomial.documentation: Does a fit model its counts as negative binomial? @noRd

.latents_dispersion_rows.name: .latents_dispersion_rows
.latents_dispersion_rows.documentation: How many dispersion rows each negative-binomial count indicator has @return `0` for Poisson, `1` when shared, the number of profiles otherwise. @noRd

.latents_set_count_model.name: .latents_set_count_model
.latents_set_count_model.documentation: Attach the count model to prepared indicators @param extra Prepared indicators, or `NULL`. @param count_model `"poisson"` or `"negative_binomial"`. @param count_dispersion `"varying"` or `"equal"`. @return `extra` with the two fields set. @noRd

.latents_negative_binomial_scores.name: .latents_negative_binomial_scores
.latents_negative_binomial_scores.documentation: Per-row scores of a negative-binomial count on its log mean and log dispersion, one column per profile  With size r = 1 / alpha: d log f / d log mu = r (y - mu) / (r + mu), and d log f / d log alpha = -r [digamma(y + r) - digamma(r) + log(r / (r + mu)) + (mu - y) / (r + mu)].  @param value Counts (unobserved ones set to anything; they are masked by   the caller). @param means,dispersion One value per profile. @return A list of two n x C matrices. @noRd

.latents_negative_binomial_dispersion_de.name: .latents_negative_binomial_dispersion_derivatives
.latents_negative_binomial_dispersion_de.documentation: Stable negative-binomial log-dispersion derivatives  `means` is one value per profile, or a rows-by-classes matrix of means. Near the Poisson limit, differences of digamma/trigamma terms lose the small dispersion score to cancellation. Expand the NB log density relative to Poisson in alpha through order four when alpha times the count or mean is below 0.001. The coefficients follow from expanding sum_j log(1 + j alpha) - (y + 1/alpha) log(1 + mu alpha). Both expansion variables (alpha y and alpha mu) are then below 0.001. Above that switch, large size parameters use the digamma asymptotic expansion, combining its logarithm with the likelihood terms before scaling. Subtracting two digamma/trigamma values there loses precision. @noRd

.latents_moment_dispersion.name: .latents_moment_dispersion
.latents_moment_dispersion.documentation: A moment start for the negative-binomial dispersion, per profile @noRd

.latents_negative_binomial_maximize.name: .latents_negative_binomial_maximize
.latents_negative_binomial_maximize.documentation: Maximize one negative-binomial count indicator's expected log likelihood  Modified Newton-Raphson on the log means and log dispersions: the analytic Hessian with its eigenvalues reflected, so every direction ascends, and step halving so every accepted step raises the objective (to rounding). A dispersion is held at or above `.latents_min_dispersion`, the Poisson limit.  @param value The indicator's counts (`NA` where unobserved). @param posteriors n x C posterior weights. @param means,dispersion The current point, one value per profile. @param shared Whether one dispersion is shared by every profile. @param max_newton Most Newton steps. @return A list with `means` and `dispersion` (one value per profile). @noRd

.latents_poisson_limit.name: .latents_poisson_limit
.latents_poisson_limit.documentation: Put a negative-binomial dispersion on its boundary when the data ask for it  The likelihood flattens as the dispersion goes to zero, so Newton steps stop short of the boundary rather than reaching it. At alpha = 0 the score of the dispersion is `sum w [(y - mu)^2 - y] / 2` (the overdispersion score test); when it is not positive the maximum is on the boundary (the Poisson limit, Karush-Kuhn-Tucker), so the dispersion is set to the floor and the mean to its Poisson maximum, the weighted mean count.  @param point A list with `means` and `dispersion`, one value per profile. @param y Observed counts; `weight` their n x C posterior weights. @param shared Whether one dispersion is shared by every profile. @return `point`, with boundary dispersions on the floor. @noRd

.latents_warn_poisson_limit.name: .latents_warn_poisson_limit
.latents_warn_poisson_limit.documentation: Warn when a negative-binomial dispersion is on its boundary @param dispersion The fitted dispersion matrix, or `NULL`. @return `NULL`, invisibly; a `latents_boundary` warning when any   dispersion is at the floor. @noRd

.latents_negative_binomial_hessian.name: .latents_negative_binomial_hessian
.latents_negative_binomial_hessian.documentation: Hessian of a negative-binomial indicator's expected log likelihood  On the log means and log dispersions, from the closed-form second derivatives of the NB2 log density (r = 1 / alpha): d2/dlog mu2 = -r mu (r + y) / (r + mu)^2, d2/dlog mu dlog alpha = -r mu (y - mu) / (r + mu)^2, d2/dlog alpha2 = r D + r^2 dD/dr, with D = digamma(y + r) - digamma(r) + log(r / (r + mu)) + (mu - y) / (r + mu) and dD/dr = trigamma(y + r) - trigamma(r) + 1 / r - 1 / (r + mu) - (mu - y) / (r + mu)^2.  @param point A list with `means` and `dispersion`, one value per profile. @param y Observed counts; `weight` their n x C posterior weights. @param shared Whether one dispersion is shared by every profile. @return A square matrix over the log means, then the log dispersion(s). @noRd

.multilpa_fixed_blocks.name: .multilpa_fixed_blocks
.multilpa_fixed_blocks.documentation: Names of the measurement blocks a fit can hold fixed @return Character vector of the accepted `fixed` values, excluding the   `"measurement"` shorthand. @noRd

.multilpa_validate_fixed.name: .multilpa_validate_fixed
.multilpa_validate_fixed.documentation: Validate a `fixed` specification against the supplied start  @param fixed Character vector naming measurement blocks to hold, possibly   containing the shorthand `"measurement"`, or `character()` for none. @param start Validated start list, or `NULL`. @param covariance_model Diagonal or full residual covariance. @param n_continuous Number of continuous indicators. @param n_categories Category counts per categorical indicator, or `NULL`. @return The expanded character vector of held block names, in a fixed order.   Raises `latents_bad_fixed` when the request cannot be met. @noRd

.multilpa_held_parameters.name: .multilpa_held_parameters
.multilpa_held_parameters.documentation: Extract the held values from a validated start  @param start Validated start list. @param fixed Expanded character vector of held block names. @param covariance_model Diagonal or full residual covariance. @return A list carrying only the held blocks, named as the maximization step   reads them, or `NULL` when nothing is held. @noRd

.multilpa_apply_held.name: .multilpa_apply_held
.multilpa_apply_held.documentation: Apply the held values to a set of initial parameters  Every restart must begin from the held values, otherwise a random start would report a measurement solution that was never estimated and never supplied.  @param parameters Initial parameters from the initializer or the start. @param held Held values from `.multilpa_held_parameters()`, or `NULL`. @return The parameters with every held block replaced. @noRd

.multilpa_fixed_parameters.name: .multilpa_fixed_parameters
.multilpa_fixed_parameters.documentation: Count the measurement parameters a `fixed` specification removes  @param fixed Expanded character vector of held block names. @param n_profiles Number of individual profiles. @param n_continuous Number of continuous indicators. @param n_categories Category counts per categorical indicator, or `NULL`. @param variance_model Varying or equal across profiles. @param covariance_model Diagonal or full residual covariance. @return Number of parameters that are no longer free. @noRd

.multilpa_complete_start.name: .multilpa_complete_start
.multilpa_complete_start.documentation: Complete a measurement-only start with free mixing values  `starting_values(what = "measurement")` deliberately drops the mixing blocks, because they are sized for the model that produced them and a staged fit usually changes the number of group classes. They are free parameters here, so only a starting point is needed, and a uniform one is used.  @param start Start list, possibly without mixing blocks, or `NULL`. @param n_profiles Number of individual profiles. @param n_group_classes Number of latent group classes. @return The start with `profile_probabilities` and `group_probabilities`   present. Blocks the caller supplied are left exactly as given, so a   mismatched one still fails validation rather than being silently replaced. @noRd

fit_staged.name: fit_staged
fit_staged.documentation: Fit a two-level model in stages, holding the measurement solution  Fits a two-level model in two stages and returns the second-stage `multilpa` object. The first stage estimates the measurement model with one group class; the second estimates the group-class structure with that measurement held fixed, so adding group classes does not change the profiles.  @inheritParams multilpa @param id Name of the observed group identifier column. Character, factor   and numeric identifiers are supported; missing identifiers are not.   Required; `id = NULL` is not accepted. @param n_group_classes Number of latent group classes to estimate in the   second stage (default 2); must be at least two. @param measurement `NULL` (the default), to fit the first stage here with   one group class, or a fitted `multilpa` model to use as the first stage.   Its profiles, indicators and measurement options must match the ones   requested here, and it must have one group class. Fits made with   `weights`, `centering` or `scaling`, with `ordinal` or `count`   indicators, with `direct_effects` or with `local_dependence` between   continuous indicators, are refused, as are covariance structures other   than EEI, VVI, EEE and VVV. Every refusal raises `latents_bad_stage`. @param n_starts Number of EM starts, used for both stages. @return A `multilpa` object for the second stage, on which every accessor,   diagnostic and method works. Its measurement parameters are exactly the   first stage's. It also carries `fixed`, naming the held blocks;   `n_parameters`, counting only the parameters this stage estimated; and   `n_parameters_with_measurement`, which adds the held measurement back.   `get_results(fit, what = "stages")` gives a two-row summary of both   stages. @details The second stage treats the measurement solution as known, so its   Wald standard errors ([parameter_inference()]'s default), information   criteria and likelihood-ratio comparisons are conditional on that solution   and narrower than under joint estimation.   `parameter_inference(fit, method = "bootstrap")` removes that conditioning   for the standard errors and intervals: every resample of the groups is   staged again, measurement first, and the table also reports the   measurement parameters with their own errors. A supplied `measurement` is   re-estimated on each resample with the same options. The criteria and   likelihood comparisons remain conditional: compare staged fits with one   another using `n_parameters`, and a staged fit with a jointly estimated   one using `n_parameters_with_measurement`; the staged likelihood is not   the joint maximum, so the latter comparison is descriptive. @seealso [multilpa()] with `fixed` for finer control over which blocks are   held, and [starting_values()] with `what = "measurement"` for the values a   stage hands on. @examples set.seed(7) example_data <- data.frame(   school = rep(seq_len(30), each = 8),   score_a = stats::rnorm(240), score_b = stats::rnorm(240) ) staged <- fit_staged(example_data, c("score_a", "score_b"), "school",                      n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 2,                      seed = 1) get_results(staged, what = "stages") get_results(staged, what = "profile_probabilities") @export

.multilpa_stage_start.name: .multilpa_stage_start
.multilpa_stage_start.documentation: The measurement values a stage hands on, with their labels kept  [starting_values()] drops dimension names, because [multilpa()] reads a start by position. A staged fit cannot afford that for the categorical block: the second stage may name `categorical` in a different order, or see the same factor with its levels declared in a different order, and a positional hand over would then attach a first-stage response distribution to the wrong item or the wrong category and report a likelihood for a model nobody asked for. The labelled blocks are handed over instead, so [multilpa()] aligns them by indicator name and category label and refuses an encoding it cannot align.  @param measurement The first-stage fitted `multilpa` model. @return A `multilpa_start` carrying the measurement blocks, with the   categorical blocks named by indicator and their columns named by category. @noRd

.multilpa_requested_levels.name: .multilpa_requested_levels
.multilpa_requested_levels.documentation: The category labels a requested stage will observe  The second stage encodes its own categorical columns, so the labels it will use come from the data it is about to be given, not from the first stage.  @param data The data frame the stage will be fitted to. @param categorical Requested categorical indicator names. @return A named list of category labels per indicator, in code order, or   `NULL` when the request names no categorical indicator or names a column   `data` does not have, in which case [multilpa()] reports the broken data   contract in its own words. @noRd

.multilpa_category_counts.name: .multilpa_category_counts
.multilpa_category_counts.documentation: Category counts of a fitted model, or NULL when it has no categorical block @param object A fitted `multilpa` model. @return Integer vector of category counts, or `NULL`. @noRd

.multilpa_check_measurement.name: .multilpa_check_measurement
.multilpa_check_measurement.documentation: Check that a supplied first stage matches the second stage being requested  A measurement solution fitted to different indicators, a different number of profiles or a different covariance structure cannot be held fixed here; the mismatch is reported rather than reshaped.  @param measurement Fitted `multilpa` model offered as the first stage. @param n_profiles Requested number of profiles. @param vars Requested indicator names. @param categorical Requested categorical indicator names. @param covariance_model Requested residual covariance structure. @param variance_model Requested variance constraint. @param levels Named list of the category labels the requested stage will   observe, in code order, or `NULL` when there are no categorical   indicators. The labels, not their order, are what must match: a stage that   sees the same categories in a different order is aligned by label, while a   stage that sees a different category cannot be aligned at all. @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises `latents_bad_stage` on the first mismatch. @noRd

.latents_gaussian_diagnostics.name: .latents_gaussian_diagnostics
.latents_gaussian_diagnostics.documentation: Descriptive covariance and support diagnostics for Gaussian components  Standardization uses the observed, sampling-weighted marginal variance (divisor sum of weights), including between-component variation. Neither the ratios nor membership measures classify a component as spurious or establish identification. Gaussian mass uses the fit's normalized sampling weights; its scale is not an independent sample count. Weight effective n is Kish's concentration measure for posterior times sampling weight.  @param parameters Gaussian means, variances and optional covariances. @param data Observation-by-Gaussian-indicator matrix on the fitted scale. @param posteriors Unweighted observation-by-component probabilities. @param weights Nonnegative observation sampling weights, or `NULL`. @param min_variance Absolute variance or covariance eigenvalue floor. @param context Name of the density level or measurement block. @return A data frame with one row per Gaussian component, or no rows when   there are no Gaussian indicators. Missing reference variances give `NA`   ratios, rather than an implied regular or irregular classification. @noRd

.latents_print_gaussian_diagnostics.name: .latents_print_gaussian_diagnostics
.latents_print_gaussian_diagnostics.documentation: Print the narrowest Gaussian direction without applying a cutoff @param table A Gaussian diagnostic table, or `NULL` for an older fit. @return `NULL`, invisibly. Called for its descriptive output. @noRd

.latents_gaussian_minimum.name: .latents_gaussian_minimum
.latents_gaussian_minimum.documentation: Smallest available component diagnostic for a model comparison row @param fit A fitted model, or `NULL` for a failed candidate. @param column A numeric column of its Gaussian diagnostic table. @return A numeric scalar; `NA` when the diagnostic is unavailable. @noRd

.multilpa_gaussian_moments.name: .multilpa_gaussian_moments
.multilpa_gaussian_moments.documentation: Evaluate observed Gaussian densities and conditional sufficient statistics @param x Numeric observation matrix, possibly containing NA. @param parameters Gaussian mixture parameter list. @return Log densities and conditional first moments and covariance adjustments. @noRd

.multilpa_bound_covariance.name: .multilpa_bound_covariance
.multilpa_bound_covariance.documentation: Constrain a covariance matrix by its minimum eigenvalue @param covariance Symmetric covariance matrix. @param min_variance Positive eigenvalue lower bound. @return Symmetric positive definite covariance matrix. @noRd

.multilpa_maximize_moments.name: .multilpa_maximize_moments
.multilpa_maximize_moments.documentation: Maximize Gaussian parameters from conditional moments @param x Numeric observation matrix. @param expectation Nested posteriors containing conditional Gaussian moments. @param variance_model Equal or varying covariance across profiles. @param min_variance Variance or eigenvalue lower bound. @param covariance_model Diagonal or full covariance. @param held Parameters to hold at supplied values, or `NULL` to estimate   every one of them. Only `means`, `variances` and `covariances` are read. @param covariance_pattern `NULL`, or a logical indicators-by-indicators   matrix marking the free covariance entries (the diagonal and the   `local_dependence` pairs); every other entry is held at zero. @return Means, diagonal variances, and optional covariance array. A held   block is returned as supplied. @noRd

.multilpa_covariance_boundary.name: .multilpa_covariance_boundary
.multilpa_covariance_boundary.documentation: Detect constrained Gaussian covariance estimates @param parameters Gaussian parameter list. @param min_variance Variance or eigenvalue lower bound. @return Whether a variance or covariance eigenvalue is on its lower bound. @noRd

get_results.name: get_results
get_results.documentation: Extract the result tables of a fitted model  Returns one tidy table of a fitted model or related object, named by `what`, as a base `data.frame`; `what = "all"` returns every table the object offers as a named list. The tables available depend on the class of the object and are listed under *Tables*.  Every object also has `print()`, which shows a compact overview, `summary()`, which collects its main tables (taking `level` and `vcov_type` where the model has standard errors), and `as.data.frame()`, which returns its primary table, the same as `get_results(x)`.  @param x A fitted model of this package, an enumeration grid, a model   comparison, a bootstrap comparison, a starting-value set, a   classification-diagnostics object, or the summary of any of them. @param what Name of the table to return, or `"all"` for every table the   object offers. `NULL` (default) returns the primary table: the   measurement model for a fit, the candidate grid for an enumeration, the   test row for a bootstrap comparison and the entropy table for a   diagnostics object. A name the object does not offer raises   `latents_bad_argument`, listing the names it does offer. @param ... Arguments for the requested table. Each table accepts only the   arguments listed for it under *Tables*; any other argument raises   `latents_bad_argument`.  @section Tables: Every fitted model offers these: \describe{   \item{`"profiles"`}{The Gaussian measurement model, one row per profile     and continuous indicator: `profile`, `indicator`, `mean`, `variance`,     `standard_deviation`, `mean_standard_error`, `variance_standard_error`.     Zero rows, with the same columns, when every indicator is categorical.     Takes `scale` and `data`.}   \item{`"responses"`}{The categorical measurement model, one row per     profile, categorical indicator and category: `profile`, `indicator`,     `category`, `probability`, `threshold`, `probability_standard_error`.     `threshold` is `qlogis(P(y <= category))` and is `NA_real_` for each     indicator's final category; a probability on its bound has an     `NA_real_` standard error. Zero rows, with the same columns, when no     indicator is categorical. Takes `data`.}   \item{`"covariances"`}{The within-profile residual covariance matrices,     one row per profile and ordered pair of continuous indicators:     `profile`, `indicator`, `indicator_2`, `covariance`. Under the diagonal     parameterization the off-diagonal covariances are reported as exact     zeros.}   \item{`"ordinal"`, `"count_means"`}{Fits with ordinal or count     indicators only: the ordinal and count measurement models. Take     `data`.}   \item{`"counts"`}{Effective class sizes, one row per class at each level     of the fit: `level`, `class`, `effective_count` (the summed posteriors)     and `effective_proportion`. These differ from the modal counts in     `"classification"` whenever entropy is below one.}   \item{`"model"`}{One row describing the fit: its dimensions, likelihood,     parameter counts, `aic`, `bic_groups`, `bic_individual` and its     convergence and boundary diagnostics. The columns differ by family (a     covariate fit adds its predictor counts); `"information_criteria"` has     the same columns for every family.}   \item{`"posteriors"`}{One row per individual and profile: `row`, `group`,     `profile`, `posterior`, `modal`. Takes `format`.}   \item{`"assignments"`}{One row per observation: the columns the fit was     built from (or those of `data`), then `profile`, `group_class` where the     model has one, `uncertainty` (one minus the posterior of the assigned     profile) and one `posterior_profile_*` column per profile, plus     `posterior_noise` for a fit with a noise component (whose cases are     profile 0). Takes `data` and `truth`; with `truth` it returns a recovery     table instead (see *Recovery*).}   \item{`"classification"`}{Classification quality, one row per level and     class: `level`, `class`, `n_modal`, `proportion_modal`, `estimated_n`,     `estimated_proportion`, `average_posterior`,     `odds_correct_classification`. Takes `level`. Under sampling weights     `estimated_n` and `estimated_proportion` (and hence the odds of correct     classification) are weighted posterior totals; the modal and average     posterior columns describe the units supplied. The odds are `Inf` for a     class classified perfectly (average posterior one to within rounding)     and `NA` where they are undefined: a class with no modal members, or a     single class, whose proportion is one.}   \item{`"average_posteriors"`}{For the units modally assigned to each     class, their mean posterior for every class: `level`, `assigned_class`,     `class`, `n_assigned`, `average_posterior`. Rows sum to one within each     assigned class. This conditions on the assigned class, whereas     `"classification_errors"` conditions on the true class. Takes `level`.}   \item{`"classification_errors"`}{The probability that a unit in one true     class is assigned to another: `level`, `true_class`, `assigned_class`,     `probability`, summing to one within each `true_class`. Takes `level`.     On a membership-covariate fit this is a marginal summary over the fitted     units, not conditional on the covariates. A fit with a noise component     raises `latents_unsupported_noise`, as [three_step()] does, and `"all"`     and `summary()` omit the table.}   \item{`"bch_weights"`}{The BCH inverse-error weights, one row per unit and     class: `level`, `unit`, `assigned_class`, `class`, `weight`. Takes     `level`; a weighted regression should use one level, not `"both"`. On a     membership-covariate fit the weights invert the marginal error matrix     and are not a conditional three-step correction. Not available for a fit     with a noise component, as for `"classification_errors"`.}   \item{`"entropy"`}{One row per level: `level`, `n_classes`, `n_units`,     `entropy_sum`, `relative_entropy`.}   \item{`"residuals"`}{Bivariate residuals for every indicator pair, testing     within-profile independence: `profile`, `indicator_1`, `indicator_2`,     `kind`, `observed`, `expected`, `residual`, `effective_n`, `statistic`,     `df`, `p_value`, `p_adjusted`. Takes `data`, `by` and `adjust`.}   \item{`"information_criteria"`}{Every information criterion the package     computes (see *Information criteria*). Takes `format` and     `definitions`.}   \item{`"sequences"`}{The assignments in occasion order, one row per     observation: `group`, `group_class`, `time`, `profile`. Takes `format`.     Raises `latents_no_time` for a fit made without `time`.}   \item{`"sequence_summary"`}{One row per group class: `group_class`,     `groups`, `observations`, `mean_length`, `median_length`, `shortest`,     `longest`, `complete`, `gaps`. Raises `latents_no_time` for a fit made     without `time`.}   \item{`"starts"`}{One row per EM start: `start`, `log_likelihood`,     `converged`, `iterations`, `error` and, where the family records it,     `boundary`. Several truth columns are stacked.    A truth column that is constant within every group is compared against   `group_class`; one that varies within any group is compared against   `profile`. The `assignment` column records which comparison was made.   Group-level recovery counts each group once. Unused factor levels are   omitted. For a fit without discrete group classes every column is   compared against `profile`.    The model's labels are arbitrary, so mass off the diagonal indicates   relabelling, not failure.  @section Information criteria: Let `q` be the number of free parameters,   `n` the chosen sample size, and `EN` the classification entropy of the   level matching that convention. The criteria are `deviance = -2L`,   `aic = -2L + 2q`, `bic = -2L + q log(n)`,   `sabic = -2L + q log((n + 2) / 24)`, `caic = -2L + q (log(n) + 1)`,   `awe = -2(L - EN) + 2q (1.5 + log(n))`, `icl = -2L + q log(n) + 2 EN`,   `kic = -2L + 3(q + 1)`, and `clc = -2L + 2 EN`. `clc`, like `icl` and   `awe`, uses the entropy sum; `tidyLPA` reports a `CLC` based on relative   entropy, and the two values are not comparable.    Every criterion that depends on a sample size is reported under both   multilevel conventions, `"groups"` and `"individuals"`, using group-level   posteriors under the first and individual-level posteriors under the   second. Use one convention consistently across compared candidates.   `deviance`, `aic` and `kic` carry `convention = NA_character_`. `clc`   depends on no sample size, but its convention selects which level's   classification entropy it penalises, so it is reported once per   convention. Individual sample sizes exclude rows with no observed   indicators, and group sample sizes exclude groups in which every row has   none (`n_informative_groups`); the classification statistics of each   level exclude the same rows and groups, as in Mplus. Where the group   classification entropy is undefined, group-level `awe`, `icl` and `clc`   are `NA`.  @section Classification quality: The odds of correct classification for   class `k` is `(p / (1 - p)) / (r / (1 - r))`, where `p` is the average   posterior in the assigned class and `r` is the model-estimated class   proportion. Values near one indicate classification no better than the   class proportions alone; values of five or more are conventionally taken   as adequate separation. It is `NA_real_` when `average_posterior` is   missing, or when it or `estimated_proportion` is zero or one, so a   single-class solution always reports `NA_real_`. `average_posterior` is   `NA_real_` for a class with no modal members. `n_modal` and   `estimated_n` differ whenever entropy is below one.    `relative_entropy` is `1 - EN / (n log K)`, between zero and one, higher   meaning sharper classification; `entropy_sum` is the raw `EN` used by the   entropy-penalised criteria, lower meaning sharper. `relative_entropy` is   `NA_real_` for a level with a single class.    A fit with individual profiles but no discrete group classes reports   individuals only for `level = "both"` and raises   `latents_no_group_classes` for `level = "groups"`.  @section Bivariate residuals: `"residuals"` tests, pair by pair, the   assumption that indicators are independent within a profile, weighting   each observation by its posterior. `data` must be in the order the model   was fitted in; the alignment is checked. A large residual indicates   local dependence between two indicators, which otherwise tends to be   absorbed by an extra profile. The p-values are approximate, and   `p_adjusted` applies the correction named by `adjust` across the pairs.   A fit with sampling weights uses them in the descriptive associations   and `effective_n`; design-based inference is not implemented, so   `statistic`, `df`, `p_value` and `p_adjusted` are `NA` for weighted fits.  @references Schwarz, G. .multilpa_coerce.name: .multilpa_coerce
.multilpa_coerce.documentation: Coerce an object of this package to its primary table  The one body behind every `as.data.frame()` method here, so no class can coerce to something other than the first entry of its own catalogue.  @param x The object. @param row.names The caller's `row.names`. @param extra `list(...)` as the method received it, which must be empty. @return A base `data.frame`. @noRd

.multilpa_dispatch_table.name: .multilpa_dispatch_table
.multilpa_dispatch_table.documentation: Resolve one `what` against an object's catalogue and build that table  The single place `what` is matched, arguments are checked and a table is built, so every method is the same three words and no class can drift from the shared contract.  @param x The object. @param what The caller's `what`, possibly `NULL`. @param extra `list(...)` as the method received it. @return A `data.frame`, or a named list of them for `what = "all"`. @noRd

.multilpa_match_table.name: .multilpa_match_table
.multilpa_match_table.documentation: Match a requested table name against what an object offers  Exact matching rather than `match.arg()`'s partial matching: the catalogues run to nineteen entries and share prefixes -- `starts`, `stages`, `sequences`, `sequence_summary` -- so a partial match would resolve to whichever happened to come first. The refusal lists every available name, so nothing is lost by being exact.  @param what The caller's `what`, possibly `NULL`. @param choices The catalogue's names. @return A single table name, or `"all"`. @noRd

.multilpa_check_table_arguments.name: .multilpa_check_table_arguments
.multilpa_check_table_arguments.documentation: Refuse an argument the requested table does not take  A dropped argument returns a table that answers a different question from the one asked, and does so without a word. Naming it back costs the caller one correction and saves them a wrong number.  @param what The table name, for the message. @param accepted The argument names that table takes. @param extra `list(...)` as the method received it. @return `NULL`, invisibly, when there is nothing to refuse. @noRd

.multilpa_absent_table_conditions.name: .multilpa_absent_table_conditions
.multilpa_absent_table_conditions.documentation: Classed refusals that mean "this object has no such table"  `what = "all"` walks the whole catalogue, and some of its entries cannot be built for every object: a fit made without `time` has no sequences, a fit without discrete group classes has no bivariate residuals. Those are refusals about the object, not failures, and `"all"` leaves the table out. Every other condition propagates, so a genuine defect is never swallowed.  @return A character vector of condition classes. @noRd

.multilpa_all_tables.name: .multilpa_all_tables
.multilpa_all_tables.documentation: Build every table an object can produce  @param x The object. @param catalogue Its catalogue. @param extra `list(...)`, which must be empty. @return A named list of `data.frame`s, without the ones this object has not. @noRd

.multilpa_catalogue.name: .multilpa_catalogue
.multilpa_catalogue.documentation: The tables an object offers, and the arguments each of them takes  One definition per table, shared by `what = <name>` and by `what = "all"`, so the two cannot return differently built versions of the same table. The first entry is the object's primary table, which is what `as.data.frame()` and a `NULL` `what` return.  A table the family defines but this particular object cannot produce stays in the catalogue and raises its classed condition, so the refusal names the reason. A table another family defines is absent, and the refusal lists what this one has.  @param x The object. @return A named list of `list(build =, args =)` entries, in reporting order:   the measurement model, then the mixing structure, then the unit-level   tables, then the diagnostics, then the sequence tables, then provenance. @noRd

.multilpa_table.name: .multilpa_table
.multilpa_table.documentation: One catalogue entry @param build A function of the object and that table's own arguments. @param args The argument names it accepts. @param in_all `FALSE` leaves the table out of `what = "all"` (and so of   `summary()`), for a table too costly to build unasked. @return A list of the three. @noRd

.multilpa_any_summary.name: .multilpa_any_summary
.multilpa_any_summary.documentation: Is this the summary of a fitted model of this package? @param x Any object. @return A single logical. @noRd

.multilpa_stored_catalogue.name: .multilpa_stored_catalogue
.multilpa_stored_catalogue.documentation: A catalogue over the tables a summary already carries  A summary is built by asking the fit for every table, so its own catalogue serves them back rather than recomputing them. That is what makes `get_results(summary(fit), what)` and `get_results(fit, what)` the same table rather than two computations that could diverge.  @param x A summary object. @return A named list of catalogue entries. @noRd

.multilpa_measurement_catalogue.name: .multilpa_measurement_catalogue
.multilpa_measurement_catalogue.documentation: The measurement tables every fitted family offers @return A named list of catalogue entries. @noRd

.multilpa_mixing_catalogue.name: .multilpa_mixing_catalogue
.multilpa_mixing_catalogue.documentation: The mixing-structure tables, which differ by model family @param x A fitted model of this package. @return A named list of catalogue entries. @noRd

.multilpa_unit_catalogue.name: .multilpa_unit_catalogue
.multilpa_unit_catalogue.documentation: The one-row-per-unit tables @param x A fitted model of this package. @return A named list of catalogue entries. @noRd

.multilpa_diagnostic_catalogue.name: .multilpa_diagnostic_catalogue
.multilpa_diagnostic_catalogue.documentation: The classification and model-fit tables every fitted family offers @return A named list of catalogue entries. @noRd

.multilpa_sequence_catalogue.name: .multilpa_sequence_catalogue
.multilpa_sequence_catalogue.documentation: The occasion-ordered tables @param x A fitted model of this package. @return A named list of catalogue entries. @noRd

.multilpa_provenance_catalogue.name: .multilpa_provenance_catalogue
.multilpa_provenance_catalogue.documentation: The tables that record how the fit was produced @param x A fitted model of this package. @return A named list of catalogue entries. @noRd

.multilpa_hide_fabricated_id.name: .multilpa_hide_fabricated_id
.multilpa_hide_fabricated_id.documentation: Hide the unit column a single-level fit fabricated for itself  `id = NULL` numbers the rows so the two-level machinery has a unit to group by, and every internal rebuild of the fitting data needs that column -- `parameter_inference()` checks the frame against it. What the caller never wrote, though, they should not be handed back, so it is dropped here, at the table the caller reads, rather than at the rebuild the package relies on.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @param frame A table that may carry the fabricated column. @return `frame`, without that column when the fit fabricated one. @noRd

.multilpa_default_level.name: .multilpa_default_level
.multilpa_default_level.documentation: Which classification levels to report when the caller named none @param x A fitted model of this package. @param level The caller's `level`, possibly `NULL`. @return A single level name. @noRd

.multilpa_diagnostic_residuals.name: .multilpa_diagnostic_residuals
.multilpa_diagnostic_residuals.documentation: The bivariate residuals a diagnostics object holds, or the reason it has none @param x A `multilpa_diagnostics` object. @return The residual table. @noRd

.multilpa_sequence_length_frame.name: .multilpa_sequence_length_frame
.multilpa_sequence_length_frame.documentation: How many occasions each group of a transition fit contributes @param x A fitted `multilpa_transitions` model. @return One row per group. @noRd

.multilpa_print_tables.name: .multilpa_print_tables
.multilpa_print_tables.documentation: Print every table an object carries  A summary is the whole of what an object holds, so its `print()` shows every table rather than a chosen few. A table longer than `rows` is shown to that depth with its remaining row count and the call that returns it whole: the alternative is either a console dump or a table the reader cannot tell was truncated.  @param tables A named list of `data.frame`s, as `get_results(x, "all")` gives. @param rows How many rows of each table to show. @param digits Printed significant digits. @return `NULL`, invisibly. Called for the printing. @noRd

.multilpa_print_table_footer.name: .multilpa_print_table_footer
.multilpa_print_table_footer.documentation: The closing line of a summary that has printed its tables @param tables The tables that were printed. @return `NULL`, invisibly. @noRd

.multilpa_check_print_arguments.name: .multilpa_check_print_arguments
.multilpa_check_print_arguments.documentation: Validate the two printing controls every summary print method takes @param digits The caller's `digits`. @param rows The caller's `rows`. @return `NULL`, invisibly. @noRd

.multilpa_wide_means.name: .multilpa_wide_means
.multilpa_wide_means.documentation: The profile means as one row per profile  The long measurement table is one row per profile *and* indicator, which is the right shape to compute on and the wrong one to read: three profiles over five indicators is fifteen lines of console for a table that has three rows. This is the shape the means are read in. It is built by reshaping the long table rather than from `x$means`, so the two cannot report different numbers.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @return A `data.frame` with one row per profile and one column per   continuous indicator. @noRd

.multilpa_print_primary.name: .multilpa_print_primary
.multilpa_print_primary.documentation: Print a fit's primary table under its header  A fitted model auto-prints its own estimates. The alternative is a header that describes a result the reader then has to fetch with a second call, which is the ritual this package exists to remove: `fit` and `as.data.frame(fit)` would otherwise be two calls showing one thing.  The measurement model is the primary table, and an all-categorical fit has none, so that fit prints its response probabilities instead of an empty block under a heading promising means.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @param rows How many rows to print before truncating. @return `NULL`, invisibly. Called for the printing. @noRd

.latents_grid_kind.name: .latents_grid_kind
.latents_grid_kind.documentation: The kind of an enumeration grid @param x Any object. @return `"profiles"`, `"transitions"`, `"families"` or `"regressions"`, or   `NA_character_` for an object that is not a grid. @noRd

.latents_grid_view_names.name: .latents_grid_view_names
.latents_grid_view_names.documentation: The views that are not criteria, in the order they are listed @return A character vector of `what` values. @noRd

.latents_grid_views.name: .latents_grid_views
.latents_grid_views.documentation: What a grid can draw  The registry every grid verb consults. A view is offered when the grid's table or fits carry what it draws: the criterion columns of the table; the classification-quality views from the fits' posteriors (or the table's entropy); the model-selection views, which lay the candidates out by number of classes and number of group classes; and the tree, which divides each named candidate's units by their posteriors. A view that is not offered has a reason, which the refusal gives.  @param x An enumeration grid. @param verb The calling function's name, for the refusal of a non-grid. @return A list: `kind`; `criteria`, the criterion columns, named by their   display titles; `default`, the criteria drawn when `what` is not given;   `using`, the criterion the selection views read by default; `axis`, the   table column on the x-axis (`"n_profiles"` or `"n_group_classes"`);   `word`, what the classes on that axis are called; `views`, the offered   views other than criteria; `refused`, a named character vector giving the   reason for each view not offered. @noRd

.latents_grid_view_table.name: .latents_grid_view_table
.latents_grid_view_table.documentation: The views of one grid, as `plot_views(x)` returns them  @param x An enumeration grid. @return A base `data.frame`, one row per `what` value: `type`, `group`   (`"criteria"`, `"quality"`, `"selection"` or `"tree"`), `supported`,   `description` and `reason` (why a view is not offered; `NA` when it is). @noRd

.latents_refuse_non_grid.name: .latents_refuse_non_grid
.latents_refuse_non_grid.documentation: Refuse an object that is not an enumeration grid @param x The object passed to a grid verb. @param verb The calling function's name, for the message. @return Does not return; raises `latents_bad_argument`. @noRd

.latents_grid_offer_text.name: .latents_grid_offer_text
.latents_grid_offer_text.documentation: Everything a grid's `what` takes, as text for a message @param views The output of `.latents_grid_views()`. @return One string. @noRd

.latents_require_grid_views.name: .latents_require_grid_views
.latents_require_grid_views.documentation: Refuse a view a grid does not offer  Criterion names are checked separately: an unknown name is an unknown criterion. This refuses the named views (quality, selection, tree) that the grid's kind cannot draw, with the reason and what the grid does offer.  @param x An enumeration grid. @param what The requested views. @param verb The calling function's name, for the message. @return `NULL`, invisibly, when every requested view is offered. @noRd

.latents_grid_table.name: .latents_grid_table
.latents_grid_table.documentation: A grid's candidates in the layout every grid view reads  One row per candidate, with `candidate`, `n_group_classes`, `model`, `log_likelihood`, `n_parameters`, the criterion columns, `converged` (never `NA`), `boundary` and `n_best_replicated`; and `n_profiles`, the number of profiles or classes, except on a family grid, whose candidates have none. A regression grid's `n_classes` is its `n_profiles`, its candidates are named `classes2` (with `_groups2` when the grid has group classes), and it records no boundary (`NA`).  @param x An enumeration grid. @return A base `data.frame`. @noRd

.latents_regression_posteriors.name: .latents_regression_posteriors
.latents_regression_posteriors.documentation: The posteriors of one regression-grid fit at one level @param fit A cell of a regression grid: a fit, or the condition it raised. @param level `"individuals"` (the units classified into classes) or   `"groups"` (the groups classified into group classes). @return A posterior matrix, or `NULL` when the cell has none at that level. @noRd

.latents_grid_quality_table.name: .latents_grid_quality_table
.latents_grid_quality_table.documentation: A grid's table with the classification quality of every candidate  Adds `profile_entropy` and `group_entropy` (relative entropy at each level) and `avepp_min` and `group_avepp_min` (the lowest average posterior probability at each level) to `.latents_grid_table()`; a profile or class grid gives `.multilpa_enumeration_grid()`, which carries the full AvePP summary. A level a candidate does not have, or has with one class, is `NA`.  @param x An enumeration grid. @param cutoff The AvePP cutoff. @return A base `data.frame`, one row per candidate. @noRd

.latents_grid_criteria_titles.name: .latents_grid_criteria_titles
.latents_grid_criteria_titles.documentation: The criteria to draw, named by their display titles  A profile grid pairs each criterion's group and individual conventions and keeps a pair once where a single-level grid makes them equal (`.multilpa_distinct_criteria()`). The other grids name each column; a column equal to one requested before it (a regression grid's `bic_rows` on single-level data, where rows are the units) is drawn once.  @param x An enumeration grid. @param grid `.latents_grid_table(x)`. @param criterion The requested criterion columns. @return The columns to draw, named by title. @noRd

.latents_grid_smallest_shares.name: .latents_grid_smallest_shares
.latents_grid_smallest_shares.documentation: The share of the smallest class of every candidate, at each level  A profile, class or transition grid takes each fit's effective class counts over the units it classifies; a regression grid reads the `smallest_share` its table carries for its classes, and has no group-level share. A candidate with fewer than two classes at a level has none (`NA`).  @param x An enumeration grid offering the `"smallest"` view. @return A list of two numeric vectors, `individuals` and `groups`, one value   per candidate. @noRd

.latents_plot_former_grid.name: .latents_plot_former_grid
.latents_plot_former_grid.documentation: Draw a transition, family or regression grid through the shared views  The `plot()` methods of these grids keep their 0.9.21 call: `what` (or its former name `criterion`) names a criterion, matched as `match.arg()` matched `"bic"`, `"aic"` and `"bic_individual"`, so a unique abbreviation such as `"bic_i"` still works. Without either, the grid's summary of its default criteria is drawn, as [plot_enumeration()] draws it. Any other value is passed to [plot_enumeration()], which draws every view the grid offers. Arguments of [plot_enumeration()] and, for the tree, of [plot_tree()] given through `...` are passed on; any other is ignored with a `latents_unused_argument` warning, as 0.9.21 ignored it.  @param x A transition or group-class family grid. @param what The caller's `what`. @param what_given Whether the caller supplied `what`. @param criterion The caller's `criterion`, `NULL` when not given. @param main,subtitle Titles. @param extra `list(...)` as the method received it. @return A ggplot object, or a `latents_plots` list. @noRd

.growth_is_correlated.name: .growth_is_correlated
.growth_is_correlated.documentation: Whether a growth specification has correlated residuals @noRd

.growth_process_covariance.name: .growth_process_covariance
.growth_process_covariance.documentation: The residual-process covariance at a vector of times @param spec The growth specification. @param correlation The process parameters: `c(rate, sd)` or `c(sd)`. @param times One person's times. @return A square matrix. @noRd

.growth_dense_patterns.name: .growth_dense_patterns
.growth_dense_patterns.documentation: Persons grouped by their times and random design  Two persons with the same times and the same rows of the random design have the same marginal covariance in every class.  @param spec The growth specification, with `residual_times`. @param rows Each person's rows (a list). @return A list of patterns, each with `members`, `random` (the pattern's   random design) and `times`. @noRd

.growth_dense_covariances.name: .growth_dense_covariances
.growth_dense_covariances.documentation: Every class's marginal covariance on every pattern @return A list over classes of lists over patterns of matrices. @noRd

.growth_dense_terms.name: .growth_dense_terms
.growth_dense_terms.documentation: Class log densities and random-effect posteriors with correlated residuals  @return A list over classes with `log_density` (per person), `mean`   (persons by random effects: posterior means of b), `u` (each row's   V^-1 r, laid out by row), `inverse` (per pattern) and `covariance`   (random by random by patterns: posterior covariances). @noRd

.growth_dense_scores.name: .growth_dense_scores
.growth_dense_scores.documentation: Per-person scores of the growth mixture with correlated residuals  Within class k, d log f / d beta = X'V^-1 r and, for any coordinate of the covariance, d log f / d theta = (u' dV u - tr(V^-1 dV)) / 2 with u = V^-1 r. The derivative dV of every class's marginal covariance on every pattern is taken by central differences of the data-free map from the coordinates to V; the class terms are weighted by the person's posterior.  @return A units-by-parameters matrix, as `.growth_scores()`. @noRd

.growth_correlated_bounds.name: .growth_correlated_bounds
.growth_correlated_bounds.documentation: Bounds of the correlated growth coordinates  Variances are floored as in the uncorrelated engine: the residual variance, the process variance and each random-effect variance (through its log-Cholesky diagonal) at `min_variance`. The process rate is kept within a factor of 10^4 of the reciprocal median time gap, beyond which an autoregressive process cannot be told from white noise (fast) or from a random intercept (slow).  @return A list with `lower` and `upper`, named like the coordinates. @noRd

.growth_correlated_refit.name: .growth_correlated_refit
.growth_correlated_refit.documentation: Fit the correlated-residual model from a fit without the correlation  The model without correlated residuals, fitted from every start, places the classes; the full likelihood is then maximized within the bounds of `.growth_correlated_bounds()` by L-BFGS-B with the analytic scores, from that fit with half of each residual variance moved to the process (at two process rates), and finished by Newton steps on the free coordinates. A coordinate left on a bound is a variance at its floor: the fit is a boundary fit, warned about with `latents_random_boundary`, and judged converged on its other coordinates.  @param spec The correlated specification. @param uncorrelated The fit without correlated residuals. @param max_iter,tol Iteration bound and relative tolerance. @return The fit, with `spec`, `stats`, `params` and the likelihood updated. @noRd

.growth_correlated_newton.name: .growth_correlated_newton
.growth_correlated_newton.documentation: Newton steps on the correlated growth likelihood  The information is the central-difference Jacobian of the analytic total score, restricted to the coordinates not on a bound; each step is halved until the likelihood does not decrease, and clipped to the bounds. Converged when every free score times its standard error (the estimate's distance from the root in standard-error units) is below 1e-4, a hundredth of the displacement at which parameter_inference() warns.  @return A list with `params`, `iterations`, `converged`, `displacement`   and `at_bound` (the coordinates left on a bound). @noRd

.growth_residual_time.name: .growth_residual_time
.growth_residual_time.documentation: Resolve and check the residual time column of a correlated growth model  By default the first numeric variable of `random`, or else of the formula's predictors. @return The column name. @noRd

.growth_statistics.name: .growth_statistics
.growth_statistics.documentation: Per-person cross-products of the growth mixture model  @param spec The model specification, with `random_design`. @return A list of per-person arrays: `n` (rows), `yy`, `xy` (persons by   regression columns), `xx` (columns by columns by persons), `zy`   (persons by random effects), `zz` (random by random by persons) and   `xz` (columns by random by persons). Regression columns are the   class-specific design followed by the common design. @noRd

.growth_patterns.name: .growth_patterns
.growth_patterns.documentation: Group persons by their random-effect design  Two persons with the same Z'Z have the same posterior covariance and the same determinant in every class, so those are computed once per pattern.  @param stats Per-person cross-products. @return `stats` with `pattern` (each person's pattern index) and   `pattern_zz` (random by random by patterns). @noRd

.growth_coefficients.name: .growth_coefficients
.growth_coefficients.documentation: Regression coefficients of one class, class-specific then common @noRd

.growth_residuals.name: .growth_residuals
