.growth_residuals.documentation: Each person's residual cross-products for one class's coefficients  @param stats Output of `.growth_statistics()`. @param coefficients Regression coefficients (class-specific, then common). @return A list with `rr` (per person r'r) and `zr` (persons by random   effects: Z'r), where r = y - X beta. @noRd

.growth_direct_residuals.name: .growth_direct_residuals
.growth_direct_residuals.documentation: Direct residual cross-products after conditioning on random effects @param stats Per-person sufficient statistics with their raw fallback. @param coefficients Class-specific and common regression coefficients. @param means Per-person conditional random-effect means. @param rows Persons whose cross-product subtraction lost precision. @return Their residual sums of squares and fixed/random design products. @noRd

.growth_class_terms.name: .growth_class_terms
.growth_class_terms.documentation: One class's per-person log densities and random-effect posteriors  Persons who share a design (the same Z'Z, as in a balanced or near-balanced study) share the q x q factorization, which is done once per pattern; everything per person is then a vector operation.  @param stats Output of `.growth_statistics()`. @param coefficients The class's regression coefficients (class-specific,   then common). @param factor Lower Cholesky factor `L` of the class's random-effect   covariance. @param sigma2 The class's residual variance. @return A list with `log_density` (one per person), `mean` (persons by   random effects: posterior means of b_i), `covariance` (random by random   by patterns: posterior covariances) and the per-person `zr` and `rr`. @noRd

.growth_covariances.name: .growth_covariances
.growth_covariances.documentation: Random-effect covariance of every class from the parameter list @return A list of q x q matrices, one per class. @noRd

.growth_factor.name: .growth_factor
.growth_factor.documentation: A Cholesky factor that tolerates a covariance on its boundary @param covariance A symmetric positive semi-definite matrix. @return A lower-triangular `L` with `L %*% t(L)` equal to `covariance` up   to a jitter of 1e-12 times its scale on a singular direction. @noRd

.growth_expectation.name: .growth_expectation
.growth_expectation.documentation: E-step of the growth mixture model  @param spec The model specification. @param stats Per-person cross-products. @param params The parameter list. @return A list with `log_likelihood` (sampling-weighted when the fit is),   `tau` (persons by classes, weighted posteriors used by the M-step),   `posterior` (per-person posteriors, rows summing to one), `log_density`   (persons by classes), and the per-class random-effect posteriors   `means` and `covariances` (lists by class). @noRd

.growth_maximization.name: .growth_maximization
.growth_maximization.documentation: M-step of the growth mixture model (one conditional maximization each)  Regression coefficients given the variances, then residual variances, random-effect covariances and class shares: each step maximizes the expected complete-data log likelihood with the random effects as missing data (Laird and Ware 1982), so the likelihood never decreases.  @return The updated parameter list. @noRd

.growth_structure.name: .growth_structure
.growth_structure.documentation: The latent structure of a growth mixture: classes over persons  Each person's random effects are integrated out of their density, so the persons are the units the classes belong to. Without clusters every person has their own class, with membership logits of person covariates -- the `"observation"` structure with persons for rows. With `cluster`, persons are nested in clusters (students in schools) and a group class of the cluster shifts how probable each trajectory class is -- the `"two-level"` structure, whose independent units are the clusters: the multilevel growth mixture model (Asparouhov and Muthen 2008; Vermunt 2003).  @param spec The growth specification. @return A structure list (see kernel-structures.R). @noRd

.growth_structure_names.name: .growth_structure_names
.growth_structure_names.documentation: Names of a structure's free membership coefficients @noRd

.growth_em.name: .growth_em
.growth_em.documentation: EM for the growth mixture model from one start @return A list with `params`, `expectation`, `converged`, `iterations`,   `history` and `degenerate`. @noRd

.growth_names.name: .growth_names
.growth_names.documentation: Names of the estimation vector of a growth mixture model @noRd

.growth_pack.name: .growth_pack
.growth_pack.documentation: Pack a growth-mixture parameter list into the estimation vector @noRd

.growth_unpack.name: .growth_unpack
.growth_unpack.documentation: Unpack an estimation vector into a growth-mixture parameter list @param template A parameter list with the right shapes and names. @noRd

.growth_scores.name: .growth_scores
.growth_scores.documentation: Per-person scores of the growth mixture log likelihood  Analytic derivatives of each person's log likelihood on the estimation scale. Within class k, with r = y - X beta, V^-1 r = (r - Z m) / sigma^2 (m the posterior mean of b), so   d/d beta = X'(r - Z m) / sigma^2,   d/d sigma^2 = (|r - Z m|^2 / sigma^2 - n + tr(Z'Z S) / sigma^2) / (2 sigma^2),   d/d G = (q q' - Z'V^-1 Z) / 2, q = Z'V^-1 r, with Z'V^-1 Z = (Z'Z - Z'Z S Z'Z / sigma^2) / sigma^2 and S the posterior covariance. The mixture weights each class's derivative by the person's posterior.  @return A units-by-parameters matrix (unweighted by sampling weights): one   row per person, or per cluster for a multilevel growth mixture. @noRd

.growth_quasi_newton.name: .growth_quasi_newton
.growth_quasi_newton.documentation: Quasi-Newton finish of the growth mixture likelihood  EM is reliable from far away and slow near the maximum; L-BFGS-B with the analytic gradient finishes from EM's point. Variances keep their floors as bounds. Convergence is judged by the relative change of the log likelihood; L-BFGS-B's line-search stop (code 52) at the maximum is checked by one restart, as for transition fits.  @return A list with `params`, `converged` and `log_likelihood`. @noRd

.growth_inference.name: .growth_inference
.growth_inference.documentation: Covariance of the growth mixture estimates  The observed information is the numerical Jacobian of the analytic total score; `"robust"` is the person-level sandwich, the only valid choice under sampling weights.  @param fit A `latents_growth_mixture` fit. @param vcov_type `"observed"`, `"robust"` or `"opg"`. @return A list with `theta`, `vcov`, `vcov_type`, `information` and   `score_norm` (the largest absolute total score at the estimate). @noRd

.growth_resolve_inference.name: .growth_resolve_inference
.growth_resolve_inference.documentation: The inference of a growth fit at a requested covariance type @noRd

.growth_class_names.name: .growth_class_names
.growth_class_names.documentation: Class names of a growth fit @noRd

.growth_delta_table.name: .growth_delta_table
.growth_delta_table.documentation: Delta-method table of a transformation of the estimates  Intervals are formed on `scale` (`"identity"`, `"log"` for variances and standard deviations, `"atanh"` for correlations, `"logit"` for shares) and carried back, so they respect the parameter's range. @noRd

.growth_coefficient_table.name: .growth_coefficient_table
.growth_coefficient_table.documentation: Regression coefficients, one row per class and term @noRd

.growth_random_table.name: .growth_random_table
.growth_random_table.documentation: Random-effect variances, standard deviations and correlations, per class @noRd

.growth_class_is_degenerate.name: .growth_class_is_degenerate
.growth_class_is_degenerate.documentation: Whether class k's random-effect covariance is degenerate @noRd

.growth_class_table.name: .growth_class_table
.growth_class_table.documentation: Class sizes, residual standard deviations and classification quality @noRd

.growth_class_prior.name: .growth_class_prior
.growth_class_prior.documentation: Each person's prior class probabilities  The membership logits of their covariates; in a multilevel growth mixture, averaged over the group classes of their cluster with the cluster's group-class probabilities.  @param spec The growth specification. @param params A parameter list. @return A persons-by-classes matrix whose rows sum to one. @noRd

.growth_membership_table.name: .growth_membership_table
.growth_membership_table.documentation: Membership logits, one row per class (against class 1) and term @noRd

.growth_entropy.name: .growth_entropy
.growth_entropy.documentation: Relative entropy of the person posteriors @noRd

.growth_random_description.name: .growth_random_description
.growth_random_description.documentation: The random effects in words: "intercept", "intercept + time", "time" @noRd

.growth_entropy_sum.name: .growth_entropy_sum
.growth_entropy_sum.documentation: Classification entropy of the person posteriors (for ICL)  Unweighted, also for a sampling-weighted fit, as the profile and class models compute it; only the log likelihood is the weighted one. @noRd

.growth_cluster_fit_table.name: .growth_cluster_fit_table
.growth_cluster_fit_table.documentation: Fit of a multilevel growth mixture  The clusters are the independent units, so `bic` counts clusters, as for the two-level regression mixture and as Lukociene, Varriale and Vermunt (2010) recommend for choosing the number of group classes; `bic_persons` and `bic_rows` count persons and observations instead. @noRd

.growth_group_class_table.name: .growth_group_class_table
.growth_group_class_table.documentation: Group classes of a multilevel growth mixture: each group class's share of the clusters and its trajectory-class probabilities @noRd

.growth_cluster_table.name: .growth_cluster_table
.growth_cluster_table.documentation: Each cluster's group-class posteriors and modal group class @noRd

.growth_assignment_table.name: .growth_assignment_table
.growth_assignment_table.documentation: Each person's posterior class probabilities and modal class @noRd

.growth_random_effects_table.name: .growth_random_effects_table
.growth_random_effects_table.documentation: Each person's predicted random effects (posterior means, modal class) @noRd

.growth_time_variable.name: .growth_time_variable
.growth_time_variable.documentation: The variable trajectories are drawn along  The caller's choice, or the first numeric variable of `random` (the time scale of a random slope), or else the first numeric predictor. @noRd

.growth_design.name: .growth_design
.growth_design.documentation: Regression design of new rows, in the fitted column order @noRd

.growth_trajectory_table.name: .growth_trajectory_table
.growth_trajectory_table.documentation: Mean trajectory of every class over a time grid, with Wald bands  Other predictors are held at their mean (numeric) or first level. @noRd

.growth_individual_table.name: .growth_individual_table
.growth_individual_table.documentation: Every observation with its class trajectory and its person's own curve  `class_mean` is the modal class's fixed trajectory; `predicted` adds the person's predicted random effects (the conditional, empirical Bayes fit). @noRd

.growth_present.name: .growth_present
.growth_present.documentation: Attach the printed layout of a growth table  The data are untouched; this only chooses the title, columns, labels and number formats `print()` uses. @noRd

confint.latents_growth_mixture.name: confint.latents_growth_mixture
confint.latents_growth_mixture.documentation: @noRd @param parm Parameter names or positions; all by default. @export

.growth_natural_parameters.name: .growth_natural_parameters
.growth_natural_parameters.documentation: The natural parameters of a growth fit, each as a function of the parameters  Coefficients and membership logits are coordinates of the estimation vector; residual standard deviations, random-effect variances, standard deviations and correlations, and class shares are transformations of it. Each row carries the scale its Wald interval is formed on, and whether a Wald test of zero is meaningful (not for a variance, whose zero is a bound).  @param x A `latents_growth_mixture` fit. @return A list with `labels` (a data frame: `block`, `class`, `term`),   `scales`, `tested` and `values`, a function of a parameter list and its   specification returning every natural parameter in row order. @noRd

.growth_permute_params.name: .growth_permute_params
.growth_permute_params.documentation: Reorder a growth fit's classes  Class-specific coefficients, residual variances, random-effect covariances (or proportional scales) and membership logits follow the classes; the membership logits are rebased on the new first class.  @param spec The growth specification. @param params A parameter list. @param order An integer vector: new class `k` is old class `order[k]`. @return The reordered parameter list. @noRd

.growth_align_refit.name: .growth_align_refit
.growth_align_refit.documentation: Match a refit's classes to the original fit's  The refit classifies the original persons, and its classes are matched to the original's by their posterior memberships of those persons, which identifies a class by whom it contains rather than by its trajectory alone.  @param x The original fit. @param refit A fit to a resample. @return The refit's parameters in the original class order. @noRd

.growth_match_classes.name: .growth_match_classes
.growth_match_classes.documentation: The order that matches a refit's classes to the original fit's @param x The original fit. @param refit Another fit of the same model. @return A list with `order` (new class `k` is the refit's class   `order[k]`) and `posterior`, the refit's posteriors of the original   persons in its own labels. @noRd

.growth_refit_arguments.name: .growth_refit_arguments
.growth_refit_arguments.documentation: The mixture_regression() arguments that refit a growth fit as it was fitted @param x A `latents_growth_mixture` fit. @param weights The weight column of the resampling data, or `NULL`. @return A named list, without `data` and the start and convergence controls. @noRd

.growth_bootstrap_inference.name: .growth_bootstrap_inference
.growth_bootstrap_inference.documentation: Person bootstrap inference for a growth fit  Persons are drawn with replacement (a person drawn twice is two persons), each resample is refitted from fresh starts, and its classes are matched to the original's before the natural parameters are read. A refit's start failures, degenerate starts and boundary variances are expected and muffled; one that does not converge is dropped with its reason.  @return The bootstrap table and its attributes. @noRd

parameter_inference.latents_growth_mixtu.name: parameter_inference.latents_growth_mixture
parameter_inference.latents_growth_mixtu.documentation: @details For a growth mixture ([mixture_regression()] with `random`), the   table has one row per natural parameter: `block` (`"coefficient"`,   `"membership"` and, for a multilevel growth mixture,   `"group_membership"`, `"residual_sd"`, `"random_variance"`,   `"random_sd"`, `"random_correlation"`, `"share"`), `class` (`"all"` for   a quantity shared by every class), `term`, `estimate`, `standard_error`,   `statistic`, `p_value`, `p_adjusted`, `conf_low` and `conf_high`. Wald   rows use the fit's covariance (`vcov_type`) with the delta method;   intervals of standard deviations and variances are formed on the log   scale, of correlations on the Fisher scale and of shares on the logit   scale, and only coefficients and logits are tested against zero.   `method = "bootstrap"` resamples persons, refits each resample from   `n_starts` starts and matches its classes to the original by their   posterior memberships of the original persons; it is refused for a   multilevel growth mixture (`latents_unsupported_inference`). In a   simulation of 1000 datasets per design, Wald intervals covered   0.936-0.965 with well-separated classes and 0.885-0.943 with weakly   separated ones, whose standard errors were 6-30% too small   (validation/GROWTH_SIMULATION.md in the source repository); the   bootstrap is preferable for weakly separated classes. A class   whose random-effect covariance is degenerate raises   `latents_boundary_fit` under `boundary = "error"`; under `"fix"` its   random-effect rows have no standard error or interval. `data`, when   given, must be the fitted data; `step` is not used (the information is   the derivative of the analytic score). @rdname parameter_inference @export

.growth_class_key.name: .growth_class_key
.growth_class_key.documentation: One row per class: share, display rank, label, colour, line type and shape @noRd

.growth_scales.name: .growth_scales
.growth_scales.documentation: Manual colour, fill, line-type and shape scales for the class key @noRd

.growth_observed_means.name: .growth_observed_means
.growth_observed_means.documentation: Posterior-weighted observed means of every class at each observed time  Drawn only when there are at most 30 distinct times; a mean needs at least one person's worth of posterior weight. @noRd

.growth_spread.name: .growth_spread
.growth_spread.documentation: Where `spread` of each class's persons' trajectories lie  From the random effects alone: mean +- z sqrt(z(t)' G z(t)), with other random-effect variables at their typical values. @noRd

.growth_new_spec.name: .growth_new_spec
.growth_new_spec.documentation: Rebuild a growth specification on new persons  The fitted terms, factor levels and membership codings evaluate `newdata`, so its design columns follow the fitted order. Every person in `newdata` is a new person, and in a multilevel growth mixture every cluster is a new cluster, classified from its own persons.  @param object A `latents_growth_mixture` fit. @param newdata A data frame with the predictors, `id` (and `cluster`). @param with_response Whether the outcome must be present. @return A growth specification for the engine, without sampling weights. @noRd

.growth_class_means.name: .growth_class_means
.growth_class_means.documentation: Each row's mean under every class (persons' random effects at zero) @return A rows-by-classes matrix. @noRd

.growth_draw.name: .growth_draw
.growth_draw.documentation: One simulated outcome vector from a growth mixture fit  Each person's class is drawn from their membership probabilities (in a multilevel growth mixture, given their cluster's group class, drawn first), their random effects from that class's covariance, and their outcomes around the class trajectory plus random effects with the class's residual variance, on the fitted design (persons, times and covariates kept). @param object A `latents_growth_mixture` fit. @return A numeric vector, one value per fitted row, in the fitted order. @noRd

.growth_check_arguments.name: .growth_check_arguments
.growth_check_arguments.documentation: Refuse growth mixture requests the model does not define @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises `latents_bad_argument` otherwise. @noRd

.growth_cluster_spec.name: .growth_cluster_spec
.growth_cluster_spec.documentation: The cluster level of a multilevel growth mixture  Every person must sit in one cluster. The group-class logits read cluster-level covariates (`group_membership`, constant within clusters); the trajectory-class logits have one intercept per group class and the person covariates' slopes (`membership`, constant within persons), shared across group classes, as in the two-level regression mixture.  @param cluster_values The cluster of every kept row. @param group_index The person of every kept row. @param row_membership The row-level person membership design (with its   intercept). @param row_group_membership The row-level cluster membership design. @param n_group_classes Number of group classes. @param check_count Whether to require more clusters than group classes,   as fitting does; prediction for a few new clusters does not. @return A list of cluster fields for the specification: `cluster_index`   (each person's cluster), `cluster_levels`, `n_clusters`,   `n_cluster_classes`, `cluster_v`, `cluster_w` and   `cluster_intercept_only`. @noRd

.growth_start.name: .growth_start
.growth_start.documentation: Starting values of the growth mixture model from a latent class growth fit  The class trajectories, class shares and memberships come from the fit without random effects. The random-effect covariance starts from the spread of per-person least-squares deviations from the class trajectory, halved, and the residual variance from half the class residual variance, because without random effects the residual absorbs all individual variation.  @param spec The model specification. @param stats Per-person cross-products. @param result One EM result of the model without random effects. @param first Whether this is the first start, which splits the clusters of   a multilevel growth mixture by their composition rather than at random. @return A growth-mixture parameter list. @noRd

.growth_two_level_start.name: .growth_two_level_start
.growth_two_level_start.documentation: Starting membership logits of a multilevel growth mixture  The first start splits the clusters into group classes by how much of the first class their persons hold (quantile groups), since group classes exist to differ in that composition; every other start splits them at random. Each group class's trajectory-class logits start from the class shares of its clusters' persons under the start's posteriors, and the covariate slopes at zero. A start with identical group classes would be a fixed point of EM, which the split avoids.  @param spec The growth specification, with its cluster fields. @param params Starting parameters with person-level `gamma`. @param posterior Persons-by-classes starting posteriors. @param first Whether to split by composition. @return `params` with `delta` and `class_logits` in place of `gamma`. @noRd

.growth_trajectory_seed.name: .growth_trajectory_seed
.growth_trajectory_seed.documentation: A start from the persons' own trajectories  Each person's least-squares coefficients on the class-specific design (the pooled ones for a person with too few observations), standardized and grouped by Ward's method -- deterministic, as the first start of the profile models is -- give the classes; one M-step of the model without random effects from those classes gives the trajectories.  @param spec The growth specification. @return A seed as `.mixture_run_starts()` returns them: `params` and an   `expectation` with the persons' (softened) class weights `group_tau`. @noRd

.growth_fit.name: .growth_fit
.growth_fit.documentation: Fit the growth mixture model from several starts  Every start of the model without random effects becomes a start here; starts are screened for 50 iterations and the better half run to convergence, as for `mixture_regression()`.  @return The fitted `latents_growth_mixture` object (without inference). @noRd

.growth_select.name: .growth_select
.growth_select.documentation: Choose among growth-mixture starts and assemble the fit @noRd

.growth_degenerate_covariances.name: .growth_degenerate_covariances
.growth_degenerate_covariances.documentation: Classes whose random-effect covariance is on its boundary  A variance at its floor, a correlation within 0.005 of +-1, or a smallest eigenvalue below 1e-6 of the largest: the likelihood is flat there and Wald errors of that covariance are not meaningful.  @return The names of the degenerate classes (`"all classes"` when one   shared matrix is degenerate); empty when none is. @noRd

.growth_order_classes.name: .growth_order_classes
.growth_order_classes.documentation: Order classes by size (then first coefficient), and group classes by composition, and relabel every block @noRd

.growth_count_parameters.name: .growth_count_parameters
.growth_count_parameters.documentation: Number of free parameters of the growth mixture model @noRd

.inference_score_information.name: .inference_score_information
.inference_score_information.documentation: Observed information by differences of an analytic score  Differentiates the total score numerically, each column with its own step, and returns minus the symmetrized Jacobian. The analytic score makes the truncation error that of the first derivative, not of a second difference of the likelihood.  @param total_score A function of a packed vector returning the summed   score. @param theta The packed estimate (named). @param step Relative step. @param scheme `"central"` (two points) or `"five_point"` (fourth order). @param h_rule `"max1"`, `"plus1"` or `"absolute"`. @return A symmetric matrix named by `theta`. @noRd

.inference_positive_definite.name: .inference_positive_definite
.inference_positive_definite.documentation: Refuse, or flag, an information matrix that is not positive definite  @param information A symmetric matrix. @param rule `"min_le_eps_max"`: refuse when the smallest eigenvalue is at   most 1e-10 times the largest; `"ratio_le_eps"`: refuse when their ratio   is at most 1e-10 (or not finite), and when the smallest is not positive;   `"min_le_eps_maxabs"`: flag when the smallest is at most 1e-10 times the   largest absolute eigenvalue. @param message The refusal's message; `"%.3g"` in it receives the ratio. @return `TRUE` when the matrix may be inverted. A failed `"min_le_eps_max"`   or `"ratio_le_eps"` check raises `latents_singular_information`; a failed   `"min_le_eps_maxabs"` check returns `FALSE`, for the caller to warn. @noRd

.inference_invert.name: .inference_invert
.inference_invert.documentation: Inverse of a positive definite information matrix  The Cholesky inverse, which is symmetric by construction, after the engine's positive-definiteness check.  @inheritParams .inference_positive_definite @return The inverse, without dimnames (the caller names it). @noRd

.inference_require_rank.name: .inference_require_rank
.inference_require_rank.documentation: Refuse a robust or OPG covariance the unit scores cannot support  The cross-product of the unit scores has the rank of the scores; with fewer independent units than parameters it is singular, and a sandwich built on it is not a covariance.  @param scores Units by parameters. @param message The refusal; `%d` placeholders receive the number of   units, the rank and the number of parameters, in that order, when   `formatted` is `TRUE`. @param formatted Whether `message` is an `sprintf()` format. @param extra Further `sprintf()` arguments after the three counts. @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises `latents_too_few_groups`. @noRd

.multilpa_inference_groups.name: .multilpa_inference_groups
.multilpa_inference_groups.documentation: Independent groups contributing to the fitted likelihood  Empty measurement units do not supply independent estimating equations. Preserve the explicit legacy empty-unit convention, but a unit with zero sampling weight never contributes under either convention. Score matrices keep all their rows for alignment with fitted groups; only validity counts and the finite-sample correction use this selection. @param object A fit with `n_groups`, `group_index` and optional `informative`   and `sampling_weights` entries. @param observed_only Require observed measurement even under the legacy   empty-unit counting convention. Used for validity and rank checks; CR1   retains the explicitly requested legacy convention. @return A logical vector in fitted-group order. @noRd

.inference_cluster_factor.name: .inference_cluster_factor
.inference_cluster_factor.documentation: Small-sample factor of a cluster-robust variance  `G / (G - 1)` for `G` independent units: the CR1 correction, which is the default of `sandwich::vcovCL()` (Cameron and Miller, 2015). Without it the variance (CR0) is biased downward when there are few units.  @param n_units Number of independent units (groups, or rows when each row   is its own unit). @return A single number above 1. @noRd

.inference_sandwich.name: .inference_sandwich
.inference_sandwich.documentation: Robust (sandwich) covariance  `bread %*% meat %*% bread`, left to right, with the meat the cross-product of the unit scores (clustered scores where units are clustered), scaled by the CR1 factor `G / (G - 1)`.  @param bread The inverse information. @param meat `crossprod()` of the unit scores. @param n_units Number of units whose scores form `meat`. @return The sandwich. @noRd

.inference_delta_covariance.name: .inference_delta_covariance
.inference_delta_covariance.documentation: Delta-method covariance of derived quantities  `J V J'`, the covariance of the derived quantities to first order, for the engines that report the matrix rather than its diagonal alone.  @param jacobian Derived quantities by packed parameters. @param covariance Covariance of the packed parameters. @return The covariance matrix of the derived quantities. @noRd

.inference_delta_se.name: .inference_delta_se
.inference_delta_se.documentation: Delta-method standard errors of derived quantities  @param jacobian Derived quantities by packed parameters. @param covariance Covariance of the packed parameters. @param form `"quadratic"`, the diagonal of `J V J'`, or `"rowsums"`,   `rowSums((J V) * J)`; the same numbers up to the last bits, and each   engine keeps the one it has always reported. @return Standard errors, `sqrt(max(variance, 0))`. @noRd

.inference_numeric_jacobian.name: .inference_numeric_jacobian
.inference_numeric_jacobian.documentation: Numerical Jacobian of a transformation by central differences  @param transform A function of the packed vector. @param theta The packed estimate. @param step Relative step: `h = step * (1 + |theta_j|)`. @return A matrix, derived quantities by packed parameters. @noRd

.inference_simplex_jacobian.name: .inference_simplex_jacobian
.inference_simplex_jacobian.documentation: Derivative of a probability vector with respect to its free logits  A softmax `p` has derivative `diag(p) - p p'` with respect to all its logits; the reference category's logit is fixed at zero, so its column is dropped -- the last category's for the profile models, the first class's for the additive families.  @param probabilities A probability vector. @param reference `"last"` or `"first"`: whose column is dropped. @return A `length(p)` by `length(p) - 1` matrix. @noRd

.inference_critical.name: .inference_critical
.inference_critical.documentation: The two-sided normal critical value @param level Confidence level. @param form `"upper"`, `qnorm((1 + level) / 2)`, or `"one_minus"`,   `qnorm(1 - (1 - level) / 2)`: equal in exact arithmetic, and each engine   keeps the spelling its published intervals used. @return A single number. @noRd

.inference_wald.name: .inference_wald
.inference_wald.documentation: Wald columns from estimates and standard errors  The symmetric interval, the z statistic and its two-sided p value.  @param estimate Estimates. @param std_error Their standard errors. @param level Confidence level. @param form The critical value's form, see `.inference_critical()`. @return A data frame: `estimate`, `std_error`, `statistic`, `p_value`,   `conf_low`, `conf_high`. @noRd

.latents_memo.name: .latents_memo
.latents_memo.documentation: Reuse an expensive deterministic result whose inputs are identical  Entries are compared with `identical()` on the whole key, so any change to a fit, its data or an argument computes the result anew; the same fit object passed again is recognised at once. Only values are stored: a computation that fails is not, and fails again the next time. The most recently used `size` entries are kept. @param store The name of the store in `.latents_cache`. @param key A list of everything the result depends on. @param compute A function of no arguments that computes the result. @param size The number of entries kept. @return The result. @noRd

.multilpa_observed_hessian.name: .multilpa_observed_hessian
.multilpa_observed_hessian.documentation: Differentiate the observed information and check that it is usable  Curvature is tested after scaling, so that indicators on different units do not by themselves make an identified model look singular. The Hessian takes two score evaluations over all the data per parameter, which makes it the slowest step of Wald inference; with a `cache_key` it is computed once per session for those inputs, so a model plotted with intervals again and again (or tabulated) does not differentiate its likelihood each time.  @param cache_key `NULL`, or a list of everything the objective and the   gradient depend on (see `.latents_memo()`). @return A list with the `scaled` and `natural` Hessians, the scaled   `condition_ratio`, and the `inverse` of the scaled Hessian. @noRd

.multilpa_opg_inverse.name: .multilpa_opg_inverse
.multilpa_opg_inverse.documentation: Invert the outer product of the group scores  The outer-product-of-gradients (BHHH) estimate of the information: the cross-product of the per-group scores, which estimates the information by the variance of the score rather than by the curvature of the likelihood. It is what `glca` reports.  @param cross The (scaled) cross-product of the group scores. @return Its inverse, or `latents_singular_information` when it has none. @noRd

.multilpa_cross_product.name: .multilpa_cross_product
.multilpa_cross_product.documentation: Robust cross-product matrix from per-group scores @param scores Groups-by-parameters score matrix. @return The summed outer product of the group scores. @noRd

.multilpa_require_clusters.name: .multilpa_require_clusters
.multilpa_require_clusters.documentation: Refuse a cluster-robust variance too few independent units can support  The meat of a cluster-robust sandwich is the sum of one outer product per independent unit, formed from that unit's summed estimating-equation contributions. Those contributions sum to zero across units at the estimate, because that sum *is* the stationarity condition the estimate solves. The meat therefore has rank at most `n_units - 1`, whatever the data: with one unit it is exactly zero, and with `n_units <= n_quantities` it is singular, so some contrast among the reported quantities is handed a variance of exactly zero. Neither is a small standard error; both are refused.  The rule this enforces, `n_units > n_quantities`, is the same one [parameter_inference()] applies to a robust model vcov through `.multilpa_check_regularity()`, so every robust path in the package asks for as many independent units as the covariance it reports has dimensions, plus one for the constraint that the contributions sum to zero.  @param n_units Number of independent units the contributions were summed   within: groups for a clustered variance, observations for an unclustered   one. @param n_quantities Number of quantities whose covariance is being reported. @param what A noun phrase naming that covariance, opening the message. @param unit What one independent unit is called in the message. @param alternative A sentence naming a legitimate non-clustered alternative,   or `NULL` when there is none. @return `invisible(TRUE)` when the rule holds. Otherwise raises   `latents_too_few_groups`. @references Cameron, A. C., & Miller, D. L. (2015). A practitioner's guide   to cluster-robust inference. *Journal of Human Resources*, 50, 317--372. @noRd

.multilpa_wald_bounds.name: .multilpa_wald_bounds
.multilpa_wald_bounds.documentation: Wald intervals on the scale where each parameter is unbounded  A symmetric interval around a probability of 0.98 with a standard error of 0.015 runs past one, and one around a small variance runs below zero: neither is a set of values the parameter can take. Each interval is formed where the parameter is unbounded and mapped back -- the logit of a probability, the log of a variance -- by the delta method, with the same standard error. It stays inside the parameter's range and becomes asymmetric near a bound, as the sampling distribution does. Every other parameter keeps the symmetric interval. @param estimate,standard_error Numeric vectors. @param kind `"probability"`, `"positive"` or anything else, per row. @param critical The normal quantile for the level. @return A list with `low` and `high`. @noRd

.multilpa_interval_kind.name: .multilpa_interval_kind
.multilpa_interval_kind.documentation: Which scale a parameter's interval is formed on @param parameter,term The tidy label columns. @param continuous The continuous indicator names. @return `"probability"`, `"positive"` or `"real"`, per row. @noRd

.multilpa_adjust_p.name: .multilpa_adjust_p
.multilpa_adjust_p.documentation: Add the adjusted p-value column an inference table reports  The family is the tests the table actually carries: a bounded parameter has no test, is `NA` in `p_value`, and must not inflate the correction for the parameters that do.  @param result An inference table carrying `statistic` and `p_value`. @param adjust One of `.multilpa_p_adjust_methods`. @return `result` with `p_adjusted` inserted after `p_value` and the   `adjust` attribute recorded. @noRd

.multilpa_parameter_names.name: .multilpa_parameter_names
.multilpa_parameter_names.documentation: Serialise a tidy parameter decomposition into one name per parameter  Every class in this package decomposes a parameter the same way -- `level`, `parameter`, `outcome`, `term` -- and those four columns are what [parameter_inference()] reports. A `coef()` name is that decomposition written on one line, dot separated and in that order, so a name can always be read back into the columns and two fits of different families spell the same concept the same way. `level`, `parameter` and `outcome` never contain a dot, so the first three separators are unambiguous and everything after the third is the term. A term that does not apply -- a group-class probability has no term -- is left off rather than spelled `NA`.  @param labels A data frame with `level`, `parameter`, `outcome` and `term`. @return A character vector, one name per row of `labels`. @noRd

.multilpa_coefficient_labels.name: .multilpa_coefficient_labels
.multilpa_coefficient_labels.documentation: The tidy decomposition of every coefficient of a fitted mixture @param object A fitted `multilpa` model. @param scale Natural estimates or unconstrained fitting coordinates. @return A data frame with `level`, `outcome`, `term` and `parameter`, one row   per coefficient, in the order `.multilpa_coefficients()` returns them. @noRd

.multilpa_coefficients.name: .multilpa_coefficients
.multilpa_coefficients.documentation: Parameterize a fitted mixture @param object A fitted `multilpa` model. @param scale Natural estimates or unconstrained fitting coordinates. @return A named numeric parameter vector, named as   `.multilpa_parameter_names()` spells them. @noRd

.multilpa_coefficients_raw.name: .multilpa_coefficients_raw
.multilpa_coefficients_raw.documentation: Parameterize a fitted mixture, in the internal generation grammar  The generated `kind[index,...]` labels are an implementation detail: they are compact to build alongside the values and they are parsed straight back into tidy columns by `.multilpa_tidy_labels()`. Nothing user facing sees them; `.multilpa_coefficients()` renames them before they leave the package.  @param object A fitted `multilpa` model. @param scale Natural estimates or unconstrained fitting coordinates. @return A named numeric parameter vector. @noRd

.multilpa_response_coordinates.name: .multilpa_response_coordinates
.multilpa_response_coordinates.documentation: Encode categorical response probabilities  Natural coordinates are the probabilities themselves; unconstrained coordinates are multinomial logits against each indicator's last category, which is the same simplex device the mixing probabilities already use.  @param object A fitted `multilpa` model. @param scale `"natural"` or `"unconstrained"`. @return A named numeric vector, empty when no indicator is categorical. @noRd

.multilpa_response_decode.name: .multilpa_response_decode
.multilpa_response_decode.documentation: Rebuild response probabilities from multinomial logits @param theta Unconstrained values for the categorical block, in encode order. @param object The fit supplying the shapes and names. @return A named list of profiles-by-categories probability matrices. @noRd

.multilpa_response_width.name: .multilpa_response_width
.multilpa_response_width.documentation: How many free parameters the categorical block contributes @param object A fitted `multilpa` model. @return A single integer, zero when no indicator is categorical. @noRd

.multilpa_covariance_coordinates.name: .multilpa_covariance_coordinates
.multilpa_covariance_coordinates.documentation: Encode unrestricted Gaussian covariance matrices @param object A fitted full-covariance model. @param scale Natural covariance or log-Cholesky coordinates. @return A named vector of nonredundant covariance parameters. @noRd

.multilpa_coordinate_widths.name: .multilpa_coordinate_widths
.multilpa_coordinate_widths.documentation: Widths of the coefficient blocks, in the order they are encoded  `.multilpa_coefficients_raw()` lays a fit out as means, spread, categorical responses, profile mixing and group mixing, in that order, on either scale. Counting those widths arithmetically -- rather than encoding the fit and measuring the result -- is what lets the free-coordinate map below be built without a Cholesky factorisation on every likelihood evaluation.  @param object A fitted `multilpa` model. @param scale `"natural"` or `"unconstrained"`. @return A named numeric vector with `means`, `variances`,   `response_probabilities`, `profile` and `group`, whose sum is the length of   `.multilpa_coefficients()` on that scale. @noRd

.multilpa_free_index.name: .multilpa_free_index
.multilpa_free_index.documentation: The coordinates a fit actually estimates  A `fixed` fit holds whole measurement blocks at the values `start` supplied, so those coordinates are constants of the likelihood, not parameters. They must still enter the likelihood -- the model is conditional on them, not without them -- but they carry no score, no row of the information matrix and no row of the inference table. Because `fixed` names whole blocks and the blocks are contiguous in the encoding, the free set is simply the complement of the held ranges; there is no partially-held block whose free remainder would need a separate identification argument.  @param object A fitted `multilpa` model. @param scale `"natural"` or `"unconstrained"`. @return An integer vector of positions into `.multilpa_coefficients()` on that   scale, ascending, naming the coordinates this fit estimated. @noRd

.multilpa_restore_held.name: .multilpa_restore_held
.multilpa_restore_held.documentation: Restore the held coordinates around a free parameter vector  The returned closure scatters free values into a template taken from the fit itself, so a held block enters every likelihood, score and Hessian evaluation at exactly the value it was held at.  @param template Full-length unconstrained coordinates of the fit whose held   values are to be restored; the centred fit, when the likelihood is   evaluated on centred indicators. @param free Positions of the free coordinates within `template`. @return A function of the free values returning the full coordinate vector. @noRd

.multilpa_decode.name: .multilpa_decode
.multilpa_decode.documentation: Decode unconstrained mixture coordinates @param theta Parameter vector with log variances and baseline-category   logits, carrying every coordinate of the model including any held block. @param object A fitted model defining the parameter dimensions. @return The four parameter blocks used by the expectation step. @noRd

.multilpa_response_scores.name: .multilpa_response_scores
.multilpa_response_scores.documentation: Score contributions of the categorical response probabilities  For one indicator the complete-data score of a multinomial logit is the posterior-weighted difference between the category actually observed and the probability the model gives it, exactly as for the mixing weights. Missing codes contribute nothing.  @param codes Integer code matrix, one column per categorical indicator. @param posteriors Individual profile posteriors. @param blocks The fitted response probabilities, one matrix per indicator. @param group_index Group indices, or `NULL` for a pooled total. @return A matrix with one row per group (or one row overall) and one column   per free response parameter, in `.multilpa_coefficients()` order. @noRd

.multilpa_score.name: .multilpa_score
.multilpa_score.documentation: Differentiate the observed mixture likelihood @param theta Unconstrained parameter vector. @param x Centered numeric indicator matrix, possibly containing NA. @param object Fitted model defining dimensions and groups. @return The gradient of the negative observed-data log likelihood. @noRd

.multilpa_full_measurement_score.name: .multilpa_full_measurement_score
.multilpa_full_measurement_score.documentation: Gaussian scores in log-Cholesky coordinates @param parameters Decoded Gaussian and mixing parameters. @param expectation Nested expectation step including Gaussian moments. @param object A fitted full-covariance model. @return Mean and log-Cholesky score vectors. @noRd

.multilpa_inference_jacobian.name: .multilpa_inference_jacobian
.multilpa_inference_jacobian.documentation: Delta-method Jacobian for mixture parameters @param object A fitted model. @return Jacobian mapping unconstrained to natural coefficients. @noRd

parameter_inference.name: parameter_inference
parameter_inference.documentation: Standard errors, confidence intervals and tests for model parameters  Returns a table of the estimated parameters of a fitted model with their standard errors, Wald tests and confidence intervals. By default the standard errors are maximum-likelihood errors from the inverse observed information, with delta-method Wald intervals; `method = "bootstrap"` resamples groups instead. The estimates are local and asymptotic, conditional on the selected numbers of classes, and do not account for model selection. Boundary solutions and unidentified Hessians are refused by the Wald path.  @param x A converged `multilpa` fit with inactive variance bounds. @param data Optional data frame the model was fitted to. When omitted it is   rebuilt from the indicators, identifiers and occasions the fit stores. A   supplied frame is checked exactly against the stored indicators and   identifiers; for an older fit without stored indicators, the likelihood   gives a weaker consistency check. @param level Confidence level, strictly between zero and one. Default   `0.95`. @param step Positive finite-difference step for the analytic score   derivative. Default `1e-4`. @param vcov_type Covariance estimator for the Wald path.   `"observed"` (default) inverts the observed information.   `"robust"` returns the Huber-White sandwich `A^-1 B A^-1`, where `B` is   the outer product of the per-group scores, multiplied by the CR1   small-sample factor `G / (G - 1)` for `G` groups (the default of   `sandwich::vcovCL()`, applied to every robust standard error in the   package). Mplus's MLR applies no such factor, so these errors are   `sqrt(G / (G - 1))` times Mplus's. Groups are the independent units:   robust errors relax the assumption that the within-group model is   correctly specified, not the assumption that groups are independent.   `"opg"` inverts the outer product of the per-group scores (the BHHH   estimator), as `glca` reports; it agrees with `"observed"` in large   samples and can differ in small ones, where `"observed"` is usually more   reliable. `"robust"` and `"opg"` need more groups than parameters. For a   fit with sampling weights the default is `"robust"`, and any other value   raises `latents_unsupported_weights`. `vcov_type` and `step` are not used   by `method = "bootstrap"`. @param adjust Multiplicity correction applied to `p_value` to give   `p_adjusted`: `"none"` (default) or one of the [stats::p.adjust()]   methods. The method applied is stored in the `adjust` attribute. The   correction is taken over the tests the table reports; bounded parameters   carry no test and are not counted. @param method `"wald"` (default) inverts the observed information in the   estimation coordinates; it is available for all fourteen covariance   structures. EEI, VVI, EEE and VVV are estimated in log variances or   log-Cholesky coordinates; the ten structures that constrain volume,   shape or orientation across profiles are estimated in log volumes, log   shapes with the determinant-one constraint built into the coordinates,   and Cayley-transform orientations (or, for VEE and EVV, determinant-one   log-Cholesky factors), so the information has one row per free   parameter. The reported variances and covariances are obtained from   these coordinates by the delta method, and their natural-scale   covariance is singular, as for the class probabilities. `"bootstrap"`   resamples groups with replacement, refits within the same covariance   structure, realigns each refit's labels, and reports the percentile   interval and the standard deviation of the replicates; it is also   available for all fourteen structures and assumes independent groups, as   `vcov_type = "robust"` does. @param iter Number of resamples for `method = "bootstrap"`, at least two.   Default `199`; a 95% percentile interval is more stable with 999 or more. @param n_starts,max_iter,tol Passed to each bootstrap refit, as in   [multilpa()]. @param seed Optional seed for the resampling: a whole number accepted by   `set.seed()`; any other value raises `latents_bad_argument` on either   path. The Wald path uses no random numbers. The caller's random state is   restored on exit. @param boundary Handling of categorical response probabilities at their   lower bound, `min_probability`, where the information is singular.   `"error"` (default) raises `latents_boundary_fit`. `"fix"` holds those   probabilities at the bound and reports every other parameter conditional   on them, as Mplus does; the held probabilities are omitted from the table   (or, for a covariate fit, reported with `NA` standard errors) and named in   the `fixed_at_bound` attribute. @return A base `data.frame` with one row per reported parameter and the   columns `level` (`"measurement"`, `"profile"` or `"group"`), `outcome`,   `term`, `parameter`, `estimate`, `standard_error`, `statistic`, `p_value`,   `p_adjusted`, `conf_low` and `conf_high`. Estimates are on the natural   scale (variances in their own units, probabilities as probabilities). A   parameter whose null value lies on the boundary of its space (a variance,   a probability, a covariance diagonal) has `NA` `statistic`, `p_value` and   `p_adjusted`, but still has an interval. All class probabilities are   reported; their sum constraints make the natural covariance singular.   Wald intervals for probabilities are formed on the logit scale and for   variances (and covariance diagonals) on the log scale, then   back-transformed, so they stay within the parameter's range; every other   interval is `estimate +/- z * standard_error`. `confint()` returns the   same intervals. A probability at or below 1e-6 is treated as on its bound   (refused, or held by `boundary = "fix"`).    A fit made with `fixed` reports only the parameters it estimated: a held   measurement block contributes no row to the table or to the information   matrix. The table has one row per estimated natural coefficient:   `n_parameters` rows plus one for each set of probabilities whose   reference category the estimation scale drops. Standard errors,   intervals and p-values are conditional on the held measurement solution   and do not include its uncertainty (see [fit_staged()]). For a   [fit_staged()] result, `method = "bootstrap"` refits both stages in each   resample, so the table includes the measurement parameters and that   uncertainty is propagated (attribute `stages_resampled` is 2).    With `method = "bootstrap"` the table has the same columns and rows;   `estimate` is the fitted value, `standard_error` the standard deviation   of the replicates and `conf_low`/`conf_high` the percentile interval.   `statistic`, `p_value` and `p_adjusted` are `NA`. Its attributes are   `covariance` (the covariance of the replicates, returned by `vcov()`),   `level`, `method`, `iter`, `n_valid`, `replicates` (the kept replicates,   one row each), `messages` (why a resample was dropped, `NA` where it was   not), `structure` and `fixed`; `covariance_unconstrained` is `NULL`.    For the Wald path, diagnostics of the whole fit are attributes:   `covariance` and `covariance_unconstrained` (natural and   estimation-scale covariance of the estimates), `hessian`, `gradient`,   `scaled_score`, `score_displacement` (the largest score times its   estimation-scale standard error, which the `latents_unconverged` warning   uses), `condition_ratio`, `level`, `step`, `method`, `vcov_type`, `fixed`   (the measurement blocks the fit held, `character()` when none),   `fixed_at_bound` (the probabilities held by `boundary = "fix"`) and   `adjust`. When `vcov_type` is `"robust"` or `"opg"`, `group_scores` holds   the groups-by-parameters score matrix and `scaling_correction` the MLR   scaling correction factor `tr(A^-1 B) / q` (with `B` without the CR1   factor), used for scaled likelihood-ratio difference tests; it is `NA`   otherwise. @section Computation: The observed information takes two evaluations of   the score over all the data for each free parameter, which makes it the   slowest part of Wald inference. For profile, class, covariate and   transition models it is computed once per R session for a fit, its data   and `step`, and reused by later calls, including those made by the plots   that draw intervals and by `get_results()`. Any change to the fit or its   data computes it anew, and the result is the same either way. @section Conditions:   Errors: `latents_no_converge` for an unconverged fit;   `latents_boundary_fit` when a variance, response probability or mixing   probability is at its bound; `latents_singular_information` when the   observed information cannot be inverted; `latents_no_free_parameters`   when `fixed` held every parameter; `latents_bad_inference_data` when a   supplied `data` does not reproduce the fit; `latents_too_few_groups` for   `vcov_type = "robust"` or `"opg"` when the fit has no more independent   groups than free parameters. The Wald path raises   `latents_unsupported_inference` for a fit made with `multilpa(prior = )`   (a posterior mode, where the score is not zero), and either path raises   `latents_unsupported_noise` for a fit with a noise component. A fit whose   score is still far from zero gives a `latents_unconverged` warning.    `method = "bootstrap"` also raises `latents_unsupported_inference` for an   additive or covariate fit, and for a   fit holding a measurement block through `multilpa(fixed = )`, since   resampling the data does not resample the held values (a [fit_staged()]   result is bootstrapped by refitting both stages instead), and   `latents_bootstrap_failed` when fewer than two resamples gave a usable   fit; its message gives the first reason. Resamples that fail or do not   converge are dropped with a `latents_bootstrap_dropped` warning stating   how many. @examples set.seed(42) example_data <- data.frame(   school = rep(seq_len(10), each = 10),   score_a = rnorm(100), score_b = rnorm(100) ) fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("score_a", "score_b"), "school",                 n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1) parameter_inference(fit)  # Many tests in one table: name the correction, do not apply one by stealth. parameter_inference(fit, adjust = "BH")  # A structure that constrains the shape across profiles (VEI) is charted in # its own free coordinates, so it has Wald standard errors too. shaped <- multilpa(example_data, c("score_a", "score_b"), "school",                    n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1,                    volume = "varying", shape = "equal", orientation = "axis") parameter_inference(shaped)  # The bootstrap resamples schools and refits inside the same family. parameter_inference(shaped, method = "bootstrap", iter = 10, n_starts = 1,                     seed = 1) @export

.multilpa_response_bound.name: .multilpa_response_bound
.multilpa_response_bound.documentation: Response probabilities sitting on their lower bound  A probability held at `min_probability` has a logit on the edge of the space, where the likelihood is flat and the information singular. The free logit of a category is on the bound when that category's probability is, or when the reference (last) category's is, since every logit of that row is then measured against a vanishing denominator; in the second case every probability of the row is on the bound too.  @param object A fitted model with `response_probabilities`. @return A list of two character vectors of parameter names, `natural`   (probabilities) and `unconstrained` (logits), in the   `level.parameter.outcome.term` spelling every fitted class uses. @noRd

.multilpa_probability_floor.name: .multilpa_probability_floor
.multilpa_probability_floor.documentation: The probability below which an estimate is on its boundary  EM approaches a zero probability slowly, so a fit rarely lands exactly on `min_probability`; it stops a little above it, at a logit of -15 or -20 where the likelihood is flat. Treating only the exact floor as the bound left such an estimate free, and the observed information was then singular. At or below 1e-6 a probability's expected count is far below one observation at any realistic sample size, so the data cannot tell it from zero and it is treated as on its bound. @param object A fitted model. @return A single probability. @noRd

.multilpa_check_regularity.name: .multilpa_check_regularity
.multilpa_check_regularity.documentation: Check that a fit admits Wald inference at all  Boundary solutions, unconverged fits and zero mixing probabilities each put the estimate where the asymptotic normal approximation does not hold, so they are refused rather than reported with a number.  @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises on the first broken contract. @noRd

.multilpa_number_single_level.name: .multilpa_number_single_level
.multilpa_number_single_level.documentation: Give the caller's frame a single-level fit's internal row numbering  A single-level fit numbered its rows itself; the caller's frame has no such column, and its row order is what the numbering was. Frames that already carry the column, or have a different number of rows, are returned as given for the caller's own checks to judge.  @param object A fitted model of this package. @param data The caller's frame. @return `data`, with the fit's identifier column added when it was absent. @noRd

.multilpa_inference_matrix.name: .multilpa_inference_matrix
.multilpa_inference_matrix.documentation: Recover and centre the indicator matrix the fit was built on  The Hessian is evaluated at the fitted estimates, so it is only meaningful if `data` really is the data that produced them. Stored indicators are compared exactly; older fits without them fall back to the likelihood check the caller performs next.  @return A list with the centred matrix `x` and the `centers` removed from it. @noRd

.multilpa_validate_bootstrap_data.name: .multilpa_validate_bootstrap_data
.multilpa_validate_bootstrap_data.documentation: Validate the original observations before any bootstrap resampling  A bootstrap reports uncertainty for the fit's estimates, so its data must reproduce the same observations, grouping, ordering and normalized sampling weights. A likelihood check also protects older fits without stored rows. @param object A fitted `multilpa` model. @param data The supplied or reconstructed original data frame. @return The checked data, including a single-level fit's internal row ID. @noRd

.multilpa_tidy_labels.name: .multilpa_tidy_labels
.multilpa_tidy_labels.documentation: Split a generated parameter name into tidy columns  The names are machine-generated with a strict grammar -- `mean[profile, indicator]`, `variance[profile,indicator]`, `covariance[profile,a,b]`, `profile_probability[group_class,profile]`, `group_probability[group_class]`, and their unconstrained counterparts `log_variance`, `cholesky`, `log_cholesky`, `response_logit`, `profile_logit` and `group_logit` -- so they can be taken apart reliably. Reporting the pieces as columns means a caller never has to parse a label to learn which level a parameter belongs to, which is the whole point of a tidy result.  @param names Character vector of generated parameter names. @param object The fit, supplying the profile and group-class counts. @return A data frame with `level`, `outcome`, `term` and `parameter`, one row   per name, in the order given. @noRd

.latents_gaussian_log_density.name: .latents_gaussian_log_density
.latents_gaussian_log_density.documentation: Diagonal Gaussian log densities of every row under every profile  @param x Observation-by-indicator matrix, complete. @param means Profiles-by-indicators matrix. @param variances Profiles-by-indicators matrix. @param constant How the normalizing constant is formed: `"separate"`,   `log(2 pi) + log(variance)` (profile and transition models), or   `"joint"`, `log(2 pi variance)` (covariate models). They are the same   number up to the last bit, and each engine keeps the one its results   have always been computed with, since robust standard errors near a   boundary amplify that last bit. @return A rows-by-profiles matrix. @noRd

.latents_measurement_log_density.name: .latents_measurement_log_density
.latents_measurement_log_density.documentation: Log densities of every row under every profile, summed over the blocks  The Gaussian block uses the conditional moments when indicators are missing or covariances are full (the M-step then reuses those moments), and the diagonal closed form otherwise. With `offset`, each row's largest Gaussian log density is removed before the other blocks are added: a very small density (log f = -5e15) would otherwise round away the priors and the small categorical contributions, and the offset is added back to the likelihood by the structure.  @param x Observation-by-indicator matrix of continuous indicators, `NA`   where unobserved; it may have zero columns. @param parameters A list with `means`, `variances`, optionally   `covariances`, `response_probabilities` and the extra-indicator blocks. @param codes Optional categorical codes. @param extra Optional ordinal and count data. @param noise_log_density Optional constant log density of a uniform noise   component, appended as the last column before the offset. @param offset Whether to remove the row maximum of the Gaussian block. @param n_profiles Number of profiles (from `means` by default). @param constant Passed to `.latents_gaussian_log_density()`. @return A list with `log_density` (rows by profiles, offset removed),   `offset` (per row; zeros when `offset = FALSE`) and `moments` (the   Gaussian conditional moments, or `NULL`). @noRd

.latents_em_settings.name: .latents_em_settings
.latents_em_settings.documentation: Settings of one engine's EM iteration  @param decrease_tolerance Relative decrease of the log likelihood, beyond   which a step is a defect: a decrease larger than   `decrease_tolerance * (1 + |log L|)` raises the decrease condition. @param decrease_condition `"plain"` raises the unclassed message   "EM likelihood decreased beyond numerical roundoff."; `"classed"` raises   `latents_em_decrease` stating the size of the decrease; a string other   than those is used verbatim as an unclassed message. @param guard_decrease Whether to check for a decrease at all (a fit under a   prior climbs the posterior, so its likelihood may fall). @param stop_on_nonfinite Whether a non-finite likelihood after a step ends   the run, keeping the step's parameters but the previous E-step. @param accelerate `NULL` for plain EM, or a list of `flatten`, `restore` and   `valid` functions over the parameter list for SQUAREM. @param max_stalled With a maximization that reports `solved`, how many   steps in a row may settle the likelihood without settling the inner solve   before the run stops unconverged; `Inf` when the maximization has no inner   solve. @return A list of settings. @noRd

.latents_em_decrease.name: .latents_em_decrease
.latents_em_decrease.documentation: Raise an engine's decrease condition @param settings From `.latents_em_settings()`. @param decrease The size of the decrease, positive. @noRd

.latents_em_step.name: .latents_em_step
.latents_em_step.documentation: One plain EM step with the engine's decrease guard  @param state The current parameter state. @param expectation Its E-step, carrying `log_likelihood`. @param evaluate E-step: a function of a state. @param maximize M-step: a function of a state and its E-step, returning   the next state. @param settings From `.latents_em_settings()`. @return A list with the next `state` and its `expectation`. @noRd

.latents_em.name: .latents_em
.latents_em.documentation: Run EM from one starting state  Plain EM steps, or SQUAREM cycles when the settings carry an accelerator and at least three steps of the budget remain. Convergence is the relative gain over one step or cycle, `|gain| <= tol * (1 + |log L|)`; a maximization that reports `attr(state, "solved")` must also have settled its inner solve.  @param state Starting parameter state. @param evaluate E-step: a function of a state returning a list with   `log_likelihood`. @param maximize M-step: a function of a state and its E-step returning the   next state. @param max_iter Maximum number of EM steps. @param tol Relative convergence tolerance. @param settings From `.latents_em_settings()`. @param pause Iteration count after which the run stops at the end of the   current step or cycle, resumable; `Inf` runs to the end. Whether a cycle   is accelerated is decided against `max_iter`, not `pause`, so a run   paused and resumed takes exactly the steps of one that was not. @param resume `NULL`, or the `checkpoint` of a paused run, which the run   continues (its E-step is recomputed from the state, which is what the run   computed there, except after a non-finite step, when it is carried). @return A list with `state`, `expectation`, `converged`, `iterations`,   `history` (the log likelihood at the start and after every step) and   `settled` (whether the last step settled the likelihood); with a finite   `pause`, also `checkpoint`, everything a resumed run needs. @noRd

.latents_squarem_cycle.name: .latents_squarem_cycle
.latents_squarem_cycle.documentation: One SQUAREM cycle over an engine's parameter state  Varadhan, R., & Roland, C. (2008). Simple and globally convergent methods for accelerating the convergence of any EM algorithm. Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, 35, 335-353.  Two EM steps from theta0 give the first and second differences r = theta1 - theta0 and v = theta2 - theta1 - r; the extrapolation theta' = theta0 - 2 alpha r + alpha^2 v uses alpha = -|r| / |v| (scheme S3), backtracked towards -1 (plain EM) until the state is valid, and one EM step from theta' returns the iterate to the constraint set.  @param step A function of a state and its E-step giving the next   `list(state, expectation)`. @param state Current state. @param expectation Its E-step. @param evaluate E-step function. @param accelerator A list of `flatten`, `restore` and `valid`. @return A list with `state`, `expectation`, `history` (three likelihoods)   and `accelerated`. @noRd

.latents_run_starts.name: .latents_run_starts
.latents_run_starts.documentation: Run every start and choose the best  Each start runs to completion or fails; a failure is recorded with its message (it appears in the starts table) rather than ending the fit, and only when every start fails is the fit refused, naming the distinct reasons. The best start is the highest likelihood under the selection rule, with ties resolved as `.multilpa_select_start()` resolves them.  @param n_starts Number of starts. @param run A function of the start index returning a list with   `expectation$log_likelihood` and `converged`. @param select_start `"likelihood"` or `"converged"`. @param score A function of a successful attempt giving its log   likelihood; the default reads `attempt$expectation$log_likelihood`. @param interior `NULL`, or a function of a successful attempt returning   `TRUE` when no variance is at its lower bound; when supplied, starts at   the bound are excluded from the choice (see `.multilpa_select_start()`). @param prepare `NULL`, or a function of the start index returning that   start's initial values; `run` is then a function of the start index and   those values. Every start is prepared first, in order and on this   process, so the random numbers are drawn exactly as when each start is   prepared and run in turn (the iterations draw none); only the   iterations are spread over `cores`. @param cores Number of cores for the iterations, from   `.latents_check_cores()`; used with `prepare` or supplied `initial` values. @param screen `NULL` for the search of latents 0.96.1 and earlier, every   start run to the end; or, for the emEM search, a list of `n_pool`,   `iterations` and `protect` (see `.latents_run_screened()`), which needs   `prepare` or already prepared `initial` values. @param initial `NULL`, or ordered wrapped values from   `.latents_prepare_starts()`, prepared in the caller's seed scope. @return A list with `attempts`, `valid`, `scores`, `converged` and   `best_start`; with `screen`, also `stage` and `screened_scores`. @noRd

.latents_prepare_starts.name: .latents_prepare_starts
.latents_prepare_starts.documentation: Prepare starting values in their original random-number order @param n_starts Number of starts to prepare. @param prepare Function of a start index returning its initial values. @return One wrapped `values` or `error` entry per start, in start order. @noRd

.latents_start_attempt.name: .latents_start_attempt
.latents_start_attempt.documentation: Run one prepared start or continue its checkpoint @param run Function of a start index and initial values; screening also   requires `pause` and `resume` arguments. @param start_index The start's original index. @param initial Wrapped initial values from `.latents_prepare_starts()`;   `NULL` when continuing a checkpoint. @param pause Screening iteration budget, or `Inf` for a complete run. @param resume Checkpoint to continue, or `NULL` for a new start. @return The attempt, or an `error` entry for an ordinary start failure. @noRd

.latents_start_failure.name: .latents_start_failure
.latents_start_failure.documentation: Retain accumulated covariance qualifications when every start fails @param message The unchanged all-starts failure message. @param attempts Start attempts, including every completed search phase. @return A `latents_all_starts_failed` error condition, with structure logs   only when an attempt recorded them. @noRd

.latents_select_starts.name: .latents_select_starts
.latents_select_starts.documentation: Select among complete start attempts @param attempts Complete attempts in their original start order. @param select_start,score,interior As for `.latents_run_starts()`. @return As `.latents_run_starts()` without screening fields. @noRd

.latents_run_screened.name: .latents_run_screened
.latents_run_screened.documentation: Screen a pool of starts and run the best to the end (emEM)  Biernacki, C., Celeux, G., & Govaert, G. (2003). Choosing starting values for the EM algorithm for getting the highest likelihood in multivariate Gaussian mixture models. Computational Statistics & Data Analysis, 41, 561-575.  Every start of the pool is prepared in order on this process (so the random numbers are drawn as when they are prepared one by one), then run for `screen$iterations` EM iterations, paused at the end of the step or cycle that reaches them. The protected starts and then those with the highest screened likelihood (ties by pool order) are resumed to the end, `n_starts` in all; a resumed start takes exactly the steps it would have taken unscreened. The best is chosen among them by `.multilpa_select_start()`; the other starts stay in the record with their screened likelihood.  @param n_starts Number of starts run to the end. @param run A function of the start index, its initial values, `pause` and   `resume`, returning an attempt that carries a `checkpoint` when paused. @param select_start,score,interior,prepare,cores,initial As for   `.latents_run_starts()`. @param screen A list of `n_pool` (starts screened, at least `n_starts`),   `iterations` (the screening budget) and `protect` (pool indices that go   to the end whatever their screened likelihood, such as a supplied start). @return As `.latents_run_starts()`, with `attempts` over the whole pool, a   screened-only attempt carrying `screened = TRUE`, its `state`,   `converged`, `iterations` and `expectation$log_likelihood`; `stage`   (`"final"` or `"screened"`) and `screened_scores`. @noRd

.latents_screen_attempt.name: .latents_screen_attempt
.latents_screen_attempt.documentation: Screen one prepared start and retain only its resumable state @param run,start_index,initial As for `.latents_start_attempt()`. @param screen Screening controls from `.latents_run_screened()`. @param score Function giving the likelihood of a successful attempt. @return A reduced screened attempt, or an `error` entry. @noRd

.latents_rank_screened.name: .latents_rank_screened
.latents_rank_screened.documentation: Rank screened starts while retaining protected starts @param screened Reduced attempts from `.latents_screen_attempt()`. @param n_starts Number of finalists. @param screen Screening controls from `.latents_run_screened()`. @param score Function reading a reduced attempt's screened likelihood. @return The ordered `finalists` and all `screened_scores`. @noRd

.latents_select_screened.name: .latents_select_screened
.latents_select_screened.documentation: Merge finalist continuations and select the best complete start @param screened Reduced attempts in original pool order. @param continued Complete attempts in `finalists` order. @param finalists Indices of starts carried to completion. @param screened_scores Screened likelihoods in original pool order. @param select_start,score,interior As for `.latents_run_starts()`. @return As `.latents_run_starts()` with screening fields. @noRd

.latents_quasi_newton.name: .latents_quasi_newton
.latents_quasi_newton.documentation: Quasi-Newton finish from an EM point  EM crawls near a maximum when classes overlap; from its point L-BFGS-B maximizes the log likelihood with the analytic gradient, inside lower bounds on the coordinates that have them. The point is kept only if the likelihood does not fall. Convergence is L-BFGS-B's own, except that its line-search stop (code 52), which rounding can trigger at the maximum on some platforms, is checked by one restart from where it stopped: if the likelihood cannot be raised by more than the tolerance, the relative-change rule EM uses is met.  @param theta Packed starting coordinates. @param lower Lower bounds, `-Inf` where there is none; `theta` is raised to   them first. @param value Negative log likelihood as a function of the coordinates. @param gradient Its gradient. @param tol Relative convergence tolerance for the code-52 check. @param control `optim()` control list. @return A list with `par`, `value` (the negative log likelihood there),   `converged`, `improved` (whether the finish was kept) and `start_value`. @noRd

.mixture_row_lse.name: .mixture_row_lse
.mixture_row_lse.documentation: Row-wise log-sum-exp of a matrix @param log_values Numeric matrix. @return Numeric vector, one value per row. @noRd

.mixture_log_softmax.name: .mixture_log_softmax
.mixture_log_softmax.documentation: Log class probabilities from a full logit coefficient matrix  @param design Numeric design matrix, one row per unit. @param coefficients Matrix with one column per class; the first column is   the reference and is zero. @return Matrix of log probabilities, one row per unit and column per class. @noRd

.mixture_weigh.name: .mixture_weigh
.mixture_weigh.documentation: Weight a mixture-regression expectation by sampling weights  Every posterior becomes its unit's weight times the posterior, so the M-steps and the scores read weighted counts, and the log likelihood is the weighted pseudo log likelihood. Integer weights equal duplication.  @param spec The specification, carrying `sampling_weights` (one per   independent unit) and `row_weights` (each row's unit weight). @param expectation An unweighted expectation. @return The weighted expectation. @noRd

.mixture_structure_expectation.name: .mixture_structure_expectation
.mixture_structure_expectation.documentation: The E-step of a structure, without sampling weights  @param spec The structure (a regression specification is one). @param params The parameter list, carrying the structure's membership   coefficients: `gamma`, or `delta` and `class_logits` for two levels. @param log_density The block's log densities: units by classes for   `"observation"` and `"two-level"`, rows by classes for `"group"`, whose   rows the structure sums to units. @return A list with `log_likelihood`, the per-unit `unit_log_likelihood`,   the posteriors `tau` (one row per row of `log_density`), `log_prior`,   `log_density` and, by nesting, `group_tau`, or `rho`,   `tau_by_group_class`, `log_prior_by_group_class` and `log_eta`. @noRd

.mixture_two_level_design.name: .mixture_two_level_design
.mixture_two_level_design.documentation: Class-logit design of the two-level model for one group class  Group class `h` contributes an indicator column for its own intercepts, followed by the shared membership covariates.  @param spec The model specification. @param h Group class index. @return An `n x (H + r)` matrix. @noRd

.mixture_solve.name: .mixture_solve
.mixture_solve.documentation: Solve a symmetric positive definite system, falling back to QR  @param a Numeric matrix. @param b Numeric vector. @return The solution vector. @noRd

.mixture_multinomial.name: .mixture_multinomial
.mixture_multinomial.documentation: Weighted multinomial logit on soft counts  Maximizes `sum_i sum_k counts_ik log p_ik(design_i)` over a coefficient matrix whose first column is fixed at zero, by Newton-Raphson with step halving. The counts need not sum to one per row: the two-level mixing step passes joint posteriors whose row sums are the group-class posteriors.  @param design Numeric design matrix. @param counts Non-negative matrix, one column per outcome category. @param start Full coefficient matrix (first column zero). @param max_newton Maximum Newton iterations. @return A list with the full `coefficients` matrix and `separation`. @noRd

.mixture_update_mixing.name: .mixture_update_mixing
.mixture_update_mixing.documentation: M-step for the mixing probabilities  Without membership covariates the maximizer is closed form; the Newton routine reaches it too, but the closed form is exact and cheaper.  @param spec The model specification. @param params The parameter list. @param expectation The E-step result. @return The parameter list with the mixing coefficients updated. @noRd

.mixture_structure_scores.name: .mixture_structure_scores
