.mixture_structure_scores.documentation: Scores of a structure's membership coefficients  By Fisher's identity a unit's score for a multinomial logit is its design row times the posterior minus the prior class probabilities (posterior counts minus their expectation). The two-level structure has cluster-level scores for the group-class logits and unit-level scores for the class logits, summed to clusters.  @param spec The structure. @param expectation Its weighted E-step. @return A matrix with one row per independent unit (row, or cluster) and   one column per free membership coefficient, in packing order. @noRd

.latents_forward_backward.name: .latents_forward_backward
.latents_forward_backward.documentation: Forward-backward pass of the Markov structure over occasions  The structure of the transition models: a profile chain per group, with group- and occasion-specific transition log probabilities (homogeneous transitions repeat one matrix over groups and occasions). Occasions a group was not observed at hold its state, so sequences of unequal length share one layout.  @param emission Offset-removed emission list (one groups x K matrix per   occasion). @param layout Sequence layout. @param log_initial Groups x K log initial probabilities. @param log_transition A homogeneous K x K log-transition matrix, or a list   over occasions 2..T of groups x K x K arrays. @return A list with `alpha`, `beta` and `log_scaled`. @noRd

.latents_scaled_forward_backward.name: .latents_scaled_forward_backward
.latents_scaled_forward_backward.documentation: Scaled-probability recursion for a homogeneous Markov chain  Emission row maxima have already been removed. Normalizing at each occasion keeps the recursion finite even for very long sequences. Log-space messages remain available for inference and other consumers. @param emission,layout As for `.latents_forward_backward()`. @param initial Groups x K initial probabilities. @param transition Homogeneous K x K transition probabilities. @return Log-space messages and likelihoods, plus scaled messages,   emission probabilities and normalizers for the expected-count step. @noRd

.latents_log_sum_exp.name: .latents_log_sum_exp
.latents_log_sum_exp.documentation: Log-sum-exp over the last dimension that tolerates rows of -Inf @noRd

.multilpa_nested_structure.name: .multilpa_nested_structure
.multilpa_nested_structure.documentation: The nested structure of the profile models  Each group belongs to one group class, and each of its rows to one profile, with profile probabilities that depend on the group class: L = prod_j sum_h omega_h prod_{i in j} sum_k pi_k|h f_k(y_i) (Vermunt 2003). One group class is the ordinary single-level mixture. The full cross-level family adds a group-level density per group class.  @param log_density Rows-by-profiles log densities, offset removed. @param density_offset The per-row offset that was removed. @param group_index Group of each row. @param parameters A list with `profile_probabilities` (group classes by   profiles), `group_probabilities` and optionally `group_log_density`   (groups by group classes). @return A list with `log_likelihood`, `group_log_likelihood`,   `group_posteriors`, `subject_posteriors` and `joint` (the row posteriors   joint with each group class). @noRd

.multilpa_logit_structure.name: .multilpa_logit_structure
.multilpa_logit_structure.documentation: The nested structure with membership covariates  As `.multilpa_nested_structure()`, with the profile and group-class probabilities multinomial logits of covariates: the profile logits of group class `h` read the design `profile_design[[h]]` (its own intercepts, shared or class-specific slopes), and the group-class logits the group design. The last class is the reference.  @param log_density Rows-by-profiles log densities, offset removed. @param density_offset The per-row offset that was removed. @param group_index Group of each row. @param profile_design List of profile design matrices, one per group class. @param group_design Group-level design matrix. @param beta Profile logit coefficients. @param gamma Group logit coefficients. @return As `.multilpa_nested_structure()`, plus `group_priors` and   `profile_priors` (one rows-by-profiles matrix per group class). @noRd

.multilpa_weigh.name: .multilpa_weigh
.multilpa_weigh.documentation: Weight an expectation step by sampling weights  Pseudo maximum likelihood maximizes the weighted sum of the independent units' log likelihoods. Its EM step is the ordinary one with every posterior multiplied by its unit's weight, so integer weights reproduce the fit to the data with each unit repeated that many times.  @param expectation An unweighted expectation step. @param weights Sampling weight per group. @param group_index Group of each row. @return The expectation with weighted posteriors, the weighted log   likelihood, and `n_total`, the weighted row count. @noRd

.mixture_structure_pack.name: .mixture_structure_pack
.mixture_structure_pack.documentation: Pack a structure's free membership coefficients  The reference class (and reference group class) has its logits fixed at zero; the rest are named `membership.<class>.<term>` and, for two levels, `group_membership.<group class>.<term>`, with the class logits of a two-level structure carrying one intercept per group class (`(Intercept):group_class_h`) and shared slopes.  @param spec The structure. @param params The parameter list. @return A named numeric vector (empty for one class). @noRd

.mixture_structure_unpack.name: .mixture_structure_unpack
.mixture_structure_unpack.documentation: Unpack a structure's free membership coefficients  @param spec The structure. @param values The packed coefficients, in `.mixture_structure_pack()` order. @param template A parameter list with the right shapes. @return `template` with `gamma`, or `delta` and `class_logits`, replaced. @noRd

.latents_table.name: .latents_table
.latents_table.documentation: Mark a data frame as a latents result table @param table A data frame. @param level The confidence level of its intervals, if any. @param title A title printed above the table. @param display A display plan (a list of `.latents_column()`), or `NULL`   to show every column in a default format. @return `table` with class `latents_table` prepended. @noRd

.latents_column.name: .latents_column
.latents_column.documentation: One displayed column of a result table  @param label The header. @param column The source column, or for `"ci"` the lower and upper bounds. @param format `"text"`, `"label"` (class and term names made readable),   `"number"`, `"share"` (three decimals), `"integer"`, `"ci"`, `"p"`,   `"percent"` or `"logical"`. @param decimals_from For `"ci"`, the column whose decimals the bounds use. @noRd

.latents_column_decimals.name: .latents_column_decimals
.latents_column_decimals.documentation: Decimals for a column: two, three or four, so its smallest value keeps a significant digit @noRd

.latents_format_p.name: .latents_format_p
.latents_format_p.documentation: APA-style p-values: no leading zero, "<.001" below a thousandth @noRd

.latents_cells.name: .latents_cells
.latents_cells.documentation: The cells of one displayed column, as text @noRd

.latents_default_display.name: .latents_default_display
.latents_default_display.documentation: The display plan of a table without one: every column, by type @noRd

.latents_render_card.name: .latents_render_card
.latents_render_card.documentation: Draw a one-row table as label-value lines @noRd

.latents_render.name: .latents_render
.latents_render.documentation: Draw a result table as aligned text lines @param x A `latents_table`. @param n Most rows drawn. @return A character vector of lines. @noRd

.latents_vuong_parts.name: .latents_vuong_parts
.latents_vuong_parts.documentation: The scores and Hessian of one fitted model, for Vuong's test  Read from [parameter_inference()] with `vcov_type = "robust"`, which keeps the per-unit (per-group) scores; its observed information is computed once per session for a fit and reused. @param fit A fitted profile or class model. @return A list of `scores` (units by free coordinates), `information`   (minus the Hessian, in the same coordinates), `log_likelihood` and   `n_parameters` and the counted independent `n_units`. @noRd

.latents_vuong_weights.name: .latents_vuong_weights
.latents_vuong_weights.documentation: The weights of the reference distribution of Vuong's statistic  With `A = -information`, `-B A^-1 = B information^-1`, so in terms of the information matrices `W = [ B1 I1^-1, B10 I0^-1 ; -B10' I1^-1, -B0 I0^-1 ]`. For two regular nested models whose information equals the variance of the score, the nonzero eigenvalues are `p1 - p0` ones, and the reference distribution is the familiar chi-square on `p1 - p0` degrees of freedom. @param alternative,null From `.latents_vuong_parts()`, on the same units. @return The eigenvalues of `W`, computed from an equivalent symmetric matrix. @noRd

.latents_imhof_upper.name: .latents_imhof_upper
.latents_imhof_upper.documentation: Upper tail of a weighted sum of chi-square(1) variables (Imhof 1961)  `P(sum_j lambda_j X_j > q)` for independent `X_j ~ chi-square(1)`: `1/2 + (1/pi) int_0^Inf sin(theta(u)) / (u rho(u)) du`, with `theta(u) = sum_j atan(lambda_j u) / 2 - q u / 2` and `rho(u) = prod_j (1 + lambda_j^2 u^2)^(1/4)`. Weights that are exactly zero contribute nothing and are dropped. Small nonzero weights are retained: their relative size does not bound the probability error near a statistic of zero. Negative statistics are handled by the symmetry `P(Q > q) = 1 - P(-Q > -q)` for the continuous nonzero-weight distribution.  The integral has two regimes, and each is integrated where it is smooth. Up to `u = 2 pi / q` the phase is dominated by the arctangents, which bend at `u = 1 / |lambda_j|`; that lead is integrated by adaptive quadrature between breakpoints at those scales and at every decade, so no segment spans more than an order of magnitude. When `q = 0` there is no oscillation at all and the lead is the whole integral, ended where Imhof's truncation bound falls below `1e-12`: with weights of both signs the integrand then decays monotonically, and extrapolating its partial sums (the method this replaces) settled on wrong limits, 32% off for weights `(1, -1e4, -1e4, -1e4)`. Beyond the lead, `sin(q u / 2)` dominates, so the tail is integrated in half-periods aligned to it, whose partial sums alternate, and accelerated by Wynn's epsilon algorithm, as QUADPACK's QAWF does for Fourier integrals. The value is accepted when two successive estimates agree to `1e-10`; otherwise, or when a segment cannot be integrated, `latents_inaccurate_probability` is raised. The integral is taken on weights normalised to unit size, which leaves the probability unchanged. Against 312 exact F and chi-square probabilities and two-weight convolutions, with weights from 1e-6 to 1e6, the absolute error is at most 3.2e-13 when `q = 0` and 1e-15 otherwise. @param q The statistic. @param lambda The weights. @return A probability. @noRd

.latents_wynn.name: .latents_wynn
.latents_wynn.documentation: The limit of a sequence by Wynn's epsilon algorithm  Builds the epsilon table column by column from the partial sums `s` (`e[-1] = 0`, `e[0] = s`, `e[j + 1][k] = e[j - 1][k + 1] + 1 / (e[j][k + 1] - e[j][k])`) and returns the last entry of the last even column, the accelerated limit. Two equal neighbours mean the sequence has already settled there. @param s Partial sums. @return The estimated limit. @noRd

.latents_vuong_row.name: .latents_vuong_row
.latents_vuong_row.documentation: One VLMR and adjusted LMR comparison of two fitted candidates  The adjusted statistic divides LR by `1 + 1 / (d log n)`, with `d` the difference in the number of parameters and `n` the number of independent units (Lo, Mendell and Rubin 2001, eq. 15, with their three parameters per added univariate normal component replaced by the models' own difference), and is referred to the same distribution. @param alternative,null From `.latents_vuong_parts()`. @return A one-row data frame: `n_units`, `parameters_added`, `lr`,   `vlmr_p`, `adjusted_lr`, `almr_p`, `reference_mean`, `reference_sd`. @noRd

.latents_lmr_table.name: .latents_lmr_table
.latents_lmr_table.documentation: The VLMR and adjusted LMR tests between neighbouring candidates of a grid  Each converged candidate is compared with the converged candidate of one more profile at the same number of group classes and structure, and with the one of one more group class at the same number of profiles and structure. A comparison that cannot be computed (a candidate on a boundary, a singular information) keeps its row, with `NA` statistics and the reason in `note`; the warnings raised while scoring a candidate are recorded there too. @param x A `multilpa_enumeration`. @return A data frame, one row per comparison: `direction`   (`"profiles"` or `"group_classes"`), `null_candidate`,   `alternative_candidate`, `n_profiles`, `n_group_classes`, `model` (of the   alternative), then the columns of `.latents_vuong_row()` and `note`. @noRd

.latents_parse_pairs.name: .latents_parse_pairs
.latents_parse_pairs.documentation: Read `local_dependence` into pairs of indicators  @param local_dependence A character vector of pairs written `"a:b"`. @return A data frame: `item_1`, `item_2` and `name` (`"a:b"`), one row   per pair; `latents_bad_argument` for a malformed or overlapping pair. @noRd

.latents_classify_pairs.name: .latents_classify_pairs
.latents_classify_pairs.documentation: Mark each pair as categorical or continuous, refusing a mixed pair @param pairs From `.latents_parse_pairs()`. @param categorical The categorical indicators. @return `pairs` with a `kind` column. @noRd

.latents_covariance_pattern.name: .latents_covariance_pattern
.latents_covariance_pattern.documentation: The free covariance entries of continuous local dependence  @param pairs From `.latents_parse_pairs()`, continuous pairs. @param vars,categorical,ordinal,count The fit's indicators by kind. @param conflicts A named logical vector: settings that set the covariance   another way, refused when any is `TRUE`. @return A logical continuous-by-continuous matrix: `TRUE` on the diagonal   and for each pair. @noRd

.latents_pattern_pairs.name: .latents_pattern_pairs
.latents_pattern_pairs.documentation: The pairs a covariance pattern frees, as `"a:b"` names @param pattern From `.latents_covariance_pattern()`. @return A character vector, one name per pair. @noRd

.latents_pattern_label.name: .latents_pattern_label
.latents_pattern_label.documentation: The covariance label of a fit with covariances for chosen pairs  The diagonal structure the pattern extends, EEI with one shared covariance matrix and VVI with one per profile, and the pairs: `"VVI + y1:y2"`. The fit is estimated as a full covariance, so its structure field reads VVV or EEE, which would describe a model with every covariance free. @param fit A fit with `covariance_pattern`. @return A single string. @noRd

.latents_mask_covariances.name: .latents_mask_covariances
.latents_mask_covariances.documentation: Hold a start's covariances to a pattern @param parameters A start, with `covariances` under a full model. @param pattern From `.latents_covariance_pattern()`, or `NULL`. @return The start, its covariances zero outside the pattern. @noRd

.latents_pattern_zeros.name: .latents_pattern_zeros
.latents_pattern_zeros.documentation: The number of covariances a pattern holds at zero, per covariance matrix @param pattern From `.latents_covariance_pattern()`. @return An integer. @noRd

.latents_joined_names.name: .latents_joined_names
.latents_joined_names.documentation: Replace the paired indicators by their joint indicator  The joint indicator takes the place of the first item of its pair, so the indicators keep their order. @param vars Indicator names. @param pairs From `.latents_parse_pairs()`. @return The indicator names after the join. @noRd

.latents_join_pairs.name: .latents_join_pairs
.latents_join_pairs.documentation: Add the joint indicator of each pair to a data frame  Each joint value is the two items' values joined by a colon, missing when either item is. A frame that already holds a joint indicator (the frame a fit stores, or one this function has joined) is left as it is, so joining is idempotent. Rows where one item of a pair is observed and the other is not lose the pair, which is reported with `latents_partial_pair`. @param data A data frame. @param pairs From `.latents_parse_pairs()`. @param min_categories Minimum observed categories of each original item;   fitting requires two, prediction subsets may have none. @param rebuild_existing Regenerate an existing joint column from its source   items when a fitted model has already established their meaning. Initial   fitting leaves this false so existing caller columns remain protected. @return The data frame with one more column per pair. @noRd

.latents_fit_local_dependence.name: .latents_fit_local_dependence
.latents_fit_local_dependence.documentation: Fit a model whose `local_dependence` pairs are joined first  Called by [multilpa()] when `local_dependence` is given: the pairs are joined in `data`, `vars` and `categorical`, and the model is fitted on the joint indicators, with the caller's own arguments otherwise unchanged. @param call The caller's `match.call()`. @param env The calling function's environment, holding the matched values. @param local_dependence The caller's pairs. @return The fit, carrying `local_dependence` (the pairs) and the caller's   `call`. @noRd

.latents_categorical_labels.name: .latents_categorical_labels
.latents_categorical_labels.documentation: A fit's categorical responses as labels, one column per original item  A joint indicator is split back into its two items through the categories the fit stored, so a model with paired items and one without describe the same data alike. @param fit A fitted model. @return A character matrix, one row per observation and one column per   categorical item of the caller, or `NULL` without categorical items. @noRd

.latents_local_dependence_table.name: .latents_local_dependence_table
.latents_local_dependence_table.documentation: The joint and independent probabilities of each locally dependent pair  For every pair and profile, every combination of the two items' categories: its probability under the fitted joint distribution, the product of the two marginal probabilities it would have if the items were independent within the profile, and their ratio. A ratio far from one in a profile is the dependence the joint indicator captures. @param x A fitted model with `local_dependence`. @return A data frame, one row per pair, profile and combination: `pair`,   `profile`, `item_1`, `category_1`, `item_2`, `category_2`,   `probability`, `independent` and `ratio`. @noRd

lpa.name: lpa
lpa.documentation: Fit a latent profile model  Fits a single-level latent profile model and returns a fitted `multilpa` object. The model is a finite mixture of multivariate normal distributions: each observation belongs to one of `n_profiles` unobserved profiles, and each profile has its own mean on every indicator. It is the model [multilpa()] fits with `id = NULL`, so every accessor, plot and inference verb of the package applies to the result.  For observations nested in groups, use [multilpa()] with the grouping column as `id`, which adds latent classes of groups above the profiles.  @param data A data frame with one row per observation. @param vars Names of the indicator columns. Numeric columns are continuous   indicators; categorical ones are named in `categorical`. @param n_profiles Number of profiles, a positive whole number. @param ... Further arguments for [multilpa()]: the covariance structure   (`model`, or `variance_model` and `covariance_model`, or `volume`,   `shape` and `orientation`), `missing`, `categorical`, `n_starts`,   `seed`, `boundary`, `prior`, `noise`, `profile_covariates` and the others   it documents, except `id` and `n_group_classes`. @return A fitted `multilpa` object, as [multilpa()] returns, whose `call`   is the `lpa()` call. @section Conditions:   `latents_bad_argument` when `id` or `n_group_classes` is passed; the   conditions [multilpa()] raises otherwise. @references Oberski, D. (2016). Mixture models: Latent profile and latent class analysis. In J. Robertson & M. Kaptein (Eds.), *Modern Statistical Methods for HCI* (pp. 275--287). Springer. @seealso [lca()] for categorical indicators; [multilpa()] for the two-level   model; [enumerate_lpa()] to compare numbers of profiles. @examples fit <- lpa(srl, c("cognitive_strategies", "intrinsic_value",                   "self_efficacy", "self_regulation", "test_anxiety"),            n_profiles = 2, variance_model = "equal",            covariance_model = "full", n_starts = 3, seed = 1) fit plot(fit, what = "raincloud") @export

lca.name: lca
lca.documentation: Fit a latent class model  Fits a single-level latent class model and returns a fitted `multilpa` object. Each observation belongs to one of `n_classes` unobserved classes, and within a class the discrete indicators are independent. Categorical indicators have unrestricted response probabilities; `ordinal` and `count` in `...` select the structured measurement models described in [multilpa()]. It is the model [multilca()] fits with `id = NULL`, so every accessor, plot and inference verb of the package applies to the result. In the results the classes are labelled `profile_1`, `profile_2`, and so on.  For observations nested in groups, use [multilca()] with the grouping column as `id`, which adds latent classes of groups above the classes of observations.  @param data A data frame with one row per observation. @param vars Names of the discrete indicator columns. Categories are taken   from the data. Columns named in `ordinal` or `count` (through `...`) are   modelled as such; the rest are categorical. @param n_classes Number of classes, a positive whole number. @param ... Further arguments for [multilca()], such as `missing`,   `n_starts`, `seed`, `min_probability` and `profile_covariates`, except   `id` and `n_group_classes`. @return A fitted `multilpa` object, as [multilca()] returns, whose `call`   is the `lca()` call. @section Conditions:   `latents_bad_argument` when `id`, `n_group_classes` or `n_profiles` is   passed; the conditions [multilca()] raises otherwise. @references Lazarsfeld, P. F., & Henry, N. W. (1968). *Latent Structure Analysis*. Houghton Mifflin. @seealso [lpa()] for continuous indicators; [multilca()] for the   two-level model; [enumerate_lca()] to compare numbers of classes. @examples fit <- lca(student_esm, c("time_with_friends", "on_social_media",                           "tv_video_games", "sports"),            n_classes = 2, n_starts = 3, seed = 1) fit plot(fit, what = "heatmap") @export

enumerate_lpa.name: enumerate_lpa
enumerate_lpa.documentation: Compare latent profile models  Fits a single-level latent profile model for each number of profiles in `n_profiles` under each covariance structure in `model`, and returns a `multilpa_enumeration` object that tabulates the information criteria, entropy and diagnostics of every fit. It is [enumerate_classes()] with `id = NULL`.  For observations nested in groups, use [enumerate_classes()] with the grouping column as `id`, which also crosses the number of group classes.  @param data A data frame with one row per observation. @param vars Names of the indicator columns. @param n_profiles Positive whole numbers of profiles to compare. @param model The covariance structures: `"basic"`, the default, for the   four that combine equal or varying variances with covariances absent or   present (`EEI`, `VVI`, `EEE`, `VVV`); `"all"` for all 14; or their   three-letter codes. See [enumerate_classes()]. @param ... Further arguments for [multilpa()], such as `missing`,   `n_starts`, `seed`, `boundary` and `categorical`, except `id` and   `n_group_classes`. @return An object of class `multilpa_enumeration`, as [enumerate_classes()]   returns: [as.data.frame()] gives one row per candidate, [summary()] the   candidate each criterion prefers, [plot()] the criteria against the   number of profiles, and [get_candidate()] one fitted candidate. @section Conditions:   `latents_bad_argument` when `id` or `n_group_classes` is passed, or when   `model` names an unknown structure. @references Celeux, G., & Govaert, G. (1995). Gaussian parsimonious clustering models. *Pattern Recognition*, 28(5), 781--793. @seealso [lpa()] to fit one model; [enumerate_lca()] for categorical   indicators; [bootstrap_lrt()] to test one number of profiles against   another. @examples models <- enumerate_lpa(srl, c("cognitive_strategies", "intrinsic_value",                                "self_efficacy", "self_regulation",                                "test_anxiety"),                         n_profiles = 1:3, n_starts = 2, seed = 1) summary(models) plot(models) @export

enumerate_lca.name: enumerate_lca
enumerate_lca.documentation: Compare latent class models  Fits a single-level latent class model for each number of classes in `n_classes`, and returns a `multilpa_enumeration` object that tabulates the information criteria, entropy and diagnostics of every fit. Every indicator is categorical unless named in `ordinal` or `count`, as in [lca()]. It is [enumerate_classes()] with `id = NULL`; the number of classes is reported in the `n_profiles` column.  For observations nested in groups, use [enumerate_classes()] with the grouping column as `id` and the indicators as `categorical`.  @param data A data frame with one row per observation. @param vars Names of the categorical indicator columns. @param n_classes Positive whole numbers of classes to compare. @param ... Further arguments for [multilca()], such as `missing`,   `n_starts`, `seed` and `min_probability`, except `id` and   `n_group_classes`. Every indicator is categorical unless named in   `ordinal` or `count`. `categorical` is accepted but has no further   effect; its names must be in `vars`. @return An object of class `multilpa_enumeration`, as [enumerate_classes()]   returns: [as.data.frame()] gives one row per candidate, [summary()] the   candidate each criterion prefers, [plot()] the criteria against the   number of classes, and [get_candidate()] one fitted candidate, named by   its `n_profiles`. @section Conditions:   `latents_bad_argument` when `id` or `n_group_classes` is passed, or when   `model` is passed (no indicator is continuous); `latents_bad_categorical`   when `categorical` names a column not in `vars`. @seealso [lca()] to fit one model; [enumerate_lpa()] for continuous   indicators. @examples models <- enumerate_lca(student_esm, c("time_with_friends",                                        "on_social_media", "sports"),                         n_classes = 1:3, n_starts = 2, seed = 1) summary(models) @export

.multilpa_single_level_call.name: .multilpa_single_level_call
.multilpa_single_level_call.documentation: Refuse the two-level arguments in a single-level verb @param verb,two_level The verb's name and the two-level verb to point to. @param extra `list(...)` as the verb received it. @return `NULL`, invisibly. @noRd

.multilpa_quiet_single_level.name: .multilpa_quiet_single_level
.multilpa_quiet_single_level.documentation: Evaluate a single-level fit without its single-level notice  The notice tells a caller of `multilpa(id = NULL)` that the model has one level. A caller of `lpa()` or `lca()` asked for exactly that by name. @param expr The fitting call. @return Its value. @noRd

.lta_bootstrap_inference.name: .lta_bootstrap_inference
.lta_bootstrap_inference.documentation: Percentile bootstrap inference for a transition fit  Called by [parameter_inference()] on a `multilpa_transitions` or `multilpa_lta` fit when `method = "bootstrap"`. Persons (the `id` groups) are the resampled units, so dependence across a person's occasions is kept. The table has the Wald path's rows and columns; `standard_error` is the standard deviation of the replicates and `conf_low`/`conf_high` their percentile interval, while `statistic`, `p_value` and `p_adjusted` are `NA`.  @param x A transition fit. @param data The data it was fitted to. @param level Interval level. @param iter,n_starts,max_iter,tol Resamples, and the controls of each refit. @param adjust Kept for a frame of the same shape as the Wald path's. @return A base `data.frame` with attributes `covariance`, `level`,   `method`, `iter`, `n_valid`, `replicates` and `messages`. @noRd

.lta_bootstrap_frame.name: .lta_bootstrap_frame
.lta_bootstrap_frame.documentation: The rows a transition bootstrap reports, with their estimates  The same rows, labels and column order as the Wald table of the fit's class, plus `name`, the coefficient each row is matched on.  @param x A transition fit. @return A base `data.frame`. @noRd

.lta_bootstrap_estimates.name: .lta_bootstrap_estimates
.lta_bootstrap_estimates.documentation: The estimates a transition bootstrap reports, named  A homogeneous fit reports its natural parameters (measurement, group shares, initial and transition probabilities); a general fit its initial, transition and second-order logits.  @param x A transition fit. @return A named numeric vector. @noRd

.lta_bootstrap_replicates.name: .lta_bootstrap_replicates
.lta_bootstrap_replicates.documentation: Bootstrap replicates of a transition fit's reported estimates  @param x A transition fit. @param data The data it was fitted to. @param iter,n_starts,max_iter,tol Resamples, and the controls of each refit. @param reference_names The coefficient names each replicate is matched to. @return A list with `estimates` (`iter` rows, `NA` for a failed resample)   and `messages` (why each failed, `NA` otherwise). @noRd

.lta_align_estimates.name: .lta_align_estimates
.lta_align_estimates.documentation: A replicate's reported estimates, in the original fit's labels  Profiles are matched on the measurement, then group classes on what the matched profiles make of them.  @param replicate A transition fit from a resample. @param reference The original fit. @return The replicate's estimates, named as the original's. @noRd

.lta_profile_signature.name: .lta_profile_signature
.lta_profile_signature.documentation: What a transition fit's profiles look like, for matching  The measurement signature of every block, in the units `.latents_measurement_signature()` uses, with no mixing column: a transition fit's profile shares change from occasion to occasion.  @param x A transition fit. @param reference The fit whose scale both signatures are measured in. @return A profiles-by-features matrix. @noRd

.lta_class_signature.name: .lta_class_signature
.lta_class_signature.documentation: What a transition fit's group classes look like, for matching  A class's share and its initial and transition parameters, once the profiles agree. A stayer class can only match a stayer class.  @param x A transition fit, its profiles already matched. @param estimates For a general fit, its logits with matched profile labels. @return A classes-by-features matrix. @noRd

.lta_relabel_profiles.name: .lta_relabel_profiles
.lta_relabel_profiles.documentation: Rename profiles in general-fit logits, rebasing the initial logits  Transitions and second-order transitions are logits against staying, which a relabelling maps to staying, so their names move and their values do not. Initial logits are against the last profile: when another profile becomes last, every initial logit is shifted by the new reference's.  @param estimates Named logits of one fit. @param order Integer permutation: new profile `j` is old profile `order[j]`. @return The logits, named in the new labels. @noRd

.lta_relabel_classes.name: .lta_relabel_classes
.lta_relabel_classes.documentation: Rename group classes in general-fit logits @param estimates Named logits, profiles already matched. @param order Integer permutation: new class `i` is old class `order[i]`. @param classes The class names, in position order. @return The logits, named in the new class labels. @noRd

.lta_permute_transitions.name: .lta_permute_transitions
.lta_permute_transitions.documentation: Reorder a homogeneous transition fit's profiles and group classes @param x A `multilpa_transitions` fit. @param profiles,classes Integer permutations: new `j` is old `order[j]`. @return The fit with every profile- and class-indexed parameter reordered. @noRd

.lta_bootstrap_dispatch.name: .lta_bootstrap_dispatch
.lta_bootstrap_dispatch.documentation: Validate bootstrap controls, scope the seed, and run the transition bootstrap @param x A transition fit. @param data,level,iter,n_starts,max_iter,tol,seed,adjust As in   [parameter_inference()]. @return The bootstrap inference table. @noRd

.lta_arguments.name: .lta_arguments
.lta_arguments.documentation: The lta() arguments that define a transition fit, so it can be refitted @noRd

.lta_general_view.name: .lta_general_view
.lta_general_view.documentation: A transition fit in the general engine's parameterization  Homogeneous fits carry probabilities; they are turned into the same logits the general engine uses (initial: reference last profile; transitions: reference staying), on an intercept-only design. @return A list with `parameters` (natural means), `designs`, `layout`,   `occasion_of_row`, `n_profiles`, `vars`, `continuous`, `categorical`. @noRd

.lta_simulate.name: .lta_simulate
.lta_simulate.documentation: Simulate indicators from a fitted transition model, keeping the data's groups, occasions and covariates (the model conditions on them) @param fit A `multilpa_transitions` or `multilpa_lta` fit. @param data The data it was fitted to. @return `data` with the indicator columns replaced. @noRd

.lta_draw_continuous.name: .lta_draw_continuous
.lta_draw_continuous.documentation: Draw continuous indicators given each row's profile  Diagonal fits draw each indicator independently, in the order the package always has, so seeded results are unchanged. A fit that carries full covariance matrices draws each profile's rows as the profile mean plus standard normals times the upper Cholesky factor of its covariance.  @param block A measurement block: `means` and `variances` (profiles by   indicators) and, for a full-covariance fit, `covariances` (indicators by   indicators by profiles). @param profile The profile of every row to draw. @param continuous The continuous indicator names. @return A rows-by-indicators matrix with those column names. @noRd

.lta_nested.name: .lta_nested
.lta_nested.documentation: Is one transition model nested in another?  Every option may only be relaxed from the null to the alternative: at most as many profiles and group classes; homogeneous inside occasion-varying transitions and invariant inside occasion-specific measurement; first order inside second; covariate sets included; equal inside varying variances. @noRd

.lta_refit.name: .lta_refit
.lta_refit.documentation: Refit a transition model's specification to (simulated) data  `NULL` for `n_starts`, `max_iter` or `tol` takes the fit's own, with its search (see `.latents_refit_controls()`). @noRd

.lta_check_data.name: .lta_check_data
.lta_check_data.documentation: Verify original indicators, occasions and covariate designs of an LTA fit @param fit A fitted transition model. @param data Its original data frame. @return `NULL`, invisibly; refuses mismatched fitting data. @noRd

.lta_bootstrap_lrt.name: .lta_bootstrap_lrt
.lta_bootstrap_lrt.documentation: Parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio test between nested transition fits @noRd

.lta_enumerate.name: .lta_enumerate
.lta_enumerate.documentation: Enumerate transition models over numbers of profiles and group classes @noRd

as.data.frame.latents_transition_enumera.name: as.data.frame.latents_transition_enumeration
as.data.frame.latents_transition_enumera.documentation: @noRd @param row.names,optional Unused; part of the generic. @export

.lta_covariate_matrix.name: .lta_covariate_matrix
.lta_covariate_matrix.documentation: Covariate columns as a numeric matrix, factors expanded to indicators @return A matrix with one row per data row and named columns, or `NULL`. @noRd

.lta_designs.name: .lta_designs
.lta_designs.documentation: Initial and transition designs on the sequence layout  @param layout Sequence layout. @param covariate_rows Row-level covariate matrix for transitions, or `NULL`. @param initial_rows Row-level covariate matrix for the initial   distribution, or `NULL`; read at each group's first occasion. @param transitions `"homogeneous"` (one intercept) or `"occasion"` (one   intercept per occasion from the second on). @return A list with `initial` (groups x p0), `transition` (a list over   occasions 2..T of groups x p matrices; transition covariates are read at   the destination occasion, zero past a group's last occasion, where no   move is made; `.lta_check_covariate_gaps()` refuses skipped positions   inside a span) and the column names. @noRd

.lta_check_covariate_gaps.name: .lta_check_covariate_gaps
.lta_check_covariate_gaps.documentation: Refuse transition covariates at grid positions a group skipped  Under `occasions = "grid"` a move into a skipped position has no data row, so its covariates have no value. Any fill-in (zero, the last value) would be an assumption the likelihood then depends on: with zero, shifting a covariate by a constant changed the fit. The move is refused instead.  @param layout Sequence layout. @param groups Prepared groups (`ids`, `index`). @param time_values Each row's position. @param transition_covariates Transition covariate names. @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises `latents_bad_data`. @noRd

.lta_log_transition.name: .lta_log_transition
.lta_log_transition.documentation: Log transition probabilities of one class at one occasion  @param design Groups x p design at that occasion. @param coefficients p x (K - 1) x K array for this class: for origin k, the   logits of the K - 1 destinations other than k, in profile order. @return A groups x K x K array of log probabilities, origin by destination. @noRd

.lta_log_initial.name: .lta_log_initial
.lta_log_initial.documentation: Log initial probabilities of one class: groups x K (reference: last profile) @noRd

.lta_moments.name: .lta_moments
.lta_moments.documentation: Posterior occupancy and pair probabilities of one class, per group and occasion, weighted by the group's class posterior @return A list with `posterior` (rows x K), `initial` (groups x K) and   `pairs` (list over occasions 2..T of groups x K x K arrays). @noRd

.lta_reduce_moments.name: .lta_reduce_moments
.lta_reduce_moments.documentation: Pair-state moments back to profile moments  Occupancy and initial counts sum over the previous profile; the first move becomes first-order counts (origin j, destination l); every later move is kept by origin pair (i, j) and destination l. @noRd

.lta_log_density.name: .lta_log_density
.lta_log_density.documentation: Measurement log densities, rows x K, invariant or per occasion @noRd

.lta_augment.name: .lta_augment
.lta_augment.documentation: Second-order transitions as a first-order chain on profile pairs  State (i, j) at occasion t holds the profile at t - 1 (i) and at t (j); index (i - 1) K + j. Occasion 1 occupies only the diagonal pairs (j, j) with the initial probabilities; the move to occasion 2 uses the first-order logits; every later move (i, j) -> (j, l) uses the second-order logits of origin pair (i, j). Emissions read the current profile j. @return A list with the augmented `log_initial` (groups x K^2) and   `log_transition` (list of groups x K^2 x K^2 arrays, -Inf where a move is   impossible). @noRd

.lta_identity_transition.name: .lta_identity_transition
.lta_identity_transition.documentation: Log transitions of a stayer class: never leaving the current profile @noRd

.lta_identity_transition2.name: .lta_identity_transition2
.lta_identity_transition2.documentation: Second-order version: from pair (i, j) the next profile is j @noRd

.lta_log_transition2.name: .lta_log_transition2
.lta_log_transition2.documentation: Log second-order transition probabilities of one class at one occasion: groups x K^2 origin pairs x K destinations (reference: staying in j) @noRd

.lta_expectation.name: .lta_expectation
.lta_expectation.documentation: E-step of the general transition model @noRd

.lta_maximization.name: .lta_maximization
.lta_maximization.documentation: M-step of the general transition model @noRd

.lta_em.name: .lta_em
.lta_em.documentation: EM for the general transition model from one start  `pause` and `resume` are as for `.latents_em()`; with either, the result also carries the `checkpoint`. @noRd

.lta_initialize.name: .lta_initialize
.lta_initialize.documentation: Starting values: the homogeneous initializer, converted to logit coefficients with zero covariate effects @param row_weights Optional sampling weights in observation order, as for   `.multilpa_initialize()`. @noRd

.lta_fit_general.name: .lta_fit_general
.lta_fit_general.documentation: Fit through the general engine from its explicit internal arguments @inheritParams .lta_setup_general @return A fitted multilpa_lta object. @noRd

.lta_setup_general.name: .lta_setup_general
.lta_setup_general.documentation: Prepare the general transition model  Called by `lta()` when transitions vary by occasion or covariate, the initial distribution depends on covariates, or measurement varies by occasion. @return A prepared start plan for the general transition engine. @noRd

.lta_run_general_start.name: .lta_run_general_start
.lta_run_general_start.documentation: Run one general transition start, including its numerical finish @param start_index Original start index. @param start Starting values, or NULL when resuming. @param pause,resume Screening budget and checkpoint. @param context Forced EM and numerical-finish inputs from setup. @return One fitted or screened attempt. @noRd

.lta_finalise_general.name: .lta_finalise_general
.lta_finalise_general.documentation: Finalise a general transition fit from its selected starts @param starts The shared start-selection result. @param context Forced setup inputs. @return A fitted multilpa_lta object. @noRd

.lta_count_parameters.name: .lta_count_parameters
.lta_count_parameters.documentation: Free parameters of the general transition model @noRd

.lta_transition_columns.name: .lta_transition_columns
.lta_transition_columns.documentation: Free design columns of a transition coefficient block @param terms Design column names. @param second Whether second-order transitions are fitted. @param block First- or second-order transition block. @param n_occasion_intercepts Number of generated occasion intercepts. @return Integer indices excluding occasion intercepts that never apply. @noRd

.lta_uses_covariance_chart.name: .lta_uses_covariance_chart
.lta_uses_covariance_chart.documentation: Does LTA measurement need a covariance chart rather than log variances? @param fit A fit or parameter specification. @return A single logical. @noRd

.lta_covariance_view.name: .lta_covariance_view
.lta_covariance_view.documentation: Core measurement view for covariance coordinates of one LTA occasion @param block Measurement parameters of one occasion. @param fit Fit or parameter specification carrying its covariance structure. @return A core model view with no categorical or mixing free blocks. @noRd

.lta_covariance_coordinates.name: .lta_covariance_coordinates
.lta_covariance_coordinates.documentation: Covariance coordinates of a single LTA measurement block @param block Measurement parameters. @param fit Fit or parameter specification. @return Named unconstrained covariance coordinates from the core charts. @noRd

.lta_covariance_names.name: .lta_covariance_names
.lta_covariance_names.documentation: Names of a single LTA covariance coordinate block @param fit Fit carrying the measurement blocks. @param block Index of its measurement block. @param label Occasion label. @return Names in the LTA coefficient grammar. @noRd

.lta_pack.name: .lta_pack
.lta_pack.documentation: Pack a parameter list onto the estimation scale @noRd

.lta_unpack.name: .lta_unpack
.lta_unpack.documentation: Unpack the estimation-scale vector into a parameter list @noRd

.lta_group_scores.name: .lta_group_scores
.lta_group_scores.documentation: Per-group scores of the general transition model on the estimation scale @noRd

.lta_chart_scores.name: .lta_chart_scores
.lta_chart_scores.documentation: Per-group scores of one measurement block in its covariance chart  The gradient of the log likelihood with respect to each profile's mean and unconstrained covariance (`.multilpa_profile_gradients()`, which also handles indicators missing at random) is carried to the block's chart coordinates by the chain rule, with the Jacobian of the coordinates-to- covariance map. That map involves no data, so its Jacobian is taken by central differences of the same decoding the parameters came from; every structure, separable or constrained, is scored the same way.  @param fit The transition fit (its blocks anchor the chart). @param b The block's index. @param block The block's decoded parameters. @param phi Its chart coordinates. @param x The block's rows of the indicator matrix. @param e The expectation at these parameters. @param rows The block's rows. @param group_index,n_units Each row's group and the number of groups. @return A groups-by-coordinates matrix: means, then the chart. @noRd

From the EM point, L-BFGS-B maximizes the log likelihood with the analytic gradient, keeping log variances at or above log(min_variance); the point is kept only if the likelihood rises. @param spec The fit-shaped specification the pack/unpack and score helpers   read. @return A list with `parameters`, `log_likelihood`, `gradient` (max abs)   and `converged`. @noRd

.lta_three_step_inputs.documentation: The data of a three-step latent Markov model  @param x A covariate-free `lta()` fit with one group class. @param data The data frame it was fitted to. @param initial_covariates,transition_covariates Covariate names. @return A list with `layout`, `designs`, `emission`, `errors`, `n_profiles`   and `n_observations`. @noRd

.lta_occasion_posteriors.name: .lta_occasion_posteriors
.lta_occasion_posteriors.documentation: Each occasion's profile posteriors from its own indicators  The step-two classification of the three-step latent Markov model reads one occasion at a time: p(k | y_it) is proportional to w_k f_k(y_it), with the transition fit's measurement densities f_k and its profile shares w_k pooled over occasions, the latent class model of the pooled data (Di Mari, Oberski and Vermunt 2016). The transition fit's own posteriors would not do: they borrow from the person's other occasions through the chain, so their errors are not independent across occasions given the profiles, and the step-three model, which assumes they are, then removes the apparent moves the smoothing already removed.  @param x A transition fit. @return An observations-by-profiles matrix whose rows sum to one. @noRd

.lta_three_step_basis.name: .lta_three_step_basis
.lta_three_step_basis.documentation: Centre and scale a logit design's covariate columns @param design A design matrix whose first column is the intercept. @param rows Which rows carry information (inside a person's span). @return The `p x p` matrix `T` with `design %*% T` standardized: natural   coefficients are `T %*% standardized`. @noRd

.lta_three_step_evaluate.name: .lta_three_step_evaluate
.lta_three_step_evaluate.documentation: Log likelihood and per-person scores of the step-three chain  The score of a multinomial logit with known emissions is the design times the posterior count minus its expectation: for the initial logits, P(s_1 = l | data) - P(s_1 = l); for a move out of k, P(s_{t-1} = k, s_t = l | data) - P(s_{t-1} = k | data) P(l | k).  @param theta Coefficients on the standardized designs. @param inputs From `.lta_three_step_inputs()`, with standardized designs. @return A list with `log_likelihood` (per person) and `scores` (persons by   coefficients). @noRd

.lta_three_step_fit.documentation: Fit the step-three chain and its covariance  @param inputs From `.lta_three_step_inputs()`. @param vcov_type `"robust"` (the sandwich over persons) or `"observed"`. @return A list with `estimates`, `covariance`, `log_likelihood` and `labels`   (a data frame: `block`, `from`, `to`, `term`). @noRd

.lta_three_step.documentation: The three-step transition table of r3step() @return A base data frame, one row per initial and transition coefficient. @noRd

.multilpa_count_frame.name: .multilpa_count_frame
.multilpa_count_frame.documentation: Effective class memberships at both levels as a tidy table  Read from the summary's stored counts where there are any and summed from the posteriors otherwise, so the one definition serves a fit and its summary alike. A family with no discrete group classes contributes one level rather than an empty second one.  @param x A fitted model of this package, or its summary. @return One row per class at each level the object has. @noRd

.multilpa_covariance_frame.name: .multilpa_covariance_frame
.multilpa_covariance_frame.documentation: Within-profile residual covariances as a tidy table  The diagonal parameterization carries no covariance array, but it does state a covariance matrix: the variances on the diagonal and exact zeros off it. Reporting that explicitly means one shape answers both parameterizations.  @param x A `summary_multilpa` object. @return One row per profile and ordered pair of continuous indicators. @noRd

.multilpa_fit_frame.name: .multilpa_fit_frame
.multilpa_fit_frame.documentation: The one-row description of a fit as a tidy table  Family-shaped rather than one column set for every family: a random intercept records its integration diagnostics and a covariate model its predictor counts, and padding those onto a two-level fit would make the common case mostly `NA`. Comparing fits across families is what the information criteria are for, and that table does have one column set.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @return One row, describing the whole fit. @noRd

.multilpa_one.name: .multilpa_one
.multilpa_one.documentation: One scalar, or a stated absence  A field an older fit or another family does not carry is `NULL`, and one recorded per class is longer than one. Either would corrupt a one-row frame, so both become the absent value of the right type.  @param value The field. @param absent What to report when it is not a single value. @return A length-one vector. @noRd

.mixture_update_regression.name: .mixture_update_regression
.mixture_update_regression.documentation: M-step for the regression coefficients  Newton-Raphson on the posterior-weighted complete-data log likelihood, `sum_ik tau_ik log f_k(y_i)`, over the class-specific coefficients and the coefficients shared by every class, holding the Gaussian variances fixed. The objective is concave in the coefficients for all three canonical-link families, and a step is halved until it does not decrease the objective, so the update can only increase the EM likelihood.  @param spec The model specification. @param params The current parameter list. @param tau Row posteriors, `n x K`. @param max_newton Maximum Newton iterations. @return The parameter list with `beta` and `common` updated, and   `separation` set when a class's coefficients diverged. @noRd

.mixture_update_variance.name: .mixture_update_variance
.mixture_update_variance.documentation: M-step for the Gaussian variances or the negative-binomial dispersions  `sigma2` holds each class's dispersion parameter: the residual variance of the Gaussian family, the dispersion alpha of the negative binomial (variance mu + alpha mu^2); binomial and Poisson classes have none.  @param spec The model specification. @param params The parameter list. @param tau Row posteriors. @return The parameter list with `sigma2` updated. @noRd

.mixture_update_dispersion.name: .mixture_update_dispersion
.mixture_update_dispersion.documentation: M-step for the negative-binomial dispersions  Modified Newton on the log dispersion (one per class, or one shared), the means held: the curvature's sign is reflected so every step ascends, and a step is halved until the posterior-weighted log likelihood does not fall. Where the overdispersion score at alpha = 0, sum tau ((y - mu)^2 - y) / 2, is not positive the maximum is the Poisson limit (Karush-Kuhn-Tucker), and the dispersion is set to its floor.  @param spec The model specification. @param params The parameter list (`sigma2` holds the dispersions). @param tau Row posteriors. @param max_newton Most Newton steps. @return The parameter list with `sigma2` updated. @noRd

.mixture_em_settings.name: .mixture_em_settings
.mixture_em_settings.documentation: EM settings of the regression and growth mixtures  Their M-steps solve inner Newton (or conditional) maximizations, whose rounding allows a looser decrease guard than a closed-form step; a step to a non-finite likelihood (a separating logit) ends the run, and a decrease is a classed defect. @noRd

.mixture_em.name: .mixture_em
.mixture_em.documentation: Run EM from a starting point  @param spec The model specification. @param params Starting parameters. @param max_iter Maximum EM iterations. @param tol Relative convergence tolerance on the log likelihood. @return A list with `params`, `expectation`, `converged`, `iterations`,   `history` and `degenerate` (a class emptied or a variance hit the floor). @noRd

enumerate_regressions.name: enumerate_regressions
enumerate_regressions.documentation: Compare mixture regressions with different numbers of classes  Fits [mixture_regression()] for every requested number of classes (crossed with numbers of group classes, for the two-level model) and returns their fit statistics in one table. Optionally adds a parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio test of `k - 1` against `k` classes, at the same number of group classes (McLachlan 1987; Nylund, Asparouhov and Muthen 2007): outcomes are simulated from the `k - 1` class fit, both models are refitted to every replicate, and the p-value is `(1 + b) / (1 + B)`, where `b` counts replicate statistics at least as large as the observed one and `B` is the number of replicates requested.  @inheritParams mixture_regression @param n_classes Positive integer class counts to fit. Default `1:4`. @param n_group_classes Positive integer group-class counts (two-level   model; needs `id`), crossed with `n_classes`. Default 1. @param bootstrap Number of bootstrap replicates for the likelihood-ratio   test; `0` (the default) skips it. Not available with sampling weights. @param bootstrap_starts Random starts for each bootstrap refit. Default 3. @param ... Further arguments to [mixture_regression()], such as `family`,   `id`, `class_level`, `common`, `membership` or `variance`. `n_classes`,   `n_group_classes` and `vcov_type` are not accepted here. @return An object of class `latents_regression_enumeration`. Its table   (from [as.data.frame()] or `get_results(x, "fit")`) has one row per   model, with columns `n_classes`, `n_group_classes`, `log_likelihood`,   `n_parameters`, `aic`, `bic`, `bic_rows`, `sabic`, `icl`, `entropy`,   `smallest_share`, `converged`, `n_best_replicated`, `note` (why a model   could not be fitted), `best_bic` (`TRUE` for the minimum-BIC row), and,   with `bootstrap > 0`, `blrt_statistic`, `blrt_p_value`,   `blrt_replicates` (the successful replicates) and `blrt_flagged` (the   failed, unconverged, separated or reversed-likelihood replicates). The   test columns are `NA` where the `k - 1` or `k` class model is missing   or failed, and the p-value is `NA` if any requested replicate fails   validation.   `get_results(x, "model", n_classes = , n_group_classes = )` returns one   fitted model. `summary()` returns the same table as [as.data.frame()].   `plot()` draws AIC, BIC, SABIC and ICL across the classes (see   [plot_enumeration()] for its other views, and `plot_views(x)` for the   views a regression grid offers). @section Conditions:   A model whose fit raises `latents_no_valid_start` or `latents_bad_data`   at some count gets a row of `NA` with the condition message in `note`;   other errors stop the enumeration. Invalid `n_classes`,   `n_group_classes`, `bootstrap` or `bootstrap_starts` fail the argument   checks. `latents_bad_argument` for an invalid `seed`, for `n_classes`,   `n_group_classes` or `vcov_type` passed through `...`, for a bootstrap   test whose outcome is not a plain column name, and from `get_results()`   for a model that is not in the grid or could not be fitted.   `latents_unsupported_weights` for a bootstrap test with sampling   weights. `latents_failed_replicates` is warned, and the p-value is `NA`,   when the observed fits or any replicate fail validation. @references McLachlan, G. J. (1987). On bootstrapping the likelihood ratio test statistic for the number of components in a normal mixture. *Applied Statistics*, 36, 318--324.  Nylund, K. L., Asparouhov, T., & Muthen, B. O. (2007). Deciding on the number of classes in latent class analysis and growth mixture modeling: A Monte Carlo simulation study. *Structural Equation Modeling*, 14, 535--569. @examples classes <- enumerate_regressions(score ~ hours, data = study_hours,                                  n_classes = 1:3, n_starts = 3, seed = 1) classes \donttest{ with_test <- enumerate_regressions(score ~ hours, data = study_hours,                                    n_classes = 1:2, n_starts = 3, seed = 1,                                    bootstrap = 19) as.data.frame(with_test) } @export
