.mixture_confint_rows.name: .mixture_confint_rows
.mixture_confint_rows.documentation: Rows of a `confint()` result picked by `parm` @param parm Parameter names, or positions among `names`. @param names The names of the estimates, in order. @return Integer positions; raises `latents_bad_argument` for a name or   position that is not an estimate. @noRd

.ordinal_response.name: .ordinal_response
.ordinal_response.documentation: Resolve an ordinal outcome to category codes  An ordered factor or a factor is read in its level order; whole numbers are read as categories in increasing order. Categories are those observed (the model frame drops unused factor levels), because a category no row takes has no finite threshold. With `levels`, the outcome of new data is coded against the fitted categories instead.  @param response The model response. @param levels `NULL`, or the fitted category labels. @return A list of numeric `y` (codes 1..C), `trials` (ones), `levels`   (labels), `values` (the categories as given: factor levels or numbers)   and `kind` (`"ordered"`, `"factor"` or `"numeric"`); raises   `latents_bad_data`. @noRd

.ordinal_check_identified.name: .ordinal_check_identified
.ordinal_check_identified.documentation: Refuse an ordinal mixture that its data cannot identify  With one outcome per class assignment (rows as the classified units), a mixture of two-category outcomes is a mixture of Bernoullis, itself a Bernoulli (Follmann and Lambert 1991), so the same rule as for `family = "binomial"` applies; and with no predictors at all a mixture of categorical distributions is again one categorical distribution, whatever the number of categories. Otherwise the classes are identified by how the predictors shift the category probabilities, which needs continuous predictors; `class_level = "group"` identifies them through each group's repeated outcomes.  @param n_categories Number of categories C. @param n_classes Number of classes. @param nesting The nesting. @param n_predictors Number of design columns (class-specific and shared). @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises `latents_not_identified`. @noRd

.ordinal_check_patterns.name: .ordinal_check_patterns
.ordinal_check_patterns.documentation: Refuse a single-level ordinal mixture with too few covariate patterns  With one outcome per row, the data determine at most C - 1 category probabilities for each distinct covariate pattern (the class-specific and shared design rows, the offset and the membership covariates), so P patterns identify at most P (C - 1) parameters. A mixture with more free parameters -- every predictor discrete, say one binary factor -- is not identified: its information matrix is singular at every estimate.  @param spec The ordinal specification. @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises `latents_not_identified`. @noRd

.ordinal_threshold_labels.name: .ordinal_threshold_labels
.ordinal_threshold_labels.documentation: Threshold labels, `"lower|upper"` as MASS::polr() names them @param spec The model specification. @return A character vector of length C - 1. @noRd

.ordinal_start_thresholds.name: .ordinal_start_thresholds
.ordinal_start_thresholds.documentation: Starting thresholds: the logits of the pooled cumulative proportions  The proportional-odds fit without predictors, the same for every class; each category is observed, so every proportion is inside (0, 1). @param spec The model specification. @return A `(C - 1) x K` matrix. @noRd

.ordinal_log1mexp.name: .ordinal_log1mexp
.ordinal_log1mexp.documentation: log(1 - exp(-gap)) for gap > 0, accurate at both ends  `-expm1(-gap)` near zero and `log1p(-exp(-gap))` beyond log 2 (Maechler 2012, "Accurately computing log(1 - exp(-|a|))"); an infinite gap gives zero, and a gap that is not positive (thresholds out of order) gives `-Inf`, an impossible model. @param gap Numeric vector or matrix. @return The same shape as `gap`. @noRd

.ordinal_bounds.name: .ordinal_bounds
.ordinal_bounds.documentation: The bounds of every row's category under every class  @param spec The model specification. @param params The parameter list (`thresholds`). @param eta Linear predictor matrix, `n x K`. @return A list of `n x K` matrices: `upper` (a = t_y - eta), `lower`   (b = t_y-1 - eta) and `gap` (a - b). @noRd

.ordinal_log_density.name: .ordinal_log_density
.ordinal_log_density.documentation: Row-by-class log probabilities of the observed categories @param spec The model specification. @param params The parameter list. @param eta Linear predictor matrix, `n x K`. @return An `n x K` matrix. @noRd

.ordinal_derivatives.name: .ordinal_derivatives
.ordinal_derivatives.documentation: First and second derivatives of the log probability in its two bounds  With r = 1 / (exp(g) - 1) and s = exp(g) / (exp(g) - 1)^2: d/da = 1 - F(a) + r, d/db = -F(b) - r, d2/da2 = -F(a)(1 - F(a)) - s, d2/db2 = -F(b)(1 - F(b)) - s, d2/da db = s. An infinite bound gives zero in every term that involves it. The derivative in eta is -(d/da + d/db) = F(a) + F(b) - 1.  @inheritParams .ordinal_log_density @return A list of `n x K` matrices `upper`, `lower`, `upper_upper`,   `lower_lower`, `upper_lower`. @noRd

.ordinal_indicators.name: .ordinal_indicators
.ordinal_indicators.documentation: Which threshold bounds each row's category from above and from below @param y Category codes. @param n_categories Number of categories C. @return A list of `n x (C - 1)` indicator matrices `upper` (threshold y)   and `lower` (threshold y - 1). @noRd

.ordinal_ordered.name: .ordinal_ordered
.ordinal_ordered.documentation: Whether every class's thresholds are strictly increasing @noRd

.ordinal_update.name: .ordinal_update
.ordinal_update.documentation: M-step for an ordinal regression mixture  Newton-Raphson on the posterior-weighted complete-data log likelihood, `sum_ik tau_ik log P_k(y_i)`, jointly over every class's thresholds and slopes and the slopes shared by every class (`common`), which couple the classes. The objective is concave, so the Newton direction ascends; a step is halved until the objective does not fall and the thresholds stay ordered, so the update can only increase the EM likelihood.  @param spec The model specification. @param params The current parameter list. @param tau Row posteriors, `n x K`. @param max_newton Maximum Newton iterations. @return The parameter list with `thresholds`, `beta` and `common` updated   and `separation` set when a threshold or slope diverged. @noRd

.ordinal_threshold_jacobian.name: .ordinal_threshold_jacobian
.ordinal_threshold_jacobian.documentation: Jacobian of one class's natural thresholds in their packed coordinates  The coordinates are the first threshold and the logs of the gaps, so d t_j / d first = 1 and d t_j / d log gap_l = gap_l for l <= j. @param thresholds One class's ordered thresholds. @return A `(C - 1) x (C - 1)` matrix, rows thresholds, columns coordinates. @noRd

.ordinal_pack.name: .ordinal_pack
.ordinal_pack.documentation: Pack every class's thresholds into named unconstrained coordinates @param spec The model specification. @param params The parameter list. @return A named numeric vector: per class, `threshold.class_k.<a|b>` and   `log_threshold_gap.class_k.<b|c>` for the gaps. @noRd

.ordinal_natural.name: .ordinal_natural
.ordinal_natural.documentation: Natural thresholds from packed coordinates, one class per column @param values Coordinates, `(C - 1) * K` of them in packing order. @param m Number of thresholds per class. @return An `m x K` matrix of ordered thresholds. @noRd

.ordinal_threshold_scores.name: .ordinal_threshold_scores
.ordinal_threshold_scores.documentation: Per-row scores of the threshold coordinates  Fisher's identity: each row's score is its posterior-weighted complete-data score, here in the natural thresholds, carried to the packed coordinates by the Jacobian. @param spec The model specification. @param params The parameter list. @param tau Row posteriors. @param derivatives From `.ordinal_derivatives()`. @return An `n x ((C - 1) K)` matrix in packing order. @noRd

.ordinal_probabilities.name: .ordinal_probabilities
.ordinal_probabilities.documentation: Category probabilities of one class @param eta Linear predictors (a vector). @param thresholds That class's ordered thresholds. @return A `length(eta) x C` matrix whose rows sum to one. @noRd

.ordinal_expected_scores.name: .ordinal_expected_scores
.ordinal_expected_scores.documentation: Expected category score of every row under every class  The categories are scored 1..C in their order, so the class "mean" of an ordinal outcome is sum_c c P_k(Y = c | x), on the scale of the category codes. @param eta Linear predictor matrix, `n x K`. @param thresholds A `(C - 1) x K` threshold matrix. @return An `n x K` matrix. @noRd

.ordinal_categories.name: .ordinal_categories
.ordinal_categories.documentation: Category values from codes, in the type the outcome was given  A factor outcome comes back as a factor with the fitted levels (ordered if it was), numbers as the fitted category values, so a simulated outcome can replace the observed column and be refitted. @param spec The model specification. @param codes Category codes. @return A factor or numeric vector. @noRd

.ordinal_draw.name: .ordinal_draw
.ordinal_draw.documentation: Draw one outcome per row from its class's category probabilities @param spec The model specification. @param params The parameter list. @param classes Each row's class. @return Category values, as `.ordinal_categories()`. @noRd

.ordinal_probability_table.name: .ordinal_probability_table
.ordinal_probability_table.documentation: Category probabilities of every row under every class, as a tidy table @param spec The (possibly new-data) specification. @param params The parameter list. @param priors Row-by-class prior probabilities. @return A data frame, one row per data row, class and category: `row`,   `class`, `category`, `prior`, `probability`. @noRd

.ordinal_threshold_table.name: .ordinal_threshold_table
.ordinal_threshold_table.documentation: Threshold rows of the coefficient table  The natural thresholds with delta-method standard errors from the packed coordinates (an exact Jacobian). @param spec The model specification. @param inference The inference list (`theta`, `vcov`). @param level Confidence level. @return A data frame with `class`, `term` (`"threshold:<a|b>"`) and the   Wald columns. @noRd

.ordinal_trajectory_band.name: .ordinal_trajectory_band
.ordinal_trajectory_band.documentation: Each ordinal class's expected-score trajectory with a delta-method band  The expected category score depends on the class's thresholds as well as its linear predictor, so its standard error comes from the delta method over every packed estimate, and the band is formed on the score scale, clipped to the range of the categories. @param x A trajectory fit with `family = "ordinal"`. @param design The regression design of the rows (class-specific columns,   then shared ones). @param inference The inference list. @param z The critical value. @param classes The class names. @return As `.trajectory_band()`. @noRd

.mixture_new_spec.name: .mixture_new_spec
.mixture_new_spec.documentation: Rebuild a specification on new data with the fitted design  Uses the fit's terms and factor levels, so a new data frame yields columns in the fitted order. The outcome is resolved only when `with_response`.  @param object A `latents_mixture_regression` fit. @param newdata A data frame. @param with_response Whether the outcome must be present. @return A specification list usable by the engine. @noRd

.mixture_row_priors.name: .mixture_row_priors
.mixture_row_priors.documentation: Prior class probabilities of every row, before seeing its outcome @noRd

.mixture_prediction_data.name: .mixture_prediction_data
.mixture_prediction_data.documentation: Translate evaluated prediction-data failures into the public condition @param expression A prediction specification or response expression. @return Its value, or an error of class `latents_bad_data`. @noRd

.mixture_prediction_trials.name: .mixture_prediction_trials
.mixture_prediction_trials.documentation: Resolve binomial exposure without changing the units of a prediction  The training response gives the fitted trial counts. New counts can come from an explicit vector/column, or the evaluated response when supplied. Without either, an aggregated fit cannot assume one trial per new row. @param object A fitted mixture regression. @param newdata `NULL` or the new data frame. @param spec The specification prepared for prediction. @param trials `NULL`, a numeric vector, or a column name. @param posterior Whether the outcome is being used to classify rows. @return A numeric trial-count vector of length `spec$n`. @noRd

.mixture_trajectory_views.name: .mixture_trajectory_views
.mixture_trajectory_views.documentation: The views of a mixture regression that classifies persons @return A character vector of `what` values. @noRd

.mixture_plot_views.name: .mixture_plot_views
.mixture_plot_views.documentation: The views a mixture regression's plot() draws  Every fit draws the fitted values, coefficients and posteriors; a fit that classifies persons (`class_level = "group"`) also draws trajectories. @param x A `latents_mixture_regression` fit. @return A character vector of `what` values. @noRd

.mixture_model_data.name: .mixture_model_data
.mixture_model_data.documentation: The data columns the model used, in fitted row order @noRd

.mixture_typical_rows.name: .mixture_typical_rows
.mixture_typical_rows.documentation: Rows varying one predictor, others held at mean or reference level @noRd

.mixture_class_scales.name: .mixture_class_scales
.mixture_class_scales.documentation: Colour, fill, shape and line-type scales for mixture classes @param classes Class labels, in order. @param lines Whether to add the line-type scale. @return A list of ggplot2 scales. @noRd

.mixture_null_params.name: .mixture_null_params
.mixture_null_params.documentation: Neutral parameters to seed the first M-step @param spec The model specification. @return A parameter list. @noRd

.mixture_soften.name: .mixture_soften
.mixture_soften.documentation: Soften a hard partition into posterior-like weights @param labels Integer labels. @param n_categories Number of categories. @return A matrix whose rows sum to one. @noRd

.mixture_residual_labels.name: .mixture_residual_labels
.mixture_residual_labels.documentation: Labels from the residuals of one pooled regression  Classes that differ in intercept separate along the residuals of a pooled fit, so cutting them into quantile bins is a deterministic start that finds the common case directly.  @param spec The model specification. @return Integer labels per top-level unit. @noRd

.mixture_seed_expectation.name: .mixture_seed_expectation
.mixture_seed_expectation.documentation: Pseudo E-step from labels, used to launch EM @param spec The model specification. @param labels Labels per top-level unit. @param group_labels Group-class labels (two-level model only). @return A list shaped like `.mixture_expectation()`'s result. @noRd

.mixture_run_starts.name: .mixture_run_starts
.mixture_run_starts.documentation: Run EM from every start @param spec The model specification. @param n_starts Number of random starts. @param max_iter Maximum EM iterations. @param tol Convergence tolerance. @return A list of EM results, the first from the residual start. @noRd

.mixture_select.name: .mixture_select
.mixture_select.documentation: Choose among starts, order the classes, and assemble the fit @param spec The model specification. @param results EM results from `.mixture_run_starts()`. @param select_start Selection rule. @return An object of class `latents_mixture_regression` without inference. @noRd

.mixture_count_parameters.name: .mixture_count_parameters
.mixture_count_parameters.documentation: Number of free parameters @param spec The model specification. @return A single integer. @noRd

.mixture_order_classes.name: .mixture_order_classes
.mixture_order_classes.documentation: Put classes in a deterministic order  Classes are ordered by decreasing size, then by their first coefficient. Group classes are ordered by decreasing probability of the (largest) first class among their rows: group classes exist to differ in that composition, whereas their sizes are often nearly equal, and ordering on a near-tie would let the labels swap between otherwise identical fits. Label switching would otherwise make the numbering depend on the start that won.  @param spec The model specification. @param params The parameter list. @param expectation The E-step at `params`. @return The reordered parameter list. @noRd

.mixture_class_orders.name: .mixture_class_orders
.mixture_class_orders.documentation: The canonical order of the classes and group classes  Classes by decreasing size, ties by their first coefficient; group classes by how much of the largest class they hold, then by size.  @param spec The structure. @param params The parameter list (for `beta`). @param expectation The structure's E-step. @return A list of `class_order` and `group_order` (`NULL` for one level). @noRd

.mixture_permute.name: .mixture_permute
.mixture_permute.documentation: Relabel classes and group classes  Every logit block is re-expressed with the new first class (and first group class) as its reference, which leaves the likelihood unchanged.  @param spec The model specification. @param params The parameter list. @param class_order New order of the classes (old indices). @param group_order New order of the group classes, or `NULL`. @return The relabelled parameter list. @noRd

mixture_regression.name: mixture_regression
mixture_regression.documentation: Fit a finite mixture of regressions  Fits a regression whose coefficients differ across `n_classes` latent classes and returns the fitted model: the class-specific regressions, the class sizes and every row's posterior class membership, estimated jointly by maximum likelihood. This is clusterwise, latent class or mixture regression (DeSarbo and Cron 1988; Wedel and DeSarbo 1995).  @section Nesting: `class_level` and `n_group_classes` choose one of three likelihoods. \describe{   \item{Single level (`id = NULL`)}{Every row is its own unit with its own     class.}   \item{`class_level = "group"`}{All rows of a group (`id`) belong to the     same class: the regression mixture for repeated measures, as     `flexmix(y ~ x | id)`. A group's likelihood contribution is the product     of its rows' densities.}   \item{`class_level = "observation"` with `id` and `n_group_classes >= 2`}{     Each row has its own class, and a second-level group class sets the     class probabilities within its groups (Vermunt 2003).     With `n_group_classes = 1`, `id` enters only the `"robust"` standard     errors, which are then clustered on `id`.} }  @section Growth mixture models: With repeated measures of persons (`id`, `class_level = "group"`), a time predictor in `formula` gives every class its own trajectory: latent class growth analysis (Nagin 2005). `random` adds random effects within classes, so that persons vary around their class trajectory: the growth mixture model (Verbeke and Lesaffre 1996; Muthen and Shedden 1999). Within class k, person i's outcomes are \deqn{y_i = X_i \beta_k + Z_i b_i + e_i, \quad b_i \sim N(0, G_k), \quad e_i \sim N(0, \sigma_k^2 I),}{y_i = X_i beta_k + Z_i b_i + e_i, b_i ~ N(0, G_k), e_i ~ N(0, sigma_k^2 I),} with `Z` built from `random`. The likelihood is exact (Gaussian, no numerical integration); estimation is EM with the random effects as missing data, finished by quasi-Newton with analytic scores. Such a fit has class `latents_growth_mixture`; its tables and plots are described on [get_results()] and [plot()][latents-plots]. Random effects require the gaussian family, `id` and `class_level = "group"`.  With `residual_correlation`, the residuals also carry a process shared by the classes, \eqn{e_i \sim N(0, W_i + \sigma_k^2 I)}{e_i ~ N(0, W_i + sigma_k^2 I)}: a continuous-time autoregressive process (`"ar"`) or Brownian motion (`"brownian"`) over `residual_time`, as in `lcmm::hlme(cor = )`; at hlme's estimates the two likelihoods agree (`equivalence/test-growth-correlated-lcmm.R` in the source repository).  With `cluster`, persons are nested in clusters (students in schools) and the multilevel growth mixture model is fitted: each cluster belongs to a group class h, and the trajectory-class logits of its persons have a group-class-specific intercept and shared covariate slopes, \deqn{L = \prod_j \sum_h \omega_h \prod_{i \in j} \sum_k \pi_{k|h} f_k(y_i)}{L = prod_j sum_h omega_h prod_(i in j) sum_k pi_(k|h) f_k(y_i)} (Asparouhov and Muthen 2008; Vermunt 2003). `group_membership` names cluster-level covariates of the group class. The group classes are returned by `get_results(fit, "group_classes")` and `"clusters"`.  @section Families: `"gaussian"` (identity link, a residual standard deviation per class, or one shared under `variance = "equal"`), `"binomial"` (logit link; the outcome is 0/1, logical, a two-level factor whose second level is the success, or `cbind(successes, failures)`), `"poisson"` (log link; `offset()` terms in the formula are honoured) and `"negative_binomial"` (log link, NB2: variance mu + alpha mu^2 with a dispersion alpha per class, or one shared under `variance = "equal"`, for overdispersed counts; a dispersion estimated at zero is the Poisson limit and raises `latents_boundary`).  `"ordinal"` fits a cumulative-logit (proportional-odds) regression within each class (McCullagh 1980), \deqn{P(Y \le c \mid x, k) = F(t_{kc} - x'\beta_k), \quad c = 1, \ldots, C - 1,}{P(Y <= c | x, k) = plogis(t_kc - x' beta_k), c = 1, ..., C - 1,} with ordered thresholds \eqn{t_{k1} < \ldots < t_{k,C-1}}{t_k1 < ... < t_k,C-1} per class in place of the intercept, and the parametrization of `MASS::polr()`: a positive slope moves the class towards higher categories. The outcome is an ordered factor, a factor (its levels taken in order) or whole-number categories; the categories are those observed, at least two. `common` terms share their slopes across classes, and `offset()` is honoured; the formula's intercept is replaced by the thresholds, so it must not be removed. The thresholds appear in the coefficient table as terms `"threshold:<lower>|<upper>"`, and `exp_estimate` of a slope is the cumulative odds ratio of a higher category. The class "mean" of an ordinal outcome (fitted values, `predict()`, trajectories) is the expected category score \eqn{\sum_c c P(Y = c)}{sum_c c P(Y = c)}, the categories scored 1 to C in order; `predict(type = "probabilities")` gives the category probabilities. With one outcome per class assignment, an ordinal mixture with no predictors or with two categories (the logistic mixture of `"binomial"`) is not identified and is refused with `latents_not_identified`, unless `class_level = "group"` gives each class assignment several outcomes. A single-level mixture is also refused when it has more free parameters than P (C - 1), the number of free category probabilities in P distinct covariate patterns (for example two classes and one binary factor).  A mixture of Bernoulli regressions with one trial per unit is not identified (a mixture of Bernoullis is again a Bernoulli), so a binary outcome requires `class_level = "group"` (several rows per class assignment) or binomial counts with more than one trial per row; other binary specifications are refused.  @param formula A model formula `outcome ~ predictors`. Factors, interactions   and `offset()` are supported. @param data A data frame. @param n_classes Number of regression classes. @param family `"gaussian"` (default), `"binomial"`, `"poisson"`,   `"negative_binomial"` or `"ordinal"` (proportional-odds cumulative logit;   see *Families*). @param id `NULL` (default), or the name of the column identifying groups   (persons, schools, ...). @param class_level `"observation"` (default; each row has its own class) or   `"group"` (all rows of a group share a class; requires `id`). @param n_group_classes Number of second-level group classes (default 1,   no second level), for `class_level = "observation"` with `id`, or for the   clusters of a multilevel growth mixture (`cluster`). @param common `NULL`, or the predictor terms whose coefficients are   shared by every class: variable names such as `"age"`, or a one-sided   formula such as `~ age`. Each term must appear in `formula`. @param membership Covariates predicting class membership (a multinomial   logit, the first class as the reference): variable names such as   `"age"`, or a one-sided formula (`~ 1`, the default, for none).   Row-level for `"observation"`; constant within groups for `"group"`. @param group_membership Group-level covariates predicting the group class,   for the two-level model, as names or a one-sided formula. Must be   constant within groups. @param variance `"varying"` (default; a residual standard deviation, or a   negative-binomial dispersion, per class) or `"equal"` (one shared).   Gaussian and negative-binomial families only. @param n_starts Number of random starts (default 10), besides one start   built from the residuals of a pooled regression. Every start runs up to   50 EM iterations; the better half (at least two) continue to   convergence. @param max_iter Maximum EM iterations per start (default 1000). @param tol Relative convergence tolerance on the log likelihood (default   `1e-8`). @param min_variance Floor for a Gaussian residual variance, relative to the   outcome's variance (default `1e-6`). Starts in which a class reaches the   floor (fits too few rows exactly) are set aside. @param seed `NULL` (default) or an integer seed. The caller's random state   is restored afterwards. @param missing `"error"` (default) refuses rows with missing values in any   variable the model uses; `"omit"` drops them with a   `latents_rows_dropped` warning stating how many. @param select_start `"likelihood"` (default) keeps the start with the   highest likelihood; `"converged"` prefers the best start that converged. @param vcov_type Covariance of the estimates stored with the fit:   `"observed"` (default; inverse observed information), `"robust"` (sandwich with   the CR1 factor `G / (G - 1)`, clustered on the top-level unit, or on `id` for a single-level fit given   `id`) or `"opg"` (outer product of the scores). `"none"` skips inference. @param weights `NULL`, or the name of a numeric column of `data` with a   sampling weight per independent unit: per row without `id`, per `id`   group otherwise (constant within it). Pseudo maximum likelihood with the   weights scaled to sum to the number of units; `vcov_type` defaults to   `"robust"` and refuses `"observed"` and `"opg"`. The information   criteria use the weighted log likelihood; the entropy term of ICL sums   the units' own posteriors unweighted, as in the profile models.  @param random `NULL` (default; no random effects), or the random effects   within classes: variable names such as `"time"` (a random intercept and   a random slope on `time`) or `"intercept"` (random intercepts only), or a   one-sided formula such as `~ 1 + time`. A slope without a random   intercept needs the formula `~ 0 + time`. See *Growth mixture models*. @param random_covariance How the random-effect covariance differs across   classes: `"varying"` (default; one per class), `"equal"` (one shared matrix, as   `lcmm::hlme()` with `nwg = FALSE`) or `"proportional"` (a shared matrix   times a class-specific scale, the last class's being one; `nwg = TRUE`). @param random_diagonal `TRUE` for uncorrelated random effects (a diagonal   covariance, as `idiag = TRUE` in lcmm); default `FALSE`. @param cluster `NULL` (default), or the name of a column grouping the   persons (`id`) into clusters, such as schools, for the multilevel growth   mixture model (with `random`): each cluster belongs to one of   `n_group_classes` group classes, which sets the trajectory-class   probabilities of its persons. The clusters are the independent units of   the likelihood, the standard errors and the BIC; with   `n_group_classes = 1` the model is the single-level growth mixture with   clusters as those units, comparable by BIC with fits with more group   classes. See *Growth mixture models*. @param residual_correlation `"none"` (default) for independent residuals   within a person; with `random`, `"ar"` adds a continuous-time   autoregressive process, covariance `sd^2 exp(-rate |t - s|)`, and   `"brownian"` Brownian motion, `sd^2 min(t, s)`, to the residual   variance, shared by the classes: `lcmm::hlme(cor = AR(time))` and   `cor = BM(time)`. The model without the process is fitted first from   every start; the process is then estimated jointly with all other   parameters. A process the data cannot separate from the residual variance or the   random effects is left on its bound and warned about   (`latents_random_boundary`); its rows then have no standard error.   Refused with `latents_bad_argument` without `random`. @param residual_time The numeric column the process runs over; by default   the first numeric variable of `random`, or else of the predictors.   Brownian motion needs non-negative times (`latents_bad_data`). @return An object of class `latents_mixture_regression`, or   `latents_growth_mixture` when `random` is given. [as.data.frame()]   returns the coefficient table and [get_results()] every table by name   (described there); [predict()], [plot()], [summary()], [coef()],   [vcov()], [confint()], [logLik()] and [nobs()] also apply.  @section Conditions:   `latents_bad_argument` for an inconsistent specification;   `latents_bad_data` for an outcome outside the family's support or a   covariate that varies within a group where it may not;   `latents_not_identified` for a binary outcome with one trial per class   assignment, or an ordinal mixture with one outcome per class assignment   and two categories, no predictors, or fewer distinct covariate patterns   times C - 1 than free parameters; `latents_missing_data` for missing   values under   `missing = "error"`; `latents_rows_dropped` (warning) under   `missing = "omit"`; `latents_no_valid_start` when every start   degenerated; `latents_unconverged` (warning) when the selected start did   not converge; `latents_degenerate_start` (warning) when some starts   degenerated; `latents_separation` (warning) when a coefficient diverged;   `latents_failed_starts` (warning) when some growth-mixture starts could   not be built (they are marked `"failed"` in the starts table);   `latents_boundary` (warning) for a negative-binomial dispersion at the   Poisson limit; `latents_random_boundary` (warning) for a degenerate   random-effect covariance; `latents_singular_information` (warning) when   some standard errors cannot be computed.  @references Asparouhov, T., & Muthen, B. (2008). Multilevel mixture models. In G. R. Hancock & K. M. Samuelsen (Eds.), *Advances in latent variable mixture models* (pp. 27--51). Information Age.  McCullagh, P. (1980). Regression models for ordinal data. *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B*, 42, 109--142.  Muthen, B., & Shedden, K. (1999). Finite mixture modeling with mixture outcomes using the EM algorithm. *Biometrics*, 55, 463--469.  Nagin, D. S. (2005). *Group-based modeling of development*. Harvard University Press.  Proust-Lima, C., Philipps, V., & Liquet, B. (2017). Estimation of extended mixed models using latent classes and latent processes: the R package lcmm. *Journal of Statistical Software*, 78(2), 1--56.  Verbeke, G., & Lesaffre, E. (1996). A linear mixed-effects model with heterogeneity in the random-effects population. *Journal of the American Statistical Association*, 91, 217--221.  DeSarbo, W. S., & Cron, W. L. (1988). A maximum likelihood methodology for clusterwise linear regression. *Journal of Classification*, 5, 249--282.  Wedel, M., & DeSarbo, W. S. (1995). A mixture likelihood approach for generalized linear models. *Journal of Classification*, 12, 21--55.  Follmann, D. A., & Lambert, D. (1991). Identifiability of finite mixtures of logistic regression models. *Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference*, 27, 375--381.  Vermunt, J. K. (2003). Multilevel latent class models. *Sociological Methodology*, 33, 213--239.  Leisch, F. (2004). FlexMix: A general framework for finite mixture models and latent class regression in R. *Journal of Statistical Software*, 11(8).  @seealso [enumerate_regressions()] to compare numbers of classes. @examples fit <- mixture_regression(score ~ hours, data = study_hours, n_classes = 2,                           n_starts = 3, seed = 1) fit as.data.frame(fit) get_results(fit, "classes")  # One class per student, several rows per student: by_student <- mixture_regression(score ~ hours, data = study_hours, n_classes = 2,                                  id = "student", class_level = "group",                                  n_starts = 3, seed = 1) get_results(by_student, "fit")  \donttest{ # Students nested in schools, each school in one of two group classes: schools <- mixture_regression(score ~ wave, growth_schools, n_classes = 2,                               id = "student", class_level = "group",                               random = "wave", random_covariance = "equal",                               cluster = "school", n_group_classes = 2,                               n_starts = 2, seed = 1) get_results(schools, "group_classes") } @export

.mixture_as_formula.name: .mixture_as_formula
.mixture_as_formula.documentation: Read variable names as a one-sided formula  `"time"` means `~ 1 + time` and `c("age", "sex")` means `~ 1 + age + sex`; `"intercept"` alone means `~ 1`. Formulas pass through unchanged, so anything names cannot say (no intercept, interactions, transformations) is still written as a formula.  A formula built from names, or one without variables (the default `~ 1`), gets the base environment: its variables all come from the data, and the environment it was made in -- the fitting function's own frame, holding the data and every start's result -- would otherwise be stored (and serialized) with the fit.  @param value `NULL`, a character vector or a formula. @param argument The argument's name, for the message. @return `NULL` or a one-sided formula; raises `latents_bad_argument`. @noRd

.mixture_weight_spec.name: .mixture_weight_spec
.mixture_weight_spec.documentation: Attach sampling weights to a mixture-regression specification  The independent units are the rows, or the `id` groups when `id` is given (they cluster the rows even when classes sit on the rows). Weights are read on the rows the complete-case pass kept.  @param spec The specification. @param data The data frame passed to the fit. @param weights Name of the weight column. @return `spec` with `sampling_weights` (per unit), `row_weights` and   `weights`. @noRd

.mixture_is_count.name: .mixture_is_count
.mixture_is_count.documentation: Is a value a single positive whole number? @noRd

.mixture_with_seed.name: .mixture_with_seed
.mixture_with_seed.documentation: Evaluate code under a seed, restoring the caller's random state  The expression form of `.latents_local_seed()`, for callers that scope a seed to one expression rather than to their whole body. @param seed `NULL` or a number. @param code Expression, evaluated lazily. @return The value of `code`. @noRd

.mixture_spec.name: .mixture_spec
.mixture_spec.documentation: Build the model specification from a formula and data  Resolves the outcome, the class-specific and shared designs, the offset, the membership designs and the group index, after one complete-case pass over every variable the model uses.  @return A list consumed by the engine; see the fields assigned below. @noRd

.mixture_common_columns.name: .mixture_common_columns
.mixture_common_columns.documentation: The design columns of the terms shared by every class  A `common` term is matched to a term of `formula` by the variables it involves (so `~ b:a` matches `a:b`), and contributes every design column that term produces in `formula`'s own coding: a factor shares its contrast columns, not the full dummy set a formula without intercept would build. Columns follow the order of the terms in `common`.  @param common A one-sided formula. @param model_terms The terms of the fitted formula. @param full_design Its model matrix (with the `assign` attribute). @return A character vector of column names of `full_design`; raises   `latents_bad_argument` for a term `formula` does not have. @noRd

.mixture_membership_design.name: .mixture_membership_design
.mixture_membership_design.documentation: Retain the membership design's coding for prediction @noRd

.mixture_response.name: .mixture_response
.mixture_response.documentation: Resolve the outcome to counts and trials @param response The model response (vector, factor or two-column matrix). @param family Family name. @param levels For the ordinal family on new data: the fitted categories. @return A list of numeric `y` and `trials` (and, for the ordinal family,   the categories; see `.ordinal_response()`). @noRd

.mixture_group_design.name: .mixture_group_design
.mixture_group_design.documentation: Collapse a row-level design to one row per group, checking constancy @param design Row-level design matrix. @param group_index Integer group of each row. @param argument Argument name, for the message. @return A `G x r` design matrix. @noRd

multilca.name: multilca
multilca.documentation: Fit a two-level latent class model  Fits a two-level latent class model for discrete indicators and returns a fitted `multilpa` object. It is [multilpa()] with every indicator in `vars` treated as categorical, except those named in `ordinal` or `count` through `...`. Each profile has unrestricted response probabilities for the categorical indicators and structured parameters for the ordinal and count ones; the group classes differ in the probability of each profile. For models that combine categorical and continuous indicators, use [multilpa()] and name the categorical ones in its `categorical` argument.  @param data A data frame with one row per observation. @param vars Names of the indicator columns. Numeric, integer, logical,   character and factor columns are accepted; factor levels keep their   declared order and other types are sorted. @param id Name of the group identifier column, or `NULL` for a single-level   model. @param n_profiles Number of observation-level latent classes (profiles). @param n_group_classes Number of group-level latent classes. Defaults to 2,   or to 1 when `id = NULL`. @param ... Further arguments to [multilpa()], such as `n_starts`, `seed`,   `missing`, `tol` or `profile_covariates`. `ordinal` and `count` name   ordinal and count indicators; the remaining indicators are categorical.   `categorical` is accepted but has no further effect; its names must be in   `vars`. @return A fitted `multilpa` object (`multilpa_covariates` when membership   covariates are given), as [multilpa()] returns it. Categorical response   probabilities are in `get_results(fit, "responses")`, one row per   profile, item and category. @section Conditions:   `latents_bad_categorical` when `categorical` names a column not in   `vars`; otherwise the conditions of [multilpa()]. @seealso [multilpa()] for continuous and mixed indicators, and   `vignette("lca", package = "latents")`. @examples activities <- c("time_with_friends", "on_social_media", "tv_video_games") fit <- multilca(subset(student_esm, day <= 1), vars = activities,                 id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2,                 n_starts = 1, seed = 1) get_results(fit, "responses") get_results(fit, "profile_probabilities") @export

.latents_lca_categorical.name: .latents_lca_categorical
.latents_lca_categorical.documentation: The categorical indicators of an all-categorical verb  Every indicator in `vars` not named in `ordinal` or `count`, together with any `categorical` the caller wrote as for [multilpa()]. A name in `categorical` that is not in `vars` is refused here, before an enumeration could turn it into a grid of failed candidates. @param vars The indicator names. @param extra `list(...)` as the verb received it. @return A character vector of indicator names. @noRd

.multilpa_pool_fallback.name: .multilpa_pool_fallback
.multilpa_pool_fallback.documentation: Whether a candidate uses a separate fitting engine @param arguments Forced arguments of one profile candidate. @return TRUE for membership covariates or joined categorical pairs. @noRd

.multilpa_pool_width.name: .multilpa_pool_width
.multilpa_pool_width.documentation: Estimate measurement work per profile for start scheduling @param data Observed data frame. @param vars Indicator names. @param extra Additional candidate arguments. @return A positive approximate parameter width per profile. @noRd

.multilpa_execute_start.name: .multilpa_execute_start
.multilpa_execute_start.documentation: Execute a flat start or one candidate using a separate fitting engine @param task Self-contained start inputs, or forced candidate arguments. @return A start attempt, a complete fallback fit, or its error condition. @noRd

.multilpa_pool_loss.name: .multilpa_pool_loss
.multilpa_pool_loss.documentation: Represent a terminal worker loss in the candidate's existing failure form @param task One start or fallback candidate task. @param message Worker-loss explanation. @return A failed-start entry or a failed-candidate condition. @noRd

.multilpa_setup_task.name: .multilpa_setup_task
.multilpa_setup_task.documentation: Prepare one profile candidate for the shared pool @param task The candidate's forced arguments and call. @return Its plan; the arguments alone for a candidate using a separate   engine; or the candidate's error condition. @noRd

.multilpa_start_tasks.name: .multilpa_start_tasks
.multilpa_start_tasks.documentation: Build profile tasks, including serial-engine candidate fallbacks @param candidates Collected plans in grid order. @param phase Screening or final runs. @param screened,ranked Per-candidate screening results and rankings. @return Self-contained tasks for one shared pool. @noRd

.multilpa_enumerate_fits.name: .multilpa_enumerate_fits
.multilpa_enumerate_fits.documentation: Prepare, pool and finalise a profile grid without nested workers @param arguments Forced argument lists in grid order. @param calls Candidate calls to retain on the fits. @param costs Positive estimated costs in grid order. @param cores Total worker budget. @param verbose Whether to report each phase with a message. @return Collected fits or error conditions, one per grid row. @noRd

.multilpa_run_start.name: .multilpa_run_start
.multilpa_run_start.documentation: Run one prepared profile-model start @param start_index Original start index. @param initial Starting values, or NULL when resuming. @param pause,resume Screening budget and checkpoint. @param context Forced EM inputs from setup. @return One EM attempt. @noRd

.multilpa_start_interior.name: .multilpa_start_interior
.multilpa_start_interior.documentation: Identify a start clear of the covariance lower bound @param attempt One completed EM attempt. @param context Forced variance-bound setting. @return TRUE when the start is interior. @noRd

.multilpa_run_plan.name: .multilpa_run_plan
.multilpa_run_plan.documentation: Run the starts of a prepared profile fit with the shared search @param plan A prepared fitting plan. @param cores Core budget for a direct fit. @return A fitted profile or latent class model. @noRd

.multilpa_report_failed_plan.name: .multilpa_report_failed_plan
.multilpa_report_failed_plan.documentation: Report covariance qualifications of an unsuccessful profile search @param plan A prepared fitting plan. @param error The selection error carrying its attempts' count records. @return NULL, invisibly. @noRd

.multilpa_finish_plan.name: .multilpa_finish_plan
.multilpa_finish_plan.documentation: Finalise a profile fit in the parent and report covariance qualifications @param plan A prepared fitting plan. @param starts Shared start-selection result. @return A fitted profile or latent class model. @noRd

.multilpa_finalise.name: .multilpa_finalise
.multilpa_finalise.documentation: Finalise a profile fit from its selected starts @param starts Shared start-selection result. @param context Forced setup inputs. @return A fitted multilpa object. @noRd

.multilpa_log_sum_exp.name: .multilpa_log_sum_exp
.multilpa_log_sum_exp.documentation: Row-wise log-sum-exp @param log_values Numeric matrix of log weights. @return Vector of log sums. @noRd

.multilpa_expectation.name: .multilpa_expectation
.multilpa_expectation.documentation: Compute nested posterior probabilities @param x Observation-by-indicator matrix of continuous indicators, optionally   containing NA. It may have zero columns when every indicator is categorical. @param group_index Integer group indices in first-occurrence order. @param parameters List of model parameters. @param codes Optional integer matrix of categorical indicator codes. @param weights Optional sampling weight per group, already scaled. @return Log likelihood, posteriors, and conditional class probabilities.   With `weights`, the log likelihood is the weighted pseudo log likelihood   and every posterior is multiplied by its group's weight, so the M-step   and the scores read weighted counts without knowing about weights;   `group_log_likelihood` stays per group and unweighted. @noRd

.multilpa_maximization.name: .multilpa_maximization
.multilpa_maximization.documentation: Maximize the expected complete-data log likelihood @param x Observation-by-indicator matrix. @param expectation Nested posterior calculation. @param variance_model Either varying or equal across profiles. @param min_variance Lower bound on every indicator variance. @param covariance_model Diagonal or full residual covariance. @param covariance_pattern `NULL`, or a logical indicators-by-indicators   matrix marking the free covariance entries (the diagonal and the   `local_dependence` pairs); every other entry is held at zero. @return Updated model parameters. @noRd

.multilpa_initialize.name: .multilpa_initialize
.multilpa_initialize.documentation: Initialize a two-level Gaussian mixture @param x Observation-by-indicator matrix. @param group_index Integer group indices. @param n_profiles Number of individual profiles. @param n_types Number of group classes. @param variance_model Variance constraint. @param min_variance Variance lower bound. @param start_index Restart number. @param covariance_model Diagonal or full residual covariance. @param row_weights Optional sampling weights in observation order. Only   positive-weight rows supply starting values; their relative weights do   not change the existing initialization algorithm. @return Strictly positive initial mixture probabilities and Gaussian parameters. @noRd

.multilpa_initialization_center.name: .multilpa_initialization_center
.multilpa_initialization_center.documentation: Internal Gaussian origin from the rows that enter the objective @param x Continuous indicator matrix. @param row_weights Optional nonnegative weights in observation order. @return Observed column means among positive-weight rows. @noRd

.multilpa_random_assignments.name: .multilpa_random_assignments
.multilpa_random_assignments.documentation: Assign rows to clusters at random, for the emEM pool  `"partition"` deals the rows into the clusters in a random order, so every cluster holds a share; `"centres"` draws distinct rows as the cluster centres and assigns every row to the nearest, each drawn row keeping its own cluster (so none is empty even when rows repeat).  @param input Standardized numeric matrix, one row per observation. @param n_clusters Number of clusters. @param kind `"partition"` or `"centres"`. @return Integer cluster labels, one per row, every cluster non-empty. @noRd

.multilpa_ward_assignments.name: .multilpa_ward_assignments
.multilpa_ward_assignments.documentation: Assign rows to clusters by Ward's hierarchical clustering  Ward's Euclidean agglomeration on standardized rows. Agglomeration needs every pairwise distance, so at most 2000 evenly spaced rows are clustered and every row is then assigned to the nearest cluster centre.  @param input Standardized numeric matrix, one row per observation. @param n_clusters Number of clusters. @return Integer cluster labels, one per row, every cluster non-empty. @noRd

.multilpa_validate_start.name: .multilpa_validate_start
.multilpa_validate_start.documentation: Validate user-supplied initial parameters @param start Initial parameter list. @param n_profiles Number of profiles. @param n_types Number of group classes. @param n_indicators Number of indicators. @param variance_model Variance constraint. @param min_variance Variance lower bound. @param covariance_model Diagonal or full residual covariance. @param n_categories Integer vector of category counts, one per categorical   indicator, or `NULL` when every indicator is continuous. @param min_probability Lower bound applied to response probabilities. @param categorical Indicator names, in the order this fit consumes them, or   `NULL` when no alignment by label is possible. @param levels Named list of category labels per categorical indicator, in   code order, or `NULL`. @return A validated copy without dimension names, with any labelled   categorical block aligned to this fit's indicator and category order. @noRd

.multilpa_align_response_start.name: .multilpa_align_response_start
.multilpa_align_response_start.documentation: Align a labelled item-response start with this fit's own encoding  Response blocks are consumed by position: the first block belongs to the first `categorical` indicator and its columns to that indicator's categories in code order. A block list carried over from another fit, or from a first stage, can therefore be attached to the wrong item, or a category to the wrong column, and every later number is silently wrong rather than visibly broken. Whenever the caller supplies labels -- names on the list, column names on a block -- the labels are the contract: the block is reordered to this fit's encoding, and a label naming an item or a category this fit does not have is refused, because there is no alignment to make.  Unlabelled input keeps the documented positional contract unchanged.  @param response_probabilities The caller's block list, possibly labelled. @param categorical Indicator names, in the order this fit consumes them. @param levels Named list of category labels per indicator, in code order, or   `NULL` to align the blocks only. @return The block list, unnamed, in this fit's item order with each block's   columns in this fit's category order. Raises `latents_bad_start` when a   supplied label cannot be aligned. @noRd

.multilpa_validate_response_start.name: .multilpa_validate_response_start
.multilpa_validate_response_start.documentation: Validate a user-supplied item-response starting block  @param response_probabilities List of profiles-by-categories matrices, one   per categorical indicator. @param n_profiles Number of profiles. @param n_categories Integer vector of category counts per indicator. @param min_probability Lower bound applied to every cell. @return The validated list, unnamed, with rows renormalized to sum to one. @noRd

.multilpa_em.name: .multilpa_em
.multilpa_em.documentation: Run one nested EM optimization @param x Observation-by-indicator matrix. @param group_index Integer group indices. @param parameters Starting model parameters. @param variance_model Variance constraint. @param min_variance Variance lower bound. @param max_iter Maximum M-steps. @param tol Relative likelihood convergence tolerance. @param covariance_model Diagonal or full residual covariance. @param covariance_pattern `NULL`, or a logical indicators-by-indicators   matrix marking the free covariance entries (the diagonal and the   `local_dependence` pairs); every other entry is held at zero. @param pause,resume As for `.latents_em()`: pause after that many   iterations, or resume a paused run (then `parameters` is not used). @return Final parameters, posterior calculation, and convergence history;   with `pause` or `resume`, also the `checkpoint`. @noRd

.multilpa_time_values.name: .multilpa_time_values
.multilpa_time_values.documentation: Validate and extract an optional time column  The model never uses the ordering; it is carried so that the assignments can be read back in sequence without the caller supplying the data again.  @param data The data frame passed to the fit. @param time `NULL`, or the name of a single column giving each observation's   position within its group. @param id Name of the group column, used for the exclusion and the   uniqueness check. It is known to name a column of `data` by the time this   is called, because the data contract is checked first. @param vars The indicator column names, which `time` may not name.   Defaults to none so that callers which have not yet been updated keep   working; `multilpa()` passes them. @return `NULL` when `time` is `NULL`, otherwise the column in input row order. @noRd

.multilpa_single_level.name: .multilpa_single_level
.multilpa_single_level.documentation: Resolve a single-level request into the two-level machinery  `id = NULL` says the observations are independent: each row is its own unit, which is the ordinary one-level mixture this model reduces to when every group holds one row and there is one group class. Nothing about the likelihood changes; only the grouping does.  The column is fabricated here rather than by the caller. A caller who writes `data$unit <- seq_len(nrow(data))` has to know that the fit stores that column, that `get_results(x, "data")` will hand it back, and that a second call must spell it the same way -- plumbing the package should own. This package's own validation harness wrote that line once per comparison before this argument existed.  @param data The caller's data frame. @param n_group_classes What the caller asked for, or `NULL` if they did not. @param latent_class Whether every indicator is categorical, which makes the   model a latent class rather than a latent profile analysis. @return A list with `data`, `id` and `n_group_classes`. @noRd

multilpa.name: multilpa
multilpa.documentation: Fit a two-level latent profile model  Fits a latent profile model for observations nested in groups and returns a fitted `multilpa` object. Each observation belongs to a Gaussian profile, and each group belongs to a latent group class that determines the profile proportions. Profile means and variances are shared across group classes (measurement invariance). By default indicators are independent within a profile; full residual covariances and observed-data maximum likelihood for missing indicators are available.  @param data A data frame containing the indicators and the group identifier. @param vars Unique character vector of indicator column names. Columns not   named in `categorical`, `ordinal` or `count` are continuous indicators. @param id Name of the group identifier column. Character, factor and   numeric identifiers are supported; missing identifiers are not. `id` has   no default: omitting it raises `latents_bad_argument`.    `id = NULL` fits a **single-level** model: each row is its own unit, the   observations are independent, and `n_group_classes` is one. The fit raises   a `latents_single_level` message. Every verb of the package works on the   result. The internal unit column is named `.observation`; it is not   returned by `get_results(x, "data")`, and a `data` that already has a   column of that name raises `latents_bad_data`. Requesting more than one   group class with `id = NULL` raises `latents_bad_argument`. @param n_profiles Positive integer number of individual profiles. @param n_group_classes Positive integer number of latent group classes   (default 2). With `id = NULL` it is one, and any other value is an error. @param profile_covariates,group_covariates Names of numeric columns of   `data` that predict individual-profile and group-class membership through   multinomial logits, with the last class as reference. Naming either fits   the one-step maximum-likelihood covariate model and returns a   `multilpa_covariates` object. Profile intercepts differ by group class;   profile slopes are shared across group classes unless   `profile_slopes = "group_class"`. A group covariate must be constant   within each group. Covariates enter in their supplied units, without   centring or scaling. The covariate model refuses `start` and `fixed`; it   accepts `missing = "fiml"` for the indicators, but the covariates must be   complete. [three_step()] and [r3step()] are the staged alternatives. @param profile_slopes `"shared"` (the default) gives each profile   covariate one slope per profile logit, common to every group class.   `"group_class"` estimates separate slopes in each group class (a   cross-level interaction), reported with terms such as `z:group_class_1`;   it multiplies the number of slope parameters by `n_group_classes`, each   set estimated from the groups in its class. Naming it without   `profile_covariates` raises `latents_bad_argument`. @param variance_model `"varying"` (the default; profile-specific variances   or covariance matrices) or `"equal"` (shared across profiles). @param n_starts Positive integer number of EM starts (default 10). The   first start is deterministic: Ward's hierarchical clustering of the   standardized indicators (on at most 2000 evenly spaced rows), each cluster   described by its own means and spread. The   remaining starts are k-means from random centres. A supplied `start`   replaces the first start, and the remaining starts are random. With   `start` and `max_iter = 0`, exactly one start is run whatever `n_starts`   is. Rows from zero-weight units do not supply initial clustering or   measurement parameters. For `search = "emEM"`, this is the finalist   budget, including the protected first start (see `search`). @param max_iter Nonnegative integer maximum number of EM updates per start   (default 1000). `max_iter = 0` performs no update: with `start`, the model   is evaluated at exactly those values, for example to score them with   `logLik()`; without `start`, the random initializations are evaluated and   the one with the highest log likelihood is returned. @param tol Positive relative log-likelihood tolerance (default `1e-8`).   Convergence requires an absolute change no greater than   `tol * (1 + abs(previous log likelihood))`. @param min_variance Positive lower bound on each variance, or on each   covariance eigenvalue under full covariance, in squared input units   (default `1e-6`); the fit is then constrained maximum likelihood.   Estimates at the bound are reported and raise a warning. @param seed Optional random seed: any whole number `set.seed()` accepts,   including negative ones. When supplied, the caller's random-number state   is restored on exit. @param start Optional list of `means` and `variances` (profiles by   indicators), `profile_probabilities` (group classes by profiles), and   `group_probabilities` (vector). Starting probabilities must be positive.   For full covariance, supply `covariances` (indicators by indicators by   profiles); `variances` may then be omitted, or must match their diagonals.   A categorical model also takes `response_probabilities`, a list of one   profiles-by-categories matrix per indicator named in `categorical`. The   list is matched by position unless it is labelled: when its elements are   named after the indicators, or its columns after the categories, each   block is matched to the indicator and category its labels name. A label   naming an indicator or category the fit does not have raises   `latents_bad_start`. @param categorical Character vector naming indicators to treat as   categorical. Each is modelled by unrestricted, profile-specific response   probabilities over its observed categories (the latent class measurement   model); binary, ordinal and unordered indicators are handled by the same   parameterization. Numeric, integer, logical, character and factor columns   are accepted. Indicators not named here stay Gaussian, so naming a subset   fits a mixed-mode model. @param model The covariance structure as an mclust code, one of   `"EII"`, `"VII"`, `"EEI"`, `"VEI"`, `"EVI"`, `"VVI"`, `"EEE"`, `"VEE"`,   `"EVE"`, `"VVE"`, `"EEV"`, `"VEV"`, `"EVV"`, `"VVV"`. The letters give the   volume, shape and orientation, each equal (`E`) or varying (`V`) across   profiles, with `I` for axis-aligned (no covariances). These are the codes   [enumerate_classes()] takes.
