Structural Equation Modeling, 12, 411--434.   doi:10.1207/s15328007sem1203_4.    Fraley, C., & Raftery, A. E. (2007). Bayesian regularization for normal   mixture estimation and model-based clustering. Journal of   Classification, 24, 155--181. doi:10.1007/s00357-007-0004-5. @examples # Course sessions nested in students: engagement profiles of sessions, and # classes of students that differ in how often they are engaged. activity <- c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance") fit <- multilpa(course_engagement, activity, "student",                 n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,                 seed = 42) summary(fit) as.data.frame(fit) get_results(fit, what = "profile_probabilities") @seealso [multilca()] for a model in which every indicator is categorical. @export @importFrom stats setNames

.multilpa_setup.name: .multilpa_setup
.multilpa_setup.documentation: Prepare a profile-model fit without running its starts @inheritParams multilpa @param .call Public fitting call to retain on the result. @return A prepared plan, or the existing fit for another fitting engine. @noRd

.multilpa_check_arguments.name: .multilpa_check_arguments
.multilpa_check_arguments.documentation: Validate the scalar arguments of a fit @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises on the first broken contract. @noRd

.multilpa_prepare_indicators.name: .multilpa_prepare_indicators
.multilpa_prepare_indicators.documentation: Split indicators into Gaussian and categorical blocks  Returns the continuous indicator matrix, which may have zero columns, and the encoded categorical codes, which may be `NULL`. Every measurement-side contract is checked here so the fitting path can assume clean input.  @return A list with `continuous`, `frame`, `x`, `encoded`, `codes` and   `n_categories`. @noRd

.multilpa_prepare_groups.name: .multilpa_prepare_groups
.multilpa_prepare_groups.documentation: Index the observed groups in first-occurrence order @return A list with `values`, `index`, `ids`, `n` and `sizes`. @noRd

.multilpa_label_parameters.name: .multilpa_label_parameters
.multilpa_label_parameters.documentation: Attach readable dimension names to the fitted parameters @return The parameter list, with profiles, indicators and categories named. @noRd

.multilpa_count_parameters.name: .multilpa_count_parameters
.multilpa_count_parameters.documentation: Count the free parameters of a fitted model  Mixing proportions contribute `(H - 1) + H (K - 1)`. Gaussian indicators add means plus variances or covariances, shared or profile-specific. Categorical measurement is always profile-specific, so `variance_model` has no categorical analogue and never reduces that block.  @return A single number of free parameters. @noRd

.latents_profile_parameters.name: .latents_profile_parameters
.latents_profile_parameters.documentation: The parameters of one profile's own Gaussian density  Its free means plus what its spread adds to the model: every variance or covariance when profiles vary, nothing when they share one, and the profile's share of a constrained structure (the parameters one more profile adds). Covariances held at zero by a pattern are excluded, as are held means; held variances cannot collapse during this fit.  @param n_continuous Number of continuous indicators. @param variance_model,covariance_model,structure As in [multilpa()]. @param covariance_pattern The free covariance entries, or `NULL`. @param fixed The expanded names of held measurement blocks. @return A single number; `0` when there are no continuous indicators or   the spread is shared by every profile or held fixed, so no profile has   a free variance of its own to collapse. @noRd

.latents_warn_thin_profiles.name: .latents_warn_thin_profiles
.latents_warn_thin_profiles.documentation: Warn when a profile has fewer members than its own parameters  This is a conservative membership-versus-parameter heuristic for profiles with class-specific spread. It is not a rank or identification test: positive soft memberships can yield full-rank covariance at arbitrarily small total mass, and a larger profile can be nearly flat. Under sampling weights the membership is normalized mass, not an independent sample count. The estimate is unchanged; continuous covariance diagnostics are reported separately without using a rejection threshold.  @param effective_counts Effective membership of each profile. @param n_parameters The output of `.latents_profile_parameters()`. @param context Optional text identifying a separately estimated measurement   block, such as `"at occasion 2"`. @return The positions of the thin profiles, invisibly; a   `latents_thin_profiles` warning when there are any. @noRd

.multilpa_covariate_model.name: .multilpa_covariate_model
.multilpa_covariate_model.documentation: Hand a covariate request to the covariate estimator  `multilpa()` is one verb over one model, and membership covariates are part of that model rather than a different one, so they are arguments and not a separate entry point. Two of `multilpa()`'s own arguments have no meaning on this path: the covariate likelihood has no starting-value contract of the shape the covariate-free EM uses, and no held-measurement machinery. Each is refused by name instead of being accepted and ignored, which would return a fit that is not the one asked for. `missing = "fiml"` is supported: the measurement density is the covariate-free model's observed-data one.  @param data,vars,id,n_profiles,n_group_classes As in [multilpa()]. @param profile_covariates,group_covariates The requested predictors. @param variance_model,n_starts,max_iter,tol,min_variance As in [multilpa()]. @param seed,time,covariance_model,categorical,min_probability As in   [multilpa()]. @param missing,profile_slopes As in [multilpa()]. @param start,fixed Refused when they are anything but their default. @param boundary As in [multilpa()]. @param call The user's call, recorded on the result. @return An object of class `multilpa_covariates`. @noRd

.multilpa_start_kmeans.name: .multilpa_start_kmeans
.multilpa_start_kmeans.documentation: One k-means run for a random start  Lloyd's algorithm warns "empty cluster" when a start's random centres leave a cluster without members. That start then fails or converges like any other, and the fit reports failed starts itself ("k of n starts failed"), so base R's warning is muffled here rather than repeated to the caller. @param x Numeric matrix to cluster. @param centers Number of clusters. @return The `stats::kmeans()` result. @noRd

.multilpa_log_hypervolume.name: .multilpa_log_hypervolume
.multilpa_log_hypervolume.documentation: The logarithm of mclust's default data hypervolume  `mclust::hypvol()`: the smaller of the volume of the axis-aligned bounding box of the data and the volume of the bounding box aligned with its principal components. In logs, since a product of ranges overflows.  @param x A complete numeric matrix. @return A single number, `log(V)`. @noRd

.multilpa_check_noise.name: .multilpa_check_noise
.multilpa_check_noise.documentation: Refuse a noise component this package does not define  @param noise The [multilpa()] argument. @param n_group_classes,categorical,fixed The corresponding arguments. @param n_covariates How many membership covariates were named. @return `NULL`, invisibly. @noRd

.multilpa_noise_start.name: .multilpa_noise_start
.multilpa_noise_start.documentation: Take the noise proportion out of a supplied start  A start for a noise fit carries `noise_probability` beside the profile probabilities, which together sum to one. The profile probabilities are returned renormalized over the Gaussian profiles, which is the shape every other start has, so the ordinary validation applies to them unchanged.  @param start The caller's start list. @return A list with `start` and `noise_probability`. @noRd

.multilpa_add_noise.name: .multilpa_add_noise
.multilpa_add_noise.documentation: Add the noise component to a set of Gaussian parameters @param parameters Parameters whose profile probabilities sum to one. @param probability The noise proportion. @param log_density The noise component's log density, `-log(V)`. @return The parameters with one more, last, profile-probability column and   `noise_log_density` set. @noRd

.multilpa_split_noise.name: .multilpa_split_noise
.multilpa_split_noise.documentation: Split a fitted noise component back out of the parameters and posteriors @param parameters The fitted parameters, noise last. @param posteriors The observation posteriors, noise last. @return A list with the Gaussian `parameters` and `posteriors`, and the   `noise_probability` and `noise_posteriors`. @noRd

.multilpa_class_posteriors.name: .multilpa_class_posteriors
.multilpa_class_posteriors.documentation: Every observation's class posteriors, the noise component included  @param x A fitted model of this package. @return The observation-by-profile posterior matrix, with a final `noise`   column when the fit has a noise component. Its rows sum to one either way. @noRd

.multilpa_informative_rows.name: .multilpa_informative_rows
.multilpa_informative_rows.documentation: Which observations have at least one observed indicator  A row with every indicator missing contributes nothing to the likelihood, so its posterior is not a classification of that row but the prior its group gives it. The sample size of the individual-level criteria already leaves such rows out; this is the same set of rows for every statistic of classification quality.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @return A logical vector, one per observation; all `TRUE` for a fit that   did not record it. @noRd

.multilpa_group_sample_size.name: .multilpa_group_sample_size
.multilpa_group_sample_size.documentation: The group sample size of the group-convention criteria @param x A fitted model of this package. @return The number of groups with an observed row, or every group under   `drop_empty = FALSE` and for fits that did not record it. @noRd

.multilpa_informative_groups.name: .multilpa_informative_groups
.multilpa_informative_groups.documentation: Which groups have at least one row with an observed indicator  A group whose every row observes nothing is unclassified for the same reason as such a row: its posterior is the group-class prior. Mplus leaves such a group out of its clusters; so do the group sample size and the group-level classification statistics here.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @return A logical vector, one per group (row of `group_posteriors`), or   `NULL` for a fit without group posteriors. @noRd

.multilpa_classified_group_posteriors.name: .multilpa_classified_group_posteriors
.multilpa_classified_group_posteriors.documentation: The group posteriors of the groups that were classified @param x A fitted model of this package. @return `group_posteriors` restricted to informative groups, or `NULL`. @noRd

.multilpa_classified_posteriors.name: .multilpa_classified_posteriors
.multilpa_classified_posteriors.documentation: The class posteriors of the observations that were classified  Entropy, average posterior probability and the entropy charge of ICL, AWE and CLC describe how well observed values separate the classes, so they are taken over the rows with at least one observed indicator. Class sizes are estimates of the population and keep every row.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @return `.multilpa_class_posteriors()` restricted to informative rows. @noRd

.multilpa_refuse_noise.name: .multilpa_refuse_noise
.multilpa_refuse_noise.documentation: Refuse a verb that does not yet account for a noise component @param x A fitted model of this package. @param verb What was asked for, for the message. @param class Extra condition classes to carry. @return `NULL`, invisibly, for a fit without one. @noRd

.latents_worker_reporter.name: .latents_worker_reporter
.latents_worker_reporter.documentation: Combine worker-loss reports from the phases of one fitting call  Each mapper retries independently. Screening and finalist pools share this reporter so a public call emits one qualification, including on error. @return A collector for zero-argument callbacks and an exit-time reporter. @noRd

.latents_check_cores.name: .latents_check_cores
.latents_check_cores.documentation: Validate `cores` @param cores The caller's `cores`. @return The number of cores as an integer. @noRd

.latents_fork_safe.name: .latents_fork_safe
.latents_fork_safe.documentation: Whether forked workers can use this R's linear algebra  Apple's Accelerate (vecLib) BLAS is not safe in a forked process once the parent has used it: the children die with a segmentation fault in the first BLAS call (`backsolve()`, `crossprod()`). R on macOS can be switched to it from the reference BLAS, so the fork is refused only where it is.  @param blas Path of the BLAS library, as `extSoftVersion()` reports it. @param sysname Operating system name, as `Sys.info()` reports it. @return `TRUE` when forked workers are safe. @noRd

.latents_stop_cluster.name: .latents_stop_cluster
.latents_stop_cluster.documentation: Stop every socket worker and close every owned connection  A dead worker can make stopCluster fail while sending DONE. Clean nodes independently and always close their connections so a cleanup failure cannot replace the original worker condition or leave sockets for GC. @param cluster A socket cluster created by makePSOCKcluster(). @return NULL, invisibly. @noRd

.latents_collect_conditions.name: .latents_collect_conditions
.latents_collect_conditions.documentation: Collect warnings and messages without changing their classes  @param fun A zero-argument callback whose conditions should be collected. @return A list with the callback's `value` and its ordered `conditions`. @noRd

.latents_worker_context.name: .latents_worker_context
.latents_worker_context.documentation: Give each worker task the parent's RNG kinds and warning policy  Whole-candidate tasks seed themselves inside the fitting engine. Fresh socket workers otherwise seed with their own default RNG kinds. Restore the kinds and .Random.seed after each task, including errors and interrupts. As with .latents_local_seed(), base R does not expose the Box-Muller cache for restoration; set.seed() resets it before each seeded candidate. @param fun A function of one task. @return A task function with the parent's execution settings captured. @noRd

.latents_task_collector.name: .latents_task_collector
.latents_task_collector.documentation: Wrap a task function without capturing its scheduler  @param fun A function of one task. @return A function returning each task's value and collected conditions. @noRd

.latents_signal_conditions.name: .latents_signal_conditions
.latents_signal_conditions.documentation: Signal collected warnings and messages in their original order  @param conditions A list of warning and message conditions. @return NULL, invisibly. @noRd

.latents_fork_pass.name: .latents_fork_pass
.latents_fork_pass.documentation: Run one fork pass, including isolated one-worker retries @param indices Forced task payloads in dispatch order. @param collected The task collector. @param cores Worker limit for this pass. @param retry Whether this is the retry, so a spawn failure remains a loss. @return Collected task results; missing worker results remain NULL/try-error. @noRd

.latents_windows_alive.name: .latents_windows_alive
.latents_windows_alive.documentation: Check Windows worker liveness without sending a signal  Signal zero also calls TerminateProcess on Windows. A successful tasklist snapshot instead identifies exited workers when TerminateProcess fails. Failed or malformed snapshots leave liveness unknown, never retired. @param pids Owned worker process IDs. @return A logical vector, with NA when liveness cannot be checked. @noRd

.latents_make_cluster.name: .latents_make_cluster
.latents_make_cluster.documentation: Start socket workers and record the processes owned by this pool @param cores Number of workers. @return A socket cluster with its worker process IDs attached. @noRd

.latents_abort_cluster.name: .latents_abort_cluster
.latents_abort_cluster.documentation: Retire owned socket workers before replacing a broken cluster  stopCluster queues DONE behind an EM task already running on a surviving worker. Terminate those processes first, so replacement workers cannot overlap the abandoned computations. A zombie may still have a PID after SIGKILL, but cannot execute another task. On Windows pskill uses the TerminateProcess API for every signal. If termination cannot be confirmed, callers raise a classed infrastructure error without starting replacements. @param cluster A cluster whose owned process IDs have been registered. @return Whether every owned worker has exited or received a fatal signal. @noRd

.latents_socket_pass.name: .latents_socket_pass
.latents_socket_pass.documentation: Run bounded socket chunks while retaining completed chunks  The exported parallel API returns no partial results when parLapplyLB loses a connection. Bound each call to one task per worker: a death loses at most that chunk, while completed chunks remain available. Restart the cluster before the next chunk; even a repeatedly dying task cannot discard later chunks. A retry uses one-task calls from the outset: every task is attempted at most twice, and a repeatedly dying task cannot lose its retry's mates. @param indices Forced task payloads in dispatch order. @param collected The task collector. @param cores Worker limit for this pass. @param retry Whether this is a retry whose startup failure remains a loss. @return Collected task results; an unfinished chunk contains NULL results. @noRd

.latents_warn_worker_lost.name: .latents_warn_worker_lost
.latents_warn_worker_lost.documentation: Report worker losses from one pool or several phases @param lost Number of tasks whose first worker result was missing. @param recovered Number recovered by the retry. @param retry_cores Worker limit used for the retry. @return NULL, invisibly. @noRd

.latents_map_candidates.name: .latents_map_candidates
.latents_map_candidates.documentation: Apply `fun` to candidates or starts in a shared worker pool  With several cores, tasks use dynamically assigned forked processes where the platform allows them, or a load-balanced socket cluster on Windows and on macOS with Accelerate's BLAS (`.latents_fork_safe()`). Optional costs send the longest estimated tasks first. Results and conditions retain the order of `indices`, independently of dispatch or completion order. Conditions retain their classes and can instead be returned for later signalling.  Missing worker results are retried once using half as many fork workers, rounded up, or one socket worker to isolate repeated losses. A classed warning reports process losses and recovery. Socket calls use bounded chunks because the exported parallel API cannot retain results from within a call whose connection breaks; previously completed chunks survive. @param indices Task identifiers. @param fun A function of one identifier returning that task's result.   It catches each candidate's own errors. @param cores Number of cores, from `.latents_check_cores()`. @param backend `"auto"`; `"socket"` or `"fork"` to force one backend   (used by the tests). @param costs NULL or positive finite estimated costs aligned with `indices`. @param signal Whether to signal collected conditions in the parent. @param on_lost NULL or a function of a task and a message, returning its   terminal failure value when its retry also loses its worker. @return A list in the order of `indices`. With `signal = FALSE`, each element   contains `value` and `conditions`; otherwise each is the task's value. @noRd

.gg_draw_on_call.name: .gg_draw_on_call
.gg_draw_on_call.documentation: Draw a plot while preserving the side effect of a former base method @param plot A ggplot object. @return The same plot, invisibly, so an interactive call draws it once. @noRd

.gg_available.name: .gg_available
.gg_available.documentation: Whether plots can be drawn, telling the caller once when they cannot  diagnostics() and report() draw by default; without ggplot2 they still print everything else and say why nothing was drawn. @noRd

.gg_theme.name: .gg_theme
.gg_theme.documentation: The house theme: white field, horizontal guides only, left-aligned titles @noRd

.gg_top_legend.name: .gg_top_legend
.gg_top_legend.documentation: Legend across the top, left-aligned, without a title @noRd

.gg_percent.name: .gg_percent
.gg_percent.documentation: A percentage for a label, never rounded down to a misleading zero @noRd

.gg_profile_key.name: .gg_profile_key
.gg_profile_key.documentation: One row per profile, indexed by profile number: share, display rank, label, colour and shape  The share is the profile's effective count over all effective counts, as every table reports it. A noise component's mass stays in the denominator, so the shares of the real profiles are what they are in the fit. @noRd

.gg_scales.name: .gg_scales
.gg_scales.documentation: Manual profile scales for the aesthetics a view maps @noRd

.gg_adjusted_note.name: .gg_adjusted_note
.gg_adjusted_note.documentation: A subtitle line for views that draw cases of a fit with direct effects @param x A fitted model. @return `""` without direct effects; otherwise a line naming them. @noRd

.gg_titles.name: .gg_titles
.gg_titles.documentation: Title and subtitle: the caller's when given, the view's default otherwise @noRd

.gg_spread.name: .gg_spread
.gg_spread.documentation: Push labels apart so no two are closer than `gap`, keeping their order  Subtracting `gap * rank` turns "at least `gap` apart" into "non-decreasing", which a cumulative maximum enforces; adding it back and re-centring on the original mean keeps the block where the data are. @noRd

.gg_ink.name: .gg_ink
.gg_ink.documentation: Ink for text on a fill: dark on light fills, white on dark ones @noRd

.gg_probability_fill.name: .gg_probability_fill
.gg_probability_fill.documentation: The white-to-blue ramp for a probability, as a colour string @noRd

.gg_probability_scale.name: .gg_probability_scale
.gg_probability_scale.documentation: A shared probability fill scale from 0 to 1, with its key @noRd

.gg_tile_theme.name: .gg_tile_theme
.gg_tile_theme.documentation: Theme adjustments shared by the tile views @noRd

.gg_group_class_text.name: .gg_group_class_text
.gg_group_class_text.documentation: "2 group classes" when there are several, nothing when there is one @noRd

.gg_mean_frame.name: .gg_mean_frame
.gg_mean_frame.documentation: Profile means (and 95% intervals) in long form, on the requested scale  @param errors A profiles-by-indicators matrix of standard errors, a string   saying why there are none, or `NULL` when intervals were not asked for. @return A list: `frame` (one row per profile and indicator), `vars`,   `note` (the subtitle fragment about intervals) and `has_errors`. @noRd

.gg_series_plot.name: .gg_series_plot
.gg_series_plot.documentation: Lines across indicators with direct labels at the right edge  Shared by the profile means and the categorical response curves: both are one series per profile across indicators, optionally with intervals. @noRd

.gg_category_scores.name: .gg_category_scores
.gg_category_scores.documentation: Numeric category scores for a categorical profile plot @noRd

.gg_categorical_summary_frame.name: .gg_categorical_summary_frame
.gg_categorical_summary_frame.documentation: Summarize the fitted categorical distributions on their score scale @noRd

.gg_view_heatmap.name: .gg_view_heatmap
.gg_view_heatmap.documentation: Profile means in observed standard deviations, with a colour key  The observed centre and spread of each indicator come from .multilpa_standardization(), the same map as `as.data.frame(scale = "standardized")`, so the tiles and the table agree. @noRd

.gg_view_response_heatmap.name: .gg_view_response_heatmap
.gg_view_response_heatmap.documentation: Every response probability as tiles, one block per indicator @noRd

.gg_view_polytomous_heatmap.name: .gg_view_polytomous_heatmap
.gg_view_polytomous_heatmap.documentation: Polytomous response probabilities: one panel per profile  Indicators run down the rows and categories across, so a row is that profile's response distribution on one indicator. Indicator names sit horizontally and each panel has only as many columns as categories, which keeps the numbers legible however many indicators there are; a block of columns per indicator ran to indicators x categories columns and overlapped. @param cells One row per indicator, category and profile. @param key The profile key from .gg_profile_key(). @noRd

.gg_view_raincloud.name: .gg_view_raincloud
.gg_view_raincloud.documentation: Each indicator's distribution per profile: density, quartiles, cases @noRd

.gg_view_responses.name: .gg_view_responses
.gg_view_responses.documentation: Categorical response probabilities, one line per profile @noRd

.gg_match_bounds.name: .gg_match_bounds
.gg_match_bounds.documentation: The confidence bounds an inference table reports for the requested cells  @param errors Measurement rows of [parameter_inference()], or `NULL`. @param parameter Which kind of parameter to take. @param profile Integer profile indices wanted, one per output row. @param term Term labels wanted, one per output row. @return A data frame with `lower` and `upper`, one row per requested cell,   `NA` where the table reports no interval. @noRd

.gg_undrawn_caption.name: .gg_undrawn_caption
.gg_undrawn_caption.documentation: A caption naming the indicators a view leaves out, and where they are  The profile views draw continuous means (or categorical summaries); an indicator of another kind is not on them, which the caption says rather than letting the indicator count in the title pass for every indicator. @param x A fitted model. @param drawn The indicators the view draws. @return A single string, or `NULL` when every indicator is drawn. @noRd

.gg_view_probabilities.name: .gg_view_probabilities
.gg_view_probabilities.documentation: Profile prevalence within each group class, one line per class @noRd

.gg_view_sequences.name: .gg_view_sequences
.gg_view_sequences.documentation: Each group's assigned profile at each position, blocked by group class @noRd

.gg_view_transitions.name: .gg_view_transitions
.gg_view_transitions.documentation: The estimated transition matrix, one panel per group class  A row with no data support is labelled in parentheses: it is uniform by construction rather than estimated. @noRd

.gg_level.name: .gg_level
.gg_level.documentation: The posteriors, counts and words of one level of classification  The diagnostic views draw the same things at both levels of a two-level fit: the individuals (cases) in their profiles, and the groups in their group classes. This is the one place that says what each level is, so a view is written once and drawn at either.  @param x A fitted model. @param level `"individuals"` or `"groups"`. @return A list: `posteriors` (units by classes, or `NULL`), `key` (as   `.gg_profile_key()`, one row per class), `class_word` and `unit_word`   (singular, lower case), `total` (units the sizes are shares of) and   `noise` (whether a noise component is excluded). @noRd

.gg_has_group_classes.name: .gg_has_group_classes
.gg_has_group_classes.documentation: Does a fit classify its groups into two or more group classes? @param x A fitted model. @return A single logical. @noRd

.gg_view_sizes.name: .gg_view_sizes
.gg_view_sizes.documentation: Effective class sizes, largest first, labelled with count and share @noRd

.gg_capitalize.name: .gg_capitalize
.gg_capitalize.documentation: The first letter of a phrase in upper case @noRd

.gg_case_values.name: .gg_case_values
.gg_case_values.documentation: Per-unit certainty and relative entropy from the fit's own posteriors @param x A fitted model. @param level `"individuals"` or `"groups"`. @noRd

.gg_case_strip.name: .gg_case_strip
.gg_case_strip.documentation: Strip plot of one per-unit value by class, with each class's mean @noRd

.gg_view_avepp.name: .gg_view_avepp
.gg_view_avepp.documentation: Average posterior probability matrix, assigned by posterior class @noRd

.gg_observed_cases.name: .gg_observed_cases
.gg_observed_cases.documentation: The observations with their profile and assignment certainty @noRd

.gg_view_parallel.name: .gg_view_parallel
.gg_view_parallel.documentation: Every case as a line across indicators, one panel per profile  Indicators are put on one scale, the observed z-score of each, so lines across them mean something whatever the units. @noRd

.gg_ellipse.name: .gg_ellipse
.gg_ellipse.documentation: Points of a 95% ellipse of a bivariate normal @noRd

.gg_pair_covariance.name: .gg_pair_covariance
.gg_pair_covariance.documentation: One profile's covariance for a pair of indicators  A diagonal structure stores variances only, so the pair's covariance is zero there. @noRd

.gg_view_pairs.name: .gg_view_pairs
.gg_view_pairs.documentation: Scatter-plot matrix: cases by profile with each profile's 95% ellipse @noRd

.gg_enumeration_frame.name: .gg_enumeration_frame
.gg_enumeration_frame.documentation: One information criterion's series across the grid, as a long frame  A series is one covariance model at one number of group classes; its label names only what tells the series apart. @noRd

.gg_view_enumeration.name: .gg_view_enumeration
.gg_view_enumeration.documentation: Information criteria against the number of profiles @noRd

.gg_flow_band.name: .gg_flow_band
.gg_flow_band.documentation: Band between two x-intervals at two heights, eased so it leaves and arrives vertically @noRd

.gg_plots.name: .gg_plots
.gg_plots.documentation: A list of ggplot objects that draws every one when printed @noRd

.gg_view_enumeration_quality.name: .gg_view_enumeration_quality
.gg_view_enumeration_quality.documentation: Entropy and lowest AvePP of every candidate, across the grid  The classification-quality view of an enumeration: relative entropy and the lowest average posterior probability (AvePP) of each candidate, at each level, against the number of classes, one line per group-class count (and structure). Higher is sharper. A dashed line marks the AvePP cutoff. A level with one class has neither number, so its panel is left out.  @param x A `multilpa_enumeration`. @param measures `"entropy"`, `"avepp"` or both. @param labels `TRUE` labels each series directly while they fit. @param main,subtitle Titles; `NULL` uses the view's own. @param cutoff The AvePP cutoff drawn on the AvePP panels. @return A ggplot object. @noRd

.multilpa_distinct_criteria.name: .multilpa_distinct_criteria
.multilpa_distinct_criteria.documentation: The criteria worth a panel, named for display  A single-level grid has one unit per observation, so every criterion's group-level and individual-level versions are the same numbers; drawing both repeats a panel. Such a pair is kept once under the criterion's plain name. A grid whose every candidate has one group class classifies nothing at the group level, so the group version of a classification criterion (AWE, ICL, CLC) is its penalty alone, and ICL over groups equals BIC over groups. When both versions are asked for, only the individual one is kept, under the criterion's plain name. @param grid The enumeration table. @param criterion Requested criterion columns. @return The criteria to draw, named by their display titles. @noRd

pool_imputations.name: pool_imputations
pool_imputations.documentation: Fit a model to multiply imputed data and pool it with Rubin's rules  Fits [multilpa()] to every completed data set, aligns each fit's profile and group-class labels to those of the first, and pools the estimates with Rubin's rules, returning a `latents_pooled` object. Use it for missing covariates, which `missing = "fiml"` cannot handle because the model conditions on covariates. Impute them first (for example with the mice package, with the indicators and the group identifier in the imputation model) and pass the completed data.  Pooling is on the reported (natural) scale: the pooled estimate is the mean over imputations, and its variance is the mean within-imputation variance plus `(1 + 1/m)` times the between-imputation variance. Degrees of freedom follow Rubin (1987) with a large complete-data sample. Pooled intervals are symmetric t intervals on this scale, so for probabilities and variances they can extend outside the parameter space, unlike the transformed Wald intervals of [parameter_inference()]. A structural constant, such as the probability of one for a single class, has zero within- and between-imputation variance and zero missing information. When the within-imputation variance is zero and the between-imputation variance is positive, `riv` is infinite and `fmi` is one.  @section Choosing the imputation model: The pooled results are only as valid as the imputations. The covariate and the indicators are related through the latent classes, which an imputation model linear in the indicators (mice's defaults) does not capture. In `validation/pool-imputations-coverage.R` (a membership slope with 30% of its covariate missing at random given the indicators, 200 replications, ten imputations), 95% intervals covered 0.925 under predictive mean matching and 0.935 under Bayesian linear regression, and 0.995 when the covariate was drawn approximately from its conditional distribution given the known generating parameters. That reference arm omits uncertainty in the imputation parameters, so it does not validate proper multiple imputation, and the study covers one design only. The imputation model should account for the latent structure and the clustering, include the indicators and relevant nonlinearities, and propagate parameter uncertainty; imputing separately within assigned classes ignores classification uncertainty. Complete-case analysis covered 0.955 in that design, but selecting on the indicators changes their within-class distributions, and the case-control argument for unbiased logistic slopes does not carry over when the outcome is latent and its measurement model is estimated.  @param imputed The completed data sets: a list of at least two data frames   with the same columns and rows in the same order, or a `mids` object from   the mice package, which is completed here. @param vars,id,n_profiles As in [multilpa()]. @param ... Further arguments for [multilpa()], such as `n_group_classes`,   `profile_covariates`, `group_covariates`, `categorical`, `n_starts` and   `seed`, used for every imputation. @param level Confidence level of the pooled intervals (default 0.95). @param vcov_type `"observed"` (default), `"robust"` or `"opg"`, as in   [parameter_inference()], applied to every imputation's fit. For fits   with sampling weights the default is `"robust"`, and the other types are   refused with `latents_unsupported_weights`. @param adjust Multiplicity correction applied to the pooled p-values to   give `p_adjusted`, as in [parameter_inference()]: `"none"` (default) or   a method of [stats::p.adjust()]. The per-imputation tables are computed   without correction. @return An object of class `latents_pooled`. [as.data.frame()] and   `get_results(x, "estimates")` give one row per parameter, with the columns   of [parameter_inference()] (`level`, `outcome`, `term`, `parameter`,   `estimate`, `standard_error`, `statistic`, `p_value`, `p_adjusted`,   `conf_low`, `conf_high`) plus `df` (Rubin's degrees of freedom),   `within` and `between` (the two variance components), `riv` (the   relative increase in variance due to missingness) and `fmi` (the fraction   of missing information). `statistic` and `p_value` are `NA` where   [parameter_inference()] reports no test (variances and probabilities).   `get_results(x, "imputations")` gives each imputation's aligned estimates,   one row per imputation and parameter, and `get_results(x, "fits")` one row   per imputation with its log likelihood, convergence and the label   permutation that aligned it. @section Conditions:   `latents_bad_data` when `imputed` is not a list of at least two data frames   with identical columns and row counts; `latents_pooling_failed` when any   imputation's fit or inference fails (the message names the imputation and   gives the original reason); `latents_missing_package` for a `mids` object   without mice installed. Warnings from the individual fits are passed on   as they are raised. @references Rubin, D. B. (1987). *Multiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys*. Wiley.  Meng, X.-L. (1994). Multiple-imputation inferences with uncongenial sources of input. *Statistical Science*, 9(4), 538--558.  van Buuren, S. (2018). *Flexible Imputation of Missing Data* (2nd ed.), section 5.2. Chapman & Hall/CRC. @examples set.seed(1) # Two stand-in completed data sets. With real missing covariates, pass the # `mids` object mice::mice() returns instead. completed <- lapply(seq_len(2), function(i) {   within(subset(course_engagement, student <= 40),          previous_grade <- previous_grade + rnorm(length(previous_grade), sd = 0.1)) }) pooled <- pool_imputations(completed, c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read"),                            "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 1,                            profile_covariates = "previous_grade",                            n_starts = 2, seed = 1) pooled get_results(pooled, "fits") @export

.multilpa_pool_step.documentation: Run one imputation's step, naming the imputation if it fails  Rubin's rules need every imputation, so a failure is not dropped: it is raised again as `latents_pooling_failed`, with the imputation's number and the original condition's class and message. @param index The imputation's number. @param stage `"fitting"` or `"inference"`. @param expr The step. @return The step's value. @noRd

.multilpa_rubin.name: .multilpa_rubin
.multilpa_rubin.documentation: Pool inference tables with Rubin's rules  Rubin (1987): the pooled estimate is the mean `Q`, the total variance `T = U + (1 + 1/m) B` with `U` the mean within-imputation variance and `B` the between-imputation variance, `r=(1 + 1/m) * B / U`, degrees of freedom `(m - 1)(1 + 1/r)^2` (infinite when `B` is zero), and the fraction of missing information `(r + 2 / (df + 3)) / (r + 1)`.  @param tables Aligned [parameter_inference()] tables, one per imputation. @param level Interval level. @param adjust A [stats::p.adjust()] method for `p_adjusted`. @return A data frame, one row per parameter. @noRd

.multilpa_rubin_covariance.name: .multilpa_rubin_covariance
.multilpa_rubin_covariance.documentation: Pool the imputations' covariance matrices  A covariate-free inference table carries its covariance; a covariate fit's comes from [vcov()] with the same `vcov_type`. Either way its diagonal must reproduce the table's squared standard errors, which is what ties its rows to the table's rows. @param tables Aligned [parameter_inference()] tables. @param fits The aligned fits the tables came from. @param vcov_type As in [parameter_inference()]. @return The total covariance `U + (1 + 1/m) B`, named by parameter. @noRd

.multilpa_pool_long.documentation: Every imputation's aligned estimates, one row per imputation and parameter @param tables Aligned [parameter_inference()] tables. @return A data frame. @noRd

prior_control.name: prior_control
prior_control.documentation: Specify a conjugate prior for Gaussian mixture estimation  Returns a `latents_prior` object requesting maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation of the Gaussian profile means and covariances under the conjugate prior of Fraley and Raftery (2007), as `mclust::priorControl()` does for `mclust::Mclust()`. Pass the result as `multilpa(prior = )`. The prior keeps the covariance estimates away from singularity.  Every argument left `NULL` takes `mclust::defaultPrior()`'s value, computed from the indicators being fitted: the prior mean is their column means, the degrees of freedom are `d + 2` for `d` indicators, and the scale is `(1/G)^(2/d)` times the sample covariance (ellipsoidal structures) or times the average sample variance (axis-parallel and spherical structures), for `G` profiles.  The updates follow mclust's fitted-model convention, including its structure-specific departures from a textbook conjugate update, so the controls have different effects across covariance structures. For `EII`, `scale` does not enter the variance update. For `EEI`, `shrinkage` and `mean` enter the variance calculation but do not shrink the fitted means. For `VEV`, `dof` does not enter the update. `EEI`, `EVI` and `EEV` count the mean-prior contribution once rather than once per profile.  @param shrinkage Non-negative prior precision factor for the means, `kappa`   (default `0.01`, as in mclust). Zero leaves the means unshrunk. @param mean Optional prior mean, one value per continuous indicator, on the   scale the profile means are estimated on: the indicators' own units, or   their centred values under [multilpa()]'s `centering`. Requires a positive   `shrinkage`. @param dof Optional prior degrees of freedom, a single positive number. @param scale Optional prior scale: a single positive number for an   axis-parallel or spherical structure, or a positive-definite `d` by `d`   matrix for an ellipsoidal one. @return An object of class `latents_prior`: a list with `shrinkage`, `mean`,   `dof` and `scale`, the last three `NULL` where the default is to be   computed from the data. @section Conditions:   `latents_bad_argument` for a negative or non-finite `shrinkage`, a   non-finite `mean`, a `mean` with a zero `shrinkage`, a non-positive or   non-finite `dof`, or a `scale` that is neither a positive number nor a   square, symmetric, positive-definite matrix. @references Fraley, C., & Raftery, A. E. (2007). Bayesian regularization for   normal mixture estimation and model-based clustering. *Journal of   Classification*, 24, 155--181. \doi{10.1007/s00357-007-0004-5} @seealso [multilpa()], whose `prior` argument takes this. @examples prior_control() prior_control(shrinkage = 0) @export

.multilpa_positive_scale.name: .multilpa_positive_scale

A matrix is checked as one: square, symmetric to a relative `1e-10` and with a positive smallest eigenvalue. diagnostics.name: diagnostics
diagnostics.documentation: Classification diagnostics of a fitted model  Gathers the four classification tables of [get_results()] (`"entropy"`, `"classification"`, `"average_posteriors"` and `"residuals"`) for a fitted model, prints one line per diagnostic, and by default draws the classification plots. The diagnostics are relative entropy, estimated class sizes, average posterior probabilities of the assigned classes, and the bivariate residuals that check the within-profile independence the model assumes.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @param data Optional. The data the model was fitted to. A fit carries the   columns it was built from, so this is only needed to override them. @param plots `TRUE` (the default) also draws the four classification plots:   effective profile sizes, posterior probabilities of the assigned   profiles, case entropy, and the average posterior probability matrix.   Without the ggplot2 package a message says so and the tables are still   returned. `FALSE` returns the tables only. @param by `"profile"` (the default) assesses each profile's bivariate   residuals separately; `"overall"` pools them. It is the only argument   forwarded to the gathered tables. The `level` of the classification   tables is set from whether the fit has discrete group classes. @param ... Not used. For `diagnostics()` and `plot()`, any further argument   raises `latents_bad_argument`; style the returned plots with ggplot2. @return An object of class `multilpa_diagnostics`. Its tables are read with   `get_results(result, what = )`, where `what` is `"entropy"`,   `"classification"`, `"average_posteriors"`, `"residuals"` or `"all"`. A   model family without bivariate residuals leaves that table out of   `"all"`, and asking for it by name raises `latents_no_group_classes`; a   fit with a noise component has none either, and raises   `latents_unsupported_noise`.    `print()` prints one line per diagnostic (relative entropy, smallest   class, lowest average posterior and largest residual, at each level the   fit has) and returns the object invisibly. `plot()` returns the four   classification plots as a `latents_plots` list of ggplot objects, which   draws all four when printed. `as.data.frame()` returns the entropy table. @seealso [get_results()] for these and the other tables, [descriptives()]   for the variables before fitting, and [summary()] for the estimates. @examples fit <- multilpa(   course_engagement,   vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),   id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,   seed = 1 ) quality <- diagnostics(fit) quality get_results(quality, what = "classification") get_results(diagnostics(fit, by = "overall"), what = "residuals") @export

as.data.frame.multilpa_diagnostics.name: as.data.frame.multilpa_diagnostics
as.data.frame.multilpa_diagnostics.documentation: @rdname diagnostics @param row.names,optional Part of the base generic; `row.names` is applied   to the returned table. @export

.multilpa_reject_extra_arguments.name: .multilpa_reject_extra_arguments
.multilpa_reject_extra_arguments.documentation: Refuse arguments a forwarding verb cannot pass on  A verb that gathers other verbs documents which of their arguments it forwards. Anything else is named back to the caller instead of being dropped: a discarded `by =` returns a table that answers a different question from the one that was asked, and does so without a word.  @param extra `list(...)` as the forwarding verb received it. @param verb The verb's name, for the message. @param advice One sentence saying what the verb does forward. @return `NULL`, invisibly, when there is nothing to refuse. @noRd

.latents_warn_unused_arguments.name: .latents_warn_unused_arguments
.latents_warn_unused_arguments.documentation: Warn about arguments a released method used to ignore  Up to latents 0.9.21 these `plot()` methods ignored any argument they did not use. Refusing one now would break code written for that release, and ignoring it silently would hide a call that does not do what it says, so the method draws as before and says what it ignored.  @param extra `list(...)` as the method received it. @param verb The call, for the message. @param advice What to do instead. @return `NULL`, invisibly; warns with class `latents_unused_argument`. @noRd

.latents_former_argument.name: .latents_former_argument
.latents_former_argument.documentation: Take a value given under an argument's 0.9.21 name  Arguments renamed after latents 0.9.21 keep their old name as a second formal, so code written for that release runs unchanged. Giving both names is ambiguous and refused.  @param current The value of the argument under its present name. @param current_given Whether the caller supplied the present name. @param former The value under the 0.9.21 name, `NULL` when not given. @param names The present and the former name, for the message. @return The value to use. @noRd

report.name: report
report.documentation: Print a full report of a fitted model  Prints the model summary, the descriptive statistics of its variables and the classification diagnostics, then draws every plot view the fit supports.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @param data Optional. The data the model was fitted to; a fit carries the   columns it was built from. @param plots `TRUE` (the default) draws the plots. `FALSE` prints only. @param rows Number of rows of each summary table to print, passed to   `print(summary(x))`. Default 10. @param by Passed to [diagnostics()] for the bivariate residuals:   `"profile"` (the default) assesses each profile separately, `"overall"`   pools them. @param ... Not used. Any further argument raises `latents_bad_argument`   before anything is printed. @section What it prints: `summary()`, then `descriptives()`, then the   one-line-per-diagnostic reading of `diagnostics()`, then every plot view   the fit supports. Views that the plot method declines for this model are   listed after the plots as not drawn. The tables themselves are obtained   from [get_results()], [summary()], [descriptives()] and [diagnostics()]. @return The fitted model, invisibly. Called for its printed and plotted   output. @seealso [summary()], [diagnostics()], [descriptives()],   [plot_views()]. @examples fit <- multilpa(   course_engagement,   vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),   id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,   seed = 1 ) report(fit, plots = FALSE) @export

.multilpa_supported_views.name: .multilpa_supported_views
.multilpa_supported_views.documentation: The plot views a given fit can actually draw  `plot_views()` lists every view the methods accept; this filters it to the ones this fit has the ingredients for, so `report()` does not stop on the first refusal.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @return A character vector of `what` values. @noRd

.multilpa_available_views_text.name: .multilpa_available_views_text
.multilpa_available_views_text.documentation: The supported views of a fit, phrased for a refusal message  @param x A fitted model of this package. @return A single string listing the views, or `"none"`. @noRd

.multilpa_group_scores.name: .multilpa_group_scores
.multilpa_group_scores.documentation: Per-group scores of the observed-data log likelihood  Decomposes the gradient into one row per independent group. The groups are the independent sampling units of the two-level likelihood, so these rows are the contributions the robust cross-product matrix accumulates.  @param theta Unconstrained parameter vector. @param x Centered numeric indicator matrix, possibly containing NA. @param object Fitted model defining dimensions and groups. @return A groups-by-parameters matrix whose column sums equal the gradient of   the positive observed-data log likelihood, that is `-.multilpa_score()`. @noRd

.multilpa_full_measurement_group_score.name: .multilpa_full_measurement_group_score
.multilpa_full_measurement_group_score.documentation: Per-group Gaussian scores in log-Cholesky coordinates @param parameters Decoded Gaussian and mixing parameters. @param expectation Nested expectation step including Gaussian moments. @param object A fitted full-covariance model. @return Groups-by-parameter mean and log-Cholesky score blocks. @noRd

.multilpa_design_scale.name: .multilpa_design_scale
.multilpa_design_scale.documentation: Column scales that make an optimization coordinate unit-free  A multinomial logit is a parameterization of the same model under any linear rescaling of a predictor: multiplying a covariate by `c` and its coefficient by `1/c` leaves every fitted probability alone. A quasi-Newton search is not invariant in that way, because it stops on a relative tolerance measured in the coordinates it was handed. A column whose units are `1e-7` times those of the rest therefore stalls the search while the score is still large, and the optimizer still reports success.  The root-mean-square of a column is exactly proportional to that column's units, so dividing each column by it gives a design matrix that does not change when a predictor is rescaled. Fitting in those coordinates and dividing the coefficients back by the same scales returns estimates in the user's units while making the search itself unit-free.  @param design A numeric design matrix with finite entries. @return A positive numeric vector with one entry per column of `design`. A   column that is exactly zero, or whose root-mean-square is not finite, gets   `1`, so the scaling is never itself a source of `NaN`. @noRd

.multilpa_covariance_coordinate_scale.name: .multilpa_covariance_coordinate_scale
.multilpa_covariance_coordinate_scale.documentation: Scales for the log-Cholesky coordinates of a residual covariance  The unrestricted residual covariance is estimated through the lower triangle of its Cholesky factor, with the diagonal logged. Those coordinates do not share one unit: a logged diagonal entry is dimensionless, while an off-diagonal entry `L[i, j]` carries the units of indicator `i`. Handing them to a finite-difference Hessian unscaled makes the information matrix's condition number grow with the square of the indicator units, and it is then declared singular for no reason but the units the data arrived in.  This is the general form of the scaling [parameter_inference()] already applies to a covariate-free `multilpa` fit (R/inference.R), written so that the covariate path can share it instead of rediscovering it.  @param variances A profiles-by-indicators matrix of residual variances, the   diagonal of each profile's residual covariance. @param dimension Number of continuous indicators. @param rows Integer indices of the rows of `variances` whose spread block is   estimated separately: every profile under a varying spread, `1L` when one   block is shared. @return A positive numeric vector of length   `length(rows) * dimension * (dimension + 1) / 2`, ordered as the   coordinates themselves are: one block per entry of `rows`, and within a   block the lower triangle including the diagonal, in column-major order.   Diagonal entries get `1` because they are logged. @noRd

.latents_search_defaults.name: .latents_search_defaults
.latents_search_defaults.documentation: Settings of the emEM search that are not arguments  Chosen by the start-search benchmark (SEARCH-PLAN.md, section 6): ten screening iterations found a lower maximum than twenty on 9 of 200 EEE datasets and a higher one on none.  @return A list of `pool_factor` (the pool is this many times `n_starts`   when `n_screen` is `NULL`), `iterations` (the screening budget) and   `protect_first` (whether start 1, Ward's, always runs to the end). @noRd

.latents_check_search.name: .latents_check_search
.latents_check_search.documentation: Validate a requested start search  @param search `NULL` (the default, chosen from the covariance structure by   `.latents_default_search()`), `"kmeans"` or `"emEM"`. @return `search`, unchanged. @noRd

.latents_default_search.name: .latents_default_search
.latents_default_search.documentation: The default start search of a profile model  When every profile shares one covariance matrix (EII, EEI, EEE), the likelihood is bounded: no profile can collapse onto a point without lowering the density of every other (McLachlan & Peel, 2000, section 3.8). A higher maximum is then a better estimate, never a degenerate one, so the screened emEM search, which reaches more of them, is the default. With profile-specific covariances a higher maximum can be such a collapse, and the kmeans search stays the default.  @param structure The resolved covariance structure code. @param continuous The continuous indicators. @return `"emEM"` or `"kmeans"`. @noRd

.latents_search_screen.name: .latents_search_screen
.latents_search_screen.documentation: Validate `n_screen` and resolve the screening plan of a fit  @param search `"kmeans"` or `"emEM"`. @param n_starts Starts run to the end. @param n_screen `NULL` or the pool size. @param max_iter The fit's iteration budget. @param supplied Whether the caller supplied a `start`. @return `NULL` when nothing is screened (`"kmeans"`, or a supplied start   that runs alone), otherwise the `screen` list for   `.latents_run_starts()`. @noRd

.latents_start_kind.name: .latents_start_kind
.latents_start_kind.documentation: The kind of start at a position of the pool  Positions up to `n_starts` are the kmeans search's starts; after them the pool alternates random partitions and random centres.  @param start_index Position in the pool. @param n_starts Starts run to the end. @return `"kmeans"`, `"partition"` or `"centres"` (`"kmeans"` also for   start 1, which the caller initializes by Ward's clustering). @noRd

.latents_start_kind_label.name: .latents_start_kind_label
.latents_start_kind_label.documentation: The label of a start's kind in the starts table @inheritParams .latents_start_kind @return `"ward"`, `"kmeans"`, `"partition"` or `"centres"`. @noRd

.latents_search_record.name: .latents_search_record
.latents_search_record.documentation: The search controls a fit records  Kept separately from what the search found, so a refit (bootstrap, sensitivity) repeats the search that was requested.  @param search `"kmeans"` or `"emEM"`. @param n_starts Starts run to the end. @param screen The resolved screening plan, or `NULL`. @param select_start The requested selection rule. @param boundary_policy The requested `boundary` (the fit's own `boundary`   field is whether the selected solution is at the bound). @return A list of `search`, `n_starts`, `n_screen` (`NULL` when nothing   was screened), `select_start` and `boundary_policy`. @noRd

.latents_refit_controls.name: .latents_refit_controls
.latents_refit_controls.documentation: The fitting controls a bootstrap refit of a model uses  A refit repeats the search and the stopping rule the model was fitted with, so the statistic and its reference distribution come from the same procedure; an explicit `n_starts`, `max_iter` or `tol` overrides them for every model. A fit made before these controls were recorded falls back to the values `bootstrap_lrt()` used to apply to every refit (10 starts, 1000 iterations, `1e-8`, the default search, selection and acceleration).  @param model A fitted model. @param n_starts,max_iter,tol `NULL` to inherit, or an override. @return A named list of `search`, `n_starts`, `n_screen`, `max_iter`,   `tol`, `acceleration`, `select_start` and `boundary`. @noRd

.latents_refit_controls_frame.name: .latents_refit_controls_frame
.latents_refit_controls_frame.documentation: The refit controls of a bootstrap, one row per model @param controls A named list (`null`, `alternative`) from   `.latents_refit_controls()`. @return A data frame, one row per model, with the role and every control   (`n_screen` is `NA` when nothing is screened). @noRd

.latents_search_columns.name: .latents_search_columns
.latents_search_columns.documentation: Add the emEM columns to a starts table  Under emEM every start of the pool has a row: its kind, whether it was run to the end, and its likelihood after screening (for a start run to the end, `log_likelihood` is its final one). A kmeans table is returned unchanged.  @param table The engine's starts table, one row per start. @param found The result of `.latents_run_starts()`. @param n_starts Starts run to the end. @param supplied Whether start 1 was supplied by the caller. @return The table, with `kind`, `stage` and `screened_log_likelihood`   under emEM. @noRd

.latents_final_stage.name: .latents_final_stage
.latents_final_stage.documentation: Whether each start was run to the end @param found The result of `.latents_run_starts()`. @return A logical vector, one per start; all `TRUE` for the kmeans search. @noRd

.latents_selection_views.name: .latents_selection_views
.latents_selection_views.documentation: The model-selection views of an enumeration grid @return The view names `plot(grid, what = )` takes for model selection. @noRd

.latents_selection_frame.name: .latents_selection_frame
.latents_selection_frame.documentation: One row per candidate with the criterion the views read  @param x A `multilpa_enumeration`. @param using The criterion column. @return A data frame: `candidate`, `n_profiles`, `n_group_classes`,   `model`, `n_parameters`, `value`, and `usable` (converged with a finite   value). @noRd

.latents_smaller_neighbour.name: .latents_smaller_neighbour
.latents_smaller_neighbour.documentation: The value of the neighbour one step smaller in one direction  @param frame The output of `.latents_selection_frame()`. @param direction `"profiles"` or `"group_classes"`. @return For every row, the criterion of the usable candidate with one   profile (or one group class) fewer and everything else equal, and that   candidate's name; `NA` where there is none. @noRd

.latents_deltas_table.name: .latents_deltas_table
.latents_deltas_table.documentation: What each added profile and each added group class buys  @param x A `multilpa_enumeration`. @param using The criterion. @return One row per candidate: `candidate`, `n_profiles`,   `n_group_classes`, `model`, `criterion`, `value`, `delta_profile` (the   criterion's decrease from the candidate with one profile fewer, the same   group classes and structure; positive means this candidate is lower),   `from_profile`, `delta_group_class` and `from_group_class` (the same for   one group class fewer). `NA` where there is no such neighbour or this   candidate did not converge. @noRd

.latents_kneedle.name: .latents_kneedle
.latents_kneedle.documentation: The maximum perpendicular chord-distance knee of one curve  Both axes are rescaled to 0-1, and the knee is the point furthest below the straight line from the first point to the last, measured perpendicular to that line. This simplified Kneedle-inspired statistic omits smoothing, local-maxima thresholds and sensitivity; a tiny positive distance may therefore still name a knee.  @param x,y The curve, ordered by `x`. The curve is a criterion that should fall as the model grows; a line whose last value is not below its first has no knee, because a bend in a criterion that only rises marks no diminishing return.  @return A list: `at` (the index of the knee, `NA` without one), `distance`   (each point's perpendicular distance below the line, in the rescaled   units) and `rising` (`TRUE` when the criterion does not fall along the   line). @noRd

.latents_knees_table.name: .latents_knees_table
.latents_knees_table.documentation: The knee of every line of the grid, in each direction  @param x A `multilpa_enumeration`. @param using The criterion. @return One row per line: `direction` (`"profiles"`: along the number of   profiles at fixed group classes; `"group_classes"`: along the group   classes at fixed profiles; `"parameters"`: every candidate, by number of   parameters), `line` (what is held fixed), `criterion`, `from`, `to`,   `n_points`, `knee_candidate`, `distance`, `knee_without_largest`,   `stable` and `note`. @noRd

.latents_selection_look.name: .latents_selection_look
.latents_selection_look.documentation: Shared look of the selection views @noRd

.latents_class_word.name: .latents_class_word
.latents_class_word.documentation: "profiles" or "classes", as the grid's indicators make them @noRd

.gg_selection_deltas.name: .gg_selection_deltas
.gg_selection_deltas.documentation: Deltas view: what each added profile and group class buys  Two panels. In each, a line holds the other count fixed, and every point is the criterion's decrease from the neighbour one step smaller. Each line is named at its end. @noRd

.gg_selection_heatmap.name: .gg_selection_heatmap
.gg_selection_heatmap.documentation: Heatmap view: the criterion over profiles and group classes @noRd

.gg_selection_smallest.name: .gg_selection_smallest
.gg_selection_smallest.documentation: Smallest-class view: the share of the smallest class of every candidate @noRd

.gg_selection_trust.name: .gg_selection_trust
.gg_selection_trust.documentation: Trust view: whether each candidate's estimate can be believed @noRd

.gg_selection_view.name: .gg_selection_view
.gg_selection_view.documentation: Draw one model-selection view @param x A `multilpa_enumeration`. @param view One of `.latents_selection_views()`. @param using The criterion. @param main,subtitle Titles. @return A ggplot. @noRd

sensitivity.name: sensitivity
sensitivity.documentation: Refit a model under several seeds  Refits the model under each of several random seeds and returns one row per seed with the maximised log likelihood, convergence, which distinct optimum the refit reached, and the proportion of observations assigned to the same profile as in the reference fit. Profile labels of each refit are matched to the reference fit's before agreement is computed.  A fit's own replication count describes only the starts within one seed's random-number stream; refitting under other seeds shows whether other streams reach the same maximum and the same classification.  A seed whose refit fails gives a row with `NA` estimates, and a `latents_sensitivity_dropped` warning reports how many seeds failed.  @param x The reference fit: a [multilpa()] model, an [lta()] model, or a   growth mixture ([mixture_regression()] with `random`). A [fit_staged()]   result varies the second-stage starts while holding its first-stage   measurement solution fixed. A directly fitted model with measurement   blocks held fixed is refused (`latents_unsupported_sensitivity`), because   its original free starting values are not retained. A   membership-covariate fit is refused with   `latents_unsupported_sensitivity`. For an [lta()] fit, `agreement` is the   share of occasions given the same profile, after matching the refit's   profiles on the measurement; for a growth mixture it is the share of   persons given the same class, after matching the refit's classes by   their posterior memberships of the fitted persons. @param data Optional for a [multilpa()] fit or a growth mixture, which   carry the columns they were built from. Required for an [lta()] fit   (`latents_bad_argument` otherwise). It must be the data the model was   fitted to, in its original row order; shared identifier and indicator   columns are checked against the fit (`latents_bad_inference_data`). @param seeds Seeds to refit under: at least two distinct whole numbers   that `set.seed()` accepts. Default `1:10`. Anything else raises   `latents_bad_argument`. If the reference fit's own seed is included, that   row reproduces the reference fit. @param n_starts Starts per refit. Defaults to the number the reference fit   used. @param max_iter,tol Passed to each refit. Default to the reference fit's   (for an [lta()] fit, to the defaults of [lta()]). @param tolerance Two log likelihoods within this of each other count as   the same optimum. Defaults to the reference fit's replication tolerance   (for a growth mixture, `1e-6 * (1 + abs(logLik))`). @return A base `data.frame`, one row per seed, with columns `seed`,   `log_likelihood`, `converged`, `iterations`, `optimum` (1 for the best   maximum found across the seeds, 2 for the next distinct one, and so on),   `best` (whether this seed reached optimum 1) and `agreement` (the   proportion of observations given the same profile as the reference fit,   after label matching). A failed refit has `NA` in every column except   `seed`. @seealso [enumerate_classes()] to vary the number of classes, and   [parameter_inference()] for uncertainty about the parameters of a single   solution. @references Hipp, J. R., & Bauer, D. J. (2006). Local solutions in the   estimation of growth mixture models. *Psychological Methods, 11*, 36--53. @examples set.seed(7) example_data <- data.frame(   school = rep(seq_len(12), each = 10),   score_a = c(rnorm(60, -1.5), rnorm(60, 1.5)),   score_b = c(rnorm(60, -1), rnorm(60, 1)) ) fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("score_a", "score_b"), "school",                 n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 3, seed = 1) sensitivity(fit, seeds = 1:3, n_starts = 3)  # Growth mixtures are known for local solutions (Hipp and Bauer 2006). growth <- mixture_regression(score ~ wave, data = subset(growth_scores, student <= 60),                              n_classes = 2, id = "student", class_level = "group",                              random = ~ 1, n_starts = 1, seed = 1) sensitivity(growth, seeds = 1:2) @export

.sensitivity_profiles.name: .sensitivity_profiles
.sensitivity_profiles.documentation: How sensitivity() refits a profile model and compares its assignments @return A list with `refit` (a function of a seed), `agreement` (a   function of a refit) and `tolerance`. @noRd

.sensitivity_transitions.name: .sensitivity_transitions
.sensitivity_transitions.documentation: How sensitivity() refits a transition model and compares its assignments  Each occasion's modal profile is compared, after the refit's profiles are matched to the reference's on the measurement (`.lta_profile_signature()`). @noRd

.sensitivity_growth.name: .sensitivity_growth
.sensitivity_growth.documentation: How sensitivity() refits a growth mixture and compares its assignments  Persons' modal classes are compared after the refit's classes are matched to the reference's by their posterior memberships of the fitted persons. @noRd

.multilpa_optimum_index.name: .multilpa_optimum_index
.multilpa_optimum_index.documentation: Number the distinct maxima a set of log likelihoods reached  Sorted from the best downwards, a new optimum begins wherever the drop from the previous one exceeds `tolerance`. Comparing the likelihoods pairwise would not do: `==` on doubles is never right here, and a chain of values each within tolerance of the last is one basin, not several.  @param likelihood Maximised log likelihoods, possibly with `NA`. @param tolerance Two values within this count as the same optimum. @return An integer vector the same length as `likelihood`; `1` is the best   maximum, and a failed fit is `NA`. @noRd

.multilpa_require_time.name: .multilpa_require_time
.multilpa_require_time.documentation: The time column of a fit, or a classed error  @param object A fitted `multilpa` model. @return The stored time values, in input row order. @noRd

.multilpa_time_name.name: .multilpa_time_name
.multilpa_time_name.documentation: Name of the column the ordering came from  Used to build self-describing occasion column names. A fit always stores the name beside the values, but a hand-assembled fixture may carry only the values, so a neutral fallback keeps the names syntactic either way.  @param object A fitted model carrying an ordering. @return A single character string. @noRd

.multilpa_sequence_matrix.name: .multilpa_sequence_matrix
.multilpa_sequence_matrix.documentation: Assigned profiles as a groups-by-occasions integer matrix  The rectangular layout the drawing code needs. A matrix is the right structure inside a function body and the wrong one to return to a caller, so this stays internal and the sequence table is a data frame instead.  @param object A fitted model carrying an ordering. @param long The long form, if the caller already has it; recomputed   otherwise, so that an outside caller needs only the fit. @return An integer matrix with one row per group and one column per position   seen anywhere in the data, holding the assigned profile or `NA`. Row names   are the group identifiers made unique, in increasing group order; column   names are `<time>_<position>`. @noRd

.multilpa_occasion_names.name: .multilpa_occasion_names
.multilpa_occasion_names.documentation: Syntactic, self-describing names for the occasion columns  @param object A fitted model carrying an ordering. @param positions The distinct positions, in increasing order. @return A character vector of syntactic, unique column names. @noRd

.multilpa_sequences.name: .multilpa_sequences
.multilpa_sequences.documentation: Profile assignments in occasion order  Documented on `?get_results`, which is where a caller reaches this table from.  @param x A fitted model of this package, fitted with `time =`. @param format `"long"` for one row per observation, `"wide"` for one row per   group with one column per occasion. @return A base `data.frame`. @noRd

.multilpa_sequence_summary.name: .multilpa_sequence_summary
.multilpa_sequence_summary.documentation: How much data each group class contributes  Documented on `?get_results`, which is where a caller reaches this table from.  @param x A fitted model of this package, fitted with `time =`. @return A base `data.frame`, one row per group class, including any class no   group was assigned to. @noRd

.latents_local_seed.name: .latents_local_seed
.latents_local_seed.documentation: Set a seed for the calling function and restore the random state on its exit  Seeded verbs must not leave the caller's random stream changed: a user who sets a seed, fits a model with its own `seed`, and then draws again should get the draw they would have got without the fit. The previous `.Random.seed` is restored when the *calling* function exits, normally or by an error; when there was none, the one `set.seed()` created is removed, so a fresh session stays fresh. Registering the restore on the caller's frame (rather than wrapping its body) lets a call site be one line placed exactly where its own block used to set the seed.  The seed is not validated here: each verb validates it with `.multilpa_check_seed()` where it always has, so the refusal comes at the same point as before.  @param seed `NULL` (nothing is done) or a seed for [set.seed()]. @param frame The function frame whose exit restores the state. @param after Passed to [on.exit()]: whether the restore runs after (the   default) or before the caller's other exit handlers. @return `NULL`, invisibly. @noRd

.latents_draw_rows.name: .latents_draw_rows
.latents_draw_rows.documentation: Draw one category per row from a matrix of row-wise probabilities  Inverse-CDF sampling in one pass, one uniform per row: the category is the first whose cumulative probability reaches the uniform. The last cumulative probability is set to exactly one, so that a rounding shortfall (a row summing to slightly less than one, as exponentiated log probabilities do) cannot leave a uniform above every cumulative total; it falls in the last category, not past it, and not back to the first.  A one-column matrix still consumes one uniform per row, so a model with a single class draws the same stream as one with several.  @param probabilities Matrix whose rows each sum to one. @return An integer vector, one column index per row. @noRd

.multilpa_resample_groups.name: .multilpa_resample_groups
.multilpa_resample_groups.documentation: One resample of the groups, as a data frame  A group drawn twice has to become two groups, or the refit would pool the two copies into one unit and the resample would carry fewer groups than it drew.  @param data The fitting data. @param rows_by_group Row indices of each group, in group order. @param id The group column's name. @param drawn Which groups were drawn, with replacement. @return A data frame with one relabelled group per draw. @noRd

.latents_cluster_bootstrap.name: .latents_cluster_bootstrap
.latents_cluster_bootstrap.documentation: Cluster bootstrap replicates of a fit's estimates  Each replicate draws the groups with replacement, refits, and reads the estimates in the original fit's labels; a refit that fails, does not converge or cannot be matched is a row of `NA` with its reason. One replicate's draw, refit and alignment happen together, so replicate `i` sees the same stream whatever the refit consumes.  @param data The fitting data. @param group_index The group of each row (integers `1..n_groups`). @param n_groups Number of groups. @param id The group column's name. @param iter How many resamples to draw. @param refit A function of the resampled data returning a fit; it may raise   (the message is recorded) and handles its own warnings. @param extract A function of a converged refit returning its estimates in   the reference labels, or a string saying why it could not. @param reference_names The estimates' names, which also fix their number. @return A list with `estimates` (`iter` rows, `NA` for a failed resample)   and `messages` (why each failed, `NA` otherwise). @noRd

.latents_blrt_replicates.name: .latents_blrt_replicates
.latents_blrt_replicates.documentation: The replicate loop of a bootstrap likelihood-ratio test  Each replicate simulates from the null and refits both models inside one call of `replicate`, so the draws interleave with the refits as they always have. A replicate that raises is recorded with its message; the warnings it raised are recorded too, and either muffled (the transition and additive verbs, whose refits warn routinely) or passed on to the caller (the profile verb, which has always shown them).  @param iter Number of replicates. @param replicate A function of the replicate number returning a list with   `statistic`, `valid`, `boundary`, `logits_settled`, `null_replications`   and `alternative_replications`. @param muffle_warnings Whether a replicate's warnings stop at the record. @return A data frame, one row per replicate. @noRd

.latents_blrt_p_value.name: .latents_blrt_p_value
.latents_blrt_p_value.documentation: The bootstrap likelihood-ratio p-value from its replicates  The p-value counts the observed statistic among the replicates, `(1 + #{T* >= T}) / (iter + 1)`, and is reported only when every replicate is valid: dropping the failed ones would condition the reference distribution on the fits that happened to succeed.  @param replicates The replicate table. @param observed The observed statistic. @param iter Number of replicates. @return A list with `p_value`, `monte_carlo_se` and `n_valid`; warns   (`latents_failed_replicates`) when the p-value is withheld. @noRd

.latents_execute_start.name: .latents_execute_start
.latents_execute_start.documentation: Execute a self-contained start task without creating workers @param task A start index, isolated runner, and initial values or checkpoint. @return A full or screened start attempt. @noRd

.latents_start_tasks.name: .latents_start_tasks
.latents_start_tasks.documentation: Build flat tasks while retaining candidate and original start order @param candidates Collected setup results, one per grid row. @param phase Screening or final runs. @param screened,ranked Per-candidate screening results and ranking records. @return Self-contained worker tasks; no finaliser or whole grid is captured. @noRd

.latents_pool_phase.name: .latents_pool_phase
.latents_pool_phase.documentation: Run one flat search phase and group its collected results in grid order @param tasks Self-contained start tasks. @param costs Estimated candidate costs in grid order. @param cores Total worker budget. @param n_candidates Number of grid rows, including failed setups. @param execute Function running one self-contained task. @param on_lost Optional terminal process-loss callback for the mapper. @return Collected attempts grouped by candidate, then original task order. @noRd

.latents_pool_setup.name: .latents_pool_setup
.latents_pool_setup.documentation: Prepare every candidate of a pooled grid  A seeded candidate sets its own seed before drawing its starts (`.latents_local_seed()`), so preparing it on a worker gives the plan this process would. Unseeded candidates draw from the caller's random stream, which only this process can continue in grid order; they, and every grid on one core, are prepared here in grid order, as they always have been. @param tasks Self-contained setup tasks in grid order. @param setup A function of one task returning its plan, or the candidate's   error condition. @param costs Estimated candidate costs in grid order. @param cores Total worker budget. @param distribute Whether the setups may run on workers: every candidate   is seeded and at least one has a setup worth distributing. @return Collected setups (`value` and `conditions`) in grid order. @noRd

.latents_pool_progress.name: .latents_pool_progress
.latents_pool_progress.documentation: Report one phase of a pooled grid, when progress was asked for  The message has its own class, `latents_progress`, so it can be told apart from a fit's qualifications, which do not depend on the number of cores. @param verbose Whether to report. @param format,...
