A `sprintf()` format and its values. @return NULL, invisibly. @noRd

.latents_count.name: .latents_count
.latents_count.documentation: A count with its noun, singular for one @param n A whole number. @param noun The singular noun; the plural adds an "s". @return One string such as `"1 worker"` or `"12 workers"`. @noRd

.latents_format_duration.name: .latents_format_duration
.latents_format_duration.documentation: A duration in words for progress messages @param seconds Elapsed seconds. @return One string such as `"under a minute"`, `"42 min"` or `"1 h 12 min"`. @noRd

.multilpa_separable_structures.name: .multilpa_separable_structures
.multilpa_separable_structures.documentation: The structures estimated in their own separable coordinates  EEI, VVI, EEE and VVV constrain nothing across profiles beyond sharing or freeing the whole block, so each profile's block is maximized by itself and is charted as log variances or log-Cholesky coordinates. The other ten tie the profiles together.  @return A character vector of mclust model codes. @noRd

.multilpa_uses_chart.name: .multilpa_uses_chart
.multilpa_uses_chart.documentation: Is a fit estimated in a constrained-structure chart? @param object A fitted `multilpa` model. @return A single logical. @noRd

.multilpa_spread_shared.name: .multilpa_spread_shared
.multilpa_spread_shared.documentation: Is the natural spread block one shared block rather than one per profile?  A block is reported once when the structure makes every profile's block the same matrix, and once per profile otherwise. For the four separable structures that is exactly `variance_model = "equal"`; of the other ten only EII makes every block identical.  @param object A fitted `multilpa` model. @return A single logical. @noRd

.multilpa_chart.name: .multilpa_chart
.multilpa_chart.documentation: Describe the free coordinates of a constrained structure  @param structure An mclust model code outside the separable four. @param k Number of profiles. @param d Number of continuous indicators. @return A list: `form` (`"spherical"`, `"diagonal"`, `"rotation"` or   `"cholesky"`), the row counts and per-profile row maps of the volume, shape   and rotation blocks, their widths and offsets, and `width`, the total. @noRd

.multilpa_chart_cholesky_positions.name: .multilpa_chart_cholesky_positions
.multilpa_chart_cholesky_positions.documentation: The (row, column) positions a Cholesky shape block is charted by  The lower triangle in column-major order, less the last diagonal entry, whose logarithm is minus the sum of the others.  @param d The dimension. @return A two-column integer matrix of positions. @noRd

.multilpa_chart_rotation_pairs.name: .multilpa_chart_rotation_pairs
.multilpa_chart_rotation_pairs.documentation: The (a, b), a < b, pairs a skew-symmetric rotation block is charted by @param d The dimension. @return A two-column integer matrix of positions. @noRd

.multilpa_fitted_blocks.name: .multilpa_fitted_blocks
.multilpa_fitted_blocks.documentation: The fitted covariance matrices of a fit, one per profile @param object A fitted `multilpa` model. @return A list of `d` by `d` matrices. @noRd

.multilpa_chart_anchor.name: .multilpa_chart_anchor
.multilpa_chart_anchor.documentation: The orientations the rotation chart is centred on  With a varying orientation each profile's own eigenvectors. With a shared one the eigenvectors of a generic positive combination of the profiles' covariances: every one of them is diagonal in the shared orientation, so any combination is too, and unequal weights keep its eigenvalues apart.  @param blocks The fitted covariance matrices. @param chart The chart, from `.multilpa_chart()`. @return A list of orthogonal matrices, one per rotation row, or `NULL`. @noRd

.multilpa_chart_encode.name: .multilpa_chart_encode
.multilpa_chart_encode.documentation: Encode fitted covariances in the constrained-structure chart  @param object A fitted `multilpa` model whose structure uses a chart. @return A list with `values` (the named chart coordinates), `scale` (a   typical magnitude for each, used only to condition the numerical Hessian),   `chart` and `anchor`. @noRd

.multilpa_chart_map.name: .multilpa_chart_map
.multilpa_chart_map.documentation: Map chart coordinates to covariance matrices, and differentiate the map  @param phi The chart coordinates, in `.multilpa_chart_encode()` order. @param chart The chart. @param anchor The orientations the rotation chart is centred on. @param derivatives Whether to return the Jacobian as well. @return A list with `sigma`, one covariance matrix per profile, and, when   asked, `jacobian`, one `d^2` by `length(phi)` matrix per profile holding   `d vec(Sigma_k) / d phi`. @noRd

.multilpa_chart_decode.name: .multilpa_chart_decode
.multilpa_chart_decode.documentation: Decode the spread block of a chart-coordinate parameter vector  @param phi The chart coordinates. @param object The fit defining the chart and its anchor. @return A list with `variances` (profiles by indicators) and, for an   ellipsoidal structure, `covariances` (`d` by `d` by profiles). @noRd

.multilpa_profile_gradients.name: .multilpa_profile_gradients
.multilpa_profile_gradients.documentation: Gradients of the log likelihood with respect to each profile's covariance  By Fisher's identity the observed-data score is the conditional expectation of the complete-data score, so with missing indicators the scatter carries the conditional covariance of what was not observed. The gradient with respect to an unconstrained symmetric `Sigma_k` is `(P S P - w P) / 2`.  @param parameters Decoded parameters. @param expectation The expectation step at those parameters. @param x The centred indicator matrix. @param group_index Group indices, or `NULL` for pooled totals. @return A list with `means` (groups, or one row, by profiles-times-indicators)   and `covariance`, one groups-by-`d^2` matrix per profile. @noRd

.multilpa_chart_scores.name: .multilpa_chart_scores
.multilpa_chart_scores.documentation: Measurement scores in the constrained-structure chart  @param parameters Decoded parameters. @param expectation The expectation step at those parameters. @param x The centred indicator matrix. @param object The fit defining the chart. @param phi The chart coordinates the parameters were decoded from. @param group_index Group indices, or `NULL` for pooled totals. @return A list with `means` and `covariances`, each a matrix with one row per   group (or one row) and one column per coordinate, of the positive log   likelihood's gradient. @noRd

.multilpa_chart_natural_jacobian.name: .multilpa_chart_natural_jacobian
.multilpa_chart_natural_jacobian.documentation: Natural spread coefficients differentiated with respect to the chart  @param object A fit whose structure uses a chart. @return A matrix with one row per natural spread coefficient, in   `.multilpa_coefficients()` order, and one column per chart coordinate. @noRd

.multilpa_step_ml_fit.name: .multilpa_step_ml_fit
.multilpa_step_ml_fit.documentation: Fit the step-three model of a continuous distal outcome  @param pieces The list from `.multilpa_level_assignments()` (or the   trajectory equivalent): `posteriors`, `modal`, `n_classes`. @param values The outcome, one value per unit. @param variance `"varying"` (a variance per class) or `"equal"`. @param tol Relative change in the log likelihood at which EM stops. @param max_iter Maximum number of EM iterations. @return A list: `means`, `variances` (one per class), `responsibilities`   (units by classes), `log_likelihood`, `converged`, `iterations`, and the   fixed `weights` (units by classes: the prior times the probability of the   unit's assigned class). @noRd

.multilpa_step_ml_polish.name: .multilpa_step_ml_polish
.multilpa_step_ml_polish.documentation: Newton steps from the EM estimate to the stationary point  EM approaches the maximum slowly near it, leaving a score that is small in standard-error units but visible against another program's printed estimates. A few Newton steps on the means and log standard deviations finish the job; each step is halved until the likelihood does not fall, so the polish never moves away from the EM estimate's likelihood. @param fit From `.multilpa_step_ml_fit()`'s EM. @param values The outcome. @param variance `"varying"` or `"equal"`. @return The fit at the stationary point, with `converged` set when the   score vanished. @noRd

.multilpa_step_ml_responsibilities.name: .multilpa_step_ml_responsibilities
.multilpa_step_ml_responsibilities.documentation: Each unit's posterior class probabilities under the step-three model @noRd

.multilpa_step_ml_scores.name: .multilpa_step_ml_scores
.multilpa_step_ml_scores.documentation: Per-unit scores of the step-three model  Coordinates: the class means, then the log standard deviations (one per class, or one shared). @param fit From `.multilpa_step_ml_fit()`. @param values The outcome. @param variance `"varying"` or `"equal"`. @param parameters Optional coordinates at which to evaluate; the fit's own   by default. @return A units-by-coordinates matrix. @noRd

.multilpa_step_ml_coordinates.name: .multilpa_step_ml_coordinates
.multilpa_step_ml_coordinates.documentation: The step-three model's coordinates at its estimate @noRd

.multilpa_step_ml_scale.name: .multilpa_step_ml_scale
.multilpa_step_ml_scale.documentation: The scale of each step-three coordinate  The means are in the outcome's units and the log standard deviations are unit free. The finite differences of the Hessian and the stopping rule on the score are taken on this scale, so neither depends on the outcome's units: an absolute step of 1e-3 is far wider than the curvature of an outcome measured in units of 1e-4. @param fit A step-three fit with `means` and `variances`. @param variance `"varying"` or `"equal"`. @return One positive scale per coordinate of `.multilpa_step_ml_coordinates()`. @noRd

.multilpa_step_ml_hessian.name: .multilpa_step_ml_hessian
.multilpa_step_ml_hessian.documentation: The Hessian of the step-three objective from its analytic gradient  Central differences of the gradient, each coordinate stepped by a fixed fraction of its own scale, then symmetrized. `stats::optimHess()` steps by 1e-3 in the coordinates' units, which on an outcome measured in units of 1e-4 is wider than the curvature it measures (an information of 0.15 for 365, and standard errors 3000 times too large); with `parscale` it was still wrong. @param gradient A function of the coordinates. @param parameters The point. @param scale From `.multilpa_step_ml_scale()`. @return A symmetric matrix. @noRd

.multilpa_step_ml_log_likelihood.name: .multilpa_step_ml_log_likelihood
.multilpa_step_ml_log_likelihood.documentation: The step-three log likelihood at given coordinates @noRd

.multilpa_step_ml_influence.name: .multilpa_step_ml_influence
.multilpa_step_ml_influence.documentation: Influence contributions of the class means, one row per unit  The sandwich A^-1 B A^-1 is the sum of the outer products of these rows, where A is the observed information of the step-three likelihood and B the cross-product of the unit scores. Rows for the means only. @param fit From `.multilpa_step_ml_fit()`. @param values The outcome. @param variance `"varying"` or `"equal"`. @return A units-by-classes matrix. @noRd

.multilpa_three_step_ml.name: .multilpa_three_step_ml
.multilpa_three_step_ml.documentation: The ML three-step table of a distal outcome  @param pieces,values The units' assignments and outcome values. @param level,variance,ci_level,contrast,adjust,vcov_type As in   [three_step()]. @return The table [three_step()] returns. @noRd

.multilpa_level_assignments.name: .multilpa_level_assignments
.multilpa_level_assignments.documentation: Posteriors and modal assignments at a chosen level @param object A fitted model of this package. @param level `"individuals"` or `"groups"`. @return A list with `posteriors`, `modal`, `units` and `group_index`. @noRd

.multilpa_check_three_step_fit.name: .multilpa_check_three_step_fit
.multilpa_check_three_step_fit.documentation: Require a first-stage fit whose classification error is not predictor-dependent @param object A fitted model of this package. @return `NULL`, invisibly, or `latents_unsupported_three_step`. @noRd

.multilpa_classification_errors.name: .multilpa_classification_errors
.multilpa_classification_errors.documentation: How often each true class is assigned to another  Documented on `?get_results`, which is where a caller reaches this table from, and consumed by [three_step()] and the BCH weights.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @param level `"individuals"`, `"groups"` or `"both"`. @return A base `data.frame`, one row per level and ordered pair of classes,   whose probabilities sum to one within each `true_class`. @noRd

.multilpa_error_frame.name: .multilpa_error_frame
.multilpa_error_frame.documentation: The classification error table for one level @param x A fitted model of this package. @param level A single level name. @return One row per ordered pair of classes at that level. @noRd

.multilpa_error_matrix.name: .multilpa_error_matrix
.multilpa_error_matrix.documentation: The classification error matrix, rows indexed by the true class @param pieces The list from `.multilpa_level_assignments()`. @return A square matrix whose rows sum to one. @noRd

.multilpa_bch_weights.name: .multilpa_bch_weights
.multilpa_bch_weights.documentation: The BCH inverse-classification-error weights  Documented on `?get_results`, which is where a caller reaches this table from.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @param level `"individuals"`, `"groups"` or `"both"`. @return A base `data.frame`, one row per level, unit and class. @noRd

.multilpa_weight_frame.name: .multilpa_weight_frame
.multilpa_weight_frame.documentation: The BCH weights for one level @param x A fitted model of this package. @param level A single level name. @return One row per unit and class at that level. @noRd

.multilpa_invert_errors.name: .multilpa_invert_errors
.multilpa_invert_errors.documentation: Invert a classification error matrix, refusing a singular one @param errors The matrix from `.multilpa_error_matrix()`. @return Its inverse. @noRd

three_step.name: three_step
three_step.documentation: Estimate a distal outcome's mean in each latent class  Estimates the mean of an outcome in each latent class of a fitted model, or the difference between every pair of classes, by the three-step approach, and returns a `data.frame`. The measurement model is fitted first, units are assigned to classes, and the outcome is then related to the assignments with a correction for classification error, so the outcome does not influence the classes. `"bch"` weights give approximately unbiased class means; `"ml"` estimates them by maximum likelihood with the classification errors held fixed; regressing on the modal class attenuates the differences (Vermunt 2010; Bakk, Tekle and Vermunt 2013; Bakk and Vermunt 2016).  @param x A covariate-free fitted [multilpa()] or [lta()] model, or a   trajectory model that classifies persons ([mixture_regression()] with   `class_level = "group"`, with or without `random` effects) fitted without   `membership` covariates. Fits with membership covariates and multilevel   growth mixtures (`cluster`) are refused with   `latents_unsupported_three_step`: the correction uses a fixed,   unconditional classification-error matrix and independent units. @param data The data frame carrying the outcome, in the fit's row order.   Columns shared with the fit are checked row by row; a frame with too   little identifying information raises a warning that alignment cannot be   verified. For a trajectory model it must be the data frame the model was   fitted to. @param outcome Name of a numeric outcome column, without missing or   infinite values, that is not a measurement indicator of `x`. For   `level = "groups"` it must be constant within each group, and for a   trajectory model within each person. @param level `"individuals"` (default) relates the outcome to profiles,   `"groups"` to group classes. For a trajectory model the outcome is   related to its person classes, reported with `level = "persons"`;   `"groups"` is refused there with `latents_bad_argument`. @param method `"bch"` (default) applies the Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars weights;   `"ml"` fits the maximum-likelihood step-three model (see *Details*);   `"proportional"` weights by the posterior probabilities (attenuated);   `"modal"` uses the uncorrected modal assignment, for comparison. @param ci_level Confidence level for the intervals (default 0.95). @param contrast `"none"` (default) reports one outcome mean per class;   `"pairs"` reports the difference between every pair of classes, with a   test against zero. @param adjust Multiplicity correction across the pairwise differences,   passed to [stats::p.adjust()]: `"BH"` (default), `"holm"`,   `"hochberg"`, `"hommel"`, `"bonferroni"`, `"BY"` or `"none"`. Ignored for   `contrast = "none"`. @param vcov_type `"cluster"` (default) sums the influence contributions   within the fit's groups and treats the groups as the independent units,   as required when the outcome is measured on observations nested in   groups. `"independent"` treats every observation as an independent unit,   which is appropriate only without nesting (for example a fit with a   single group). The choice is recorded in the result's `vcov_type`   attribute. @param variance For `method = "ml"`: `"varying"` (default) estimates a   variance of the outcome in each class, `"equal"` one variance shared by   the classes. Given with another method it raises `latents_bad_argument`. @return A base `data.frame`. For `contrast = "none"`, one row per class   with the columns `level`, `method`, `class`, `estimate`,   `standard_error`, `conf_low`, `conf_high` and `effective_n`; class means   are not tested. For `method = "ml"`, a `variance` column (the outcome's   estimated variance in the class) comes before `effective_n`, which is   then the expected number of units in the class under the step-three   model; the `variance` attribute records the choice. For `contrast = "pairs"`, one row per pair of classes   with the columns `level`, `method`, `class`, `reference_class`,   `estimate` (the mean of `class` minus the mean of `reference_class`),   `standard_error`, `statistic`, `p_value`, `p_adjusted`, `conf_low` and   `conf_high`, as in [r3step()]. A contrast with zero standard error has   `NA_real_` statistic and p-values.    The result's `vcov_type` attribute records the variance used; for   `contrast = "pairs"` the `adjust` attribute records the correction   applied to `p_adjusted`. @details The correction assumes the outcome is independent of the assigned   class given the true class. On an [lta()] fit, `level = "individuals"`   uses one row per occasion and relates the outcome to the profile at that   occasion, with the default group-clustered variance accounting for the   repeated occasions within a group. This is a marginal profile-outcome   analysis, not a model of outcome effects on transitions or of a   sequence-level outcome.    The cluster-robust variance is the sum of one outer product per   independent unit, scaled by the small-sample (CR1) factor `G / (G - 1)`   for `G` units (groups, or observations under `vcov_type =   "independent"`). These contributions sum to zero at the estimate, so the   variance has rank at most `G - 1`: it is zero with a single group and   singular with as many groups as classes. Both cases are refused with   `latents_too_few_groups`; `vcov_type = "independent"` gives the   unclustered variance.    With `method = "ml"` the assigned class is an indicator of the true   class whose error probabilities are those of step one, and the outcome is   normal within each true class. The log likelihood   `sum_i log sum_t pi_t D[t, W_i] phi(z_i; mu_t, sigma_t)` is maximised over   the class means and variances by EM followed by Newton steps, with the   class sizes `pi_t` fixed at the average posterior probabilities and the   classification errors `D` fixed, as in Latent GOLD's step-three model for   a dependent variable. That likelihood can have several maxima (a skewed   or heavy-tailed outcome lets a class absorb the tail), so EM runs from a   fixed set of starts, Latent GOLD's proportional start among them, and   keeps the highest. Twenty of the starts are random draws from a fixed   internal seed, so the result does not depend on the random seed and the   caller's random stream is left as it was. The standard errors are the   sandwich of that likelihood, clustered as for the other methods; a   class carried by a single unit has none (`NA`, with a   `latents_small_classes` warning). Maximum likelihood   relies on the normal distribution within classes: when the outcome is   skewed, or its variance differs between classes while `variance =   "equal"`, ML can shift the class means, and BCH is the more robust choice   (Bakk and Vermunt 2016).    The classification-error matrix is treated as known, so the intervals   are too narrow. Over 60 replications of a two-profile design with 8%   misclassification and a true class difference of 10, `"bch"` had a bias   of -0.13 (against -1.28 for `"modal"` and -1.82 for `"proportional"`)   and its nominal 95% intervals covered the true difference in 85% of   replications; the intervals of the other two methods covered it in none. @references Vermunt, J. K. (2010). Latent class modeling with covariates: two   improved three-step approaches. *Political Analysis*, 18, 450--469.   Bakk, Z., Tekle, F. B., & Vermunt, J. K. (2013). Estimating the   association between latent class membership and external variables   using bias-adjusted three-step approaches. *Sociological Methodology*,   43, 272--311.   Bakk, Z., & Vermunt, J. K. (2016). Robustness of stepwise latent class   modeling with continuous distal outcomes. *Structural Equation Modeling*,   23, 20--31. @examples set.seed(11) group <- rep(seq_len(40), each = 10) truth <- 1L + as.integer(runif(400) > 0.5) example_data <- data.frame(   g = group,   a = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.1, -1.1)),   b = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.1, -1.1)),   y = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 10, 0)) ) fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("a", "b"), "g", n_profiles = 2,                 n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 4, seed = 1) three_step(fit, example_data, "y") three_step(fit, example_data, "y", contrast = "pairs") @export

.multilpa_step_clusters.name: .multilpa_step_clusters
.multilpa_step_clusters.documentation: Sum influence contributions over the independent units, scaled by CR1  Shared by every three-step method: the contributions are summed within each group (`vcov_type = "cluster"`) or kept per observation, and scaled by `sqrt(G / (G - 1))`, which scales every variance and covariance formed from them, class means and differences alike. @param influence Units-by-classes influence contributions. @param pieces The list from `.multilpa_level_assignments()`. @param vcov_type `"cluster"` or `"independent"`. @return The scaled contributions, one row per independent unit. @noRd

.multilpa_step_pairs.name: .multilpa_step_pairs
.multilpa_step_pairs.documentation: Pairwise differences between class outcome means  @param estimates The per-class weighted means. @param clustered Group-summed influence contributions, one column per class. @param level,method The call's level and method, carried into the result. @param quantile The normal quantile for the interval. @param adjust A [stats::p.adjust()] method applied across the pairs. @param vcov_type The variance requested, carried into the result's attribute. @return One row per unordered pair of classes. @noRd

.multilpa_outcome_values.name: .multilpa_outcome_values
.multilpa_outcome_values.documentation: The outcome, at the level being analysed @return A numeric vector, one value per unit at that level. @noRd

.multilpa_step_weights.name: .multilpa_step_weights
.multilpa_step_weights.documentation: Weights for the requested three-step method @return A matrix with one row per unit and one column per class. @noRd

.multilpa_logit_prior.name: .multilpa_logit_prior
.multilpa_logit_prior.documentation: Class-membership priors from a multinomial logit @param gamma Coefficient matrix, predictors by non-reference classes. @param design The model matrix. @return A matrix of class probabilities, one row per unit. @noRd

r3step.name: r3step
r3step.documentation: Regress latent class membership on covariates by the three-step approach  Fits a multinomial logit of latent class membership on covariates after the measurement model (the R3STEP approach) and returns its coefficients as a `data.frame`. The assigned class is treated as an error-prone indicator of the true class, with the classification-error rates fixed at their step-one values; regressing the modal class directly attenuates the coefficients (Vermunt 2010; Asparouhov and Muthen 2014).  @param x A covariate-free fitted [multilpa()] or [lta()] model, or a   trajectory model from [mixture_regression()] that classifies persons   (with or without `random`), whose person classes are then predicted.   Fits with membership covariates and multilevel growth mixtures   (`cluster`) are refused with `latents_unsupported_three_step`: the   correction uses a fixed, unconditional classification-error matrix and   independent units. @param data The data frame carrying the covariates, in the fit's row order.   Columns shared with the fit are checked row by row; a frame with too   little identifying information raises a warning that alignment cannot be   verified. @param covariates Character vector of numeric columns, without missing or   infinite values, that are not measurement indicators of `x`. For   `level = "groups"` each must be constant within a group; for a   trajectory model each must be constant within a person and not part of   the trajectory regression (`latents_bad_covariate`). @param level `"individuals"` (default) predicts profile membership,   `"groups"` group-class membership. For a trajectory model the rows have   `level = "persons"` and outcomes `class_1`, `class_2`, ...; `"groups"` is   refused there with `latents_bad_argument`. @param ci_level Confidence level for the intervals (default 0.95). @param vcov_type `"robust"` (default) uses the sandwich clustered on the   fit's groups with the small-sample (CR1) factor `G / (G - 1)` for `G`   groups, as the default of [three_step()]. `"observed"` uses the observed   information; for the pooled regression it treats every observation as   independent, and with `by_group_class = TRUE` it is the model-based   variance of the two-level likelihood. `"robust"` requires more   independent groups than the regression has coefficients, because the   group score contributions sum to zero at the estimate; otherwise it is   refused with `latents_too_few_groups`, and `"observed"` remains   available. @param adjust Multiplicity correction across the covariate terms of every   non-reference class (not the intercepts), passed to   [stats::p.adjust()]: `"BH"` (default), `"holm"`, `"hochberg"`,   `"hommel"`, `"bonferroni"`, `"BY"` or `"none"`. @param by_group_class `FALSE` (default) fits one pooled multinomial logit   with a single intercept per profile. `TRUE` fits the two-level form of   the one-step model: each group class has its own profile intercepts, the   covariate slopes are shared across group classes, and a group's   observations share one latent group class whose proportions are   estimated jointly. Between-group differences not explained by the   covariates are then captured by the group classes; the pooled regression   attenuates the slopes and inflates their clustered standard errors in   that case. Only for `level = "individuals"` on a covariate-free   [multilpa()] fit; refused with `latents_bad_argument` otherwise. @param initial_covariates,transition_covariates For an [lta()] fit with one   group class: covariates of the profile at the first occasion (constant   within a person) and of every transition (read at the destination   occasion, so they may vary over occasions). Either one fits the   three-step latent Markov model described below instead of the   occasion-by-occasion profile regression; `covariates` must then be   empty, and `level` and `by_group_class` do not apply. Refused with   `latents_bad_argument` on a fit that is not a transition model. @return A base `data.frame` with one row per non-reference class and term,   and the columns `level`, `outcome`, `term`, `estimate`,   `standard_error`, `statistic`, `p_value`, `p_adjusted`, `conf_low` and   `conf_high`. `p_value` is uncorrected; `p_adjusted` applies `adjust`   (also recorded in the `adjust` attribute) and is `NA` on the intercept   rows. A coefficient with zero standard error has `NA_real_` statistic   and p-value. Coefficients are log odds against the last class, as in   `multilpa(profile_covariates = )`; the reference class is named in the   `reference_class` attribute and the variance used in the `vcov_type`   attribute. With `by_group_class = TRUE` there is one intercept row per   group class (`group_class_1`, `group_class_2`, ...), followed by the   shared slopes and, at `level = "groups"`, the group-class logits against   the last group class; the result also carries the attributes   `by_group_class` and `log_likelihood` (the maximised log likelihood).    With `initial_covariates` or `transition_covariates`, one row per   coefficient of the step-three chain: `block` (`"initial"` or   `"transition"`), `from` (the origin profile of a transition, `NA` for an   initial logit), `to`, `term`, `estimate`, `standard_error`, `statistic`,   `p_value`, `p_adjusted`, `conf_low` and `conf_high`, with the attributes   `log_likelihood`, `classification_errors` (the step-two error matrix,   rows the true profile), `vcov_type` and `adjust`. Initial logits are   against the last profile and transition logits against staying, as in   `lta(initial_covariates =, transition_covariates =)`; `p_adjusted` covers   the covariate terms. @details The classification-error matrix is held fixed rather than   estimated jointly, so the covariates do not change the classes.   On an [lta()] fit, `level = "individuals"` models the marginal profile at   each occasion; it does not regress initial-state or transition   probabilities on the covariates. `vcov_type = "robust"` clusters the   occasion scores by group; `"observed"` treats them as independent.   On a trajectory model the units are persons, each with one covariate   value, and `"robust"` is the sandwich over persons.    The three-step latent Markov model (`initial_covariates`,   `transition_covariates`) classifies each occasion from its own   indicators, using the transition fit's measurement model and its profile   shares pooled over occasions (the latent class model of the pooled   data), and assigns it to its modal profile. Step three is a hidden Markov   model for those assignments, with the classification errors fixed at   their step-two values and the initial and transition logits regressed on   the covariates (Di Mari, Oberski and Vermunt 2016). The transition fit's   own posteriors are not used for the assignments, because they draw on a   person's other occasions and their errors are therefore not independent   across occasions, as step three assumes. The step-one fit must have no   covariates and one group class (`latents_unsupported_three_step`   otherwise). Results agree with Latent GOLD 6.1's `step3 modal ml` latent   Markov model to its printed precision on three designs   (equivalence/latentgold-step3-markov in the source repository);   `"robust"` is the sandwich over persons and `"observed"` the information   Latent GOLD reports.    Over 60 replications of a two-profile design with a true log-odds slope   of 1.2 and intercept -0.3, the slope had a bias of -0.002 and the   intercept +0.006, against -0.163 on the slope for a logistic regression   on the modal class. The standard deviation of the slope across   replications was 0.127 (0.100 for the modal regression), and the nominal   95% intervals covered the true slope in 95% of replications. The   profiles in that design were well separated; because the error matrix is   treated as known, intervals are expected to be too narrow where   classification is poorer (see `get_results(x, "classification_errors")`). @references Vermunt, J. K. (2010). Latent class modeling with covariates: two   improved three-step approaches. *Political Analysis*, 18, 450--469.   Asparouhov, T., & Muthen, B. (2014). Auxiliary variables in mixture   modeling: three-step approaches using Mplus. *Structural Equation   Modeling*, 21, 329--341.   Di Mari, R., Oberski, D. L., & Vermunt, J. K. (2016). Bias-adjusted   three-step latent Markov modeling with covariates. *Structural Equation   Modeling*, 23, 649--660. @seealso [three_step()] for a distal outcome, and   `multilpa(profile_covariates = )` for the   one-step alternative that estimates everything jointly. @examples set.seed(21) g <- rep(seq_len(50), each = 12) x <- rnorm(600) truth <- 1L + as.integer(runif(600) < plogis(-0.3 + 1.2 * x)) example_data <- data.frame(   g = g, x = x,   a = rnorm(600, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.2, -1.2)),   b = rnorm(600, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.2, -1.2)) ) fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("a", "b"), "g", n_profiles = 2,                 n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 4, seed = 1) r3step(fit, example_data, "x")  # Covariates of the moves between profiles, three steps on from lta(). moves <- lta(course_engagement,              vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),              id = "student", n_profiles = 2, time = "sequence", n_starts = 2, seed = 1) r3step(moves, course_engagement, transition_covariates = "sequence") @export

.r3step_require_classes.name: .r3step_require_classes
.r3step_require_classes.documentation: Refuse a membership regression on a single class @param pieces The level's assignments. @return `NULL`, invisibly, or `latents_inseparable_classes`. @noRd

.r3step_transitions.name: .r3step_transitions
.r3step_transitions.documentation: r3step() with covariates of the initial profile and of the transitions @return The table of `.lta_three_step()`. @noRd

.multilpa_r3step_design.name: .multilpa_r3step_design
.multilpa_r3step_design.documentation: The covariate design at the level being analysed @return A model matrix with an intercept. @noRd

.multilpa_r3step_check_rank.name: .multilpa_r3step_check_rank
.multilpa_r3step_check_rank.documentation: Refuse a rank-deficient R3STEP design @param design A model matrix with an intercept. @return `design`, or `latents_bad_covariate`. @noRd

.multilpa_r3step_frame.name: .multilpa_r3step_frame
.multilpa_r3step_frame.documentation: Assemble the R3STEP coefficient table @return One row per non-reference class and term. @noRd

.multilpa_r3step_by_group_class.name: .multilpa_r3step_by_group_class
.multilpa_r3step_by_group_class.documentation: R3STEP with an intercept for every group class  The membership regression of [r3step()] for profiles, with the two-level structure the one-step model has: each group class has its own profile intercepts, the covariate slopes are shared across group classes, and a group's observations share one latent group class. With the step-one error matrix `E` held fixed, a group's likelihood is `sum_h eta_h prod_i sum_k pi_hk(z_i) E[k, a_i]`, where `a_i` is the assigned profile. Its scores are posterior-weighted residuals, summed within group, so the observed information and the group-clustered sandwich both come from the same per-group rows.  @param x The step-one fit. @param z The covariate matrix, one row per observation, no intercept. @param pieces The result of `.multilpa_level_assignments()` for individuals. @param errors The step-one classification-error matrix. @param ci_level,vcov_type,adjust As for [r3step()]. @return The tidy table [r3step()] returns, with group-class intercept rows   and the group-class logits. @noRd

.multilpa_r3step_group_model.name: .multilpa_r3step_group_model
.multilpa_r3step_group_model.documentation: The likelihood of R3STEP with group-class intercepts  @param x The step-one fit. @param z The covariate matrix, one row per observation, no intercept. @param pieces The result of `.multilpa_level_assignments()` for individuals. @param errors The step-one classification-error matrix. @return A list with `objective` (negative log likelihood), `gradient`,   `group_scores` (one row per group), `start`, and `transform`, the matrix   that returns the search coordinates to the covariates' own units and   origin. @noRd

.multilpa_r3step_group_frame.name: .multilpa_r3step_group_frame
.multilpa_r3step_group_frame.documentation: Assemble the table of R3STEP with group-class intercepts @return One row per coefficient: profile intercepts for every group class,   the shared slopes, then the group-class logits. @noRd

.multilpa_measured_items.name: .multilpa_measured_items
.multilpa_measured_items.documentation: Every item that entered a fit's measurement model  The fit's indicators and, for a fit with `local_dependence`, the items each joint indicator was made from: `"a:b"` stands in `vars`, and `"a"` and `"b"` helped define the classes just as much. @param x A fitted model. @return A character vector of column names. @noRd

get_tna.name: get_tna
get_tna.documentation: Build one transition network for the whole sample  Builds a single [tna::tna()] model from a fitted transition model, aggregated over all latent group classes, and returns it.  The network's transition probabilities are the expected transition counts summed across group classes and normalised by row, so each class contributes in proportion to its share of the expected transitions, not its class probability. If a profile has no expected outgoing transitions in any class, its row is the class rows averaged by class probability, and a warning states that the row is unestimated; absent transitions are not treated as self-transitions.  @param x A fitted model from [lta()]. @param ... Passed to [tna::tna()]. @return An object of class `tna`, as returned by [tna::tna()], to which the   functions of the tna package apply, including `centralities()`,   `communities()`, `cliques()` and `plot()`. @seealso [get_group_tna()] for one network per latent class. @examples if (requireNamespace("tna", quietly = TRUE)) {   activity <- c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read")   moves <- lta(course_engagement, vars = activity, id = "student",                            time = "sequence", n_profiles = 2,                            n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)   get_tna(moves) } @export

get_group_tna.name: get_group_tna
get_group_tna.documentation: Build one transition network per latent group class  Builds one [tna::tna()] model per latent group class of a fitted transition model and returns them as a `group_tna` object, the input of tna's grouped functions. A class row with no expected outgoing transitions keeps the fit's unestimated transition probabilities and raises the warning `latents_empty_transition_row`.  @param x A fitted model from [lta()], or a [multilpa()] / [multilca()] fit   made with `time =`, whose modal profile sequences are then used. @param label Name given to the classes in tna's output (default   `"Group class"`). @param ... Passed to [tna::tna()] for each class. @return An object of class `group_tna`, a list of `tna` models, one per   latent group class. `centralities()` returns one table with a `group`   column, `compare()` contrasts two classes, and `plot()` draws all   networks. @seealso [get_tna()] for one network over the whole sample. @examples if (requireNamespace("tna", quietly = TRUE)) {   activity <- c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read")   moves <- lta(course_engagement, vars = activity, id = "student",                            time = "sequence", n_profiles = 2,                            n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)   get_group_tna(moves) } @export

get_tna.multilpa_lta.name: get_tna.multilpa_lta
get_tna.multilpa_lta.documentation: @rdname get_tna @details A general [lta()] fit (occasion-varying or covariate-dependent   transitions, second order, movers and stayers, or ordinal, count or   weighted data) has no single transition matrix and is refused with   `latents_unsupported_tna`; its transitions are returned by   `get_results(x, "transitions")`. @export

.lta_refuse_tna.name: .lta_refuse_tna
.lta_refuse_tna.documentation: Refuse a transition network for a general transition fit @param verb The verb, for the message. @return Never returns; raises `latents_unsupported_tna`. @noRd

.multilpa_warn_tna_empty_rows.name: .multilpa_warn_tna_empty_rows
.multilpa_warn_tna_empty_rows.documentation: Warn when a network contains fitted transition rows without move data @return `NULL`, invisibly. @noRd

.multilpa_require_tna.name: .multilpa_require_tna
.multilpa_require_tna.documentation: Is the tna package available? @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises `latents_missing_package` when it is not. @noRd

.multilpa_state_labels.name: .multilpa_state_labels
.multilpa_state_labels.documentation: State labels for a transition network @param x A fitted model from [lta()]. @return A character vector, one per profile. @noRd

.multilpa_aggregate_transitions.name: .multilpa_aggregate_transitions
.multilpa_aggregate_transitions.documentation: The transition model marginal over latent group classes  @param x A fitted model from [lta()]. @return A list with `probabilities`, a square matrix; `initial`, the state   distribution; and `estimated`, marking rows with positive expected counts. @noRd

.multilpa_as_group_tna.name: .multilpa_as_group_tna
.multilpa_as_group_tna.documentation: Collect per-class models into tna's grouped object  tna builds a `group_tna` from sequence data, so there is no public constructor for one made from estimated matrices. The object is a named list of `tna` models carrying the attributes tna's grouped verbs read; `groups` and `cols` describe the sequence data a model built from matrices does not have, and are empty rather than invented.  @param models A named list of `tna` models, one per class. @param label What the classes are called. @return An object of class `group_tna`. @noRd

get_tna.multilpa.name: get_tna.multilpa
get_tna.multilpa.documentation: @rdname get_tna @details A [multilpa()] or [multilca()] fit made with `time =` has no   estimated transition matrix: the network is built by [tna::tna()] from   each group's sequence of modal profiles in time order.   `get_group_tna()` splits those sequences by each group's modal group   class. A fit made without `time` is refused. @export

.multilpa_modal_sequences.name: .multilpa_modal_sequences
.multilpa_modal_sequences.documentation: Each group's modal profiles in time order, one row per group  @param x A fitted model made with `time =`. @return A list with `states`, a data frame with one row per group and one   column per position (`T1`, `T2`, ...), holding `profile_k` labels and `NA`   after a group's last observation; and `group_class`, each group's modal   group class, in the same row order. @noRd

.trajectory_view.name: .trajectory_view
.trajectory_view.documentation: The pieces of a trajectory fit the tables and plots read  @param x A `latents_growth_mixture` fit, or a `latents_mixture_regression`   fit that classifies persons. @return A list: `growth` (whether there are random effects), `spec`,   `posterior` (persons by classes, rows summing to one), `modal`,   `classes`, `family`, `inverse_link`, `response_mean` (a function of   linear predictors and their classes giving the outcome's mean: the   inverse link, or for the ordinal family the expected category score   under that class's thresholds), `weights` (per person, or `NULL`). @noRd

.trajectory_inference.name: .trajectory_inference
.trajectory_inference.documentation: The estimates and their covariance, for either kind of trajectory fit @noRd

.trajectory_observed.name: .trajectory_observed
.trajectory_observed.documentation: The outcome on the response scale (a proportion for binomial counts) @noRd

.trajectory_band.name: .trajectory_band
.trajectory_band.documentation: Each class's mean trajectory at given rows, with a Wald band  The class's linear predictor is linear in its coefficients, so its standard error is exact given their covariance; the band is formed on the link scale and carried to the response scale. An ordinal class's mean (the expected category score) also depends on its thresholds, so its band is the delta method's on the score scale and `std_error` is on that scale.  @param x A trajectory fit. @param rows A data frame of predictor values. @param inference From `.trajectory_inference()`. @param level Confidence level. @return A data frame: `class`, `estimate`, `std_error` (response scale),   `conf_low`, `conf_high`, one row per class and row of `rows`. @noRd

.trajectory_is_fit.name: .trajectory_is_fit
.trajectory_is_fit.documentation: Whether a fit is a trajectory model (persons classified) @noRd

.trajectory_check_three_step.name: .trajectory_check_three_step
.trajectory_check_three_step.documentation: Check a trajectory fit can take a three-step correction  A multilevel growth mixture is refused (its persons are dependent within clusters), as is a fit with membership covariates (the correction has no classification-error adjustment conditional on them), and `data` must be the data frame the model was fitted to.  @param x A trajectory fit. @param data The data frame passed to the three-step verb. @return The fit's `.trajectory_view()`. @noRd

.trajectory_check_data.name: .trajectory_check_data
.trajectory_check_data.documentation: Require the data frame a trajectory model was fitted to @param x A trajectory fit. @param data A data frame. @return `NULL`, invisibly, or `latents_bad_inference_data`. @noRd

.trajectory_pieces.name: .trajectory_pieces
.trajectory_pieces.documentation: The person-level assignments of a trajectory fit, as three-step reads them @return A list as `.multilpa_level_assignments()` builds. @noRd

.trajectory_uses.name: .trajectory_uses
.trajectory_uses.documentation: Whether a variable is part of a trajectory model's own regression @noRd

.trajectory_three_step_inputs.name: .trajectory_three_step_inputs
.trajectory_three_step_inputs.documentation: Three-step inputs of a trajectory model: person posteriors and one distal outcome value per person  The outcome must be constant within persons (it is measured once, or is a person-level quantity) and must not be the trajectory outcome; the fit and `data` are checked by `.trajectory_check_three_step()`.  @return A list with `pieces` (as `.multilpa_level_assignments()` builds)   and `values`. @noRd

.trajectory_r3step_inputs.name: .trajectory_r3step_inputs
.trajectory_r3step_inputs.documentation: R3STEP inputs of a trajectory model: person posteriors and covariates  Each covariate must be constant within persons, because it predicts a person's class, and must not be part of the trajectory model.  @return A list with `pieces` and `design` (persons by intercept and   covariates). @noRd

.multilpa_transition_view.name: .multilpa_transition_view
.multilpa_transition_view.documentation: A `multilpa`-shaped view of a transition fit's measurement model  The coefficient encoders, the delta-method Jacobian and the full-covariance group scores of the cross-sectional model read only measurement fields, the group-class shares and the grouping. This view carries exactly those, so the transition path uses the same code rather than a copy of it. Its `profile_probabilities` are the fitted initial distribution, present only because the cross-sectional encoder lays out a block of that shape; the transition path discards that block.  @param x A `multilpa_transitions` fit. @param centers Column centres to take off the means, or `NULL`. @return A list of class `multilpa`. @noRd

.multilpa_transition_shared_blocks.name: .multilpa_transition_shared_blocks
.multilpa_transition_shared_blocks.documentation: Which cross-sectional coordinates the transition model shares  Everything but the profile block, which the transition model replaces with its initial and transition logits. @param view A view from `.multilpa_transition_view()`. @param scale `"natural"` or `"unconstrained"`. @return A list of integer positions: `measurement`, `profile`, `group`. @noRd

.multilpa_transition_encode.name: .multilpa_transition_encode
.multilpa_transition_encode.documentation: Encode a transition fit as one parameter vector  Measurement, then group-class shares, then each group class's initial distribution, then each group class's transition matrix row by row (from profile, then to profile). On the unconstrained scale every distribution is a baseline-category logit against its last profile.  @param x A `multilpa_transitions` fit. @param scale `"natural"` or `"unconstrained"`. @param centers Column centres taken off the means, or `NULL`. @return A named numeric vector; names in the internal `kind[index,...]`   grammar. @noRd

.multilpa_transition_decode.name: .multilpa_transition_decode
.multilpa_transition_decode.documentation: Decode a transition parameter vector into the parameters the E-step reads @param theta Unconstrained vector in `.multilpa_transition_encode()` order. @param view The measurement view the vector was encoded from. @param n_measurement,n_group Widths of the measurement and group blocks. @return A parameter list for `.multilpa_transition_expectation()`. @noRd

.multilpa_transition_group_scores.name: .multilpa_transition_group_scores
.multilpa_transition_group_scores.documentation: Per-group scores of a transition model's observed-data log likelihood  @param theta Unconstrained vector in `.multilpa_transition_encode()` order. @param x Centred continuous indicator matrix, `NA` where unobserved. @param layout The sequence layout. @param view The measurement view. @param widths Named widths `measurement` and `group`. @param codes Categorical codes, or `NULL`. @return A groups-by-parameters matrix whose column sums are the gradient of   the log likelihood. @noRd

.multilpa_transition_group_counts.name: .multilpa_transition_group_counts
.multilpa_transition_group_counts.documentation: Expected first-occasion and move counts, one row per group  The per-group terms that `.multilpa_sequence_moments()` sums over groups, kept apart because the sandwich estimators need each group's own score.  @param x Centred continuous indicator matrix. @param layout The sequence layout. @param parameters Decoded parameters. @param codes Categorical codes, or `NULL`. @param group_posteriors Groups-by-group-classes posteriors. @return A list with `initial` (per group class, groups-by-profiles) and   `transition` (per group class, groups-by-profile-pairs, column-major as   the transition matrix). @noRd

.multilpa_transition_jacobian.name: .multilpa_transition_jacobian
.multilpa_transition_jacobian.documentation: Delta-method Jacobian from a transition fit's logits to its probabilities @param x A `multilpa_transitions` fit. @param view Its measurement view. @return A natural-by-unconstrained matrix. @noRd

.multilpa_transition_labels.name: .multilpa_transition_labels
.multilpa_transition_labels.documentation: Tidy labels for a transition fit's coefficients @param names Internal names from `.multilpa_transition_encode()`. @param view The measurement view. @return A data frame with `level`, `outcome`, `term` and `parameter`. @noRd

parameter_inference.multilpa_transitions.name: parameter_inference.multilpa_transitions
parameter_inference.multilpa_transitions.documentation: Standard errors and intervals for a latent transition model  Returns standard errors, tests and intervals for every parameter of an [lta()] fit: the measurement model, the group-class shares, each group class's initial profile distribution and its transition matrix. The scores follow the Fisher identity (each is an expected count from the forward-backward pass minus the count implied by the fitted probabilities), and the observed information is the numerical Jacobian of that analytic score.  @param x A fitted `multilpa_transitions` model from [lta()]. @param data Optional data frame the model was fitted to. Not needed for   the Wald path, since the fit stores its indicators, codes, groups and   occasions; when given it must reproduce them. Required for   `method = "bootstrap"`. @param level Confidence level of the intervals. Default `0.95`. @param step Finite-difference step for the observed information. @param vcov_type `"observed"` (default; observed information), `"robust"`   (the sandwich clustered on groups, which are the sequences) or `"opg"`   (the outer product of the group scores). @param adjust Multiplicity correction for `p_adjusted`: `"none"` (default)   or one of the [stats::p.adjust()] methods. @param method `"wald"` (default) or `"bootstrap"`. The bootstrap resamples   persons with replacement, refits the same specification and matches each   replicate's profiles and group classes to the original's;   `standard_error` is the standard deviation of the replicates,   `conf_low` and `conf_high` their percentile interval, and `statistic`,   `p_value` and `p_adjusted` are `NA`. @param iter,n_starts,max_iter,tol,seed Number of bootstrap resamples, the   controls of each refit, and an optional seed (the caller's random state   is restored). @param boundary Accepted for consistency with the generic. Transition   inference holds no parameter at a bound: without an active bound   `"fix"` gives the same table as `"error"`, and a fit with an active bound   raises `latents_boundary_fit` under either. @param ... For `confint()`, further arguments to `parameter_inference()`,   such as `vcov_type`. `vcov()` takes none and warns   (`latents_unused_argument`) about any it is given. @return A base `data.frame` with one row per natural parameter and the   columns of [parameter_inference()]: `level`, `outcome`, `term`,   `parameter`, `estimate`, `standard_error`, `statistic`, `p_value`,   `p_adjusted`, `conf_low` and `conf_high`, named as [coef()] names them.   An initial probability (`parameter = "initial_probability"`,   `level = "profile"`) has `outcome` the profile and `term` the group   class; a transition probability (`"transition_probability"`) has   `outcome` the profile moved to and `term` `group_class_h:profile_j`, the   group class and the profile moved from. Probabilities and variances have   no Wald test. The Wald table has attributes `covariance` (natural   scale), `covariance_unconstrained`, `level`, `step`, `method` and   `vcov_type`. @section Conditions:   `latents_no_converge` for an unconverged fit; `latents_boundary_fit` when   a variance, a response, initial or transition probability, or a   group-class share is at its bound, or a transition row has no   information (a profile no group occupies before its last occasion);   `latents_singular_information` when the information cannot be inverted;   `latents_bad_inference_data` when a supplied `data` does not reproduce   the fit; `latents_too_few_groups` for robust or OPG errors with no more   groups than parameters; `latents_bad_argument` for `method = "bootstrap"`   without `data`; `latents_bootstrap_failed` when fewer than two resamples   give a usable fit, with a `latents_bootstrap_dropped` warning for resamples   that were dropped. @examples fit <- lta(subset(course_engagement, student <= 40),            c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read"), "student",            n_profiles = 2, time = "sequence", n_starts = 2, seed = 1) parameter_inference(fit) @rdname parameter_inference.multilpa_transitions @export

.multilpa_transition_covariance.name: .multilpa_transition_covariance
.multilpa_transition_covariance.documentation: Covariance of a transition fit's parameters @param x A `multilpa_transitions` fit. @param data Optional fitting data. @param step Finite-difference step. @param vcov_type `"observed"`, `"robust"` or `"opg"`. @return A list with `covariance` (natural), `covariance_unconstrained` and   the measurement `view`. @noRd

.multilpa_check_transition_regularity.documentation: Refuse Wald inference where it is not defined for a transition fit @param x A `multilpa_transitions` fit. @param vcov_type The requested covariance. @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises on the first broken condition. @noRd

confint.multilpa_transitions.documentation: @rdname parameter_inference.multilpa_transitions @param parm Parameters to report, as names or positions of the natural   coefficients; all by default. @export

.multilpa_sequence_layout.name: .multilpa_sequence_layout
.multilpa_sequence_layout.documentation: Lay observations out as one row per group and one column per occasion  Groups differ in length and may skip positions, so the recursion runs on a padded rectangle. Two logical masks distinguish the two kinds of absence: an occasion past a group's last one carries neither an emission nor a transition, while a position skipped inside a group's span carries a transition but no emission.  @param group_index Integer group indices in first-occurrence order. @param time_values Position of each observation within its group. @param n_groups Number of observed groups. @param occasions `"observed"` numbers each group's own occasions   consecutively; `"grid"` places them on the grid of every position seen in   the data, so that a skipped position still consumes a transition. @return A list with `slot` (groups by occasions, holding the row index or   `NA`), `within` (whether the occasion lies inside the group's span),   `span`, `n_occasions`, `occasions` and `n_observations`. @noRd

.multilpa_sequence_emission.name: .multilpa_sequence_emission
.multilpa_sequence_emission.documentation: Emission log densities laid out by occasion, with the shared offset removed  The recursion accumulates sums of log densities, so a common offset must be taken out before log transition probabilities are added to them; otherwise a very small density rounds the priors away, exactly as it would in the cross-sectional E-step. The offset cancels from every posterior and is added back once to the log likelihood.  @param validate Check inputs for direct calls; disabled inside validated fits. @param log_density Observation-by-profile matrix of measurement log densities. @param layout Sequence layout from `.multilpa_sequence_layout()`. @return A list with `log_density` (one groups-by-profiles matrix per   occasion, offset removed) and `offset` (one total per group). @noRd

.multilpa_forward_backward.name: .multilpa_forward_backward
.multilpa_forward_backward.documentation: Forward and backward recursions over every group at once  Groups share the occasion grid, so each step of the recursion is a single matrix update rather than one pass per group. A group whose sequence has ended keeps its state unchanged, which leaves its likelihood and posteriors identical to those of the shorter sequence it actually has.  @param emission Offset-removed emission list from `.multilpa_sequence_emission()`. @param layout Sequence layout from `.multilpa_sequence_layout()`. @param validate Check inputs for direct calls; disabled inside validated fits. @param initial Initial profile probabilities for one group class. @param transition Profile transition matrix for one group class, rows from. @return A list with `alpha`, `beta` (one groups-by-profiles matrix per   occasion) and `log_scaled`, the offset-removed sequence log likelihoods. @noRd

.multilpa_sequence_moments.name: .multilpa_sequence_moments
.multilpa_sequence_moments.documentation: Posterior occupancy and transition counts for one group class  @param validate Check inputs for direct calls; disabled inside validated fits. @param pass Forward and backward recursions from `.multilpa_forward_backward()`. @param emission Offset-removed emission list. @param layout Sequence layout. @param transition Profile transition matrix for this group class. @param weights Posterior probability that each group belongs to this class. @param n_observations Number of input rows. @return A list with `posterior` (observations by profiles, weighted by   `weights`), `initial` (expected first-occasion counts) and `transition`   (expected from-to counts). @noRd

.multilpa_transition_validate.name: .multilpa_transition_validate
.multilpa_transition_validate.documentation: Check fixed transition inputs once before iterating @param x,layout,parameters Inputs to the homogeneous transition E-step. @noRd

.multilpa_transition_prevalence.name: .multilpa_transition_prevalence
.multilpa_transition_prevalence.documentation: Profile prevalence implied by a transition expectation  The prevalence of each profile within a group class is a summary of the fitted model rather than a free parameter of it, so it is read off the expectation that is actually reported, exactly as the empty transition rows are. EM leaves the parameters one M-step behind that expectation, and with `max_iter = 0` there is no M-step at all, which previously left the field absent and the assembled fit unusable.  @param expectation Expected counts from `.multilpa_transition_expectation()`. @return A group-classes-by-profiles numeric matrix whose rows sum to one. @noRd

.multilpa_transition_expectation.name: .multilpa_transition_expectation
.multilpa_transition_expectation.documentation: Nested expectation step for a latent transition model @param x Observation-by-indicator matrix of continuous indicators. @param layout Sequence layout. @param parameters Model parameters, including `initial_probabilities` and   `transition_probabilities`. @param codes Optional integer matrix of categorical indicator codes. @param validate Check inputs for direct calls; disabled inside validated fits. @return Log likelihood, posteriors and expected sequence counts. @noRd

.multilpa_transition_maximization.name: .multilpa_transition_maximization
.multilpa_transition_maximization.documentation: Maximize the expected complete-data log likelihood of a transition model  The measurement parameters are those of the cross-sectional model and are maximized by the same function; only the initial and transition probabilities are new, and both are bounded multinomial shares.  @param x Observation-by-indicator matrix. @param expectation Expected counts from `.multilpa_transition_expectation()`. @param variance_model Either varying or equal across profiles. @param min_variance Lower bound on every indicator variance. @param covariance_model Diagonal or full residual covariance. @param codes Optional integer matrix of categorical indicator codes. @param n_categories Integer vector of category counts per categorical indicator. @param min_probability Lower bound on every fitted probability. @return Updated model parameters. @noRd

.multilpa_transition_em.name: .multilpa_transition_em
.multilpa_transition_em.documentation: Run EM for a latent transition model @param x Observation-by-indicator matrix. @param layout Sequence layout. @param parameters Initial parameters. @param variance_model Variance constraint. @param min_variance Variance lower bound. @param max_iter Maximum number of updates. @param tol Relative log-likelihood tolerance. @param covariance_model Diagonal or full residual covariance. @param codes Optional categorical codes. @param n_categories Category counts per categorical indicator. @param min_probability Lower bound on every fitted probability. @param acceleration SQUAREM or plain EM. @param pause,resume As for `.latents_em()`. @return Parameters, the final expectation, convergence and history; with   `pause` or `resume`, also the `checkpoint`. @noRd

.multilpa_transition_initialize.name: .multilpa_transition_initialize
.multilpa_transition_initialize.documentation: Initialize a latent transition model  The measurement model and the group-class split reuse the cross-sectional initializer. Transition matrices start persistent, because a mixture whose states are freely exchangeable at every occasion carries no sequence information to separate them; the persistence is randomized across starts.  @param x Observation-by-indicator matrix. @param group_index Integer group indices. @param n_profiles Number of profiles. @param n_types Number of group classes. @param variance_model Variance constraint. @param min_variance Variance lower bound. @param start_index Restart number. @param covariance_model Diagonal or full residual covariance. @param codes Optional categorical codes. @param n_categories Category counts per categorical indicator. @param min_probability Lower bound on every fitted probability. @param kind The kind of start, as for `.multilpa_initialize()`. @param row_weights Optional sampling weights in observation order, as for   `.multilpa_initialize()`. @return Strictly positive initial parameters for EM. @noRd

.lta_check_time_order.name: .lta_check_time_order
.lta_check_time_order.documentation: Refuse numbers written as text whose alphabetical order is not numeric  Occasions are ordered by `sort()`, which orders character strings alphabetically. Positions written as `"1"`, ..., `"10"` would put `"10"` second and fit transitions between the wrong occasions without a word. Strings whose alphabetical order is already right (zero-padded numbers, ISO dates, labels) are accepted.  @param values The time values. @param time The time column name, for the message. @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises `latents_bad_time` (also `latents_bad_data`). @noRd

.multilpa_count_transition_parameters.name: .multilpa_count_transition_parameters
.multilpa_count_transition_parameters.documentation: Count the free parameters of a latent transition model @param n_profiles Number of profiles. @param n_group_classes Number of group classes. @param n_continuous Number of continuous indicators. @param n_categories Category counts per categorical indicator, or `NULL`. @param variance_model Variance constraint. @param covariance_model Diagonal or full residual covariance. @return Number of free parameters. @noRd

lta.name: lta
lta.documentation: Fit a latent transition model  Fits latent profiles to repeated observations of the same group, estimates the probabilities of moving between profiles from one occasion to the next, and returns a `multilpa_transitions` (or `multilpa_lta`) object. The measurement model is that of [multilpa()] (Gaussian, categorical or mixed indicators) and is invariant across occasions by default, so a profile has the same meaning at every occasion. With more than one group class, each class has its own initial distribution and its own transition matrix, so the group classes are a mixture over transition patterns. [multilpa()] is the cross-sectional counterpart.  @inheritParams multilpa @param search How the starts are found: `"kmeans"` (the default) or   `"emEM"`, as described for [multilpa()]. Unlike [multilpa()], `lta()`   does not choose its default by the covariance structure. @param cores Number of processor cores for the random starts (default 1).   The starting values are drawn in order in the current process and only   the EM runs are distributed, so with `seed` given the result is identical   to `cores = 1`. Under `search = "emEM"` both screening and the final runs   are distributed. Workers are forked processes on macOS and Linux, and a   socket cluster on Windows and on macOS with Apple's Accelerate BLAS, as   in [enumerate_classes()]. Lost worker results are retried once with half   as many workers (rounded up), with one `latents_worker_lost` warning   reporting losses and recovery and suggesting fewer cores. A start still   lost is recorded as failed; the fit uses the remaining starts. If all   starts fail, the usual `latents_all_starts_failed` error is raised.   Socket workers use bounded chunks; completed tasks within a failed chunk   may also be retried. To fit many models, give `cores` to   [enumerate_classes()], which runs starts across candidates in one pool. @param id Name of the observed group identifier column. Character, factor   and numeric identifiers are supported; missing identifiers are not.   Required; `id = NULL` is not accepted. @param n_profiles Integer number of individual profiles, at least two   (`latents_bad_transition` otherwise). @param time Name of the column giving each observation's occasion within   its group. Required. Values must be complete and unique within each   group. They are ordered as [sort()] orders them: numbers numerically, a   factor by its levels, and character strings alphabetically. Numbers   stored as text whose alphabetical order is not their numeric order   (`"2"`, `"10"`) raise `latents_bad_time` (also `latents_bad_data`);   zero-padded numbers and ISO dates are accepted. @param n_group_classes Positive integer number of latent group classes   (default 1). One gives an ordinary latent transition model; more than one   fits a mixture of transition models over groups. @param select_start Which start the fit reports. `"likelihood"` (the   default) takes the highest log likelihood across starts, preferring a   converged start only among those within a relative `1e-10` of it.   `"converged"` takes the highest log likelihood among the converged starts   when at least one converged, and among all starts otherwise. The two   differ when an unconverged start exceeds a converged one by a negligible   amount, as happens when a membership logit drifts along a flat ridge of   the likelihood; only the converged start is a maximum on which standard   errors can be based. `summary()` and `get_results(fit, "starts")` show   every start. @param occasions How a group's occasions are placed on the transition grid.   `"observed"` (the default) numbers each group's own observations   consecutively, so a transition always links two adjacent observations.   `"grid"` places them on the grid of every position seen in the data, so a   group that skips a position still makes a transition across the gap and   contributes no measurement information at it. The two agree when every   group is observed at every position. Under either, a group's first   observation is its first occasion: occasion-specific transitions and   measurement count occasions from each group's own start, not from the   first position in the data. @param transitions `"homogeneous"` (the default) uses one transition matrix   for every occasion; `"occasion"` estimates a separate one for each move   (occasion 1 to 2, 2 to 3, ...). @param transition_covariates Names of columns whose values shift the   transition probabilities through a multinomial logit per origin profile:   the log odds of moving to each other profile rather than staying. A   column may change over occasions; the value at the destination occasion   is used. Factors are expanded to indicator columns. With `occasions =   "grid"`, a move into a position the group skipped has no row to read the   covariates from, and the fit raises `latents_bad_data`; use   `occasions = "observed"`, or add the skipped rows with their covariate   values (their indicators may be missing under `missing = "fiml"`). @param initial_covariates Names of columns that shift the initial profile   distribution (a multinomial logit, reference: the last profile), read at   each group's first occasion. @param measurement `"invariant"` (the default) keeps the profiles' means,   variances and response probabilities equal across occasions;   `"occasion"` estimates them separately at each occasion. @param tol Positive relative log-likelihood tolerance (default `1e-10`,   tighter than the `1e-8` of [multilpa()]). Convergence requires an   absolute change no greater than `tol * (1 + abs(previous log likelihood))`.   The group-class shares are re-estimated from posteriors one EM step   behind them; at `1e-8` the two differed by up to about `2e-4`, at `1e-10`   by about `2e-5`, for roughly 1.5 times the iterations. @param acceleration `"squarem"` (the default) accelerates EM with SQUAREM   (Varadhan & Roland, 2008), as [multilpa()] does: each cycle extrapolates   along the last two EM steps, including the initial and transition   probabilities, and ends with an ordinary EM step. An extrapolated point   that would lower the likelihood, or that leaves a probability   non-positive or a row not summing to one, is replaced by the plain EM   point, so the iteration stays monotone. Convergence is assessed over a   whole cycle, so it is never looser than plain EM's. Under the strict   default `tol` plain EM can creep along a flat likelihood for thousands of   steps; SQUAREM usually stops in far fewer, at the same or a slightly   higher maximum. `"none"` runs plain EM, which reproduces fits from   versions before this argument existed. `iterations` and `max_iter` count   EM steps under either setting. @param max_iter Nonnegative integer maximum number of EM updates per start   (default 5000, higher than the 1000 of [multilpa()] to match the tighter   `tol`). A fit that stops short warns with `latents_unconverged`.   `max_iter = 0` updates nothing and evaluates the starting values. @param order `1` (the default) or `2`. With `2`, the profile at each   occasion from the third on depends on the profiles at the two previous   occasions (a second-order Markov chain); the first move stays first   order. @param mover_stayer `FALSE` (the default), or `TRUE` to add a class of   stayers: groups that never change profile (identity transitions) and have   their own initial profile distribution (Goodman's mover-stayer model).   `n_group_classes` then counts the mover classes; the stayer class is   reported as `"stayers"`. @param weights `NULL`, or the name of a column of `data` holding one   sampling weight per `id` (constant over its occasions). As in   [multilpa()]: pseudo maximum likelihood with the weights scaled to sum to   the number of `id` units, sandwich standard errors by default, and   integer weights equal to repeating each sequence. A weighted fit uses the   general transition engine and returns a `multilpa_lta`, whose   model-implied `"transitions"` and `"initial"` tables average the groups   with their weights. @param ordinal,count,count_model,count_dispersion Ordinal and count   indicators, as in [multilpa()]; with `measurement = "occasion"` their   parameters are estimated per occasion. Read them with   `get_results(fit, "ordinal")` and `get_results(fit, "count_means")`. A   fit with them uses the general transition engine. @param model A covariance structure as `multilpa()` takes it (`"EEI"`,   `"VVI"`, `"VEI"`, ... ; mclust's codes). Standard errors are given for   every structure with the extensions (covariate, occasion-varying or   second-order transitions, occasion-specific measurement), and for EEI,   VVI, EEE and VVV in the homogeneous model, which refuses the other ten   with `latents_unsupported_inference`. @return A `multilpa_transitions` object containing `means`, `variances`,   optional `covariances` and `response_probabilities`,   `initial_probabilities` (group classes by profiles),   `transition_probabilities` (profiles by profiles by group classes, rows   indexing the profile moved from), `group_probabilities`, posterior   matrices, classifications, log likelihood, information criteria, restart   diagnostics and convergence history. [get_results()] returns the tidy   transition table and the other tables, [parameter_inference()] Wald or   bootstrap standard errors, and [bootstrap_lrt()] compares nested fits.   Global optimality is not guaranteed.    With `transitions = "occasion"`, `transition_covariates`,   `initial_covariates`, `measurement = "occasion"`, `order = 2`,   `mover_stayer = TRUE`, `weights`, `ordinal` or `count`, the result is a   `multilpa_lta` object, read with [get_results()]: transition and initial   logit coefficients with Wald standard errors (observed, robust or OPG,   from analytic scores), model-implied transition probabilities per   occasion, and profiles per occasion. Missing indicators   (`missing = "fiml"`) and covariance structures are supported; diagonal   fits are finished by a quasi-Newton search on the exact likelihood,   others by EM. Agreement with Mplus (User's Guide examples 8.13, 8.14;   occasion-specific thresholds), depmixS4 and LMest is recorded in   `equivalence/lta-extensions/` of the source repository. @details By default transitions are first order and homogeneous over   occasions: the probability of moving from one profile to another does not   depend on the occasion or on earlier profiles. Measurement parameters are   shared across occasions and across group classes. A profile that no group   occupies before its final occasion leaves its transition row without   information; the row is then uniform by construction, not estimated. Such   a row raises a warning when the model is fitted, is flagged by the   `estimated` column of the transition table and is listed by   `get_results(fit, "transitions", estimated = FALSE)`. Profile labels are   arbitrary and are not comparable across fits without alignment.    `max_iter = 0` updates nothing: the starting values are evaluated and   returned with the expectation they imply, and the fit reports   `converged = FALSE` after zero iterations. Every reported quantity,   including `expected_count` and the implied profile prevalence, is then   read off that single expectation. @references Collins, L. M., & Lanza, S. T. (2010). Latent class and latent   transition analysis. Wiley.    Varadhan, R., & Roland, C. (2008). Simple and globally convergent methods   for accelerating the convergence of any EM algorithm. Scandinavian   Journal of Statistics, 35, 335--353.    Vermunt, J. K. (2003). Multilevel latent class models. Sociological   Methodology, 33, 213--239. doi:10.1111/j.0081-1750.2003.t01-1-00131.x. @seealso [get_results()] for the fitted transition probabilities and for the   assignments in order, and [multilpa()] for the   cross-sectional model this one shares its measurement parameters with. @examples # Students take their courses in their own order, which `sequence` records, # so the same enrolments that fit a cross-sectional model fit a transition # one. Engagement mostly persists from one course to the next. fit <- lta(   course_engagement,   vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),   id = "student", n_profiles = 2, time = "sequence", n_starts = 2, seed = 1 ) get_results(fit, what = "transitions") summary(fit) @export
