.multilpa_initial_frame.documentation: Initial profile probabilities as a tidy table @param x A fitted `multilpa_transitions` model. @return One row per group class and profile. @noRd

.latents_tree_specs.name: .latents_tree_specs
.latents_tree_specs.documentation: The trees a call asks for  @param x A `multilpa_enumeration`. @param level `"individuals"` or `"groups"`. @param n_profiles,n_group_classes,model Optional filters: the one that   indexes trees selects trees, the other selects rows. @param candidates `NULL`, or two or more candidate names drawn as the rows   of one tree, in that order. @return A list of trees, each a list of `name`, `label`, `row_facet`,   `col_facet` and `rows` (a data frame: `at`, the grid row; `candidate`;   `key`, the count matched across trees; `label`, the row's axis label). @noRd

.latents_tree_candidates.name: .latents_tree_candidates
.latents_tree_candidates.documentation: The candidates `from` and `to` name, or the caller's `candidates`  `from` and `to` each name one candidate as a grid names it everywhere: by its name, by its class counts `c(n_profiles, n_group_classes)`, or by one count for one group class. @param x The grid. @param candidates The caller's `candidates`. @param from,to The caller's `from` and `to`. @return A character vector of candidate names, or `NULL`. @noRd

.latents_check_tree_arguments.name: .latents_check_tree_arguments
.latents_check_tree_arguments.documentation: Check the arguments of a tree before anything is drawn  @param level The caller's `level`. @param n_profiles,n_group_classes,model The caller's filters. @param combine The caller's `combine`. @return The matched `level`. @noRd

.latents_tree_word.name: .latents_tree_word
.latents_tree_word.documentation: What a grid's lower-level classes are called, for titles and labels @param x An enumeration grid. @return `"profiles"` or `"classes"`. @noRd

.latents_tree_table_of.name: .latents_tree_table_of
.latents_tree_table_of.documentation: The table a tree reads: every grid in one layout  The layout of `.latents_grid_table()`, with a column of profile counts on a family grid (whose candidates have none) so every tree reads the same columns. @param x An enumeration grid. @return A data frame with `candidate`, `n_profiles`, `n_group_classes`,   `model` and `converged`, one row per candidate. @noRd

.latents_tree_fit.name: .latents_tree_fit
.latents_tree_fit.documentation: The fitted candidate in one row of a grid a tree reads @param x An enumeration grid. @param at A row of its table. @return The fit; a candidate that was not fitted raises   `latents_failed_candidate`. @noRd

.latents_singular.name: .latents_singular
.latents_singular.documentation: The singular of a class word @param word `"profiles"`, `"classes"` or `"group classes"`. @return The singular. @noRd

.latents_check_tree_filter.name: .latents_check_tree_filter
.latents_check_tree_filter.documentation: Refuse a tree filter that names nothing in the grid @param value The caller's filter, or `NULL`. @param available The values present among converged candidates. @param argument The argument's name. @return `NULL`, invisibly. @noRd

.latents_tree_posteriors.name: .latents_tree_posteriors
.latents_tree_posteriors.documentation: The posteriors a tree divides, with the weight of each unit @param fit A fitted candidate. @param level `"individuals"` or `"groups"`. @return A list of `posteriors` (units x classes) and `weights`. @noRd

.latents_permutations.name: .latents_permutations
.latents_permutations.documentation: Every ordering of `seq_len(n)`, one per row @param n A small positive integer. @return An integer matrix with `factorial(n)` rows. @noRd

.latents_match_classes.name: .latents_match_classes
.latents_match_classes.documentation: Match the classes of one solution to those of another  The one-to-one assignment with the largest total shared posterior mass: exact for square matrices of up to eight classes, and greedy otherwise (the largest overlap first, ties broken by class number). A class whose assigned reference class shares no mass with it is left unmatched. @param overlap A classes-by-reference-classes matrix of shared mass. @return For each class (row), the matched reference class, or `0`. @noRd

.latents_greedy_match.name: .latents_greedy_match
.latents_greedy_match.documentation: Greedy one-to-one matching, the largest overlap first @param overlap A classes-by-reference-classes matrix of shared mass. @return For each class (row), the matched reference class, or `0`. @noRd

.latents_distinct_colours.name: .latents_distinct_colours
.latents_distinct_colours.documentation: Make the colours of one row distinct  The first class with a colour keeps it; a later class with the same colour takes the first palette colour the row does not use yet. With more classes than palette colours, the extra classes repeat palette colours. @param colours The row's colours, indexed by class. @return The colours, distinct while the palette lasts. @noRd

.latents_tree_layout.name: .latents_tree_layout
.latents_tree_layout.documentation: Shares, flows, positions and lineage colours of one tree  Each row's classes are ordered by the flow-weighted centre of their parents, so bands cross only where units really are reshuffled. A class that is its dominant parent's main continuation keeps the parent's colour; any other class takes a new one (Zappia and Oshlack, 2018). @param x The grid. @param tree One element of `.latents_tree_specs()`. @param level `"individuals"` or `"groups"`. @return The tree with `posteriors` and `weights` (one per row), `shares`,   `flows` (between consecutive rows), `segments` (per row: `class`,   `xmin`, `xmax`, `share`) and `colours` (per row, indexed by class). @noRd

.latents_tree_anchor.name: .latents_tree_anchor
.latents_tree_anchor.documentation: Give every tree the colours of the matching classes of the first tree  A row of a later tree whose key (number of classes, or of group classes) also occurs in the first tree has its classes matched to that row's classes by shared posterior mass, and takes their colours. Other rows keep their own lineage colours. @param layouts Trees from `.latents_tree_layout()`. @return The trees, recoloured. @noRd

.latents_tree_results.name: .latents_tree_results
.latents_tree_results.documentation: `get_results(x, "tree", ...)` on a grid whose method has its own tables @param x A transition, family or regression grid. @param extra The caller's `...`: the arguments of the tree. @return The table of `.latents_tree_table()`. @noRd

.latents_tree_table.name: .latents_tree_table
.latents_tree_table.documentation: The flows of every tree, one row per pair of classes in consecutive rows  @inheritParams .latents_tree_specs @return A data frame: `tree`, `level`, `from_candidate`, `from_class`,   `from_share`, `to_candidate`, `to_class`, `to_share`, `mass` (the share   of all units the two classes share), `share_of_from` and `share_of_to`. @noRd

.gg_tree_frames.name: .gg_tree_frames
.gg_tree_frames.documentation: The data of drawn trees: bars and bands, with each tree's facets @param trees Anchored layouts. @return A list of `bars` and `bands` data frames. @noRd

.gg_tree_plot.name: .gg_tree_plot
.gg_tree_plot.documentation: Draw one tree, or several as panels of one plot  @param trees Anchored layouts, all drawn in this plot. @param titles A list of `main`, `subtitle`, `caption` and `y`. @return A ggplot object. @noRd

.gg_view_tree.name: .gg_view_tree
.gg_view_tree.documentation: The trees of an enumeration grid, drawn  @inheritParams .latents_tree_specs @param combine `TRUE` draws every tree as a panel of one plot. @param main,subtitle Titles; `NULL` uses the view's own. @return A ggplot object for one tree or `combine = TRUE`; otherwise a   `latents_plots` list named by tree. @noRd

.multilpa_any_fit.name: .multilpa_any_fit
.multilpa_any_fit.documentation: Is this any fitted model of this package?  `multilpa_covariates` deliberately does not inherit from `multilpa`, because most methods for the latter assume fixed mixing weights that a covariate model does not have. `multilpa_transitions` is kept separate for the same reason: its mixing weights are an initial distribution and a transition matrix, not one prevalence vector. The diagnostics are the exception: they read only posteriors and counts, which every fit carries, so they accept any of them.  @param object Any object. @return `TRUE` for a fitted model of any of these classes. @noRd

.multilpa_is_seed.name: .multilpa_is_seed
.multilpa_is_seed.documentation: Which values are seeds that `set.seed()` takes exactly?  A seed is a whole number within the integer range, of either sign: that is what `set.seed()` accepts. A fraction is rejected because `set.seed()` would truncate it without notice, so two different seeds would give one stream.  @param seed Any vector. @return A logical vector, one element per element of `seed`. @noRd

.multilpa_check_seed.name: .multilpa_check_seed
.multilpa_check_seed.documentation: Refuse a seed argument that `set.seed()` would not take exactly @param seed The supplied seed, or `NULL`. @return `NULL`, invisibly; raises `latents_bad_argument` otherwise. @noRd

.multilpa_select_start.name: .multilpa_select_start
.multilpa_select_start.documentation: Choose the start a fit reports  Restarts of a mixture routinely reach the same optimum under different label permutations, and then differ only in the last bits of the likelihood. Picking by `which.max()` alone makes the reported labelling turn on floating-point noise, so the maximum is taken up to a relative tolerance far below any difference that could matter, a converged start is preferred among those tied, and then the earliest.  @param log_likelihood Numeric vector, one entry per start; `-Inf` for a   start that failed. @param converged Logical vector of the same length. @param rule `"likelihood"` takes the highest likelihood whether or not that   start converged. `"converged"` takes the highest likelihood among the   converged starts, falling back to every start when none converged. @param interior `NULL`, or a logical vector of the same length flagging   the starts with no variance at its lower bound. When supplied, only those   starts are candidates, and the rule chooses among them; when none is   flagged, every start is, with a `latents_all_starts_boundary` warning. @return A single integer index. @noRd

.multilpa_row_max.name: .multilpa_row_max
.multilpa_row_max.documentation: Row maxima of a numeric matrix  `pmax()` over the columns: the same values as `apply(x, 1L, max)`, including `NA` propagation, without one R call per row. The E-steps call this every iteration, where the per-row version dominated their cost.  @param x A numeric matrix. @return A numeric vector with one value per row. @noRd

.multilpa_notice.name: .multilpa_notice
.multilpa_notice.documentation: Raise a classed message  Base R builds classed errors and warnings (`errorCondition()`, `warningCondition()`) but has no constructor for a message, so a notice that a caller may want to silence by class is built here. @param text The message text. @param class The condition class, first in the class vector. @return `NULL`, invisibly. Called for its side effect. @noRd

.multilpa_single_level_notice.name: .multilpa_single_level_notice
.multilpa_single_level_notice.documentation: Say that a two-level verb fitted a single-level model  `multilpa()`, `multilca()` and `enumerate_classes()` are the verbs for observations nested in groups. Given `id = NULL` they fit the single-level model, which is a legitimate choice, so this is a one-line message rather than a warning, naming the model that was estimated. `lpa()`, `lca()`, `enumerate_lpa()` and `enumerate_lca()` muffle it, since their names already say it.  @param latent_class Whether every indicator is categorical. @return `NULL`, invisibly, after signalling a `latents_single_level`   message. @noRd

.multilpa_missing_id.name: .multilpa_missing_id
.multilpa_missing_id.documentation: Refuse a two-level verb called without `id`  R's own error for a missing argument names the argument but not what to do. A caller who left `id` out usually has single-level data and wants the verb that fits it by name.  @param verb The two-level verb, and `single` the single-level verbs to   point to. @return Does not return; raises `latents_bad_argument`. @noRd

.latents_sampling_weights.name: .latents_sampling_weights
.latents_sampling_weights.documentation: Resolve sampling weights to one scaled weight per unit  Sampling weights belong to the independent units the likelihood sums over: the groups of a two-level fit, the rows of a single-level one, the persons of a transition fit. A weight that varies inside a unit would be a within-unit weight, which needs a different estimator, so it is refused. The weights are scaled to sum to the number of units, as Mplus does, so the pseudo log likelihood and the information criteria stay on the sample's scale.  @param data The data frame of the fit. @param weights `NULL`, or the name of a numeric column of `data`. @param group_index Integer unit of each row, `1..n_groups`. @param n_groups Number of units. @return `NULL` for no weights, otherwise a numeric vector of length   `n_groups` that sums to `n_groups`. @noRd

.latents_refuse_weights.name: .latents_refuse_weights
.latents_refuse_weights.documentation: Refuse an option that sampling weights do not support @param what The option, as the caller should read it. @return Never returns; raises `latents_unsupported_weights`. @noRd

.latents_weighted_vcov.name: .latents_weighted_vcov
.latents_weighted_vcov.documentation: Weighted fits report sandwich standard errors only  Under pseudo maximum likelihood the inverse Hessian of the weighted log likelihood is not the variance of the estimate, and neither is the outer product of the weighted scores alone; the sandwich is (Skinner, 1989). A weighted fit therefore defaults to `"robust"` and refuses the others.  @param weighted Whether the fit carries sampling weights. @param vcov_type The requested type, already matched. @param defaulted Whether the caller left `vcov_type` at its default. @return The type to use. @noRd

.latents_is_weighted.name: .latents_is_weighted
.latents_is_weighted.documentation: Whether a fit carries sampling weights @param fit Any fit of the package. @return `TRUE` when the fit was made with `weights`. @noRd

.latents_print_weights.name: .latents_print_weights
.latents_print_weights.documentation: Print the sampling-weight line of a weighted fit  Kish's effective sample size, `(sum w)^2 / sum w^2`, says how much the weights cost in precision; it is shown beside the column name.  @param x A fit. @return `NULL`, invisibly; prints one line for a weighted fit, nothing   otherwise. @noRd
